children.translated_text: I salute <s>Śiva</s>, the abode of eternal knowledge, the treasury of supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>);
by whom alone the great [universe] beginning with <s>mahat</s> was born — by that very one, this [world], together with its agent, [was made]. //1//
Having crossed to the other shore of the oceans of all philosophical systems,
having fulfilled the purposes of all people through conduct befitting himself,
the son of the illustrious <s>Śārṅgapāṇi</s>, the knower of all <s>āgamas</s> (sacred traditions) —
the omniscient guru <s>Viṣṇu</s> — him I take refuge in daily. //2//
By the illustrious <s>Mādhavācārya</s>, the <s>Kaustubha</s>-jewel of the milk-ocean of the blessed <s>Sāyaṇa</s>, [endowed] with great might,
the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṅgraha</s> (Compendium of All Philosophical Views) is composed. //3//

children.text: pūrveṣām atidustarāṇi sutarām āloḍya śāstrāṇy asau
children.translated_text: Having thoroughly examined the exceedingly difficult-to-traverse scriptures of the ancients,
the illustrious lord <s>Sāyaṇa-Mādhava</s> will expound [them] for the delight of the virtuous.
Let the good-hearted listen with a mind from which envy has been cast far away —

children.text: mālyaṃ kasya vicitrapuṣparacitaṃ prītyai na saṃjāyate //4//
children.translated_text: a garland fashioned of variegated flowers — for whose delight does it not arise? //4//
The <s>Cārvāka</s> System //1//

children.text:
atha kathaṃ parameśvarasya niḥśreyasapradatvam abhidhīyate/ bṛhaspatimatānusāriṇā
          nāstikaśiromaṇinā cārvākeṇa tasya dūrotsāritatvāt/ durucchedaṃ hi cārvākasya ceṣṭitam/
          prāyeṇa sarvaprāṇinas tāvat
children.translated_text: Now, how can the granting of the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) be attributed to the Supreme Lord? For the <s>Cārvāka</s>, the crest-jewel of the atheists, who follows the doctrine of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, has thoroughly cast that aside. Indeed, the activity of the <s>Cārvāka</s> is hard to uproot; for virtually all living beings

children.text: yāvajjīvaṃ sukhaṃ jīven nāsti mṛtyor agocaraḥ/
children.translated_text: 'As long as one lives, one should live happily; there is no [place] beyond the reach of death.
Once the body has been reduced to ashes, whence could there be a return?'

children.text:
iti lokagāthām anurundhānā nītikāmaśāstrānusāreṇārthakāmāv eva puruṣārthau manyamānāḥ
          pāralaukikam artham apahnuvānāś cārvākamatam anuvartamānā evānubhūyante/ ata eva tasya
          cārvākamatasya lokāyatam ity anvartham aparaṃ nāmadheyam/
children.translated_text: — conforming to this popular verse, following the teachings of the science of polity and desire (<s>nīti</s> and <s>kāma</s>), considering only wealth (<s>artha</s>) and desire (<s>kāma</s>) as the goals of human life, denying any otherworldly purpose, they are observed to follow the <s>Cārvāka</s> doctrine. For this very reason, the <s>Cārvāka</s> doctrine has the fitting alternative name '<s>Lokāyata</s>' (that which is prevalent among the people).

children.text:
tatra pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni catvāri tattvāni/ tebhya eva dehākārapariṇatebhyaḥ kiṇvādibhyo
          madaśaktivac caitanyam upajāyate/ teṣu vinaṣṭeṣu satsu svayaṃ vinaśyati/ tad āhuḥ:
          vijñānaghana evaitebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya tāny evānuvinaśyati na pretya saṃjñāsti iti/
          taccaitanyaviśiṣṭadeha evātmā/ dehātirikta ātmani pramāṇābhāvāt/
          pratyakṣaikapramāṇavāditayānumānāder anaṅgīkāreṇa prāmāṇyābhāvāt/ aṅganādyāliṅganādijanyaṃ
          sukham eva puruṣārthaḥ/ na cāsya duḥkhasaṃbhinnatayā puruṣārthatvam eva nāstīti mantavyam/
          avarjanīyatayā prāptasya duḥkhasya parihāreṇa sukhamātrasyaiva bhoktavyatvāt/ tad yathā
          matsyārthī saśalkān sakaṇṭakān matsyān upādatte sa yāvad ādeyaṃ tāvad ādāya nivartate/
          yathā vā dhānyārthī sapalālāni dhānyāny āharati sa yāvad ādeyaṃ tāvad ādāya nivartate/
          tasmād duḥkhabhayān nānukūlavedanīyaṃ sukhaṃ tyaktum ucitam/ na hi mṛgāḥ santīti śālayo
          nopyante/ na hi bhikṣukāḥ santīti sthālyo nādhiśrīyante/ yadi kaścid bhīrur dṛṣṭaṃ sukhaṃ
          tyajet tarhi sa paśuvan mūrkho bhavet/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: Therein, the four elements — earth, water, fire, and air — are the [only] realities (<s>tattvas</s>). From these very [elements], when transformed into the configuration of a body, consciousness arises — just as the power of intoxication arises from fermented ingredients such as <s>kiṇva</s> (yeast) and the like. When those [elements] are destroyed, [consciousness] itself perishes. As they say: 'Consciousness is a mass that arises from these very elements, and, arising, perishes along with them; there is no awareness after death.' Thus, the body endowed with consciousness is itself the self (<s>ātman</s>) — because there is no means of valid knowledge for a self beyond the body. Since they hold that perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is the only valid means of knowledge, inference (<s>anumāna</s>) and the like are not accepted, and thus have no validity. Pleasure born from the embrace of a woman's limbs and the like is the [sole] goal of human life. Nor should it be thought that because [pleasure] is mixed with pain, it therefore is not a goal of human life — for the pleasure alone should be enjoyed while avoiding the pain that inevitably accompanies it. Just as one who desires fish takes fish along with scales and thorns, and then takes what is to be taken and discards [the rest]; or just as one who desires grain takes grain along with the straw, and then takes what is to be taken and discards [the rest]. Therefore, one should not, out of fear of pain, abandon pleasure that is agreeable to experience. For fields of grain are not left unsown just because deer exist; cooking-pots are not left unheated just because beggars exist. If some timid person were to abandon evident pleasure, he would be a fool like a beast. As it is said:
'That the pleasure born of sensory contact should be abandoned by men
because it is accompanied by pain — this is the reasoning of fools;
who, desiring his own welfare, would cast away rice grains

children.text: ko nāma bhos tuṣakaṇopahitān hitārthī// iti
children.translated_text: rich in excellent white kernels, merely because they are covered with husks?'

children.text:
nanu pāralaukikasukhābhāve bahuvittavyayaśarīrāyāsasādhye ´gnihotrādau vidyāvṛddhāḥ
          kathaṃ pravartiṣyanta iti cet tad api na pramāṇakoṭiṃ praveṣṭum īṣṭe/
          anṛtavyāghātapunaruktadoṣair dūṣitatayā vaidikaṃmanyaiṛ eva dhūrtabakaiḥ parasparaṃ
          karmakāṇḍaprāmāṇyavādibhir jñānakāṇḍasya jñānakāṇḍaprāmāṇyavādibhiḥ karmakāṇḍasya ca
          pratikṣiptatvena trayyā dhūrtapralāpamātratvenāgnihotrāder jīvikāmātraprayojanatvāt/ tathā
          cābhāṇakaḥ:
children.translated_text: Objection: 'In the absence of otherworldly happiness, how would those learned in the <s>Vedas</s> engage in the <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire-sacrifice) and the like, which require the expenditure of much wealth and the exertion of the body?' Reply: Even that cannot enter the category of valid evidence. Because it is vitiated by the faults of falsehood, self-contradiction, and tautology — and because, among those who consider themselves Vedic, the cunning imposters (<s>dhūrtabakas</s>) who advocate the authority of the ritual section (<s>karmakāṇḍa</s>) reject the knowledge section (<s>jñānakāṇḍa</s>), and those who advocate the authority of the knowledge section reject the ritual section — [it follows that] the three <s>Vedas</s> are nothing but the prattle of rogues, and the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like serve merely as a means of livelihood. And thus the [well-known] saying goes:
'The <s>Agnihotra</s>, the three <s>Vedas</s>, the triple staff, and smearing oneself with ashes —
these are the livelihood of those devoid of intelligence and manliness, says <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.'

children.text:
ata eva kaṇṭakādijanyaṃ duḥkham eva narakaḥ/ lokasiddho rājā parameśvaraḥ/ dehocchedo
          mokṣaḥ/ dehātmavāde ca sthūlo ’haṃ kṛśo ’haṃ kṛṣṇo ’ham ityādi sāmānādhikaraṇyopapattiḥ/
          mama śarīram iti vyavahāro rāhoḥ śira ityādivad aupacārikaḥ/ tad etat sarvaṃ
          samagrāhi:
children.translated_text: For this very reason, pain caused by thorns and the like is itself hell; the king well-established in the world is the Supreme Lord; the cessation of the body is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). And in the doctrine that the body is the self, the co-referentiality in expressions like 'I am stout,' 'I am thin,' 'I am dark' is justified; and the usage 'my body' is merely figurative, like [the expression] '<s>Rāhu</s>'s head.' All of this has been comprehensively stated:
The pleasure born of the embrace of limbs is itself the goal of human life;
pain born of thorns and the like is called hell. //1//

children.text: lokasiddho bhaved rājā pareśo nāparaḥ smṛtaḥ/
children.translated_text: The king well-established in the world is the Supreme Lord — no other is so held;

children.text: dehasya nāśo muktis tu na jñānān muktir iṣyate //2//
children.translated_text: the destruction of the body is liberation — liberation is not accepted as arising from knowledge. //2//
Here, the four elements — earth, water, fire, and air — [are the only realities];
from these four elements alone, consciousness arises. //3//
Just as the power of intoxication from ingredients like <s>kiṇva</s> (yeast) and the like when combined;
from the co-referentiality [seen] in 'I am stout,' 'I am thin,' //4//

children.text: dehaḥ sthaulyādiyogāc ca sa evātmā na cāparaḥ/
children.translated_text: the body — since it possesses corpulence and the like — is itself the self, and nothing else;

children.text: mama deho ´yam ity uktiḥ saṃbhaved aupacārikī //5// iti
children.translated_text: the expression 'this is my body' would be [merely] figurative. //5//

children.text:
syād etat/ syād eṣa manoratho yady anumānādeḥ prāmāṇyaṃ na syāt/ asti ca prāmāṇyam/
          katham anyathā dhūmopalambhānantaraṃ dhūmadhvaje prekṣāvatāṃ pravṛttir upapadyeta/ nadyās
          tīre phalāni santīti vacanaśravaṇasamanantaraṃ phalārthināṃ nadītīre pravṛttir iti/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'This might be a fantasy if inference and the like had no validity. But they do have validity. For how else would the activity of discerning persons toward fire after perceiving smoke be justified? [Similarly,] upon hearing the statement "there are fruits on the bank of the river," the activity of those desiring fruits toward the riverbank [is justified through verbal testimony].'

children.text:
tad etan manorājyavijṛmbhaṇam/ vyāptipakṣadharmatāśāli hi liṅgaṃ gamakam abhyugatam
          anumānaprāmāṇyavādibhiḥ/ vyāptiś cobhayavidhopādhividhuraḥ saṃbandhaḥ/ sa ca sattayā
          cakṣurādivan nāṅgabhāvaṃ bhajate/ kiṃ tu jñātatayā/ kaḥ khalu jñānopāyo bhavet/ na tāvat
          pratyakṣam/ tac ca bāhyam āntaraṃ vābhimatam/ na prathamaḥ/ tasya
          saṃprayuktaviṣayajñānajanakatvena bhavati prasarasaṃbhave ’pi bhūtabhaviṣyatos
          tadasaṃbhavena sarvopasaṃhāravatyā vyāpter durjñānatvāt/ na ca vyāptijñānaṃ sāmānyagocaram
          iti mantavyam/ vyaktyor avinābhāvābhāvaprasaṅgāt/ nāpi caramaḥ/ antaḥkaraṇasya
          bahirindriyatantratvena bāhye ’rthe svātantryeṇa pravṛttyanupapatteḥ/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: Reply: This is merely an expansion of fantasy. For the proponents of inferential validity accept a probans (<s>liṅga</s>) possessing pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) and the property of the minor term (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) as probative. And pervasion is a relation free from both kinds of limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>). And that [pervasion] does not become a component [of inference] through [mere] existence, like the eye and the like, but rather through being known. Now what means of knowledge could [establish] it? Not direct perception, first of all. And that [perception] is held to be either external or internal. Not the first [external perception] — because, although [the senses] produce knowledge of the objects with which they are in contact, and even though they may have scope [for present objects], since [pervasion includes] past and future [instances] where such [contact] is impossible, pervasion — which involves universal generalization — is impossible to know [by perception]. Nor should it be thought that the knowledge of pervasion has [mere] universals as its object — for then there would be the undesirable consequence of the absence of invariable concomitance between individual instances. Nor [is it established by] the latter [internal perception] — because the inner organ, being dependent on the external senses, cannot independently engage with external objects. As it is said:
'The mind, [directed at] the object indicated by the eye and the rest, is dependent [when dealing with] external [objects].'

children.text:
nāpy anumānaṃ vyāptijñānopāyaḥ/ tatra tatrāpy evam ity anavasthādauḥsthyaprasaṅgāt/ nāpi
          śabdas tadupāyaḥ/ kāṇādamatānusāreṇānumāna evāntarbhāvāt/ anantarbhāve vā
          vṛddhavyavahārarūpaliṅgāvagatisāpekṣatayā prāguktadūṣaṇalaṅghanājaṅghālatvāt/
          dhūmadhūmadhvajayor avinābhāvo ´stīti vacanamātre manvādivad viśvāsābhāvāc ca/
          anupadiṣṭāvinābhāvasya puruṣasyārthāntaradarśanenārthāntarānumityabhāve
          svārthānumānakathāyāḥ kathāśeṣatvaprasaṅgāc ca kaiva kathā parārthānumānasya/ upamānādikaṃ
          tu dūrāpāstam/ teṣāṃ
          saṃjñāsaṃjñisaṃbandhādibodhakatvenānaupādhika-saṃbandhabodhakatvāsaṃbhavāt/
children.translated_text: Nor is inference the means of knowing pervasion — because even there, the same [problem would recur], and the undesirable consequence of infinite regress would arise. Nor is verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) the means for that — because, according to the <s>Kaṇāda</s> (Vaiśeṣika) system, it is subsumed under inference; or, if not subsumed, because [verbal testimony] depends on the apprehension of a probans in the form of the convention of the elders — and thus it lacks the strength to overcome the previously stated objections. And because there is no trust — as with the words of <s>Manu</s> and the like — in the mere statement 'there is invariable concomitance between smoke and fire.' And because, for a person to whom invariable concomitance has not been taught, in the absence of inferring one thing from seeing another thing, the discourse on inference-for-oneself would be reduced to a mere tale — what then is the point of discussing inference-for-others? As for analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) and the rest, they are far removed [from establishing pervasion] — since, being productive of knowledge of the relation between name and named and the like, they cannot possibly produce knowledge of an unconditional (<s>anupādhika</s>) relation.

children.text:
kiṃ ca, upādhyabhāvo ´pi duravagamaḥ/ upādhīnāṃ pratyakṣatvaniyamāsaṃbhavena pratyakṣāṇām
          abhāvasya pratyakṣatve ´py apratyakṣāṇām abhāvasyāpratyakṣatayānumānādyapekṣāyām
          uktadūṣaṇānativṛtteḥ/ api ca sādhanāvyāpakatve sati sādhyasamavyāptir iti tallakṣaṇaṃ
          kakṣīkartavyam/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: Moreover, the absence of limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) is also difficult to ascertain — since the absence of perceptible [conditions] cannot be established by perception alone, and the absence of imperceptible [conditions], being itself imperceptible, requires inference and the like — the previously stated objections are not overcome. Furthermore, the definition [of upādhi] that should be accepted is: 'that which is co-extensive with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) while not pervading the <s>sādhana</s> (probans).' As it is said:

children.text: avyāptasādhano yaḥ sādhyasamavyāptir ucyate sa upādhiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'That which does not pervade the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) and is co-extensive with the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) — that is called an <s>upādhi</s> (limiting condition).'
is to be proved — being-produced-by-an-agent, pot-ness, and non-hearingness —
'In the case of sound, when impermanence

children.text: vyāvartayitum upāttāny atra kramato viśeṣaṇāni trīṇi/
children.translated_text: three qualifications have been adopted here in order

children.text: tasmād idam anavadyaṃ samāsametyādinoktam ācāryaiś ca// iti
children.translated_text: to exclude [each of these] respectively; therefore this [definition] is faultless, as stated by the masters beginning with <s>Samāsametin</s>.'

children.text:
tatra vidhyadhyavasāyapūrvakatvān niṣedhādhyavasāyasyopādhijñāne jāte
          tadabhāvaviśiṣṭasaṃbandharūpavyāptijñānaṃ vyāptijñānādhīnaṃ copādhijñānam iti
          parasparāśrayavajraprahāradoṣo vajralepāyate/ tasmād avinābhāvasya durbodhatayā
          nānumānādyavakāśaḥ/ dhūmādijñānānantaram agnyādijñāne pravṛttiḥ pratyakṣamūlatayā bhrāntyā
          vā yujyate/ kvacit phalapratilambhas tu maṇimantrauṣadhādivad yādṛcchikaḥ/ atas tatsādhyam
          adṛṣṭādikam api nāsti/
children.translated_text: Therein, since the cognitive ascertainment of negation presupposes the cognitive ascertainment of [something] positive — when the knowledge of the limiting condition has arisen, the knowledge of pervasion in the form of a relation qualified by the absence of that [condition] is dependent on the knowledge of pervasion; and the knowledge of the limiting condition is dependent on the knowledge of pervasion — thus the flaw of mutual dependence strikes like a thunderbolt, [and then] is sealed like a thunderbolt-plaster. Therefore, since invariable concomitance is difficult to know, there is no scope for inference and the like. Activity toward the knowledge of fire and the like following the knowledge of smoke and the like is justified either through [prior] perception or through error. And the occasional obtaining of results [from inference] is accidental, like [the effects of] gems, <s>mantras</s>, and herbs. Therefore, even the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) and the like, which are established through that [inference], do not exist.

children.text: nanv adṛṣṭāniṣṭau jagadvaicitryam ākasmikaṃ syād iti cen
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Without the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), the variety of the world would be accidental.'

children.text: na tad bhadram/ svabhāvād eva tadupapatteḥ/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: Reply: Not so — because it is justified by [the entities'] own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) alone. As it is said:

children.text: agnir uṣṇo jalaṃ śītaṃ samasparśas tathānilaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Fire is hot, water is cold, and the touch of wind is temperate —

children.text: kenedaṃ citritaṃ tasmāt svabhāvāt tadvyavasthitiḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: by whom was this variegated? Therefore, its arrangement is from [its own] nature.'
All this has been stated by <s>Bṛhaspati</s> as well:

children.text: na svargo nāpavargo vā naivātmā pāralaukikaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'There is no heaven, no final liberation, nor any soul in the other world;
nor do the rites of the <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> produce any fruit. //1//
The <s>Agnihotra</s>, the three <s>Vedas</s>, the triple staff, and smearing with ashes —
these are the livelihood fashioned by the Creator for those devoid of intelligence and manliness. //2//

children.text: paśuś cen nihataḥ svargaṃ jyotiṣṭome gamiṣyati/
children.translated_text: If an animal slain in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice goes to heaven,

children.text: svapitā yajamānena tatra kasmān na hiṃsyate //3//
children.translated_text: then why does the sacrificer not slay his own father there? //3//

children.text: mṛtānām api jantūnāṃ śrāddhaṃ cet tṛptikāraṇam/
children.translated_text: If the <s>śrāddha</s> (funerary rite) is a cause of satisfaction for dead beings,
then oil should be able to augment the flame of an extinguished lamp. //4//
If provision for the journey is futile for beings traveling here [in this world] —

children.text:
The second halves of verses 4 and 5 are absent from all earlier editions; see
                Bhattacharya 2011.

children.translated_text: then [why not claim that] satisfaction on the road is achieved by the <s>śrāddha</s> performed at home? //5//

children.text: svargasthitā yadā tṛptiṃ gaccheyus tatra dānataḥ/
children.translated_text: If those dwelling in heaven could attain satisfaction through offerings [made] there,
then why is [food] not given [from below] to those standing on the upper floor of a building? //6//

children.text: yāvaj jīvet sukhaṃ jīved ṛṇaṃ kṛtvā ghṛtaṃ pibet/
children.translated_text: As long as one lives, one should live happily; let one drink ghee even by taking on debt;
once the body has been reduced to ashes, whence could there be a return? //7//

children.text: yadi gacchet paraṃ lokaṃ dehād eṣa vinirgataḥ/
children.translated_text: If one who has departed from the body goes to another world,
why does he not come back again, overwhelmed by affection for his kinsmen? //8//

children.text: tataś ca jīvanopāyo brāhmaṇair vihitas tv iha/
children.translated_text: Therefore, the means of livelihood has been devised here by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>;

children.text: mṛtānāṃ pretakāryāṇi na tv anyad vidyate kvacit //9//
children.translated_text: the funerary rites for the dead [serve this purpose], and nothing else exists anywhere. //9//
The authors of the three <s>Vedas</s> are buffoons, knaves, and demons;
'<s>Jarbharī</s>, <s>Turpharī</s>' and the like are regarded as the words of the learned. //10//

children.text: aśvasyātra hi śiśnaṃ tu patnīgrāhyaṃ prakīrtitam/
children.translated_text: The phallus of a horse is proclaimed to be grasped by the [sacrificer's] wife here;

children.text: bhaṇḍais tadvat paraṃ caiva grāhyajātaṃ prakīrtitam //11//
children.translated_text: and by buffoons, other things of a similar nature to be grasped are likewise proclaimed. //11//
The eating of flesh is likewise prompted by demons.' //

children.text: tasmād bahūnāṃ prāṇinām anugrahārthaṃ cārvākamatam āśrayaṇīyam iti ramaṇīyam//
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the benefit of many living beings, the <s>Cārvāka</s> doctrine should be resorted to — how delightful!
Thus [ends] the <s>Cārvāka</s> system in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Now, the Buddhist (<s>Bauddha</s>) system. //2//
Section 2.1

children.text:
atra bauddhair abhidhīyate/ yad abhyadhāyi avinābhāvo durbodha iti tad asādhīyaḥ/
          tādātmyatadutpattibhyām avinābhāvasya sujñānatvāt/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: Here the Buddhists say: That which was stated — that invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) is difficult to know — that is incorrect, because invariable concomitance is easily known through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and causal relation (<s>tadutpatti</s>). As stated:
"The restriction of invariable concomitance [is established] either from the relation of cause and effect, or from essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) as the determining factor;
it is [established] from perception, not from non-perception."
Section 2.6

children.text:
anvayavyatirekāv avinābhāvaniścāyakāv iti pakṣe sādhyasādhanayor avyabhicāro
          duravadhāraṇo bhavet/ bhūte bhaviṣyati vartamāne cānupalabhyamāne ´rthe vyabhicāraśaṅkāyā
          anivāraṇāt/
children.translated_text: If the position is that positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) are the determinants of invariable concomitance, then the non-deviation between what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) and the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) would be difficult to ascertain, because the suspicion of deviation cannot be prevented regarding an object that is not apprehended in the past, future, or present.

children.text: nanu tathāvidhasthale tāvake ´pi mate vyabhicāraśaṅkā duṣparihāreti cet
children.translated_text: Now, if [one says]: "Even in your own view, the suspicion of deviation in such a case is difficult to remove" —

children.text:
māivaṃ vocaḥ/ vināpi kāraṇaṃ kāryam utpadyatām ity evaṃvidhāyāḥ śaṅkāyā
          vyāghātāvadhikatayā nivṛttatvāt/ tad eva hy āśaṅkyeta yasminn āśaṅkyamāne vyāghātādayo
          nāvatareyuḥ/ tad uktam: vyāghātāvadhir āśaṅkā iti/ tasmāt tadutpattiniścayenāvinābhāvo
          niścīyate/ tadutpattiniścayaś ca kāryahetvoḥ
          pratyakṣopalambhānupalambhapañcakanibandhanaḥ/ (1) kāryasyotpatteḥ prāg anupalambhaḥ (2-3)
          kāraṇopalambhe saty upalambhaḥ (4-5) upalabdhasya paścāt kāraṇānupalambhād anupalambhaḥ
          iti pañcakāraṇyā dhūmadhūmadhvajayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo niścīyate/ tathā tādātmyaniścayenāpy
          avinābhāvo niścīyate/ yadi śiṃśapā vṛkṣatvam atipatet svātmānam eva jahyād iti vipakṣe
          bādhakapravṛtteḥ/ apravṛtte tu bādhake bhūyaḥ sahabhāvopalambhe ´pi vyabhicāraśaṅkāyāḥ ko
          nivārayitā/ śiṃśapāvṛkṣayoś ca tādātmyaniścayo vṛkṣo ´yaṃ śiṃśapeti sāmānādhikaraṇyabalād
          upapadyate/ na hy atyantābhede tat saṃbhavati/ paryāyatvena yugapat prayogāyogāt/ nāpy
          atyantabhede/ gavāśvayor anupalambhāt/ tasmāt kāryātmānau kāraṇātmānāv anumāpayata iti
          siddham/
children.translated_text: Do not say so! Because the suspicion of the type "Let an effect arise even without a cause" is eliminated, since it is bounded by self-contradiction (<s>vyāghāta</s>). For only that can be doubted which, when doubted, would not entail self-contradiction and the like. As stated: "Doubt is bounded by self-contradiction." Therefore, invariable concomitance is ascertained by the ascertainment of causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>). And the ascertainment of causal origination depends on the fivefold [procedure] of perception and non-perception between cause and effect: (1) the non-perception of the effect before its origination; (2-3) its perception when the cause is perceived; (4-5) and after being perceived, its non-perception upon the non-perception of the cause — by this fivefold reasoning, the cause-effect relation between smoke and fire is ascertained. Likewise, invariable concomitance is also ascertained through the ascertainment of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). If the <s>śiṃśapā</s> (a type of tree) were to transcend tree-ness, it would abandon its own nature — because the invalidating argument operates in the counter-instance. But when no invalidating argument operates, even upon repeated co-observation, who would prevent the suspicion of deviation? And the ascertainment of identity between <s>śiṃśapā</s> and tree is established by the force of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) in the expression "This tree is a <s>śiṃśapā</s>." For that [co-referentiality] is not possible in the case of complete identity, because of the impossibility of simultaneous use as synonyms; nor in the case of complete difference, because it is not observed for cow and horse. Therefore, what have the nature of effect infer what have the nature of cause — this is established.
Section 2.25

children.text:
yadi kaścit prāmāṇyam anumānasya nāṅgīkuryāt taṃ prati brūyāt/ anumānaṃ pramāṇaṃ na
          bhavatīty etāvanmātram ucyate tatra na kiṃcana sādhanam upanyasyata upanyasyate vā/ na
          prathamaḥ/ aśiraskavacanasyopanyāse sādhyāsiddheḥ/
children.translated_text: If someone does not accept the validity of inference, one should say to him: "Inference is not a valid means of knowledge" — is this much merely stated, and no proof adduced, or is proof being adduced? Not the first, because from the adduction of a headless statement, the thing to be proved remains unestablished.

children.text: ekākinī pratijñā hi pratijñātaṃ na sādhayet/
children.translated_text: "A mere assertion alone does not establish what is asserted" —

children.text:
iti nyāyāt/ nāpi caramaḥ/ anumānaṃ pramāṇaṃ na bhavatīti bruvāṇena vacanapramāṇam
          anabhyupagacchatā tvayā svaparakīyaśāstre prāmāṇyenopagṛhītasya vacanasyopanyāse mama mātā
          vandhyetivad vyāghātāpātāt/ kiṃ ca pramāṇatadābhāsavyavasthāpanaṃ tatsamānajātīyatvād iti
          vadatā bhavataiva svīkṛtaṃ svabhāvānumānam/ paragatā vipratipattis tu vacanaliṅgeneti
          bruvatā kāryaliṅgakam anumānam/ anupalabdhyā kaṃcid arthaṃ
          pratiṣedhayatānupalabdhiliṅgakam anumānam/ tathā coktaṃ tathāgataiḥ:
children.translated_text: by this principle. Nor the second; for by you who, while saying "Inference is not a valid means of knowledge," do not accept verbal testimony as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, in adducing a statement accepted as valid in your own and others' treatises, the fallacy of self-contradiction arises, like [saying] "My mother is barren." Moreover, by you yourself, in saying "The determination of valid means of knowledge and their semblances [is possible] because of being of the same class as those" — a <s>svabhāva</s>-inference (inference from essential nature) has been accepted. And by saying "The misapprehension in the opponent is [known] through the mark of speech" — an inference based on the mark of effect (<s>kāryaliṅga</s>) [has been accepted]. And by one who negates some object through non-apprehension — an inference based on the mark of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhiliṅga</s>) [has been accepted]. And thus it has been stated by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>:
"Because of the common position with other means of knowledge, because of the going to a different cognition,
and because of the negation of something — the existence of other means of knowledge [is established]."

children.text: parākrāntaṃ cātra sūribhir iti granthabhūyastvabhayād uparamyate/
children.translated_text: The learned have gone far in this matter, but we desist for fear of the volume of the treatise.
Section 2.41

children.text:
te ca bauddhāś caturvidhayā bhāvanayā paramapuruṣārthaṃ kathayanti/ te ca
          mādhyamikayogācārasautrāntikavaibhāṣikasaṃjñābhiḥ prasiddhā bauddhā yathākramaṃ
          sarvaśūnyatvabāhyārthaśūnyatvabāhyārthānumeyatvabāhyārtha-pratyakṣatvavādān ātiṣṭhante/
          yady api bhagavān buddha eka eva bodhayitā tathāpi boddhavyānāṃ buddhibhedāc cāturvidhyam/
          yathā gato ´stam arka ity ukte jāracaurānūcānādayaḥ
          sveṣṭānusāreṇābhisaraṇaparasvaharaṇasadācaraṇādisamayaṃ budhyante/
children.translated_text: And those Buddhists, through fourfold meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), teach the supreme goal of human existence. Those Buddhists, known by the designations <s>Mādhyamika</s>, <s>Yogācāra</s>, <s>Sautrāntika</s>, and <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>, uphold respectively the doctrines of the emptiness of all things, the emptiness of external objects, the inferability of external objects, and the perceptibility of external objects. Although the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> is one and the same teacher, the fourfold division arises because of the differences in the intellects of those to be taught. Just as when it is said "The sun has set," the paramour, the thief, the Vedic student, and the like understand the time for assignation, theft, proper conduct, and so forth, each according to their own interest.

children.text:
sarvaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ śūnyaṃ śūnyam iti
          bhāvanācatuṣṭayam upadiṣtaṃ draṣṭavyam/
children.translated_text: "Everything is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>), momentary; suffering, suffering; having its own characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), having its own characteristic; empty (<s>śūnya</s>), empty" — this fourfold meditation is taught and should be understood.
Section 2.48

children.text:
tatra kṣaṇikatvaṃ nīlādikṣaṇānāṃ sattvenānumātavyaṃ yat sat tat kṣaṇikaṃ yathā
          jaladharapaṭalaṃ santaś cāmī bhāvā iti/ na cāyam asiddho hetuḥ/
          arthakriyākāritvalakṣaṇasya sattvasya nīlādikṣaṇānāṃ pratyakṣasiddhatvāt/ vyāpakavyāvṛttyā
          vyāpyavyāvṛttir iti nyāyena vyāpakakramākramavyāvṛttāv akṣaṇikāt sattvavyāvṛtteḥ
          siddhatvāc ca/ tac cārthakriyākāritvaṃ kramākramābhyām vyāptam/ na ca kramākramābhyām
          anyaḥ prakāraḥ saṃbhavati/
children.translated_text: Therein, momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) of moments such as blue and the like is to be inferred through existence (<s>sattva</s>): whatever exists is momentary, like a mass of clouds; and these entities exist — thus. And this is not an unestablished reason (<s>hetu</s>), because existence — defined as the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>) — is established by direct perception for moments such as blue and the like. And it is established because, by the principle "the exclusion of the pervaded follows from the exclusion of the pervader," when the pervader — sequence and simultaneity — is excluded from the non-momentary, existence is excluded. And that causal efficacy is pervaded by sequence and simultaneity. Nor is any other mode possible besides sequence and simultaneity.
"For when there is mutual opposition, there is no other mode;
nor is there unity of contradictories, because of contradiction from mere statement alone" —

children.text:
iti nyāyena vyāghātasyodbhaṭatvāt/ tau ca kramākramau sthāyinaḥ sakāśād vyāvartamānāv
          arthakriyām api vyāvartayantau kṣaṇikatvapakṣa eva sattvaṃ vyavasthāpayata iti
          siddham/
children.translated_text: by this principle, since the self-contradiction is blatant. And those two — sequence and simultaneity — being excluded from the permanent, while also excluding causal efficacy, establish existence only in the thesis of momentariness. This is proven.
Section 2.60

children.text: nanv akṣaṇikasyārthakriyākāritvaṃ kiṃ na syād iti cet
children.translated_text: Now, if [one asks]: "Why could the non-momentary not have causal efficacy?" —

children.text:
tad ayuktam/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ tathā hi: vartamānārthakriyākaraṇakāle ´tītānāgatayoḥ kim
          arthakriyayoḥ sthāyinaḥ sāmarthyam asti no vā/
children.translated_text: That is improper, because it does not withstand analysis. For thus: at the time when [the permanent entity] is performing a present causal action, does the permanent [entity] have the capacity for the past and future causal actions, or not?

children.text:
i) ādye tayor anirākaraṇaprasaṅgaḥ/ samarthasya kṣepāyogāt/ yad yadā yatkaraṇasamarthaṃ
          tat tadā tat karoty eva yathā sāmagrī svakāryaṃ samarthaś cāyaṃ bhāva iti prasaṅgānumānāc
          ca/
children.translated_text: (i) In the first case, the absurd consequence of their non-exclusion [follows], because what is capable cannot be prevented. Whatever is capable of doing something at some time does that very thing at that time, like a complete set of causes [producing] its effect; and this entity is capable — [this follows] from the <s>prasaṅga</s>-inference (reductio ad absurdum) as well.

children.text:
(ii) dvitīye kadāpi na kuryāt/ sāmarthyamātrānubandhitvād arthakriyākāritvasya/ yad yadā
          yan na karoti tat tadā tatrāsamarthaṃ yathā hi śilāśakalam aṅkure/ na caiṣa
          vartamānārthakriyākaraṇakāle vṛttavartiṣyamāṇe arthakriye karotīti tadviparyayāc ca/
children.translated_text: (ii) In the second case, it would never perform [any action], because causal efficacy depends solely on capacity. Whatever does not do something at some time is incapable of that at that time, like a piece of stone [is incapable] of [producing] a sprout. And this [permanent entity] does not perform the past and future causal actions at the time of performing the present causal action — and from the converse of that as well.

children.text:
nanu kramavatsahakārilābhāt sthāyino ’tītānāgatayoḥ krameṇa karaṇam upapadyata iti
          cet
children.translated_text: Now, if [one says]: "Like [things that act in] sequence, through the obtaining of auxiliary conditions, the permanent [entity] performs [past and future actions] sequentially" —

children.text: tatredaṃ bhavān pṛṣṭo vyācaṣṭām/ sahakāriṇaḥ kiṃ bhāvasyopakurvanti na vā/
children.translated_text: Then here, let the honorable one, when asked, explain: Do the auxiliary conditions contribute something to the entity, or not?

children.text:
(A) na cen nāpekṣaṇīyās te/ akiṃcitkurvatāṃ teṣāṃ tādarthyāyogāt/ [atha bhāvas taiḥ
          sahakāribhiḥ sahaiva kāryaṃ karotīti svabhāva iti cet/
children.translated_text: (A) If not, then they need not be relied upon, since things that do nothing have no purpose for that [entity]. [If one says: "The entity performs action together with those auxiliary conditions — this is its nature" —

children.text:
aṅga tarhi sahakāriṇo na jahyāt/ pratyuta palāyamānān api gale pāśena baddhvā kṛtyaṃ
          kāryaṃ kuryāt/ svabhāvasyānapāyāt/]
This passage is situated immediately after the verse

children.translated_text: Then it should not let go of the auxiliary conditions! Rather, it should even bind them by a noose around the neck when they flee, and make them do their work — since its nature does not depart.]

children.text: (B) upakārakatvapakṣe so ’yam upakāraḥ kiṃ bhāvād bhidyate na vā/
children.translated_text: (B) If they do contribute, then this contribution — does it differ from the entity, or not?

children.text:
(B1) bhedapakṣa āgantukasyaiva tasya kāraṇatvaṃ syāt/ na bhāvasyākṣaṇikasya/
          āgantukātiśayānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyitvāt kāryasya/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: (B1) In the case of difference, only that adventitious [contribution] would be the cause, not the non-momentary entity, because the effect conforms to the positive and negative concomitance of the adventitious enhancement alone. As stated:

children.text: varṣātapābhyāṃ kiṃ vyomnaś carmaṇy asti tayoḥ phalam/
children.translated_text: "What [benefit] is there of rain and sunshine to space? Their fruit belongs to leather.

children.text: carmopamaś cet so ’nityaḥ khatulyaś ced asatphalaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: If [the entity is] like leather, then it is non-permanent; if like space, then it bears no fruit."
Section 2.80

children.text:
kiṃ ca sahakārijanyo ´tiśayaḥ kim atiśayāntaram ārabhate na vā/ ubhayathāpi
          dūṣaṇapāṣāṇavarṣaṇaprasaṅgaḥ/ atiśayāntarārambhapakṣe bahumukhānavasthādauḥsthyam api
          syāt/ atiśaye janayitavye sahakāryantarāpekṣāyāṃ tatparamparāpāta ity ekānavasthāstheyā/
          tathā sahakāribhiḥ salilapavanādibhiḥ padārthasārthair ādhīyamāne bījasyātiśaye bījam
          utpādakam abhyupeyam/ aparathā tadabhāve ´py atiśayaḥ prādurbhavet/ bījaṃ cātiśayam
          ādadhānaṃ sahakārisāpekṣam evādhatte/ anyathā sarvadopakārāpattāv aṅkurasyāpi sadodayaḥ
          prasajyeta/ tasmād atiśayārtham apekṣyamāṇaiḥ sahakāribhir atiśayāntaram ādheyaṃ bīje/
          tasminn apy upakāre pūrvanyāyena sahakārisāpekṣasya bījasya janakatve
          sahakārisaṃpādyabījagatātiśayānavasthā prathamā vyavasthitā/
children.translated_text: Moreover, does the enhancement produced by the auxiliary condition initiate another enhancement, or not? In both cases, there is a downpour of stones of refutation. In the case of initiating another enhancement, there would be the misery of a many-branched infinite regress. When another auxiliary condition is required for the enhancement to be produced, there would be an infinite chain of such [conditions] — one infinite regress must be accepted. Likewise, when enhancement is produced in the seed by auxiliary conditions such as water, wind, and the like — hosts of substances — the seed must be accepted as the producer. Otherwise, the enhancement would manifest even in its absence. And the seed, producing the enhancement, does so only in dependence on auxiliary conditions; otherwise, if contribution were possible at all times, even the sprout would always arise. Therefore, another enhancement must be produced in the seed by the auxiliary conditions required for the purpose of enhancement. And when, in that contribution too, the seed is the producer through dependence on auxiliary conditions by the same prior reasoning — the first infinite regress of enhancement residing in the seed brought about by auxiliary conditions is established.

children.text:
athopakāraḥ kāryārtham apekṣyamāṇo ´pi bījādinirapekṣaṃ kāryaṃ janayati tatsāpekṣaṃ vā/
          prathame bījāder ahetutvam āpatet/ dvitīye ´pekṣyamāṇena bījādinopakāre ´tiśaya
          ādheyaḥ/evaṃ tatra tatrāpīti bījādijanyātiśayaniṣṭhātiśayaparamparāpāta iti
          dvitīyānavasthā sthirā bhavet/ evam apekṣyamāṇenopakāreṇa bījādau dharmiṇy upakārāntaram
          ādheyam ity upakārādheyabījāśrayātiśayaparamparāpāta iti tṛtīyānavasthāduravasthā
          syāt/
children.translated_text: Now, does the contribution, even though required for the effect, produce the effect independently of the seed and the like, or dependently? In the first case, the absurd consequence of the seed and the like not being causes would follow. In the second case, the seed and the like, being required, must produce enhancement in the contribution — thus, there too likewise — and so the second infinite regress of successive enhancements produced by the seed and the like would be firm. Likewise, when the required contribution must produce another contribution in the substratum, namely the seed and the like — the third infinite regress of successive enhancements resting in the seed that receives the contribution would be a most unfortunate predicament.

children.text:
(B2) atha bhāvād abhinno ´tiśayaḥ sahakāribhir ādhīyata ity abhyupagamyeta tarhi prācīno
          bhāvo ´natiśayātmā nivṛtto ´nyaś cātiśayātmā kurvadrūpādipadavedanīyo jāyata iti phalitaṃ
          mamāpi manorathadrumeṇa/ tasmāt krameṇākṣaṇikasyārthakriyā durghaṭā/
children.translated_text: (B2) Now, if it is accepted that the enhancement, which is non-different from the entity, is produced by the auxiliary conditions — then the old entity, which did not have the nature of enhancement, has ceased, and another, having the nature of enhancement and cognizable as having a functioning form, has arisen — this is the fruit of my wish-fulfilling tree as well. Therefore, the sequential causal efficacy of the non-momentary is impossible to establish.
[Section 2.101]

children.text:
nāpy akrameṇa ghaṭate/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ tathā hi/ yugapat sakalakāryakaraṇasamarthaḥ
          svabhāvas taduttarakālam anuvartate na vā/
children.translated_text: Nor does it work simultaneously, because it does not withstand analysis. For thus: does the nature that is simultaneously capable of performing all effects continue to exist at a subsequent time, or not?

children.text:
prathame tatkālavat kālāntare ´pi tāvat kāryakaraṇam āpatet/ dvitīye sthāyitvavṛttyāśā
          mūṣikabhakṣitabījādāv aṅkurādijananaprārthanām anuharet/
children.translated_text: In the first case, the absurd consequence of performing [all] effects at another time too, just as at that time, would follow. In the second case, the hope based on the continued existence of the permanent would be like praying for the sprout and the like from a seed eaten by mice.

children.text:
yad viruddhadharmādhyastaṃ tan nānā yathā śītoṣṇe/ viruddhadharmādhyastaś cāyam iti
          jaladhare pratibandhasiddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: "That upon which contradictory properties are superimposed is manifold, like hot and cold; and this [entity] has contradictory properties superimposed upon it" — thus is the invariable connection established, as with a mass of clouds.

children.text:
na cāyam asiddho hetuḥ/ sthāyini kālabhedena sāmarthyāsāmarthyayoḥ
          prasaṅgatadviparyayasiddhatvāt/ tatrāsāmarthyasādhakau prasaṅgatadviparyayau prāg uktau/
          sāmarthyasādhakāv abhidhīyete/
children.translated_text: And this is not an unestablished reason, because in the case of a permanent [entity], both capability and incapability across temporal distinctions are established through <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and its converse. Therein, the two arguments establishing incapability — the <s>prasaṅga</s> and its converse — have been stated before. The two establishing capability are now stated:

children.text:
[1) yad yadā yajjananāsamarthaṃ tat tadā tan na karoti yathā śilāśakalam aṅkuram/
          asamarthaś cāyaṃ vartamānārthakriyākaraṇakāle ´tītānāgatayor arthakriyayor iti prasaṅgaḥ/
          (2) yad yadā yat karoti tat tadā tatra samarthaṃ yathā sāmagrī svakārye/ karoti cāyam
          atītānāgatakāle tatkālavartinyāv arthakriye bhāva iti prasaṅgavyatyayo viparyayaḥ/
children.translated_text: (1) That which at a given time is incapable of producing a given effect does not produce that effect at that time, like a piece of stone [not producing] a sprout. And this [entity] is incapable at the time of producing present causal efficacy of the causal efficacies of past and future -- such is the consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>). (2) That which at a given time produces a given effect is capable of that at that time, like the aggregate of causes in its own effect. And this [entity] at the past and future time produces the causal efficacies existing at that time -- thus the consequence is reversed (<s>viparyaya</s>).

children.text:
tasmād vipakṣe kramayaugapadyavyāvṛttyā vyāpakānupalambhenādhigatavyatirekavyāptikaṃ
          prasaṅgatadviparyayabalād gṛhītānvayavyāptikaṃ ca sattvaṃ kṣaṇikatvapakṣa eva
          vyavasthāsyatīti siddham/ tad uktaṃ jñānaśriyā:
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the opposing position, through the exclusion of both succession and simultaneity, through non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>), having ascertained the <s>vyatireka</s> (negative) pervasion, and through the force of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and its reversal, having grasped the <s>anvaya</s> (positive) pervasion -- existence (<s>sattva</s>) will be established only in the thesis of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>). It is proven. Thus stated by <s>Jñānaśrī</s>:
[reference marker]

children.text: yat sat tat kṣaṇikaṃ yathā jaladharaḥ santaś ca bhāvā amī
children.translated_text: Whatever exists is momentary, like a cloud; and these entities exist;

children.text: sattā śaktir ihārthakarmaṇi miteḥ siddheṣu siddhā na sā/
children.translated_text: existence is the capacity for causal efficacy -- when [entities] are established, that [existence] is established for cognition, not otherwise.

children.text: nāpy ekaiva vidhānyathā parakṛtenāpi kriyādir bhaved
children.translated_text: Nor is it one alone; otherwise, even action and the like produced by another would occur.

children.text: dvedhāpi kṣaṇabhaṅgasaṃgatir ataḥ sādhye ca viśrāmyati// iti/
children.translated_text: In both ways, the conclusion of momentary destruction [follows]; therefore it rests in what is to be proven.
reference marker

children.text:
na ca kaṇabhakṣākṣacaraṇādipakṣakakṣīkāreṇa sattāsāmānyayogitvam eva sattvam iti
          mantavyam/ sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyānām asattvaprasaṅgāt/ na ca tatra svarūpasattānibandhanaḥ
          sadvyavahāraḥ/ prayojakagauravāpatteḥ/ anugatatvānanugatatvavikalpaparāhateś ca/
          sarṣapamahīdharādiṣu vilakṣaṇeṣu kṣaṇeṣv anugatasyākārasya maṇiṣu sūtravad bhūtagaṇeṣu
          guṇavac cāpratibhāsanāc ca/ kiṃ ca sāmānyaṃ sarvagataṃ svāśrayasarvagataṃ vā/ prathame
          sarvavastusaṃkaraprasaṅgaḥ/ apasiddhāntāpattiś ca/ yataḥ proktaṃ praśastapādena
          svaviṣayasarvagatam iti/ kiṃ ca vidyamāne ghaṭe vartamānaṃ sāmānyam anyatra jāyamānena
          saṃbadhyamānaṃ tasmād āgacchat saṃbadhyate anāgacchad vā/ ādye dravyatvāpattiḥ/ dvitīye
          saṃbandhānupapattiḥ/ kiṃ ca vinaṣṭe ghaṭe sāmānyam avatiṣṭhate vinaśyati sthānāntaraṃ
          gacchati vā/ prathame nirādhāratvāpattiḥ/ dvitīye nityatvavācoyuktyayuktiḥ/ tṛtīye
          dravyatvaprasaktiḥ/ ityādidūṣaṇagrahagrastatvāt sāmānyam aprāmāṇikam/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: Nor should it be thought, by adopting the position of <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> (i.e., <s>Kaṇāda</s>), <s>Akṣacaraṇa</s> (i.e., <s>Gautama</s>), and others, that existence consists merely in the possession of the universal of being (<s>sattāsāmānya</s>). Because of the consequence that universals, particulars, and inherence would be non-existent. Nor is worldly usage of 'existent' based on intrinsic existence there, because of the fault of excessive explanatory burden. And because of the defeat by the dilemma of being pervading or not pervading. And because in mustard seeds, mountains, and the like -- in dissimilar moments -- a pervading form does not appear, as a thread in gems or as a quality in groups of elements. Moreover, is the universal all-pervading or pervading only its own substrata? In the first case, there is the consequence of mixture of all things, and the fault of going against one's own doctrine. For <s>Praśastapāda</s> has stated: 'pervading all within its own domain.' Moreover, does the universal existing in a present pot, being connected with [a pot] arising elsewhere, come from that [first pot] to be connected, or is it connected without coming? In the first case, there is the consequence of being a substance. In the second, the impossibility of relation. Moreover, when a pot is destroyed, does the universal remain, perish, or go to another location? In the first case, there is the consequence of being without a substratum. In the second, the inappropriateness of calling it eternal. In the third, the consequence of being a substance. Being seized by such and other refutations, the universal is without valid authority. Thus it is stated:
reference marker
That which, while existing elsewhere, [is said to have] activity in another place at the arising [of its substratum there],

children.text: tasmād acalataḥ sthānād vṛttir ity atiyuktatā//
children.translated_text: without moving from its location -- that is extremely far-fetched!

children.text: yatrāsau vartate bhāvas tena saṃbadhyate na tu/
children.translated_text: It does not connect with the entity where it exists,

children.text: taddeśinaṃ ca vyāpnoti kim apy etan mahādbhutam//
children.translated_text: yet it pervades what is in that place -- this indeed is a great wonder!

children.text: na yāti na ca tatrāsīd asti paścān na cāṃśavat/
children.translated_text: It does not go, nor was it there before; it exists afterwards but not in parts;

children.text: jahāti pūrvaṃ nādhāram aho vyasanasaṃtatiḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: it does not abandon its former substratum -- what a chain of absurdities!
reference marker
If asked: what is the basis of the cognition of continuity (<s>anuvṛttapratyaya</s>)?

children.text: aṅga, anyāpohālambana eveti saṃtoṣṭavyam āyuṣmatety alam atiprasaṅgena/
children.translated_text: Dear friend, one should be satisfied that it is based on exclusion of the other (<s>anyāpoha</s>) alone, O long-lived one! Enough with over-extension.
reference marker

children.text:
sarvasya saṃsārasya duḥkhātmakatvaṃ sarvatīrthakarasaṃmatam/ anyathā tannivivṛtsūnāṃ
          teṣāṃ tannivṛttyupāye pravṛttyanupapatteḥ/ tasmāt sarvaṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkham iti
          bhāvanīyam/
children.translated_text: That all of <s>saṃsāra</s> has suffering as its nature is accepted by all <s>tīrthakaras</s> (founders of schools). Otherwise, for those who desire to turn away from it, their engagement in the means of cessation would be inexplicable. Therefore, 'everything is suffering, suffering' -- this is to be contemplated.

children.text: nanu kiṃvad iti pṛṣṭe dṛṣṭāntaḥ kathanīya iti cet
children.translated_text: But if asked 'like what?' -- should an example be stated? --

children.text:
maivam/ svalakṣaṇānāṃ kṣaṇānāṃ kṣaṇikatayā sālakṣaṇyābhāvād etena sadṛśam aparam iti
          vaktum aśakyatvāt/ tataḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ svalakṣaṇam iti bhāvanīyam/
children.translated_text: Not so. Since unique particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), being moments, due to their momentariness have no similarity with others, it is impossible to say 'another like this.' Therefore, 'a unique particular is a unique particular' -- this is to be contemplated.

children.text:
evaṃ śūnyaṃ śūnyam ity api bhāvanīyam/ svapne jāgaraṇe ca na mayā dṛṣṭam idaṃ rajatādīti
          viśiṣṭaniṣedhasyopalambhāt/ yadi dṛṣṭaṃ sat tadā tadviśiṣṭasya darśanasyedaṃtāyā
          adhiṣṭhānasya ca tasminn adhyastasya rajatatvādes tatsaṃbandhasya ca samavāyādeḥ sattvaṃ
          syāt/ na caitad iṣṭaṃ kasyacid vādinaḥ/ na cārdhajaratīyam ucitam/ na hi kukkuṭyā eko
          bhāgaḥ pākāyāparo bhāgaḥ prasavāya kalpyatām iti kalpyate/ tasmād
          adhyastādhiṣṭhānatatsaṃbandhadarśanadraṣṭṝṇāṃ madhya ekasyānekasya vā asattve
          niṣedhaviṣayatvena sarvasyāsattvaṃ balād āpated iti bhagavatopadiṣṭe mādhyamikās tāvad
          uttamaprajñā ittham acīkathan: bhikṣupādaprasāraṇanyāyena kṣaṇabhaṅgādyabhidhānamukhena
          sthāyitvānukūlavedanīyatvānugatatvasarvasatyatvabhramavyāvartanena sarvaśūnyatāyām eva
          paryavasānam/ atas tattvaṃ sadasadubhayānubhayātmakacatuṣkoṭivinirmuktaṃ śūnyam eva/ tathā
          hi/ yadi ghaṭādeḥ sattvaṃ svabhāvas tarhi kārakavyāpāravaiyarthyam/ asattvaṃ svabhāva iti
          pakṣe prācīna eva doṣaḥ prāduḥṣyāt/ yathoktam:
children.translated_text: Thus, 'void, void' is also to be contemplated. In dream and in waking, [the cognition] 'this silver and the like has not been seen by me' -- since such qualified negation is apprehended. If it had been seen as real, then the reality of the seeing of that qualified [object], of its 'thisness,' of the substratum, of the superimposed silver-nature and the like upon it, and of the relation of inherence and the like -- all would follow. And this is not desired by any disputant. Nor is the 'half-old' [argument] appropriate. For one cannot assign one part of a hen for cooking and another part for laying eggs. Therefore, among the seen object, the substratum, their relation, the seeing, and the seers -- when one or many are unreal, then by being the object of negation, the unreality of all would forcibly follow. Thus the Blessed One taught, and the <s>Mādhyamikas</s>, being of supreme wisdom, explained it thus: by the method of the monk's stretching of legs, through statements of momentary destruction and the like, by removing the errors of permanence, favorable feeling, continuity, and the reality of everything, the conclusion is in universal voidness (<s>sarvaśūnyatā</s>) alone. Hence, reality is void alone, free from the four alternatives (<s>catuṣkoṭi</s>) of being, non-being, both, and neither. For thus: if existence is the nature of pots and the like, then the operations of agents would be purposeless. If non-existence is the nature -- the very same defect as before would arise. As stated:
reference marker

children.text: na sataḥ kāraṇāpekṣā vyomāder iva yujyate/
children.translated_text: For what exists, dependence on a cause is not appropriate, like space and the like;
a cause is impossible for an effect that is non-existent, like a sky-flower.

children.text: virodhād itarau pakṣāv anupapannau/ taduktaṃ bhagavatā laṅkāvatāre:
children.translated_text: Due to contradiction, the other two positions are untenable. Thus stated by the Blessed One in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>:
When things are analyzed by the intellect, their own-nature cannot be ascertained;

children.text: ato nirabhilapyās te niḥsvabhāvāś ca darśitāḥ/ iti/
children.translated_text: therefore they are shown to be inexpressible and devoid of own-nature.
This is arrived at by the force of reality, which the wise declare:

children.text: yathā yathārthāś cintyante viśīryante tathā tathā// iti ca/
children.translated_text: the more things are reflected upon, the more they disintegrate.

children.text:
na kvacid api pakṣe vyavatiṣṭhata ity arthaḥ/ dṛṣṭārthavyavahāraś ca svapnavyavahāravat
          saṃvṛtyā saṃgacchate/ ata evoktam:
children.translated_text: The meaning is: [reality] does not abide in any position whatsoever. Observed worldly activity is reconciled by convention (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), like the activity in a dream. Therefore it is stated:
reference marker
Regarding one and the same woman's body -- for the renunciant, the lustful man, and the dog,

children.text: kuṇapaḥ kāminī bhakṣya iti tisro vikalpanāḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: [there arise] three conceptions: a corpse, a beloved, and food.

children.text:
tad evaṃ bhāvanācatuṣṭayavaśān nikhilavāsanānivṛttau paranirvāṇaṃ śūnyarūpaṃ setsyatīti
          vayaṃ kṛtārthāḥ nāsmākam upadeśyaṃ kiṃcid astīti/ śiṣyais tāvad yogaś cācāraś ceti dvayaṃ
          karaṇīyam/ tatrāprāptasyārthasya prāptaye paryanuyogo yogaḥ/ gurūktasyārthasyāṅkīkaraṇam
          ācāraḥ/ gurūktasyāṅgīkaraṇād uttamāḥ paryanuyogasyākaraṇād adhamāś ca/ atas teṣāṃ
          mādhyamikā iti prasiddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: Thus, through the force of the fourfold contemplation, when all latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) have ceased, the supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s>, whose form is voidness, will be accomplished -- thus we are fulfilled; we have nothing to teach. Meanwhile, disciples must do two things: yoga (practice) and <s>ācāra</s> (conduct). Among these, yoga is the pursuit of attaining what has not yet been attained. <s>Ācāra</s> is the acceptance of what the guru has taught. Those who accept what the guru has taught are the highest; those who do not engage in further inquiry are the lowest. Hence they are known as <s>Mādhyamikas</s> (the Middle Way proponents).
reference marker

children.text:
gurūktaṃ bhāvanācatuṣṭayaṃ bāhyārthasya śūnyatvaṃ cāṅgīkṛtyāntarasya śūnyatvaṃ cāṅgīkṛtaṃ
          katham iti paryanuyogasya karaṇāt keṣāṃcid yogācāraprathā/ eṣā hi teṣāṃ paribhāṣā:
          svayaṃvedanaṃ tāvad aṅgīkāryam/ anyathā jagadāndhyaṃ prasajyeta/ tat kīrtitaṃ
          dharmakīrtinā:
children.translated_text: Having accepted the guru's teaching of the fourfold contemplation and the voidness of external objects, some [asked] 'how is the voidness of the internal [mind] also accepted?' -- from this inquiry, the reputation of some as <s>Yogācāras</s> [arose]. For this is their definition: self-awareness (<s>svayaṃvedana</s>) must be accepted; otherwise, universal blindness of the world would follow. That was stated by <s>Dharmakīrti</s>:
reference marker
For one whose apprehension is not perception, the vision of objects is not established.

children.text:
bāhyaṃ grāhyaṃ nopapadyata eva/ vikalpānupapatteḥ/ artho jñānagrāhyo bhavann utpanno
          bhavati anutpanno vā/ na pūrvaḥ/ utpannasya sthityabhāvāt/ nāparaḥ/ anutpannasyāsattvāt/
          atha manyethāḥ atīta evārtho jñānagrāhyas tajjanakatvād iti tad api bālabhāṣitam/
          vartamānatāvabhāsavirodhāt/ indriyāder api jñānajanakatvena grāhyatvaprasaṅgāc ca/ kiṃ ca
          grāhyaḥ kiṃ paramāṇurūpo ´rtho ´vayavirūpo vā/ na caramaḥ/ kṛtsnaikadeśavikalpādinā
          tannirākaraṇāt/ na prathamaḥ/ atīndriyatvāt/ ṣaṭkena yugapad yogasya bādhakatvāc ca/
          yathoktam:
children.translated_text: The external graspable object is simply untenable -- due to the impossibility of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>). An object grasped by cognition is either arisen or not arisen. Not the first, because what has arisen has no persistence. Not the second, because what has not arisen is non-existent. If you think the past object alone is grasped by cognition because it is its generator -- that too is childish talk. Because it contradicts the appearance of presentness. And because the sense-faculties too, being generators of cognition, would absurdly be graspable. Moreover, is the graspable object of atomic form or of aggregate form? Not the latter, because that is refuted by the dilemma of whole and part and the like. Not the former, because of being beyond the senses. And because the conjunction of six [atoms] simultaneously is contradictory. As stated:
reference marker
From the simultaneous conjunction of six [atoms], the atom would have six parts;

children.text: teṣām apy ekadeśatve piṇḍaḥ syād aṇumātrakaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: if those [six] occupy the same location, the aggregate would be merely atom-sized.

children.text:
tasmāt svavyatiriktagrāhyavirahāt tadātmikā buddhiḥ svayam eva svātmarūpaprakāśikā
          prakāśavad iti siddham/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: Therefore, since there is no graspable object distinct from itself, cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), having that [object] as its nature, is self-luminous by itself alone, like light. Thus it is established. As stated:
There is nothing other to be experienced by cognition, nor is there another experience of it;
due to the absence of the distinction of graspable and grasper, it illuminates itself alone.

children.text:
grāhyagrāhakayor abhedaś cānumātavyaḥ/ yad vedyate yena vedanena tat tato na bhidyate
          yathā jñānenātmā/ vedyante taiś ca nīlādayaḥ/ bhede hi saty adhunānenārthasya
          saṃbandhitvaṃ na syāt/ tādātmyasya niyamahetor abhāvāt/ tadutpatter aniyāmakatvāt/ yaś
          cāyaṃ grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittīnāṃ pṛthag avabhāsaḥ sa ekasmiṃś candramasi dvitvāvabhāsa iva
          bhramaḥ/ atrāpy anādir avicchinnapravāhā bhedavāsanaiva nimittam/ yathoktam:
children.translated_text: And the non-difference of graspable and grasper is to be inferred: what is cognized by a given cognition is not different from it, just as the self [is not different] from knowledge. And blue and the like are cognized by those [cognitions]. For if there were difference, the relation of the object to this [cognition] at this moment would not obtain, because of the absence of an invariable cause for identity, and because its production is not invariably connected. And this appearance of graspable, grasper, and awareness as separate is an error, like the appearance of duality in a single moon. Here too, the beginningless, unbroken flow of the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of difference is the cause. As stated:
reference marker
Due to the invariable rule of co-apprehension, blue and the cognition of it are non-different;

children.text: bhedaś ca bhrāntivijñānair dṛśyetendāv ivādvaye// iti/
children.translated_text: and difference is seen through erroneous cognitions, as [duality is seen] in the non-dual moon.
Even the nature of cognition, though undifferentiated, by those whose vision is distorted,
appears as if possessing the distinctions of graspable, grasper, and awareness.

children.text:
na ca rasavīryavipākādi samānam āśāmodakopārjitamodakānāṃ syād iti veditavyam/ vastuto
          vedyavedakākāravidhurāyā api buddher vyavahartṛparijñānānurodhena
          vibhinnagrāhyagrāhakākārarūpavattayā timirādyupahatākṣṇāṃ keśoṇḍukanāḍījñānabhedavad
          anādyupaplavavāsanāsāmarthyād vyavasthopapatteḥ paryanuyogāyogāt/ yathoktam:
children.translated_text: Nor should it be thought that the taste, potency, post-digestive effect, and the like of directionally-obtained and purchased sweets would be the same [just because they appear identical]. In reality, even though cognition is devoid of the forms of known and knower, because of the conformity to the understanding of the practical agent, through the form of having differentiated graspable and grasper aspects -- like the difference of cognitions of hairs, spots, and tubes for those whose eyes are affected by cataracts and the like -- because convention is explicable through the power of beginningless latent impressions of error, there is no occasion for objection. As stated:
reference marker
Just as [cognition], devoid of the forms of known and knower, is perceived by the deluded
as having the distortion of separate graspable and grasper aspects --
just so is this convention established, like the difference of cognitions of hairs and the like;
when [this is understood] thus, the [convention] characterized by graspable and grasper should not be questioned.

children.text:
tasmād buddhir evānādivāsanāvaśād anekākārāvabhāsata iti siddham/ tataś ca
          prāguktabhāvanāpracayabalān
          nikhilavāsanocchedavigalitavividhaviṣayākāropaplavaviśuddhavijñānodayo mahodaya iti/
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that cognition alone, due to beginningless latent impressions, appears in manifold forms. And from the accumulation of the aforementioned contemplation, through the eradication of all latent impressions, the arising of pure consciousness freed from the distortion of the manifold forms of objects -- that dissolution is the great arising (<s>mahodaya</s>).
reference marker

children.text:
anye tu manyante/ yathoktaṃ bāhyaṃ vastujātaṃ nāstīti tad ayuktam/ pramāṇābhāvāt/ na ca
          sahopalambhaniyamaḥ pramāṇam iti vaktavyam/ vedyavedakayor abhedasādhakatvenābhimatasya
          tasyāprayojakatvena saṃdigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikatvāt/
children.translated_text: Others, however, maintain: the external world of entities, as described, does not exist -- this is not correct, due to the absence of valid means of knowledge. Nor should it be said that the invariable rule of co-apprehension is the valid means of knowledge; because that [rule], intended as establishing the non-difference of the known and the knower, being non-probative, has doubtful exclusion of the counter-instance.

children.text:
nanu bhede sahopalambhaniyamātmakaṃ sādhanaṃ na syād iti cen na/ jñānasyāntarmukhatayā
          jñeyasya bahirmukhatayā ca bhedena pratibhāsamānatvāt/
          ekedeśatvaikakālatvalakṣaṇasahatvaniyamāsaṃbhavāc ca/ kiṃ ca nīlādyarthasya jñānākāratve
          ´ham iti pratibhāsaḥ syāt/ na tv idam iti pratipattiḥ/ pratyayād avyatirekāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'In [the case of] difference, the proof consisting of the invariable co-perception [of blue and its cognition] would not hold.' Reply: No, because cognition appears as different [from the object] due to its being inward-facing, and the object [appears different] due to its being outward-facing; and because the togetherness-invariability characterized by being in one place and at one time is impossible. Moreover, if the external object such as blue were of the form of cognition, the appearance would be 'I' — not the apprehension 'this'; because [in that case the object] would be non-different from the cognition.

children.text:
athocyate jñānasvarūpo ´pi nīlākāro bhrāntyā bahirvad bhedena pratibhāsata iti na ca
          tatrāhamullekha iti/ tathoktam:
children.translated_text: If it is said: 'Even the blue-form, though of the nature of cognition, appears through error as if external, as different — yet there is no I-reference there,' then it has been stated:

children.text: paricchedāntarād yo ´yaṃ bhāgo bahir iva sthitaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'That portion of cognition which, through another delimitation, stands as if external —
the appearance of difference in what is non-different in cognition is also a disturbance.' And also:

children.text: yad antarjñeyatattvaṃ tad bahirvad avabhāsate/ iti ca/
children.translated_text: 'That which is internally the reality of the known appears as if external.'

children.text:
tad ayuktam/ bāhyārthābhāve tadvyutpattirahitatayā bahirvad ity upamānokter ayukteḥ/ na
          hi vasumitro vandhyāputravad avabhāsata iti prekṣāvān ācakṣīta/ bhedapratibhāsasya
          bhrāntatve ´bhedapratibhāsasya prāmāṇyaṃ tatprāmāṇye ca bhedapratibhāsasya bhrāntatvam iti
          parasparāśrayaprasaṅgāc ca/ avisaṃvādān nīlatādikam eva saṃvidānā bāhyam evopādadate
          jagaty upekṣante cāntaram iti vyavasthādarśanāc ca/ evaṃ cāyam abhedasādhako hetur
          gomayapāyasīyanyāyavad ābhāsatāṃ bhajet/ ato bahirvad iti vadatā bāhyaṃ grāhyam eveti
          bhāvanīyam iti bhavadīya eva bāṇo bhavantaṃ praharet/
children.translated_text: That is incorrect. In the absence of external objects, the simile 'as if external' would be improper, since there would be no familiarity with that [external]. For no discerning person would say 'Vasumitra appeared like a barren woman's son.' And because, if the appearance of difference is erroneous, the appearance of non-difference would be valid — [but] if that [non-difference] is valid, then the erroneousness of the appearance of difference [follows] — there would be the fallacy of mutual dependence. And because in the world, being non-deceived, sentient beings adopt only external [objects] such as blue and the like, and disregard the internal — from the observation of [this] settled practice. Thus, this proof of non-difference would partake of the fallacy [illustrated by] the maxim of the cowdung and the milk-pudding. Therefore, by one who says 'as if external,' the point to be recognized is that the graspable is indeed external — and thus your own arrow would strike you.

children.text: nanu jñānād bhinnakālasyārthasya grāhyatvam anupapannam iti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: 'The graspability of an object that exists at a different time from cognition is untenable.'

children.text:
tad anupapannam/ indriyasaṃnikṛṣṭasya viṣayasyotpādye jñāne svākārasamarpakatayā
          samarpitena cākāreṇa tasyārthasyānumeyatopapatteḥ/ ata eva paryanuyogaparihārau
          samagrāhiṣātām:
children.translated_text: That is untenable. Because the object, being in contact with the sense-organ, is capable of imparting its own form to the cognition that is [subsequently] produced; and through the form thus imparted, that object is amenable to being inferred. Therefore, the objection and the reply have encompassed [the matter]:

children.text: bhinnakālaṃ kathaṃ grāhyam iti ced grāhyatāṃ viduḥ/
children.translated_text: 'If [one asks] how can what exists at a different time be graspable? — they know graspability

children.text: hetutvam eva ca vyakter jñānākārārpaṇakṣamam// iti/
children.translated_text: to be nothing but causality, capable of imparting [its] form to the cognition.' Thus:

children.text:
tathā ca yathā puṣṭyā bhojanam anumīyate yathā ca bhāṣayā deśaḥ yathā vā saṃbhrameṇa
          snehaḥ tathā jñānākāreṇa jñeyam anumeyam/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: And just as nourishment is inferred from plumpness, and a region from language, and affection from agitation — so too the object to be known is to be inferred from the form of cognition. Thus it has been stated:

children.text: arthena ghaṭayaty enāṃ na hi muktvārtharūpatām/
children.translated_text: '[Cognition] connects it [the knower] with the object — not indeed by abandoning object-form.
Therefore, the means of knowledge for the ascertainment of the knowable is its [cognition's] having the form of the knowable.' Thus.

children.text:
na hi vittisattaiva tadvedanā yuktā/ tasyāḥ sarvatrāviśeṣāt/ tāṃ tu sārūpyam āviśat
          sarūpayituṃ ghaṭayed iti ca/ tathā bāhyārthasadbhāve prayogaḥ: ye yasmin saty api
          kādācitkās te sarve tadatiriktasāpekṣāḥ/ yathā avivakṣati ajigamiṣati mayi
          vacanagamanapratibhāsā vivakṣujigamiṣupuruṣāntarasaṃtānasāpekṣāḥ/ tathā ca vivādādhyāsitāḥ
          pravṛttipratyayāḥ saty apy ālayavijñāne kadācid eva nīlādyullekhina iti/ tatrālayavijñānaṃ
          nāmāhamāspadaṃ vijñānam/ nīlādyullekhi ca vijñānaṃ pravṛttivijñānam/ yathoktam:
children.translated_text: For the mere existence of awareness is not rightly its apprehension [of an object], since that [existence] is undifferentiated everywhere. But it is the similarity [between cognition and object] that, having entered [the cognition], enables it to be assimilated. And thus the argument for the existence of external objects: 'Those that are occasional even in the presence of something — they all require something additional to that. Just as, in the case of one who does not wish to speak [or] does not wish to go — the appearances of speech and movement in me [require] another person's series, [namely] one who wishes to speak or wishes to go. And thus the subject-matter of the dispute: the <s>pravṛttivijñānas</s> (active cognitions), even in the presence of <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness), are only occasionally manifesting blue and the like.' Therein, <s>ālayavijñāna</s> is the cognition that is the locus of the 'I.' And the cognition that manifests blue and the like is <s>pravṛttivijñāna</s> (active cognition). As stated:

children.text: tat syād ālayavijñānaṃ yad bhaved ahamāspadam/
children.translated_text: 'That which would be the locus of "I" — that would be the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness);

children.text: tat syāt pravṛttivijñānaṃ yan nīlādikam ullikhet// iti/
children.translated_text: that which manifests blue and the like — that would be the <s>pravṛttivijñāna</s> (active cognition).' Thus.

children.text:
tasmād ālayavijñānasaṃtānātiriktaḥ kādācitkapravṛttivijñānahetur bāhyo ´rtho grāhya eva
          na vāsanāparipākapratyayakādācitkatvāt kadācit utpāda iti veditavyam/
children.translated_text: Therefore, the external object, as the cause of the occasional <s>pravṛttivijñāna</s> over and above the continuum of <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, is indeed graspable — not [is it the case] that the arising is occasional because of the occasionality of the condition of the ripening of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). This should be understood.

children.text:
vijñānavādinaye hi vāsanā nāmaikasaṃtānavartinām ālayavijñānānāṃ
          tattatpravṛttivijñānajananaśaktiḥ/ tasyāś ca svakāryotpādaṃ praty ābhimukhyaṃ paripākaḥ/
          tasya ca pratyayaḥ kāraṇaṃ svasaṃtānavartipūrvakṣaṇaḥ kakṣīkriyate/
          saṃtānāntaranibandhanatvānaṅgīkārāt/
children.translated_text: For in the doctrine of the <s>Vijñānavādin</s> (Consciousness-only school), <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) is the power of <s>ālayavijñānas</s> (store-cognitions) existing within a single continuum to produce their respective <s>pravṛttivijñānas</s> (active cognitions). And its 'ripening' (<s>paripāka</s>) is its turning toward the production of its own effect. And its 'condition' (<s>pratyaya</s>) — that is, its cause — is taken to be the preceding moment existing within its own continuum, since the grounding in another continuum is not accepted.

children.text:
tataś ca pravṛttivijñānajanakālayavijñānavartivāsanāparipākaṃ prati sarve ´py
          ālayavijñānavartinaḥ kṣaṇāḥ samarthā eveti vaktavyam/ na ced eko ´pi na samarthaḥ syāt/
          ālayavijñānasaṃtānavartitvāviśeṣāt/ sarve samarthā iti pakṣe kālakṣepānupapattiḥ/ tataś ca
          kādācitkatvanirvāhāya śabdasparśarūparasagandhaviṣayāḥ sukhādiviṣayāḥ ṣaḍ api pratyayāś
          caturaḥ pratyayān pratītyotpadyanta iti catureṇānicchatāpy acchamatinā svānubhavam
          anācchādya paricchettavyam/
children.translated_text: Consequently, it must be said that all moments existing within the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> continuum are equally capable with respect to the ripening of the <s>vāsanā</s> residing in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> that generates <s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>. If not, not even one [moment] would be capable, since there is no difference in [their] being within the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> continuum. If all are capable — then the non-occurrence of delay is untenable. Therefore, in order to maintain the occasionality, [it must be acknowledged that] the six cognitions — having for their objects sound, touch, form, taste, smell, and pleasure and the like — arise dependent on four conditions. This must be discerned by the clever person of clear intellect, without concealing one's own experience, even if unwillingly.

Those four conditions are well-known as having the forms of: <s>ālambana</s> (object-condition), <s>samanantara</s> (immediately preceding condition), <s>sahakārya</s> (co-operative condition), and <s>adhipati</s> (dominant condition).

children.text:
(i) tatra jñānapadavedanīyasya nīlādyavabhāsasya cittasya nīlād ālambanapratyayān
          nīlākāratā bhavati/
children.translated_text: (i) Therein, the blue-form of the mind — the appearance of blue and the like that is to be experienced in the domain of cognition — its blue-form arises from the <s>ālambanapratyaya</s> (object-condition) [which is] blue.
(ii) From the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> (immediately preceding condition) — the prior cognition — [arises] the nature of awareness.
(iii) From the <s>sahakāripratyaya</s> (co-operative condition) — light — [arises] clarity.

children.text:
(iv) cakṣuṣo ´dhipatipratyayād viṣayagrahaṇapratiniyamaḥ/ uditasya jñānasya
          rasādisādhāraṇye prāpte niyāmakaṃ cakṣur adhipatir bhavitum arhati/ loke
          niyāmakasyādhipatitvopalambhāt/
children.translated_text: (iv) From the eye as the <s>adhipatipratyaya</s> (dominant condition) [arises] the restriction of object-apprehension. Since, when cognition has arisen, there would be [the unwanted consequence of its] being common to taste and the like, the eye deserves to be the dominant [condition] as the restrictor — because in the world, the restrictor is observed to be the dominant one.

children.text:
evaṃ cittacaittātmakaḥ skandhaḥ pañcavidho rūpavijñānavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārasaṃjñakaḥ/
          tatra rūpyanta ebhir viṣayā iti rūpyanta iti ca vyutpattyā saviṣayāṇīndriyāṇi
          rūpaskandhaḥ/ ālayavijñānapravṛttivijñānapravāho vijñānaskandhaḥ/
          prāguktaskandhadvayasaṃbandhajanyaḥ sukhaduḥkhādipratyayapravāho vedanāskandhaḥ/ gaur
          ityādiśabdollekhisaṃvitpravāhaḥ saṃjñāskandhaḥ/ vedanāskandhanibandhanā rāgadveṣādayaḥ
          kleśā upakleśāś ca madamānādayo dharmādharmau ca saṃskāraskandhaḥ/
children.translated_text: Thus, the aggregate (<s>skandha</s>) consisting of mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitta</s>) is fivefold, designated as <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception/naming), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (formations). Therein, the sense-organs together with their objects — etymologically, 'those by which objects are formed' and 'they are formed' — constitute the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form). The stream of <s>ālayavijñāna</s> and <s>pravṛttivijñāna</s> is the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness). The stream of cognitions of pleasure, pain, and the like, born from the connection of the two aforementioned aggregates, is the <s>vedanāskandha</s> (aggregate of feeling). The stream of awareness that manifests words such as 'cow' and the like is the <s>saṃjñāskandha</s> (aggregate of naming). The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) such as desire, aversion, and the like, and the <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions) such as pride, conceit, and the like, grounded in the <s>vedanāskandha</s>, as well as merit and demerit — [these constitute] the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations).

children.text:
tad idaṃ sarvaṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhāyatanaṃ duḥkhasādhanaṃ ceti bhāvayitvā tannirodhopāyaṃ
          tattvajñānaṃ saṃpādayet/ ata evoktaṃ duḥkhasamudāyanirodhamārgāś catvāra
          āryabuddhasyābhimatāni tattvāni/ tatra duḥkhaṃ prasiddham/ samudāyo duḥkhakāraṇam/ tad
          dvividhaṃ pratyayopanibandhato

children.translated_text: and through the grounding of causes (<s>hetu</s>).
Therein, the sūtra that summarizes the grounding of conditions
[states]: 'This is the fruit of conditions' —

children.text:
idaṃ kāryaṃ ye anye hetavaḥ pratyayanti gacchanti teṣām ayamānānāṃ hetūnāṃ bhāvaḥ
          pratyayatvaṃ kāraṇasamavāyaḥ, tanmātrasya phalaṃ na cetanasya kasyacid iti sūtrārthaḥ/
          yathā bījahetur aṅkuro dhātūnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ samavāyāj jāyate/ tatra pṛthivīdhātur aṅkurasya
          kāṭhinyaṃ gandhaṃ ca janayati/ abdhātuḥ snehaṃ rasaṃ ca janayati/ tejodhātū rūpam auṣṇyaṃ
          ca/ vāyudhātuḥ sparśanaṃ calanaṃ ca/ ākāśadhātur avakāśaṃ śabdaṃ ca/ ṛtudhātur yathāyogaṃ
          pṛthivyādikam/
children.translated_text: this is the effect; those other causes that go toward it (<s>pratyayanti</s>) — the conditionality of these present causes is the conjunction of causes. The fruit is of that alone [i.e., the conjunction of conditions], not of any conscious being — this is the meaning of the sūtra. Just as from the cause [that is] the seed, the sprout arises from the conjunction of the six elements. Therein, the earth-element produces the hardness and smell of the sprout; the water-element produces its oiliness and taste; the fire-element produces its form and heat; the air-element produces its touch and movement; the space-element produces its room and sound; and the season-element [produces effects] according to the appropriate [combination of] earth and the rest.
