Having contemplated that all this is suffering, the ground of suffering, and the means to suffering — one should accomplish the means to its cessation, [namely] the knowledge of reality. Therefore it is stated: suffering, origination, cessation, and the path — these are the four truths accepted by the noble <s>Buddha</s>. Therein, suffering is well-known. Origination (<s>samudāya</s>) is the cause of suffering. That is twofold: through the grounding of conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>)

children.text:
ca saṃgrāhakaṃ sūtram: utpādād vā tathāgatānām anutpādād vā sthitaivaiṣāṃ
          dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā dharmasthititā dharmaniyāmakatā ca pratītyasamutpādānulomatā iti/
children.translated_text: [states]: 'Whether or not <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise, the lawfulness of these <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), the stability of <s>dharmas</s>, the regularity of <s>dharmas</s>, and the conformity with <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) are [always] established.'
And the sūtra that summarizes the grounding of causes

children.text:
tathāgatānāṃ buddhānāṃ mate dharmāṇāṃ kāryakāraṇarūpāṇāṃ yā dharmatā kāryakāraṇabhāvarūpā
          eṣotpādād anutpādād vā sthitā/ yasmin sati yad utpadyate yasminn asati yan notpadyate tat
          tasya kāraṇasya kāryam iti/
children.translated_text: In the view of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>dharmatā</s> (lawfulness) of <s>dharmas</s> — which have the form of causes and effects — that dharmatā having the form of the cause-effect relation, is established whether or not [they] arise. Whatever arises when something is present, and whatever does not arise when something is absent — that is the effect of that cause.

children.text:
dharmatety asya vivaraṇaṃ dharmasthititetyādi/ dharmasya kāryasya kāraṇānatikrameṇa
          sthitiḥ/ svārthikas talpratyayaḥ/ dharmasya kāraṇasya kāryaṃ prati niyāmakatā/
children.translated_text: The explanation of '<s>dharmatā</s>' is '<s>dharmasthititā</s>' and the rest. The stability of the effect (<s>dharma</s>) without transgressing its cause. The <s>tadpratyaya</s> suffix [indicates] its own meaning. The regularity of the cause (<s>dharma</s>) with respect to the effect.

children.text:
nanv ayaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaś cetanam antareṇa na saṃbhavatīty ata uktaṃ pratītyeti/ kāraṇe
          sati tat pratītya prāpya samutpāde ´nulomatānusāritā yā saiva dharmatotpādād anutpādād vā
          dharmāṇāṃ sthitā/ na cātra kaścic cetano ´dhiṣṭhātopalabhyata iti sūtrārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'This cause-effect relation is not possible without a conscious [agent].' Therefore, [the sūtra] states '<s>pratītya</s>' — the condition being present, having reached that [condition], the conformity — the correspondence — with origination is precisely the <s>dharmatā</s>, established whether or not <s>dharmas</s> arise. And no conscious [agent] as superintendent is perceived here — this is the meaning of the sūtra.

children.text:
yathā: bījād aṅkuro ´ṅkurāt kāṇḍaṃ kāṇḍān nālo nālād garbhas tataḥ śūkaṃ tataḥ
          puṣpaṃ tataḥ phalam/ na cātra bāhye samudāye kāraṇaṃ bījādi kāryam aṅkurādi vā cetayate
          aham aṅkuraṃ nirvartayāmi ahaṃ bījena nirvartita iti/ evam ādhyātmikeṣv api kāraṇadvayam
          avagantavyam/
children.translated_text: is as follows: from the seed [arises] the sprout, from the sprout the stalk, from the stalk the stem, from the stem the bud, from that the awn, from that the flower, from that the fruit. And herein, in the external aggregate, neither the cause — seed and the like — nor the effect — sprout and the like — thinks 'I produce the sprout' or 'I am produced by the seed.' Likewise, even in the internal [psychophysical] domain, the twofold causation should be understood.
The grounding of causes of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)
With the ocean of objects to be known spread out before [us], by those who fear the expansion of the text —

children.text:
iti nyāyenoparamyate/ tadubhayanirodhaḥ tadanantaraṃ vimalajñānodayo vā muktiḥ/
          tannirodhopāyo mārgaḥ/ sa ca tattvajñānam/ tac ca prācīnabhāvanābalād bhavatīti paramaṃ
          rahasyam/ sūtrasyāntaṃ pṛcchatāṃ kathitaṃ bhavantaś ca sūtrasyāntaṃ pṛṣṭavantaḥ
          sautrāntikā bhavantv iti/ bhagavatābhihitatayā sautrāntikasaṃjñā saṃjāteti/
children.translated_text: thus, by this method, [we] desist. The cessation of both of those [suffering and its origination], or alternatively the arising of pure knowledge — that is liberation (<s>mukti</s>). The means to that cessation is the path. And that is the knowledge of reality. And that comes about through the force of prior cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — this is the supreme secret. Those who ask about the end of the sūtra are told — and you too have asked about the end of the sūtra — 'be <s>Sautrāntikas</s>!' Because it was spoken by the Blessed One, the designation '<s>Sautrāntika</s>' arose.

children.text:
kecana bauddhāḥ: bāhyeṣu gandhādiṣv āntareṣu rūpādiskandheṣu satsv api tatrānāsthām
          utpādayituṃ sarvaṃ śūnyam iti prāthamikān vineyān acakathad bhagavān dvitīyāṃs tu
          vijñānamātragrahāviṣṭān vijñānam evaikaṃ sad iti tṛtīyān ubhayaṃ satyam ity āsthitān
          vijñeyam anumeyam iti seyaṃ viruddhā bhāṣeti varṇayantaḥ: vaibhāṣikākhyayā khyātāḥ/ eṣā hi
          teṣāṃ paribhāṣā samunmiṣati/ vijñeyānumeyatvavāde prātyakṣikasya kasyacid apy
          arthasyābhāvena vyāptisaṃvedanasthānābhāvenānumānapravṛttyanupapattiḥ
          sakalalokānubhavavirodhaś ca/ tataś cārtho dvividhaḥ: grāhyo ´dhyavaseyaś ca/ tatra
          grahaṇaṃ nirvikalpakarūpaṃ pramāṇam/ kalpanāpoḍhatvāt/ adhyavasāyaḥ savikalpakarūpo
          ´pramāṇam/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: Certain Buddhists [say]: 'Even though external [objects] such as smell and the like, and internal aggregates such as form and the like, exist, in order to produce non-attachment toward them, the Blessed One taught the first disciples to be guided that "everything is empty"; to the second [group], who were seized by the grasping of consciousness-only, [he taught] "consciousness alone is the one reality"; to the third, established in [the view that] "both are real," [he taught that] "the object is to be inferred" — these are contradictory statements.' Those who thus explain are known by the name <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>. For this is their interpretive framework that comes to light. In the doctrine that the knowable is to be inferred, since there is no directly perceived object whatsoever, there would be no basis for the cognition of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), and hence the functioning of inference would be untenable — and [there would be] contradiction with the experience of the entire world. Therefore, the object is twofold: graspable (<s>grāhya</s>) and determinable (<s>adhyavaseya</s>). Therein, grasping — which has the form of non-conceptual cognition — is the means of knowledge, because it is free from conceptual construction. Determination — which has the form of conceptual cognition — is not a means of knowledge. Thus it has been stated:
'Direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is [cognition that is] free from conceptual construction and non-erroneous — [it is] non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>).
Conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), since it has an appearance of a non-entity, is a disturbance due to non-correspondence.' Thus.

children.text: grāhyaṃ vastu pramāṇaṃ hi grahaṇaṃ yad ito ´nyathā/
children.translated_text: The graspable thing is indeed the means of knowledge — for grasping is [the valid cognition]; what is otherwise from this

children.text: na tad vastu na tan mānaṃ śabdaliṅgendriyādijam// iti ca/
children.translated_text: 'That is not an object, nor is that a means of knowledge — born of word, inferential mark, sense-faculty, and the like.' Thus it is said.

children.text:
nanu savikalpakasyāprāmāṇye katham tataḥ pravṛttasyārthaprāptiḥ saṃvādaś copapadyeyātām
          iti cet
children.translated_text: Now, if it be objected: 'If conceptual cognition (<s>savikalpaka</s>) is not a valid means of knowledge, how could the attainment of an object and the agreement [between cognition and object] for one who acts on that basis be accounted for?' —

children.text:
na tad bhadram/ maṇiprabhāviṣayamaṇivikalpanyāyena pāraṃparyeṇārthapratilambhasaṃbhavena
          tadupapatteḥ/ avaśiṣṭaṃ sautrāntikaprastāve prapañcitam iti neha pratanyate/
children.translated_text: That is not right, good sir! Because by the analogy of the conceptual cognition of a gem [based on] the radiance of the gem, through an indirect succession, the attainment of the object is possible, and that [agreement] is thereby accounted for. The remainder has been elaborated in the presentation of the <s>Sautrāntika</s> system, and so is not extended here.

children.text:
na ca vineyāśayānurodhenopadeśabhedaḥ sāṃpradāyiko na bhavatīti bhaṇitavyam/ yato
          bhaṇitaṃ bodhicittavivaraṇe:
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that the difference in teaching according to the dispositions of those to be trained is not traditional. For it has been stated in the <s>Bodhicittavivaraṇa</s>:
'The teachings of the Lords of the World follow the dispositions of beings;

children.text: bhidyante bahudhā loka upāyair bahubhiḥ punaḥ//
children.translated_text: they are divided manifoldly in the world, again through many skillful means.',
'With the division of profound and plain, and sometimes having both characteristics,
the teaching, though differentiated, is [ultimately] undifferentiated — having the characteristic of the non-duality of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>).' Thus.
That the worship of the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) brings well-being — this is well-known in the Buddhist doctrine:
'Having earned wealth abundantly, the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> indeed

children.text: paritaḥ pūjanīyāni kim anyair iha pūjitaiḥ//
children.translated_text: should be worshipped all around — what use are other things worshipped here?
The five sense-faculties of knowledge and likewise the five faculties of action,

children.text: mano buddhir iti proktaṃ dvādaśāyatanaṃ budhaiḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: mind and intellect — thus the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> have been declared by the wise.' Thus.
In the <s>Vivekavilāsa</s>, the Buddhist doctrine was stated thus:

children.text: bauddhānāṃ sugato devo viśvaṃ ca kṣaṇabhaṅguram/
children.translated_text: 'For the Buddhists, the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One, i.e., the <s>Buddha</s>) is the deity, and the universe is momentarily perishing.
This fourfold truth, named the Noble Truths (<s>Āryasatya</s>), in order [is]:

children.text: duḥkham āyatanaṃ caiva tataḥ samudayo mataḥ/
children.translated_text: suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), the sense-base (<s>āyatana</s>), then the origin (<s>samudaya</s>) is considered,

children.text: mārgaś cety asya ca vyākhyā krameṇa śrūyatām ataḥ//
children.translated_text: and the path (<s>mārga</s>)' — and the explanation of these should be heard in order from here.

children.text: duḥkhaṃ saṃsāriṇaḥ skandhās te ca pañca prakīrtitāḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Suffering is the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) of the one in <s>saṃsāra</s>, and they are declared to be five:

children.text: vijñānaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskāro rūpam eva ca//
children.translated_text: consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and form (<s>rūpa</s>) itself.
The five sense-faculties, the five objects beginning with sound, the mind,
and the <s>dharmāyatana</s> (mental-object base) — these are the twelve <s>āyatanas</s>.

children.text: rāgādīnāṃ gaṇo yasmāt samudeti nṛṇāṃ hṛdi/
children.translated_text: Since the group of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the like arises in the hearts of human beings,
that which is called the nature of self and mine — that would again be the origin (<s>samudaya</s>).

children.text: kṣaṇikāḥ sarvasaṃskārā iti yā vāsanā sthirā/
children.translated_text: "All formations are momentary" — the firm impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) that this [conviction produces] —

children.text: sa mārga iti vijñeyaḥ sa ca mokṣo ´bhidhīyate//
children.translated_text: that should be known as the path (<s>mārga</s>), and that is called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).
Direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>) — thus the twofold means of knowledge.
The Buddhists, of four schools, are known as <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> and the rest.
The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> highly regards the object as accompanied by cognition.
For the <s>Sautrāntika</s>, the object grasped by direct perception is not considered external.
Cognition accompanied by form (<s>ākāra</s>) is approved by the <s>Yogācāra</s>.

children.text: kevalāṃ saṃvidaṃ svasthāṃ manyante madhyamāḥ punaḥ//
children.translated_text: The <s>Mādhyamikas</s>, again, consider [only] pure awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>), self-contained, [as real].
Liberation, arising from the severance of the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the continuum of cognition of attachment and the like,

children.text: caturṇām api bauddhānāṃ muktir eṣā prakīrtitā//
children.translated_text: is proclaimed as the [goal] of all four [schools of] Buddhists.',
'Bark-garments, water-pot, shaved head, bark-cloth, eating before noon,
the <s>saṃgha</s> (community), and wearing red robes — these are adopted by Buddhist monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>).'
Thus [ends] the Buddhist system in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Now, the <s>Ārhata</s> (Jaina) system. //3//

children.text:
tad itthaṃ muktakacchānāṃ matam asahamānā vivasanāḥ kathaṃcit sthāyitvam āsthāya
          kṣaṇikatvapakṣaṃ pratikṣipanti/ yady ātmā kaścin nāsthīyeta sthāyī
          tadaihalaukikapāralaukikaphalasādhanasaṃpādanaṃ viphalaṃ bhavet/ na hy etat saṃbhavaty
          anyaḥ karoty anyo bhuṅkta iti/ tasmād yo ´haṃ prāk karmākaravaṃ so ´haṃ saṃprati tatphalaṃ
          bhuñja iti pūrvāparakālānuyāyinaḥ sthāyinas tasya spaṣṭapramāṇāvasitatayā
          pūrvāparabhāgavikalakālakalāvasthitilakṣaṇakṣaṇikatā parīkṣakair arhadbhir na
          parigrahārhā/
children.translated_text: Thus, the unclad ones (Jains), unable to tolerate the view of the loincloth-wearers (Buddhists), somehow establishing permanence, reject the position of momentariness. [They argue:] If no enduring self were accepted, then the accomplishment of the means to both worldly and other-worldly fruits would be futile. For it is not possible that one person acts and another experiences [the result]. Therefore, 'I who formerly performed actions am now enjoying their fruits' — [this requires] a permanent [self] that continues through earlier and later times; since its [existence] is ascertained by clear means of knowledge, the momentariness characterized by the division of temporal portions — lacking earlier and later parts — is not acceptable to the discerning <s>Arhats</s>.
Now, if you should think:
'By the principle: Since a stream that has arrived is possessed of a valid means [of knowledge], by what can it be blocked?' —

children.text:
iti nyāyena yat sat tat kṣaṇikam ityādinā pramāṇena kṣaṇikatāyāḥ pramitatayā tadanusāreṇa
          samānasaṃtānavartinām eva prācīnaḥ pratyayaḥ karmakartā taduttaraḥ pratyayaḥ phalabhoktā/
          na cātiprasaṅgaḥ/ kāryakāraṇabhāvasya niyāmakatvāt/ yathā madhurarasabhāvitānām
          āmrabījānāṃ parikarṣitāyāṃ bhūmāv uptānām aṅkurakāṇḍaskandhaśākhāpallavādiṣu taddvārā
          paraṃparayā phale mādhuryaniyamaḥ/ yathā vā lākṣārasāvasiktānāṃ kārpāsabījādīnām
          aṅkurādipāraṃparyeṇa kārpāsādau raktimaniyamaḥ/ yathoktam:
children.translated_text: that is, since momentariness has been ascertained by such a means of knowledge as 'whatever exists is momentary,' one should follow that accordingly — [the reply is:] among things existing in the same continuum, the earlier mental state is the agent of action and the later mental state is the experiencer of the fruit. And there is no over-extension, because the cause-effect relation serves as the restrictor. Just as in the case of mango seeds conditioned by sweet taste, sown in tilled earth, there is a restriction of sweetness in the fruit through the successive [stages] of sprout, stem, trunk, branch, leaf, and the like; or just as in the case of cotton seeds and the like sprinkled with lac-dye solution, there is a restriction of redness in the cotton through the succession of sprout and the like. As stated:

children.text: yasminn eva hi saṃtāne āhitā karmavāsanā/
children.translated_text: 'In whichever continuum the <s>karma</s>-impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) has been deposited,

children.text: phalaṃ tatraiva badhnāti kārpāse raktatā yathā//
children.translated_text: the fruit is bound in that very [continuum] — as redness in cotton.',
'In the flower of the citron and the like, whatever lac-dye is sprinkled,

children.text: śaktir ādhīyate tatra kācit tāṃ kiṃ na paśyasi// iti/
children.translated_text: a certain power is deposited therein — do you not see it?' Thus.

children.text:
tad api kāśakuśāvalambanakalpam/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ jaladharādau dṛṣṭānte kṣaṇikatvam anena
          pramāṇena pramitaṃ pramāṇāntareṇa vā/ nādyaḥ/ bhavadabhimatasya kṣaṇikatvasya kvacid apy
          adṛṣṭacaratvena dṛṣṭāntāsiddhāv asyānumānasyānutthānāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/ tenaiva nyāyena
          sarvatra kṣaṇikatvasiddhau sattvānumānavaiphalyāpatteḥ/ arthakriyākāritvaṃ sattvam ity
          aṅgīkāre mithyāsarpadaṃśāder apy arthakriyākāritvena sattvāpātāc ca/ ata evoktam:
          utpādavyayadhrauvyayuktaṃ sad iti/ athocyate
          sāmarthyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇaviruddhadharmādhyāsāt siddhir iti tad asādhu/ syādvādinām
          anekāntatāvādasyeṣṭatayā virodhāsiddheḥ/
children.translated_text: But even that is like grasping at <s>kāśa</s>-grass and <s>kuśa</s>-grass [for support] — because it cannot withstand analysis. Has momentariness been ascertained in the example of clouds and the like by this means of knowledge or by another? Not the first — because, since the momentariness you maintain has never been observed anywhere, the example being unestablished, this inference does not arise. Nor the second — because, by the same reasoning, if momentariness were established everywhere, the inference from existence would become futile. And if existence (<s>sattva</s>) is accepted as [defined by] causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), then even a false snake-bite and the like would have existence attributed to them, since they too have causal efficacy. Therefore it has been said: 'What exists possesses origination, destruction, and persistence (<s>dhrauvya</s>).' Now if it be said that establishment [comes] from the superimposition of contradictory properties characterized by capability and incapability — that is not right, because for the <s>Syādvādins</s> (proponents of qualified assertion), since the doctrine of non-absolutism (<s>anekāntatāvāda</s>) is accepted, the contradiction is not established.

children.text:
yad uktaṃ kārpāsādidṛṣṭānta iti tad uktimātram/ yukter anukteḥ/ tatrāpi
          niranvayanāśasyānaṅgīkārāc ca/ na ca saṃtānivyatirekeṇa saṃtānaḥ pramāṇapadavīm upāroḍhum
          arhati/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: As for the stated example of cotton and the like — that is mere assertion, since no reasoning has been adduced. And because in that case too, destruction without remainder is not accepted. Nor is a continuum (<s>saṃtāna</s>), apart from the individual members of the continuum (<s>saṃtānin</s>), fit to ascend the path of valid means of knowledge. As stated:
'Individuals (<s>vyakti</s>) of the same class, produced in sequence, mutually proximate —

children.text: vyaktayas tāsu saṃtānaḥ sa caika iti gīyate// iti/
children.translated_text: the continuum in those [individuals] is regarded as one.' Thus.

children.text:
na ca kāryakāraṇabhāvaniyamo ´tiprasaṅgaṃ bhaṅktum arhati/ tathā hy
          upādhyāyabuddhyanubhūtasya śiṣyabuddhiḥ smaret tadupacitakarmaphalam anubhaved vā/ tathā
          ca kṛtapraṇāśākṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgaḥ/ tad uktaṃ siddhasenavākyakāreṇa:
children.translated_text: Nor is the restriction of the cause-effect relation fit to break the over-extension. For thus: the cognition of the disciple would remember what was experienced by the cognition of the teacher, or would experience the fruit of <s>karma</s> accumulated by the latter. And thus, the undesirable consequences of the destruction of what was done (<s>kṛtapraṇāśa</s>) and the encountering of what was not done (<s>akṛtābhyāgama</s>) [would follow]. As stated by <s>Siddhasena Vākyakāra</s>:
'Overlooking the faults of the destruction of what was done, the experience of <s>karma</s> not done, the disruption of [meaningful] existence, liberation, and memory —

children.text: upekṣya sākṣāt kṣaṇabhaṅgam icchann aho mahāsāhasikaḥ paro ´sau// iti/
children.translated_text: directly wishing for momentary destruction, alas, that adversary is a great daredevil!' Thus.

children.text:
kiṃ ca kṣaṇikatvapakṣe jñānakāle jñeyasyāsattvena jñeyakāle jñānasyāsattvena ca
          grāhyagrāhakabhāvānupapattau sakalalokayātrāstam iyāt/ na ca samasamayavartitā śaṅkanīyā/
          savyetaraviṣāṇavat kāryakāraṇabhāvāsaṃbhavenāgrāhyasyālambanapratyayatvānupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: Moreover, on the thesis of momentariness, since at the time of cognition the knowable does not exist, and at the time of the knowable, cognition does not exist, the relation of grasped and grasper would be impossible, and all worldly activity would come to a halt. Nor should simultaneity be suspected — because, like the right and left horns [of a bull], there would be an impossibility of the cause-effect relation, and the unapprehended [object] could not function as the objective condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>).
Now, if [one says:] 'Even that which is of a different time, through its imparting of its form [to cognition], is graspable' —

children.text:
tad apy apeśalam/ kṣaṇikasya jñānasyākārārpakatāśrayatāyā durvacatvena
          sākārajñānavādapratyādeśāt/
children.translated_text: That too is inelegant. Because, since the momentary cognition's [capacity to serve as] the substratum for form-imparting is difficult to maintain, the doctrine of cognition-with-form (<s>sākārajñānavāda</s>) is thereby refuted.

children.text:
nirākārajñānavāde ´pi yogyatāvaśena pratikarmavyavasthāyāḥ sthitatvāt/ tathā hi
          pratyakṣeṇa viṣayākārarahitam eva jñānaṃ pratipuruṣam ahamahamikayā ghaṭādigrāhakam
          anubhūyate na tu darpaṇādivat pratibimbākrāntam/ viṣayākāradhāritve ca jñānasyārthe
          dūranikaṭādivyavahārāya jalāñjalir vitīryeta/
children.translated_text: Even on the doctrine of formless cognition (<s>nirākārajñānavāda</s>), the per-object functional distinction stands by virtue of fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>). For thus: by direct perception, cognition devoid of the form of the object is experienced by each person, each vying with the other, as the grasper of pots and the like — but not as pervaded by a reflected image, like a mirror and the like. And if cognition were to bear the form of the object, then for [establishing] the conventional usage of 'distant' and 'near' and the like regarding the object, a palmful of water would have to be conceded.

children.text: na cedam iṣṭāpādanam eṣṭavyam/ davīyān mahīdharo nedīyān madīyo
ASS, IV, A. This is a tentative emendation, based on the facts that

(on sūtra 1.7; p. 103 l. 14)
              has, in the same context:

bāhur iti vyavahārasya nirābādhaṃ jāgarūkatvāt/ na cākārādhāyakasya tasya
          davīyastvādiśālitayā tathā vyavahāra iti kathanīyam/
children.translated_text: since this conventional usage is unobstructedly operative for one who is awake. Nor should it be said that the form-imparting [cognition] itself, being endowed with far-ness and the like, produces such conventional usage —
Nor should this objection be pursued as establishing one's desired [conclusion]. [Consider:] 'That mountain is far, this arm of mine is near' —

children.text:
darpaṇādau tathānupalambhāt/ kiṃ cārthād upajāyamānaṃ jñānaṃ yathā tasya nīlākāratām
          anukaroti tathā yadi jaḍatām api tarhy arthavat tad api jaḍaṃ syāt/ tathā ca vṛddhim
          iṣṭavato mūlam api te naṣṭaṃ syād iti mahat kaṣṭam āpannam/
children.translated_text: because that is not observed in mirrors and the like. Moreover, if cognition arising from the object imitates the blue-form of that [object], then if it also imitates its inertness, it too would be inert like the object. And thus, for one who wished for increase [of consciousness], the very capital would be lost — what a great calamity!

children.text:
athaitaddoṣaparijihīrṣayā jñānaṃ jaḍatāṃ nānukarotīti brūṣe hanta tarhi tasyā grahaṇaṃ na
          syād ity ekam anusaṃdhitsato ´paraṃ pracyavata iti nyāyāpātaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, if, desiring to avoid this fault, you say 'Cognition does not imitate inertness' — well then, it would not grasp that [inertness]! This results in the logical pitfall of: 'While intending one thing, another slips away.'

children.text:
nanu mā bhūj jaḍatāyā grahaṇam/ kiṃ naś chinnam/ tadagrahaṇe ´pi nīlākāragrahaṇe tayor
          bhedo ´nekānto vā bhavet/ nīlākāragrahaṇe cāgṛhītā jaḍatā kathaṃ tasya svarūpaṃ syāt/
          aparathā gṛhītasya stambhasyāgṛhītaṃ trailokyam api rūpaṃ bhavet/ tad etat prameyajātaṃ
          prabhācandraprabhṛtibhir arhanmatānusāribhiḥ prameyakamalamārtaṇḍādau (p. 27) prabandhe
          prapañcitam iti granthabhūyatvabhayān nopanyastam/
children.translated_text: But [you say:] 'Let there be no grasping of inertness! What is cut off from us?' Even without the grasping of that [inertness], in the grasping of the blue-form, there would be either a difference or a non-absolute [relation] between the two. And if inertness is not grasped while the blue-form is grasped, how would that [inertness] be its essential nature? Otherwise, for one who has grasped a pillar, even the three worlds, ungrasped, would be its form. This entire range of topics has been elaborated in treatises such as the <s>Prameyakamalamārtaṇḍa</s> by <s>Prabhācandra</s> and other followers of the <s>Arhat</s>'s system, so it is not presented here for fear of the volume of the work.

children.text:
tasmāt puruṣārthābhilāṣukaiḥ puruṣaiḥ saugatī gatir nānugantavyā/ api tv ārhaty
          evārhaṇīyā/
children.translated_text: Therefore, the path of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddhist path) should not be followed by persons who desire the goals of human life. Rather, the <s>Ārhata</s> (Jaina) path alone is worthy of honor.
And the essential nature of the <s>Arhat</s> has been stated without hesitation by <s>Hemacandrasūri</s> in the <s>Āptanirṇayālaṃkāra</s>:
'Omniscient, free from the faults of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, worshipped by the three worlds,
a speaker of things as they are — such a deity is the <s>Arhat</s>, the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>).' Thus.

children.text:
nanu na kaścit puruṣaviśeṣaḥ sarvajñapadavedanīyaḥ pramāṇapaddhatim adhyāste/
          tatsadbhāvagrāhakasya pramāṇapañcakasya tatrānupalambhāt/ tathā coktaṃ tautātitaiḥ:
children.translated_text: Now, [the objection:] No particular person describable by the word 'omniscient' occupies the path of valid means of knowledge — because the fivefold means of knowledge that would establish his existence is not observed in his case. And thus it has been stated by the <s>Tautātitas</s> (followers of <s>Kumārila</s>):
'An omniscient being is currently not perceived by us and the like;

children.text: dṛṣṭo na caikadeśo ´sti liṅgaṃ vā yo ´numāpayet//1//
children.translated_text: nor is there a partial [perception] or an inferential mark that would lead to inference [of his existence]. //1//',
'Nor is there any scriptural injunction that reveals an eternally omniscient being;

children.text: na ca tatrārthavādānāṃ tātparyam api kalpyate//2//
children.translated_text: nor is the purport of <s>arthavādas</s> (laudatory passages) to be attributed to that [injunction]. //2//',
'Nor is his existence enjoined by those [arthavādas] whose chief purpose is something else;

children.text: na cānuvadituṃ śakyaḥ pūrvam anyair abodhitaḥ//3//
children.translated_text: nor can one who has not been previously made known by others be restated (<s>anuvāda</s>). //3//',

children.text: anāder āgamasyārtho na ca sarvajña ādimān/
children.translated_text: 'The meaning of the beginningless <s>āgama</s> (scripture) is not an omniscient being who has a beginning;

children.text: kṛtrimeṇa tv asatyena sa kathaṃ pratipādyate//4//
children.translated_text: how can he be conveyed by [a scripture that is] constructed and unreal? //4//',
'If the omniscient being is known by the ignorant solely through his own statement,
how could the establishment of those two, which are mutually dependent, be construed? //5//',
'Because spoken by the omniscient, the statement is true; by that, his existence [is established] —

children.text: kathaṃ tad ubhayaṃ sidhyet siddhamūlāntarād ṛte//6//
children.translated_text: how could both be established without another established basis? //6//',
'From a statement that lacks foundation, composed by a non-omniscient being,

children.text: sarvajñam avagacchantaḥ svavākyāt kiṃ na jānate//7//
children.translated_text: those who cognize an omniscient being — why do they not know [him] from their own statement? //7//',
'If we were to see someone resembling an omniscient being now,
then by analogy we would know the omniscient — [but we do not]. //8//',
'Even the instruction of the <s>Buddha</s>, pertaining to <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the like,
would not be possible otherwise — if omniscience did not exist. //9//',

children.text: evam arthāpattir api pramāṇaṃ nātra yujyate/
children.translated_text: 'Thus, even <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is not a valid means of knowledge here,

children.text: upadeśasya satyatvaṃ yato nādhyakṣam īkṣyate//10// ityādi/
children.translated_text: since the truth of the instruction is not seen by direct perception. //10//' And so on.

children.text:
atra vidhīyate/ yad abhyadhāyi tatsadbhāvagrāhakasya pramāṇapañcakasya tatrānupalambhād
          iti tad ayuktam/ tatsadbhāvāvedakasyānumānādeḥ sadbhāvāt[/] tathā hi kaścid ātmā
          sakalapadārthasākṣātkārī tadgrahaṇasvabhāvatve sati prakṣīṇapratibandhapratyayatvāt/ yad
          yadgrahaṇasvabhāvatve sati prakṣīṇapratibandhapratyayaṃ tat tatsākṣātkāri
          yathāpagatatimirādipratibandhaṃ locanavijñānaṃ rūpasākṣātkāri/ tadgrahaṇasvabhāvatve sati
          prakṣīṇapratibandhapratyayaś ca kaścid ātmā/ tasmāt sakalapadārthasākṣātkārīti/ na tāvad
          aśeṣārthagrahaṇasvabhāvatvam ātmano ´siddham/ codanābalān
          nikhilārthajñānotpattyanyathānupapattyā sarvam anekāntātmakaṃ sattvād iti
          vyāptijñānotpatteś ca/ codanā hi bhūtaṃ bhavantaṃ bhaviṣyantaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vyavahitaṃ
          viprakṛṣṭam ity evaṃjātīyakam artham avagamayatīty evaṃjātīyakair adhvaramīmāṃsāgurubhir
          vidhipratiṣedhavicāraṇānibandhanaṃ sakalārthaviṣayajñānaṃ pratipadyamānaiḥ
          sakalārthagrahaṇasvabhāvakatvam ātmano ´bhyupagatam/ na
          cākhilārthapratibandhakāvaraṇaprakṣayānupapattiḥ/
          samyagdarśanāditrayalakṣaṇasyāvaraṇaprakṣayahetubhūtasya sāmagrīviśeṣasya pratītatvāt/
          anayā mudrayāpi kṣudropadravā vidrāvyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Here it is stated: That which was asserted — that there is no apprehension [of the omniscient], because the fivefold means of valid knowledge that would establish his existence are not found there — that is incorrect, because there do exist inference and other [means] that make known his existence. For thus: a certain Self (<s>ātman</s>) directly perceives all objects, because, having the nature of grasping them, its obstructing conditions have been exhausted. Whatever, having the nature of grasping [objects] and having its obstructing conditions exhausted, is such — that directly perceives those [objects], like ocular consciousness which, when the obstruction of blindness and the like is removed, directly perceives form. And a certain Self, having the nature of grasping them and having its obstructing conditions exhausted, [exists]. Therefore, it directly perceives all objects. Now, the nature of the Self as capable of grasping all objects is not unestablished; through the force of injunction (<s>codanā</s>), since there is no other explanation for the arising of knowledge of all objects, and because the cognition of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) arises [from the inference] "Everything has a manifold nature, because of existing." For injunction communicates objects of such kinds as past, present, future, subtle, concealed, and remote — and the teachers of ritual inquiry (<s>adhvaramīmāṃsā</s>), understanding knowledge pertaining to all objects as grounded in the investigation of injunctions and prohibitions of such kinds, have accepted the Self's nature as capable of grasping all objects. Nor is there any impossibility of the destruction of the obscuration that obstructs all objects, because the specific aggregate of causes — characterized by the triad of right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>) and the rest — which is the cause of the destruction of obscuration, is known. By this seal, minor objections too should be driven away.
Section 3.112

children.text:
nanv āvaraṇaprakṣayavaśād aśeṣaviṣayaṃ vijñānaṃ viśadaṃ mukhyapratyakṣaṃ prabhavatīty
          uktaṃ tad ayuktam/ tasya sarvajñasyānādimuktatvenāvaraṇasyaivāsaṃbhavād iti cet
children.translated_text: Now, if [one objects]: "It was stated that through the destruction of obscuration, all-encompassing knowledge becomes clear and arises as primary direct perception — but that is improper, because for that omniscient being, since he is eternally liberated from beginningless time, obscuration itself is impossible" —

children.text:
tan na/ anādimuktatvasyaivāsiddheḥ/ na sarvajño ´nādimuktaḥ/ muktatvād itaramuktavat/
          baddhāpekṣayā ca muktavyapadeśaḥ/ tadrahite cāsyāpy abhāvaḥ syād ākāśavat/
children.translated_text: That is not so, because eternal liberation itself is not established. The omniscient one is not eternally liberated; because of being liberated, like any other liberated being. And the designation "liberated" is relative to [a prior state of] bondage; in the absence of that, this [designation] too would be absent, like space.

children.text:
nanv anādeḥ kṣityādikāryaparaṃparāyāḥ kartṛtvena tatsiddhiḥ/ tathā hi: kṣityādikaṃ
          sakartṛkaṃ kāryatvād ghaṭavad iti/
children.translated_text: Now, if [one argues]: the establishment of that [omniscient being] is through his being the creator of the beginningless series of effects such as earth and the like. For thus: Earth and the like have a creator, because of being effects, like a pot.

children.text:
tad apy asamīcīnam/ kāryatvasyaivāsiddheḥ/ na ca sāvayavatvena tatsādhanam ity
          abhidhātavyam/ yasmād idaṃ vikalpajālam avatarati/ sāvayavatvaṃ kim avayavasaṃyogitvam
          avayavasamavāyitvam avayavajanyatvaṃ samavetadravyatvaṃ sāvayavabuddhiviṣayatvaṃ vā/ na
          prathamaḥ/ ākāśādāv anaikāntyāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/ sāmānyādau vyabhicārāt/ na tṛtīyaḥ/
          sādhyāviśiṣṭatvāt/ na caturthaḥ/ vikalpayugalārgalagrastagalatvāt

ASS, IV, A. The
              expression remains obscure.

/ samavāyasaṃbandhamātravad dravyatvaṃ samavetadravyatvam anyatra
          samavetadravyatvaṃ vā vivakṣitaṃ hetūkriyate/ ādye gaganādau vyabhicāraḥ/ tasyāpi
            guṇādisamavāya
children.translated_text: Is what is intended as the reason "being a substance in which [qualities] inhere" [defined as] being a substance through mere inherence-relation, or being a substance in which [qualities] inhere in something other [than itself]? In the first case, there is deviation in space and the like, because for that too, being a substance possessing inherence
[continued]

children.text:
tvadravyatvayoḥ saṃbhavāt/ dvitīye
          sādhyāviśiṣṭatā/ anyaśabdārtheṣu samavāyikāraṇabhūteṣv
children.translated_text: of qualities and the like is possible. In the second case, there is no difference from what is to be proved, because inherence in the parts — which are the inherent causes —

children.text:
avayaveṣu samavāyasya sādhanīyatvāt/ abhyupagamyaitad abhāṇi/ vastutas tu samavāya
          eva na samasti/ pramāṇābhāvāt/ nāpi pañcamaḥ/ ātmādinānaikāntyāt/ tasya
          sāvayavabuddhiviṣayatve ´pi kāryatvābhāvāt/ na ca niravayavatve ´py asya
          sāvayavārthasaṃbandhena sāvayavabuddhiviṣayatvam aupacārikam ity eṣṭavyam/ niravayavatve
          vyāpitvavirodhāt paramāṇuvat/ kiṃ ca kim ekaḥ kartā sādhyate kiṃ vāneke/ prathame
          prāsādādau vyabhicāraḥ/ sthapatyādīnāṃ bahūnāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ tatra kartṛtvopalambhāt/ dvitīye
          bahūnāṃ viśvanirmātṛtve teṣu mitho vaimatyasaṃbhāvanāyā anivāryatvād ekaikasya vastuno
          ´nyānyarūpatayā nirmāṇe sarvam asamañjasam āpadyeta/ sarveṣāṃ sāmarthyasāmyenaikenaiva
          sakalajagadutpattisiddhāv itaravaiyarthyaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: designated by the word "other" — needs to be established. This has been stated by way of concession; but in reality, <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) does not exist at all, because of the absence of a means of valid knowledge [for it]. Nor the fifth, because of inconclusiveness regarding the Self and the like, since even though it is the object of the cognition "having parts," it does not have effect-hood. And one should not claim that even in its being without parts, its being the object of the cognition "having parts" is figurative, through its connection with things that do have parts; for partlessness would conflict with all-pervasiveness, like an atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>). Moreover, is one creator being established, or many? In the first case, there is deviation in a palace and the like, because multiple persons — the architect and others — are observed to be creators thereof. In the second case, if many were the creators of the universe, since the possibility of disagreement among them cannot be prevented, in each one's creating of each thing in different ways, everything would become incoherent. And when, through the equal capacity of all, the production of the entire world is established by one alone, the others would be rendered purposeless.

That too is incorrect, because effect-hood itself is not established. And one should not say that it is established through having parts (<s>sāvayavatva</s>); for this net of alternatives descends: Does having-parts mean conjunction with parts, inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) in parts, being produced from parts, being a substance in which [qualities] inhere, or being the object of the cognition "having parts"? Not the first, because of inconclusive application to space and the like. Not the second, because of deviation in universals and the like. Not the third, because of being no different from what is to be proved. Not the fourth, because its throat is grasped by the bolt of a pair of alternatives:
Section 3.138
Thus it is stated in the Praise of the Passionless One (<s>Vītarāgastuti</s>):
"There is some creator of the world, and he is one,

children.text: sa sarvagaḥ sa svavaśaḥ sa nityaḥ/
children.translated_text: he is omnipresent, he is self-governed, he is eternal —
where would these magician's tricks be

children.text: teṣāṃ na yeṣām anuśāsakas tvam// iti/
children.translated_text: for those who do not have You as their teacher?"
And elsewhere:

children.text: kartā na tāvad iha ko ´pi yathecchayā vā
children.translated_text: "No creator whatsoever is here seen [creating] according to his wish;
otherwise, that absurd consequence would apply even in the making of a mat.

children.text: kāryaṃ kim atra bhavatāpi ca takṣakādyair
children.translated_text: What work is done here even by you, or by the carpenter and the like?

children.text: āhatya ca tribhuvanaṃ puruṣaḥ karoti// iti/
children.translated_text: A person creates the three worlds by striking [alone]."
Section 3.148

children.text:
tasmāt prāguktakāraṇatritayabalād āvaraṇaprakṣaye sārvajñyaṃ yuktam/ na
          cāsyopadeṣṭrantarābhāvāt samyagdarśanāditritayānupapattir iti bhaṇanīyam/
          pūrvasarvajñapraṇītāgamaprabhavatvād amuṣyāśeṣārthajñānasya/ na cānyonāśrayādidoṣaḥ/
          āgamasarvajñaparaṃparāyā bījāṅkuravad anāditvāṅgīkārād ity alam/
children.translated_text: Therefore, through the power of the aforementioned threefold cause, omniscience upon the destruction of obscuration is reasonable. And one should not say that there is an impossibility of the triad of right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>) and the rest due to the absence of another teacher; because this all-encompassing knowledge has its origin in the scripture (<s>āgama</s>) composed by a prior omniscient being. Nor is there the fault of mutual dependence and the like, because we accept the beginninglessness of the succession of scripture and omniscient beings, like the seed and the sprout — enough.
Section 3.153

children.text:
ratnatrayapadavedanīyatayā prasiddhaṃ samyagdarśanāditritayam arhatpravacanasaṃgrahapare
          paramāgamasāre prarūpitaṃ samyagdarśanajñānacāritrāṇi mokṣamārga iti/ vivṛtaṃ ca
          yogadevena/ yena rūpeṇa jīvādyartho vyavasthitas tena rūpeṇārhatā pratipādite tattvārthe
          viparītābhiniveśarahitatvādyaparaparyāyaṃ śraddhānaṃ samyagdarśanam/ tathā ca
          tattvārthasūtraṃ: tattvārthaṃ śraddhānaṃ samyagdarśanam iti/ anyad api:
children.translated_text: The triad of right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>) and the rest, well known as cognizable through the designation "three jewels" (<s>ratnatraya</s>), has been set forth in the supreme essence of the <s>āgama</s>, which encompasses the discourses of the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One): "Right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct are the path to liberation." And <s>Yogadeva</s> has explained: Right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>) is the belief — synonymous with being free from perverted attachment and the like — in the reality (<s>tattvārtha</s>) taught by the <s>Arhat</s> in the form in which the soul (<s>jīva</s>) and other objects are established. And thus the <s>Tattvārthasūtra</s>: "Belief in the reality of things is right faith." And also:
"Inclination toward the truths taught by the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) is called right belief;

children.text: jāyate tannisargeṇa guror adhigamena vā// iti/
children.translated_text: it arises either by nature (<s>nisarga</s>) or through the instruction of a teacher (<s>guru</s>)."

children.text:
paropadeśanirapekṣam ātmasvarūpaṃ nisargaḥ/ vyākhyānādirūpaparopadeśajanitaṃ jñānam
          adhigamaḥ/
children.translated_text: Nature (<s>nisarga</s>) is the own-nature of the Self, independent of the instruction of others. Instruction (<s>adhigama</s>) is knowledge generated by the instruction of others in the form of exposition and the like.
Section 3.163

children.text:
yena svabhāvena jīvādayaḥ padārthā vyavasthitās tena svabhāvena
          mohasaṃśayarahitatvenāvagamaḥ samyagjñānam/ yathoktam:
children.translated_text: The apprehension of the soul (<s>jīva</s>) and other objects in the form in which they are established, free from delusion and doubt, is right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>). As stated:
"That understanding of realities as they actually are, whether in summary or in detail,

children.text: yo ´vabodhas tam atrāhuḥ samyagjñānaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: the wise ones here call right knowledge."

children.text:
taj jñānaṃ pañcavidhaṃ matiśrutāvadhimanaḥparyāyakevalabhedena/ tad uktam:
          matiśrutāvadhimanaḥparyāyakevalāni jñānam iti/ asyārthaḥ: jñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśame
          satīndriyamanasī puraskṛtya vyāpṛtaḥ san yathārthaṃ manute sā matiḥ/
          jñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśame sati matijanitaṃ spaṣṭaṃ jñānaṃ śrutam/
          samyagdarśanādiguṇajanitakṣayopaśamanimittam avacchinnaviṣayaṃ jñānam avadhiḥ/
          īrṣyāntarāyajñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśame sati paramanogatasyārthasya sphuṭaṃ paricchedakaṃ
          jñānaṃ manaḥparyāyaḥ/ tapaḥkriyāviśeṣān yadarthaṃ sevante tapasvinas tajjñānam
          anyajñānāsaṃsṛṣṭaṃ kevalam/ tatrādye

children.translated_text: are indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>); the others are direct (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). As stated:

That knowledge is fivefold, through the division into <s>mati</s> (sensory knowledge), <s>śruta</s> (scriptural knowledge), <s>avadhi</s> (clairvoyance), <s>manaḥparyāya</s> (telepathy), and <s>kevala</s> (omniscience). As stated: "Knowledge is <s>mati</s>, <s>śruta</s>, <s>avadhi</s>, <s>manaḥparyāya</s>, and <s>kevala</s>." Its meaning: When the obstruction of the knowledge-obscuring [<s>karma</s>] is destroyed and subsided, one who operates with the senses and mind as instruments and apprehends objects as they are — that is <s>mati</s>. When the knowledge-obscuring [<s>karma</s>] is destroyed and subsided, the clear knowledge generated by <s>mati</s> is <s>śruta</s>. Knowledge whose object is limited, whose occasion is the destruction and subsidence [of <s>karma</s>] produced by qualities such as right faith and the like, is <s>avadhi</s> (clairvoyance). When the envy-obstructing and knowledge-obscuring [<s>karma</s>] is destroyed and subsided, the knowledge that clearly determines the object situated in another's mind is <s>manaḥparyāya</s> (telepathy). The knowledge for the sake of which ascetics practice particular austerities and actions, unmixed with other knowledge, is <s>kevala</s> (omniscience). Of these, the first [two]
"Consciousness that illuminates itself and others, that is a valid means of knowledge free from contradiction,

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ ca parokṣaṃ ca dvidhā meyaviniścayāt// iti/
children.translated_text: is twofold — direct and indirect — from the determination of the object to be known."
But the sub-classifications within [each type] should be understood in detail from the <s>āgama</s> (scripture) itself.
Section 3.179

children.text:
saṃsaraṇakarmocchittāv udyatasya śraddadhānasya jñānavataḥ pāpagamanakāraṇakriyānirvṛttiḥ
          samyakcāritram/ tad etat saprapañcam uktam arhatā:
children.translated_text: For one who has faith, possesses knowledge, and is devoted to the cessation of the <s>karma</s> of transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>), the cessation of the activity that is the cause of sinful conduct is right conduct (<s>samyakcāritra</s>). This has been stated in detail by the <s>Arhat</s>:
"The abandonment of all connections with what is blameworthy is called conduct;
it is described as fivefold through the division of vows beginning with non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>):
Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truthfulness (<s>sūnṛta</s>), non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>).
That which does not, through carelessness, cause the destruction of the life

children.text: carāṇāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca tad ahiṃsāvrataṃ matam/
children.translated_text: of moving or stationary beings — that is considered the vow of non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>).

children.text: priyaṃ pathyaṃ vacas tathyaṃ sūnṛtaṃ vratam ucyate//
children.translated_text: Speech that is pleasant, beneficial, and true is called the vow of truthfulness (<s>sūnṛta</s>);

children.text: tat tathyam api no tathyam apriyaṃ cāhitaṃ ca yat/
children.translated_text: that which is true but unpleasant and unhelpful is not [considered truthful].
The non-taking of what has not been given is declared as the vow of non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>).

children.text: bāhyāḥ prāṇā nṛṇām artho haratā taṃ hatā hi te/
children.translated_text: Wealth is the external life-breath of human beings; by one who steals it, they are [as if] killed.
Through acts done, approved, or caused to be done, by mind, speech, and body,
the renunciation of divine, bodily, and sensual [pleasures] — celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) is considered eighteenfold.
The abandonment of attachment (<s>mūrcchā</s>) in all things would be non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>);

children.text: yad asatsv api jāyeta mūrchayā cittaviplavaḥ//
children.translated_text: that which is the agitation of mind arising through attachment even toward non-existent things.
Cultivated by the fivefold meditations, the five [vows],

children.text: mahāvratāni lokasya sādhayanty avyayaṃ padam// iti/
children.translated_text: each progressively, as great vows (<s>mahāvrata</s>), accomplish for the world the imperishable state."
And the elaboration of the fivefold meditation has been set forth:
"Through the constant refusal of laughter, greed, fear, and anger,
and by reflecting upon and also speaking [about it], one should cultivate the vow of truthfulness" —

children.text:
ityādinā/ etāni samyagdarśanajñānacāritrāṇi militāni mokṣakāraṇaṃ na pratyekam/ yathā
          rasāyanam/ tathā cātra jñānaśraddhānācaraṇāni saṃbhūya phalaṃ sādhayanti na pratyekam/
children.translated_text: and so forth. These — right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct — combined together are the cause of liberation, not individually; like a medicinal compound. And thus here, faith, knowledge, and conduct, coming together, accomplish the fruit, not individually.
Section 3.202

children.text:
atra saṃkṣepatas tāvaj jīvājīvākhye dve tattve staḥ/ tatra bodhātmako jīvaḥ/ abodhātmakas
          tv ajīvaḥ/ tad uktaṃ padmanandinā:
children.translated_text: Here, in brief, there are two realities (<s>tattva</s>) called <s>jīva</s> (soul) and <s>ajīva</s> (non-soul). Therein, the <s>jīva</s> is of the nature of consciousness. The <s>ajīva</s> is of the nature of non-consciousness. Thus it is stated by <s>Padmanandin</s>:

children.text: cid acid dve pare tattve vivekas tadvivecanam/
children.translated_text: "Consciousness (<s>cit</s>) and non-consciousness (<s>acit</s>) are the two supreme realities; discrimination (<s>viveka</s>) is the discernment of them.

children.text: upādeyam upādeyaṃ heyaṃ heyaṃ ca kurvataḥ//
children.translated_text: For one who makes what is to be accepted, accepted, and what is to be rejected, rejected:
what is to be rejected is attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the like of the agent, and its effect is non-discrimination;
what is to be accepted is the supreme light, characterized solely by consciousness (<s>upayoga</s>)."

children.text:
sahajacidrūpapariṇatiṃ svīkurvāṇe jñānadarśane upayogaḥ/ sa parasparapradeśānāṃ
          pradeśabandhāt karmaṇaikībhūtasyātmano ´nyatvapratipattikāraṇaṃ bhavati/
          sakalajīvasādhāraṇaṃ caitanyam upaśamakṣayakṣayopaśamavaśād
          aupaśamikakṣayātmakakṣāyaupaśamikabhāvena karmodayavaśāt kaluṣānyākāreṇa ca
          pariṇatajīvaparyāyavivakṣāyāṃ jīvasvarūpaṃ bhavati/ yad avocad vācakācāryaḥ:
          aupaśamikakṣāyikau bhāvau miśraś ca jīvasya svatattvam audayikapāriṇāmikau ca iti/
          anudayaprāptirūpe karmaṇa upaśame sati jīvasyotpadyamāno bhāva aupaśamikaḥ/ yathā paṅke
          kaluṣatāṃ kurvati katakādidravyasaṃbandhād adhaḥpatite jalasya svacchatā/
          ārhatatattvānusaṃdhānavaśād rāgādipaṅkakṣālanena nirmalatāpādakaḥ kṣāyiko bhāvaḥ/ karmaṇaḥ
          kṣaye sati jāyamāno bhāvaḥ kṣāyikaḥ yathā paṅkāt pṛthagbhūtasya nirmalasya
          sphāṭikādibhājanāntargatasya jalasya svacchatā/ yathā mokṣaḥ/ ubhayātmā bhāvo miśraḥ/
          yathā jalasyārdhasvacchatā/ karmodaye sati bhavan bhāva audayikaḥ/ karmopaśamādyanapekṣaḥ
          sahajo bhāvaś cetanatvādiḥ pāriṇāmikaḥ/ tad etad yathāsaṃbhavaṃ bhavyasyābhavyasya vā
          jīvasya svarūpam iti sūtrārthaḥ/ tad uktaṃ svarūpasaṃbodhane:
children.translated_text: When one accepts the innate transformation of consciousness-nature, the <s>upayoga</s> (active cognition) consists of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and perception (<s>darśana</s>). That [upayoga] becomes the cause of the cognition of otherness of the self, which has become one due to the bondage of spatial points (<s>pradeśas</s>) to one another's spatial points through <s>karma</s>. Consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), which is common to all <s>jīvas</s> (souls), by the force of subsidence (<s>upaśama</s>), destruction (<s>kṣaya</s>), and destruction-cum-subsidence (<s>kṣayopaśama</s>), takes the form of the subsidential (<s>aupaśamika</s>), destructional (<s>kṣāyika</s>), and destructional-subsidential (<s>kṣāyopaśamika</s>) states; and by the force of karmic fruition, [it takes] a turbid form — when one intends [to describe] the modifications of the <s>jīva</s> transformed [in these ways], this constitutes the essential nature of the <s>jīva</s>. As the <s>Vācakācārya</s> (<s>Umāsvāti</s>) stated: 'The subsidential, the destructional, the mixed — these are the soul's own nature; and also the fruition-born (<s>audayika</s>) and the transformational (<s>pāriṇāmika</s>).' The state that arises in the <s>jīva</s> when there is subsidence of <s>karma</s> — characterized by non-fruition — is the subsidential (<s>aupaśamika</s>) [state]. Just as when mud causes turbidity, through association with <s>kataka</s> and other substances, when [the mud] settles to the bottom, the water becomes clear. The destructional (<s>kṣāyika</s>) state produces purity through the cleansing of the mud of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, by the force of contemplation upon the reality of the <s>Arhat</s>. The state that arises upon the destruction of <s>karma</s> is the destructional (<s>kṣāyika</s>) — just as the clarity of water that has been separated from mud and placed in a pure vessel of crystal and the like. Like <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). The state that partakes of both natures is the mixed (<s>miśra</s>). Like the half-clarity of water. The state that comes about when <s>karma</s> is in fruition is the fruition-born (<s>audayika</s>). The innate state — such as the quality of being sentient (<s>cetanatva</s>) — which does not depend on the subsidence or destruction of <s>karma</s>, is the transformational (<s>pāriṇāmika</s>). This, then, as applicable, is the essential nature of the <s>jīva</s>, whether capable of liberation (<s>bhavya</s>) or incapable of liberation (<s>abhavya</s>) — such is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. As stated in the <s>Svarūpasaṃbodhana</s>:

children.text: jñānād bhinno na nābhinno bhinnābhinnaḥ kathaṃcana/
children.translated_text: Neither different from knowledge nor non-different, [yet] somehow both different and non-different;

children.text: jñānaṃ pūrvāparībhūtaṃ so ´yam ātmeti kīrtitaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: knowledge that has become prior and subsequent — that is declared to be the self (<s>ātman</s>).
reference marker

children.text:
nanu bhedābhedayoḥ parasparaparihāreṇāvasthānād anyatarasyaiva vāstavatvād
          ubhayātmakatvam ayuktam iti cet
children.translated_text: Now, if [it be objected:] since difference and non-difference subsist by mutual exclusion, only one of them can be real; therefore having both natures is unjustified —

children.text:
tad ayuktam/ bādhe pramāṇābhāvāt/ anupalambho hi bādhakaṃ pramāṇam/ na so ´sti/ samasteṣu
          vastuṣv anekāntātmakatvasya syādvādino mate suprasiddhatvād ity alam/
children.translated_text: that is not valid. Because there is no means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) to refute [it]. For non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) is the refuting means of valid knowledge. But that [non-apprehension] does not obtain. Because in the view of the <s>Syādvādin</s> (the Jaina proponent of conditional predication), the many-sided nature (<s>anekāntātmakatva</s>) of all entities is well established. Enough [of this].
reference marker

children.text:
apare punar jīvājīvayor aparaṃ prapañcam ācakṣate
          jīvākāśadharmādharmapudgalāstikāyabhedāt/ eteṣu pañcasu tattveṣu
          kālatrayasaṃbandhitayāstīti sthitivyapadeśaḥ/ anekapradeśatvena śarīravat kāyavyapadeśaḥ/
          tatra jīvā dvividhāḥ saṃsāriṇo muktāś ca/ bhavād bhavāntaraprāptimantaḥ saṃsāriṇaḥ/ te ca
          dvividhāḥ, samanaskā amanaskāś ca/ tatra saṃjñinaḥ samanaskāḥ/ śikṣākriyālāpagrahaṇarūpā
          saṃjñā/ tadvidhurās tv amanaskāḥ/ te cāmanaskā dvividhāḥ, trasasthāvarabhedāt/ tatra
          dvīndriyādayaḥ śaṅkhagaṇḍolakaprabhṛtayaś caturvidhās trasāḥ/
          pṛthivyaptejovāyuvanaspatayaḥ sthāvarāḥ/ tatra mārgagatadhūliḥ pṛthivī/ iṣṭakādiḥ
          pṛthivīkāyaḥ/ pṛthivī kāyatvena yena gṛhītā sa pṛthivīkāyikaḥ/ pṛthivīṃ kāyatvena yo
          grahīṣyati sa pṛthivījīvaḥ/ evam abādiṣv api bhedacatuṣṭayaṃ yojyam/ tatra pṛthivyādi
          kāyatvena gṛhītavanto grahīṣyantaś ca sthāvarā gṛhyante na pṛthivyādipṛthivīkāyādayaḥ/
          teṣām ajīvatvāt/ te ca sthāvarāḥ sparśanaikendriyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Others further expound a different elaboration of <s>jīva</s> (soul) and <s>ajīva</s> (non-soul), through the division into the extended substances (<s>astikāyas</s>) of <s>jīva</s>, <s>ākāśa</s> (space), <s>dharma</s> (principle of motion), <s>adharma</s> (principle of rest), and <s>pudgala</s> (matter). Among these five categories, the designation 'existent' (<s>asti</s>) is [applied] because of their connection with the three times. The designation 'body' (<s>kāya</s>) is [applied] because of their having many spatial points (<s>pradeśas</s>), like a body. Therein, <s>jīvas</s> are of two kinds: those in <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) and the liberated (<s>mukta</s>). Those who attain passage from one existence to another are in <s>saṃsāra</s>. And they are of two kinds: those with mind (<s>samanaska</s>) and those without mind (<s>amanaska</s>). Among these, the rational (<s>saṃjñin</s>) are those with mind. <s>Saṃjñā</s> (rationality) consists of learning, activity, speech, and comprehension. Those devoid of that are without mind. And those without mind are of two kinds, by the division of mobile (<s>trasa</s>) and immobile (<s>sthāvara</s>). Among these, those with two or more senses — such as conches, worms, and the like — constitute the four types of mobile beings. Earth, water, fire, air, and plants are the immobile (<s>sthāvara</s>) beings. Therein, dust on a road is 'earth.' Bricks and the like constitute the 'earth-body' (<s>pṛthivīkāya</s>). One who has taken earth as a body is an 'earth-bodied being' (<s>pṛthivīkāyika</s>). One who will take earth as a body is an 'earth-soul' (<s>pṛthivījīva</s>). Likewise, the fourfold division should be applied to water and the rest as well. Therein, those who have taken or will take earth and so forth as a body are understood as immobile beings — not [the inert] earth, earth-bodies, and so forth [themselves]. Because those [inert substances] are non-living (<s>ajīva</s>). And those immobile beings have touch as their single sense.
reference marker
Those devoid of attaining another existence are the liberated (<s>mukta</s>).

children.text:
dharmādharmākāśāstikāyās ta ekatvaśālino niṣkriyāś ca dravyasya deśāntaraprāptihetavaḥ/
          tatra dharmādharmau prasiddhau/ ālokenāvacchinne nabhasi lokākāśapadavedanīye tayoḥ
          sarvatrāvasthitiḥ/ gatisthityupagraho dharmādharmayor upakāraḥ/ ata eva dharmāstikāyaḥ
          pravṛttyanumeyaḥ/ adharmāstikāyaḥ sthityanumeyaḥ/ anyavastupradeśamadhye ´nyasya vastuno
          praveśo ´vagāhaḥ/ tad ākāśakṛtyam/
children.translated_text: The extended substances (<s>astikāyas</s>) of <s>dharma</s> (principle of motion), <s>adharma</s> (principle of rest), and <s>ākāśa</s> (space) — these possess unity and are inactive; they are the causes of a substance's reaching another location. Among these, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are well known. In the space (<s>nabhas</s>) delimited by light, designated as 'world-space' (<s>lokākāśa</s>), there is the presence of those two everywhere. The assistance of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> consists in facilitating motion and rest [respectively]. Hence the <s>dharmāstikāya</s> (principle of motion) is inferable from movement. The <s>adharmāstikāya</s> (principle of rest) is inferable from stationariness. The penetration of one substance into the spatial points occupied by another substance is called <s>avagāha</s> (interpenetration). That is the function of <s>ākāśa</s> (space).
reference marker

children.text:
sparśarasagandhavarṇavantaḥ pudgalāḥ/ te ca dvividhā aṇavaḥ skandhāś ca/ bhoktum aśakyā
          aṇavaḥ/ dvyaṇukādayaḥ skandhāḥ/ tatra dvyaṇukādiskandhabhedād aṇvādir utpadyate/
          aṇvādisaṃghātād dvyaṇukādir utpadyate/ kvacid bhedasaṃghātābhyāṃ skandhotpattiḥ/ ata eva
          pūrayanti galantīti pudgalāḥ/ kālasyānekapradeśatvābhāvenāstikāyatvābhāve ´pi dravyatvam
          asti/ tallakṣaṇayogāt/ tad uktaṃ guṇaparyāyavad dravyam iti dravyāśrayā nirguṇā guṇāḥ/
          yathā jīvasya jñānatvādidharmarūpāḥ pudgalasya rūpatvādisāmānyasvabhāvāḥ/
          dharmādharmākāśakālānāṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ gatisthityavagāhavartanāhetutvādisāmānyāni guṇāḥ/
          tasya dravyasyoktarūpeṇa bhavanaṃ paryāyaḥ/ utpādas tadbhāvaḥ pariṇāmaḥ paryāya iti
          paryāyāḥ/ yathā jīvasya ghaṭādijñānasukhakleśādayaḥ/ pudgalasya mṛtpiṇḍaghaṭādayaḥ/
          dharmādīnāṃ gatyādiviśeṣāḥ/ ata eva ṣaḍ dravyāṇīti prasiddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Pudgalas</s> (material atoms) possess touch, taste, smell, and color. They are of two kinds: atoms (<s>aṇu</s>) and aggregates (<s>skandha</s>). Atoms are those that cannot be [separately] experienced. Dyads and so forth are aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). Among these, from the division of aggregates beginning with dyads, atoms and the rest are produced. From the combination of atoms and the rest, dyads and the rest are produced. In some cases, the production of an aggregate occurs through both division and combination. Hence they are called <s>pudgalas</s> — because they 'fill up' (<s>pūrayanti</s>) and 'ooze away' (<s>galanti</s>). Although time (<s>kāla</s>) does not have the status of an extended substance (<s>astikāya</s>) because it lacks multiple spatial points, it still possesses the status of a substance (<s>dravya</s>). Because it possesses the characteristics [of a substance]. As stated: 'A substance is that which has qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and modifications (<s>paryāya</s>).' Qualities are those that depend on the substance and are themselves without [further] qualities. Such as the properties of knowledge and the like that constitute the <s>dharma</s>-nature of the <s>jīva</s>; the generic natures such as color and the like of <s>pudgala</s> (matter); and for <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, <s>ākāśa</s>, and <s>kāla</s>, the generic [properties] of being the cause of motion, rest, interpenetration, and change, respectively. The existing in the stated form of that substance is a modification (<s>paryāya</s>). Origination, that-state, and transformation are called modifications. For example, the <s>jīva's</s> [modifications include] knowledge of a pot and so forth, pleasure, affliction, and so forth. The <s>pudgala's</s> [modifications include] a lump of clay, a pot, and so forth. For <s>dharma</s> and the rest, the particular instances of motion and so forth. Hence the well-known [doctrine of] six substances.
reference marker

children.text: kecana sapta tattvānīti varṇayanti/ tad āha: jīvājīvāsravabandhasaṃvaranirjarā

mokṣās tattvāni iti/ tatra jīvājīvau nirūpitau/ āsravo nirūpyate:
          audārikādikāyādicalanadvāreṇātmanaś calanaṃ yogapadavedanīyaṃ āsravaḥ/ yathā salilāvagāhi
          dvāraṃ jalādyāsravaṇakāraṇatvād āsrava iti nigadyate tathā yogapraṇāḍikayā karmāsravatīti
          sa yoga āsravaḥ/ yathārdraṃ vastraṃ samantād vātānītaṃ reṇujātam upādatte tathā
          kaṣāyajalārdra ātmā yogānītaṃ karma sarvapradeśair gṛhṇāti/ yathā vā niṣṭaptāyaḥpiṇḍo jale
          kṣipto ´mbhaḥ samantād gṛhṇāti tathā kaṣāyoṣṇo jīvo yogānītaṃ karma samantād ādatte/
          kaṣati hinasty ātmānaṃ kugatiprāpaṇād iti kaṣāyaḥ krodho māno māyā lobhaś ca/ sa dvividhaḥ
          śubhāśubhabhedāt/ atrāhiṃsādiḥ śubhaḥ kāyayogaḥ/ satyamitahitabhāṣaṇādiḥ śubho vāgyogaḥ/
          arhatsiddhācāryopādhyāyasādhunāmadheya-pañcaparameṣṭhibhaktitaporuciśrutavinayādiḥ śubho
          manoyogaḥ/ etadviparītas tv aśubhas trividho yogaḥ/ tad etad āsravabhedaprabhedajātaṃ
          kāyavāṅmanaḥkarma yogaḥ/ sa āsravaḥ/ śubhaḥ puṇyasya/ aśubhaḥ pāpasya ityādinā
          sūtrasaṃdarbheṇa sasaṃrambham abhāṇi/ apare tv evaṃ menire: āsravayati puruṣaṃ viṣayeṣv
          indriyapravṛttir āsravaḥ/ indriyadvārā hi pauruṣaṃ jyotir viṣayān spṛśad rūpādijñānarūpeṇa
          pariṇamata iti/
children.translated_text: and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — these are the categories.' Among these, <s>jīva</s> and <s>ajīva</s> have been explained. <s>Āsrava</s> (influx) is now explained: The movement of the self through the channel of bodily and other activities beginning with the gross (<s>audārika</s>) body — that which is designated by the term <s>yoga</s> (activity) — is <s>āsrava</s>. Just as a water-submerged opening, being the cause of the inflow of water and the like, is called <s>āsrava</s> (influx) — so through the channel of <s>yoga</s> (activity), <s>karma</s> flows in, and that <s>yoga</s> is called <s>āsrava</s>. Just as a wet cloth, [blown by wind] from all sides, takes up the dust particles carried by the wind — so the self, moist with the water of passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>), grasps with all its spatial points the <s>karma</s> carried by activity (<s>yoga</s>). Or just as a heated iron ball thrown into water absorbs water from all sides — so the self, heated by passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>), takes in <s>karma</s> carried by activity from all sides. That which injures the self by leading it to an evil destiny is called <s>kaṣāya</s> (passion) — namely anger (<s>krodha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), deceit (<s>māyā</s>), and greed (<s>lobha</s>). That [āsrava] is of two kinds, by the division of auspicious (<s>śubha</s>) and inauspicious (<s>aśubha</s>). Herein, non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) and the like constitute auspicious bodily activity (<s>kāyayoga</s>). Truthful, measured, and beneficial speech and the like constitute auspicious verbal activity (<s>vāgyoga</s>). Devotion to the five supreme beings (<s>pañca parameṣṭhins</s>) — namely the <s>Arhat</s>, the <s>Siddha</s>, the <s>Ācārya</s>, the <s>Upādhyāya</s>, and the <s>Sādhu</s> — and austerity, interest in scripture, discipline, and the like constitute auspicious mental activity (<s>manoyoga</s>). The opposite of these constitutes the threefold inauspicious <s>yoga</s>. This entire set of divisions and subdivisions of <s>āsrava</s> (influx) — [namely] the <s>karma</s> of body, speech, and mind, which is <s>yoga</s> (activity) — that is <s>āsrava</s>. The auspicious [influx] is [the influx] of merit (<s>puṇya</s>); the inauspicious, of demerit (<s>pāpa</s>) — and so forth, as was spoken with vigor through the <s>sūtra</s> passages. Others, however, held this view: <s>Āsrava</s> is the activity of the senses toward objects, which causes the person to flow out (<s>āsravayati</s>). For the luminosity of the person, through the doors of the senses, touching objects, transforms into cognition of form and so forth.

Some describe seven categories (<s>tattvas</s>). As stated: '<s>Jīva</s> (soul), <s>ajīva</s> (non-soul), <s>āsrava</s> (influx), <s>bandha</s> (bondage), <s>saṃvara</s> (stoppage), <s>nirjarā</s> (shedding),
reference marker

children.text:
mithyādarśanāviratipramādakaṣāyavaśād yogavaśāc cātmā sūkṣmaikakṣetrāvagāhinām
          anantapradeśānāṃ pudgalānāṃ karmabhāvayogyānām

° A, ASS, IV. This correction is justified by the next line.
              Material particles (
karma; they are rather capable of

ādānam upaśleṣaṇaṃ yat karoti sa bandhaḥ/ tad uktaṃ sakaṣāyatvāj jīvaḥ
          karmabhāvayogyān pudgalān ādatte sa bandhaḥ iti/ tatra kaṣāyagrahaṇaṃ
          sarvabandhahetūpalakṣaṇārtham/ bandhahetūn papāṭha vācakācāryaḥ:
          mithyādarśanāviratipramādakaṣāyayogā bandhahetavaḥ iti/
children.translated_text: the taking in and adhesion that [the self] performs — that is <s>bandha</s> (bondage). As stated: 'Because the <s>jīva</s> has passions, it takes in <s>pudgalas</s> suitable for becoming <s>karma</s> — that is bondage.' Therein, the mention of passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>) is for the purpose of indicating all causes of bondage collectively. The <s>Vācakācārya</s> enumerated the causes of bondage: 'Wrong view, non-restraint, heedlessness, passions, and activities are the causes of bondage.'

Due to wrong view (<s>mithyādarśana</s>), non-restraint (<s>avirati</s>), heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>), and activity (<s>yoga</s>), the self takes in <s>pudgalas</s> (material particles) — which are infinitely many in spatial points, occupying a single spatial field with [the soul], and suitable for becoming <s>karma</s> —

children.text:
mithyādarśanaṃ dvividhaṃ mithyākarmodayāt paropadeśānapekṣaṃ tattvāśraddhānaṃ naisargikam
          ekam/ aparaṃ paropadeśajam/ pṛthivyādiṣaṭkopādānaṃ ṣaḍindriyāsaṃyamanaṃ cāviratiḥ/
          pañcasamititriguptiṣv anutsāhaḥ pramādaḥ/ kaṣāyaḥ krodhādiḥ/ tatra kaṣāyāntāḥ
          sthityanubhavabandhahetavaḥ prakṛtipradeśabandhahetur yoga iti vibhāgaḥ/ bandhaś
          caturvidha ity uktaṃ prakṛtisthityanubhavapradeśās tadvidhayaḥ iti/ yathā nimbaguḍādes
          tiktatvamadhuratvādisvabhāva evam āvaraṇīyasya jñānadarśanāvaraṇatvam
          ādityaprabhācchādakāmbhodharavat pradīpaprabhātirodhāyakakumbhavac ca/ sadasadvedanīyasya
          sukhaduḥkhotpādakatvam asidhārāmadhulehanavat/ darśane mohanīyasya
          tattvārthāśraddhānakāritvaṃ durjanasaṅgavat/ cāritre mohanīyasyāsaṃyamahetutvaṃ
          madyamadavat/ āyuṣo dehabandhakartṛtvaṃ jalavat/ nāmno vicitranāmakāritraṃ citrikavat/
          gotrasyoccanīcakāritraṃ kumbhakāravat/ dānādīnāṃ vighnanidānatvam antarāyasya svabhāvaḥ
          kośādhyakṣavat/ so ´yaṃ prakṛtibandho ´ṣṭavidho
          dravyakarmāvāntarabhedamūlaprakṛtivedanīyaḥ/ tathāvocad umāsvātivācakācāryaḥ: ādyo
          jñānadarśanāvaraṇavedanīyamohanīyāyurnāmagotrāntarāyāḥ iti/ tadbhedaṃ ca samagṛhṇāt
          pañcanavadvyaṣṭāviṃśaticaturdvicatvāriṃśaddvipañcabhedā yathākramam iti/ etac ca sarvaṃ
          vidyānandādibhir vivṛtam iti vistarabhayān na prastūyate/

children.translated_text: Just as the milks of goats, cows, buffaloes, and the like

children.text:
etāvantam anehasaṃ mādhuryasvabhāvād apracyutisthitis
          tathā jñānāvaraṇādīnāṃ mūlaprakṛtīnām “āditas tisṛṇām antarāyasya ca
          triṃśatsāgaropamakoṭikoṭyaḥ parā sthitiḥ” ityādyuktakālā durdāntavat svīyasvabhāvād
          apracyutisthitiḥ/
children.translated_text: have a fixed duration of [such-and-such] extent of sweetness by [their] inherent nature of sweetness — so for the fundamental natures of knowledge-obscuration and the rest, [the statement:] 'For the first three and for obstructive [karma], the maximum duration is thirty <s>sāgaropama-koṭi-koṭis</s> (ocean-measured periods)' and so forth — the duration, like that of an untamed [animal], is fixed by [their] own inherent nature.
Just as the milks of goats, cows, buffaloes, and the like

children.text:
tīvramandādibhāvena svakāryakaraṇe sāmaṛthyaviśeṣo ´nubhāvas tathā karmapudgalānāṃ
          svakāryakaraṇe sāmarthyaviśeṣo ´nubhāvaḥ/ karmabhāvapariṇatapudgalaskandhānām
          anantānantapradeśānām ātmapradeśānupraveśaḥ pradeśabandhaḥ/
children.translated_text: have a particular capacity in producing their respective effects through intense, mild, and other degrees — so the karmic <s>pudgalas</s> (material particles) have a particular capacity (<s>anubhāva</s>) in producing their respective effects. The penetration of the infinite-times-infinite spatial points of the <s>pudgala</s>-aggregates that have been transformed into the state of <s>karma</s> into the spatial points of the self is the bondage of spatial points (<s>pradeśabandha</s>).

Wrong view (<s>mithyādarśana</s>) is of two kinds: one is innate (<s>naisargika</s>), arising from the fruition of wrong-view-<s>karma</s>, being disbelief in reality independent of others' instruction. The other is born from others' instruction. Non-restraint (<s>avirati</s>) consists of the taking in of the sixfold [matter beginning with] earth and the non-control of the six senses. Heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>) is lack of enthusiasm in the five <s>samitis</s> (careful conduct) and three <s>guptis</s> (restraints). Passion (<s>kaṣāya</s>) is anger and the rest. Among these, [the causes] ending with passions are the causes of bondage of duration (<s>sthiti</s>) and intensity of fruition (<s>anubhava</s>); activity (<s>yoga</s>) is the cause of bondage of nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) and spatial points (<s>pradeśa</s>) — this is the distinction. And bondage is fourfold, as stated: 'Nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), duration (<s>sthiti</s>), intensity of fruition (<s>anubhava</s>), and spatial points (<s>pradeśa</s>) — these are its varieties.' Just as neem, jaggery, and the like have the inherent natures of bitterness, sweetness, and so forth — so the obscuring (<s>āvaraṇīya</s>) [karma's] nature is the obscuration of knowledge and perception, like a cloud covering the light of the sun, or like a pot concealing the light of a lamp. The pleasant and unpleasant experiential [karma's] nature is the production of happiness and suffering, like licking honey on a sword-blade. The deluding <s>karma</s> pertaining to view (<s>darśanamohanīya</s>) causes disbelief in the true nature of reality, like the company of wicked people. The deluding <s>karma</s> pertaining to conduct (<s>cāritramohanīya</s>) causes non-restraint, like intoxication from liquor. Lifespan-determining [<s>karma</s>] (<s>āyus</s>) binds the body, like water. Name-determining [<s>karma</s>] (<s>nāma</s>) produces various bodily forms, like a painter. Status-determining [<s>karma</s>] (<s>gotra</s>) produces high and low status, like a potter. The nature of obstructive [<s>karma</s>] (<s>antarāya</s>) is being the cause of hindrance to giving and the like, like a treasurer. This bondage of nature is eightfold, and the sub-varieties of the fundamental karmic matter are experienceable. Thus spoke <s>Umāsvāti</s>, the <s>Vācakācārya</s>: 'The primary [types] are: knowledge-obscuring, perception-obscuring, experiential, deluding, lifespan-determining, name-determining, status-determining, and obstructive.' And he summarized their sub-divisions: 'Five, nine, two, twenty-eight, four, two, forty-two, two, and five [sub-types] respectively.' All this has been elaborated by <s>Vidyānanda</s> and others — therefore it is not expounded [here] for fear of prolixity.
reference marker

children.text:
āsravanirodhaḥ saṃvaraḥ/ yenātmani praviśat karma pratiṣidhyate sa guptisamityādiḥ
          saṃvaraḥ/ saṃcārakāraṇāyogād ātmano gopanaṃ guptiḥ/ sā trividhā kāyavāṅmanonigrahabhedāt/
          prāṇipīḍāparihāreṇa samyagayanaṃ samitiḥ/ seryābhāṣādibhedāt pañcadhā/ prapañcitaṃ ca
          hemacandrācāryaiḥ:
children.translated_text: The cessation of influx (<s>āsrava</s>) is restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>). That by which <s>karma</s> entering into the self is prevented -- the restraints of guarding (<s>gupti</s>), carefulness (<s>samiti</s>), and the like -- is <s>saṃvara</s>. Guarding (<s>gupti</s>) is the protection of the self by preventing the causes of wandering. It is threefold, by the distinction of restraint of body, speech, and mind. Carefulness (<s>samiti</s>) is proper movement with the avoidance of harm to living beings. It is fivefold, by the distinctions of walking (<s>īryā</s>), speaking (<s>bhāṣā</s>), and the like. And it has been elaborated by the teacher <s>Hemacandra</s>:
reference marker
On a path traversed by the world, kissed by the rays of the sun,

children.text: janturakṣārtham ālokya gatir īryā matā satām//
children.translated_text: walking after looking [carefully] for the sake of protecting living beings -- this is regarded by the virtuous as <s>īryā</s> (proper walking).
Blameless, truthful, universally benign, measured speech --
that restraint of speech pleasing [to all] is called <s>bhāṣāsamiti</s> (carefulness of speech).
Alms-food that is never defiled by the forty-two defects of begging --

children.text: munir yad annam ādatte saiṣaṇāsamitir matā//
children.translated_text: that which the ascetic accepts is regarded as <s>eṣaṇāsamiti</s> (carefulness of seeking).
Having inspected seats and the like and carefully passed over [them],
one should take, put down, and meditate -- this is known as <s>ādānasamiti</s> (carefulness of taking and putting).
On ground free of living beings, [covered] mainly with phlegm, urine, and excrement,

children.text: yatnād yad utsṛjet sādhuḥ sotsargasamitir bhavet//
children.translated_text: that which the virtuous one discards with care -- that is <s>utsargasamiti</s> (carefulness of excretion).
reference marker
Therefore:
<s>Saṃvara</s> (restraint) closes the door of the stream of influx (<s>āsrava</s>);
thus they have explained. The authoritative ones have stated:
Influx (<s>āsrava</s>) is the cause of worldly existence; restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) is the cause of liberation.

children.text: itīyam ārhatī sṛṣṭir anyad asyāḥ prapañcanam//
children.translated_text: This is the creation of the <s>Ārhata</s> (Jaina) [doctrine]; the rest is its elaboration.

children.text:
arjitasya karmaṇas tapaḥprabhṛtibhir nirjaraṇaṃ nirjarākhyaṃ tattvam/
          cirakālapravṛttakaṣāyakalāpaṃ puṇyaṃ sukhaduḥkhe ca dehena jarayati nāśayati
          keśolluñcanādikaṃ tapa ucyate/ sā nirjarā dvividhā yathākālaupakramikabhedāt/ tatra
          prathamā yasmin kāle yat karma phalapradatvenābhimataṃ tasminn eva kāle phaladānād
          bhavantī nirjarā kāmādipākajeti ca jegīyate/ yat karma tapobalāt svakāmanayodayāvaliṃ
          praveśya prapadyate saupakramikanirjarā/ yad āha:
children.translated_text: The wearing away (<s>nirjaraṇa</s>) of accumulated <s>karma</s> through austerity (<s>tapas</s>) and the like is the category called <s>nirjarā</s> (dissipation). It causes the decay and destruction by the body of the aggregate of passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>) accumulated over a long time, and merit, and pleasure and pain. The plucking of hair and the like is called austerity (<s>tapas</s>). That <s>nirjarā</s> is twofold, by the distinction of natural (<s>yathākāla</s>) and deliberate (<s>aupakramika</s>). Among these, the first is the <s>nirjarā</s> that occurs when <s>karma</s> that is considered to yield fruit at a certain time gives fruit at that very time -- and it is also called <s>kāmādipākajā</s> (ripening of desire and the like). That <s>karma</s> which, through the power of austerity, having entered the sequence of its own desired and natural arising, is brought about -- that is deliberate <s>nirjarā</s>. As stated:
The wearing away here of <s>karmas</s> that are the seeds of <s>saṃsāra</s>
is accepted as <s>nirjarā</s>, of two kinds: with desire (<s>sakāma</s>) and without desire (<s>akāma</s>).

children.text: smṛtā sakāmā yaminām akāmā tv anyadehinām// iti
children.translated_text: <s>Sakāmā</s> (with desire) is for ascetics; <s>akāmā</s> (without desire) is for other embodied beings.
reference marker

children.text:
mithyādarśanādīnāṃ bandhahetūnāṃ nirodhe ’bhinavakarmābhāvān nirjarā
          hetusannidhānenārjitasya karmaṇo nirasanād ātyantikakarmamokṣaṇaṃ mokṣaḥ/ tad āha:
          bandhahetvabhāvanirjarābhyāṃ kṛtsnakarmavipramokṣaṇaṃ mokṣaḥ iti/ tadanantaram ūrdhvaṃ
          gacchaty ā lokāntāt/ yathā hastadaṇḍādibhramipreritaṃ kulālacakram uparate ´pi tasmiṃs
          tadbalād evāsaṃskārakṣayaṃ bhramati tathā bhavasthenātmanāpavargaprāptaye bahuśo yat kṛtaṃ
          praṇidhānaṃ muktasya tadabhāve ´pi pūrvasaṃskārāt ālokāntaṃ gamanam upapadyate/ yathā vā
          mṛttikālepakṛtagauravam alābudravyaṃ jale ´dhaḥ patati punar apetamṛttikābandham ūrdhvaṃ
          gacchati tathā karmarahita ātmā asaṅgatvād ūrdhvaṃ gacchati/ bandhacchedād eraṇḍabījavac
          cordhvaṃ gatisvabhāvāc cāgniśikhāvat/ anyonyaṃ pradeśānupraveśe saty avibhāgenāvasthānaṃ
