          evaṃvidhaniyamaviśeṣasamāsāditapuruṣottamaprasādavidhvastatamaḥ-svāntasyānanyaprayojanānavarataniratiśayapriyaviśadātmapratyayāvabhāsatā-pannadhyānarūpayā
          bhaktyā puruṣottamapadaṃ labhyata iti siddham/ tad uktaṃ yāmunena: ubhayaparikarmitasvāntasyaikāntikātyantikabhaktiyogalabhya

children.translated_text: meaning: for one whose inner organ has been refined by <s>jñānayoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge) and <s>karmayoga</s> (the yoga of action).

Thus, for one whose mind has been purified by the grace of <s>Puruṣottama</s> obtained through such specific observances, and whose darkness [of ignorance] has been dispelled — through devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) in the form of meditation, which has the appearance of a vivid self-cognition that is without other purpose, unceasing, of unsurpassing dearness — the abode of <s>Puruṣottama</s> is obtained. This is established. Thus <s>Yāmuna</s> has stated: "[The supreme abode] is obtainable through <s>bhaktiyoga</s> that is exclusive and absolute, for one whose mind has been purified by both [<s>karma</s> and <s>jñāna</s>]" —
Section 4.362

children.text:
kiṃ punar brahma jijñāsitavyam ity apekṣāyāṃ lakṣaṇam uktaṃ "janmādy asya
          yataḥ" iti/ janmādīti sṛṣtisthitipralayam/ tadguṇasaṃvijñāno bahuvrīhiḥ/
          asyācintyavividhavicitraracanasya
          niyatadeśakālabhogabrahmādistambaparyantakṣetrajñamiśrasya jagato yato yasmāt sarveśvarān
          nikhilaheyapratyanīkasvarūpāt satyasaṃkalpādyanavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇāt
          sarvajñāt sarvaśakteḥ puṃsaḥ sṛṣṭisthitipralayāḥ pravartanta iti sūtrārthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, when the question arises, 'What then is <s>Brahman</s> that is to be inquired into?' — the defining characteristic is stated: 'That from which the origination [and so on] of this [universe arises].' 'Origination and so on' means creation, maintenance, and dissolution. This is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound qualifying that [<s>Brahman</s>]. The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: of this universe — of inconceivable, manifold, and wonderful construction, comprising the individual souls (<s>kṣetrajñas</s>) mixed [with matter] from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, with determined places, times, and enjoyments — from the supreme Lord (<s>Sarveśvara</s>), whose essential nature is opposed to all that is to be rejected, endowed with innumerable auspicious qualities of unsurpassable excellence such as infallible will (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>) and the rest, omniscient and omnipotent — from that Person, creation, maintenance, and dissolution proceed.

children.text:
itthaṃbhūte brahmaṇi kiṃ pramāṇam iti jijñāsāyāṃ śāstram eva pramāṇam ity uktaṃ
          śāstrayonitvāt iti/ śāstraṃ yoniḥ kāraṇaṃ pramāṇaṃ yasya tac chāstrayoni/ tasya bhāvas
          tattvaṃ tasmāt/ brahmajñānakāraṇatvāc chāstrasya tadyonitvaṃ brahmaṇa ity arthaḥ/ na ca
          brahmaṇaḥ pramāṇāntaragamyatvaṃ śaṅkituṃ śakyam/ atīndriyatvena pratyakṣasya tatra
          pravṛttyanupapatteḥ/ nāpi mahārṇavādikaṃ sakartṛkaṃ kāryatvād ghaṭavad ity anumānam/ tasya
          pūtikūṣmāṇḍāyamānatvāt/ tallakṣaṇaṃ brahma "yato vā imāni bhūtāni" ityādivākyaṃ
          pratipādayatīti sthitam/
children.translated_text: When the question arises, 'What is the means of knowledge regarding <s>Brahman</s> of such a nature?' — it is stated that scripture alone is the means of knowledge, by [the sūtra]: 'Because [<s>Brahman</s>] is the source of scripture' (<s>śāstrayonitvāt</s>). That of which scripture is the source (<s>yoni</s>), i.e., the cause, i.e., the means of knowledge — is <s>śāstrayoni</s>; its nature is that [quality]; from that. The meaning is: because scripture is the cause of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> has scripture as its source. Nor can it be suspected that <s>Brahman</s> is knowable through another means of knowledge. Because, being beyond the senses (<s>atīndriya</s>), direct perception cannot operate there. Nor [is valid] the inference: 'The great ocean and the like have a maker, because of being effects, like a pot' — because that [inference] has turned into a rotten gourd [i.e., is worthless]. It is established that the Vedic sentence 'From which indeed these beings [are born]' and the like conveys <s>Brahman</s> of that nature.

children.text:
yady api brahma pramāṇāntaragocaratāṃ nāvatarati tathāpi pravṛttinivṛttiparatvābhāve
          siddharūpaṃ brahma na śāstraṃ pratipādayituṃ prabhavatīty etatparyanuyogaparihārāyoktaṃ:
          tat tu samanvayāt iti/ tuśabdaḥ prasaktāśaṅkāvyāvṛttyarthaḥ/ tacchāstrapramāṇakatvaṃ
          brahmaṇaḥ saṃbhavaty eva/ kutaḥ/ samanvayāt/ paramapuruṣārthabhūtasyaiva brahmaṇo
          ’bhidheyatayānvayād ity arthaḥ/ na ca pravṛttinivṛttyor anyataravirahiṇaḥ
          prayojanaśūnyatvam/ svarūpapareṣv api putras te jāto nāyaṃ sarpa ityādiṣu
          harṣaprāptibhayanivṛttirūpaprayojanavattvaṃ dṛṣṭam eveti na kiṃcid anupapannam/ diṅmātram
          atra pradarśitam/ vistaras tv ākarād evāvagantavya iti vistarabhīruṇodāsyata iti sarvam
          anākulam//
children.translated_text: Although <s>Brahman</s> does not fall within the scope of other means of knowledge, nevertheless, in the absence of [scripture] being concerned with injunction and prohibition, [it might be thought that] scripture is not able to convey <s>Brahman</s>, which is of an already established nature. To counter this objection, it is stated: 'But that, because of consistency' (<s>tat tu samanvayāt</s>). The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for the purpose of removing the suspected doubt. The scripture-means-of-knowledge status of <s>Brahman</s> is indeed possible. Why? Because of consistency — meaning, because <s>Brahman</s>, which is itself the supreme goal of human existence, is consistently presented [throughout the <s>Vedānta</s> texts] as the thing to be conveyed. Nor is there purposelessness in [statements] devoid of either injunction or prohibition, because even in [sentences] concerned with [conveying] the nature of [established] things — such as 'A son is born to you!' and 'This is not a snake!' — purposefulness in the form of the attainment of joy and the removal of fear is indeed observed. Thus nothing is problematic. Only the direction has been indicated here; the elaboration should be understood from the source-text itself — thus it has been set aside by one averse to prolixity. All is clear.
Thus [ends] the <s>Rāmānuja</s> system in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Now, the <s>Pūrṇaprajña</s> (Madhva) system. //5//

children.text:
tad etad rāmānujamataṃ
          jīvāṇutvadāsatvavedāpauruṣeyatvasiddhārthabodhakatvasvataḥpramāṇatva-pramāṇatritvapañcarātropajīvyatvaprapañcabhedasatyatvādisāmye
          'pi parasparaviruddhabhedādipakṣatrayakakṣīkāreṇa kṣapaṇakapakṣanikṣiptam ity upekṣamāṇaḥ
          sa ātmā tat tvam asi ityādivedāntavākyajātasya bhaṅgyantareṇārthāntaraparatvam upapādya
          brahmamīmāṃsāvivaraṇavyājenānandatīrthaḥ prasthānāntaram āsthiṣata/
children.translated_text: Now, this <s>Rāmānuja</s> doctrine — despite the commonality regarding the atomicity of the individual soul, the servanthood [of the soul to God], the non-human authorship of the <s>Vedas</s>, [scripture's capacity for] conveying established realities, self-validity [of knowledge], the threefold means of knowledge, the reliance on the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, and the reality of the manifold world — <s>Ānandatīrtha</s>, regarding it as having been cast into the camp of the Jain position on account of its embracing mutually contradictory positions such as [the doctrine of] difference [combined with non-difference], established an alternative school under the guise of a commentary on the <s>Brahmamīmāṃsā</s>, having demonstrated that the body of <s>Vedānta</s> statements such as 'That Self, that thou art' (<s>tat tvam asi</s>) and the like have a different meaning through an alternative interpretation.
For in his doctrine, reality (<s>tattva</s>) is twofold, through the division of independent (<s>svatantra</s>) and dependent (<s>paratantra</s>).
As stated in the <s>Tattvaviveka</s>:

children.text: svatantraṃ paratantraṃ ca dvividhaṃ tattvam iṣyate/
children.translated_text: 'Reality is regarded as twofold: independent and dependent.
The independent is the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from all defects, possessed of all auspicious qualities.' Thus.

children.text:
nanu sajātīyavijātīyasvagatanānātvaśūnyaṃ brahmatattvam iti pratipādakeṣu vedānteṣu
          jāgarūkeṣu katham aśeṣasadguṇatvaṃ tasya kathyata iti cen
children.translated_text: Now, if [one asks]: 'Given that the <s>Vedānta</s> texts, which teach that <s>Brahman</s>-reality is devoid of homogeneous, heterogeneous, and internal plurality, are authoritative — how can the possession of all auspicious qualities be attributed to it?'

children.text:
maivam/ bhedapramāpakabahupramāṇavirodhena teṣāṃ tatra prāmāṇyānupapatteḥ/ tathā hi —
          pratyakṣaṃ tāvad idam asmād bhinnam iti nīlapītāder bhedam adhyakṣayati/
children.translated_text: Do not say so! Because of the contradiction with the many means of knowledge that establish difference, their authority in that regard is not tenable. For thus — direct perception first: it directly perceives the difference of blue, yellow, and the like [from each other] as 'This is different from that.'

children.text:
atha manyethāḥ — kiṃ pratyakṣaṃ bhedam evāvagāhate kiṃ vā dharmipratiyogighaṭitam/ na
          prathamaḥ/ dharmipratiyogipratipattim antareṇa tatsāpekṣasya bhedasyāśakyādhyavasāyatvāt/
          dvitīye 'pi dharmipratiyogigrahaṇapuraḥsaraṃ bhedagrahaṇam atha vā yugapat
          tatsarvagrahaṇam/ na pūrvaḥ/ buddher viramya vyāpārābhāvāt/ anyonyāśrayaprasaṅgāc ca/ nāpi
          caramaḥ/ kāryakāraṇabuddhyor yaugapadyābhāvāt/ dharmipratītir hi bhedapratyayasya kāraṇam/
          evaṃ pratiyogipratītir api/ saṃnihite 'pi dharmiṇi vyavahitapratiyogijñānam antareṇa
          bhedasyājñātatvenānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvāvagamāt/ tasmān na bhedapratyakṣaṃ
          suprasaram iti cet —
children.translated_text: Now, if you think: Does direct perception apprehend difference alone, or [does it apprehend it] as constituted by the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) and the counter-positive (<s>pratiyogin</s>)? Not the first — because without the apprehension of the property-bearer and the counter-positive, difference, which is dependent on those, cannot be determined. In the second case too, [the question arises:] is the apprehension of difference preceded by the grasping of the property-bearer and counter-positive, or is the grasping of all of them simultaneous? Not the former — because of the absence of the intellect's operation after ceasing [one cognition to begin another], and because of the undesirable consequence of mutual dependence. Nor the latter — because there is no simultaneity of cause-cognition and effect-cognition, for the cognition of the property-bearer is the cause of the cognition of difference; likewise, the cognition of the counter-positive. [This is known] because, even when the property-bearer is present, without the knowledge of the intervening counter-positive, difference is unknown — and this [causal relation] is ascertained through positive and negative concomitance. Therefore, the perception of difference has no scope — if [one argues] thus,

children.text:
kiṃ vastusvarūpabhedavādinaṃ pratīmāni dūṣaṇāny udghuṣyante kiṃ vā dharmabhedavādinaṃ
          prati/ prathame corāparādhān māṇḍavyanigrahanyāyāpātaḥ/ bhavadabhidhīyamānadūṣaṇānāṃ
          tadaviṣayatvāt/ nanu vastusvarūpasyaiva bhedatve pratiyogisāpekṣatvaṃ na ghaṭate ghaṭavat/
          pratiyogisāpekṣa eva sarvatra bhedaḥ prathata iti cen na/ prathamaṃ sarvato vilakṣaṇatayā
          vastusvarūpe jñāyamāne pratiyogyapekṣayā viśiṣṭavyavahāropapatteḥ/ tathā hi/
          parimāṇaghaṭitaṃ vastusvarūpaṃ prathamam avagamyate/ paścāt pratiyogiviśeṣāpekṣayā hrasvaṃ
          dīrgham iti tad eva viśiṣya vyavahārabhājanaṃ bhavati/ tad uktaṃ viṣṇutattvanirṇaye —
children.translated_text: are these objections raised against one who holds the difference of the essential nature of things, or against one who holds the difference of properties? In the first case, there would be the error of punishing <s>Māṇḍavya</s> for the crime of a thief — because the stated objections do not pertain to that [position]. But [you say:] 'If difference belongs to the essential nature of the thing itself, the dependence on a counter-positive does not work, as with a pot.' [We reply:] If [it is said that] difference everywhere shines forth only as dependent on a counter-positive — no! Because when the essential nature of a thing, as entirely distinct [from all else], is first known, specific conventional usage depending on the counter-positive is then possible. For thus: the essential nature of a thing, constituted by its measure, is first apprehended; subsequently, depending on the specific counter-positive, that very [thing] is conventionally designated as 'short' or 'long.' This is stated in the <s>Viṣṇutattvanirṇaya</s>:

children.text:
na ca viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatayā bhedasiddhiḥ/ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaś ca bhedāpekṣaḥ/
          dharmipratiyogyapekṣayā bhedasiddhiḥ/ bhedāpekṣaṃ ca dharmipratiyogitvam ity
          anyonyāśrayatayā bhedasyāyuktiḥ/ padārthasvarūpatvād bhedasya —
children.translated_text: 'Nor is the establishment of difference through the qualifier-qualified relation [valid]; and the qualifier-qualified relation itself depends on difference. The establishment of difference depends on the property-bearer and counter-positive; and the property-bearer-counter-positive status itself depends on difference — thus, through mutual dependence, difference is untenable. [But this objection fails] because difference is the essential nature of things' —

children.text:
ityādinā/ ata eva gavārthino gavayadarśanān na pravartante gośabdaṃ ca na smaranti/ na ca
          nīrakṣīrādau svarūpe gṛhyamāṇe bhedapratibhāso 'pi syād iti bhaṇanīyam/
          samānābhihārādipratibandhakabalād bhedabhānavyavahārābhāvopapatteḥ/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: and so on. For this very reason, those desiring a cow do not proceed [to action] from seeing a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox), nor do they remember the word 'cow.' Nor should it be said that when the essential nature [of things like] water and milk is grasped, there would also be an appearance of difference [which there isn't] — because the absence of the conventional usage of difference-appearance is accounted for by the force of obstacles such as similarity of appearance and the like. As stated:
'Due to excessive distance, excessive proximity, defect of the sense-faculty, instability of the mind,

children.text: saukṣmyād vyavadhānād abhibhavāt samānābhihārāc ca// iti/
children.translated_text: subtlety, interposition, overshadowing, and similarity of appearance —' thus.

children.text:
atidūrād giriśikharavartitarvādau, atisāmīpyāl locanāñjanādau, indriyaghātād vidyudādau,
          manonavasthānāt kāmādyupaplutamanaskasya sphītālokavartini ghaṭādau, saukṣmyāt
          paramāṇvādau vyavadhānāt kuḍyādyantarhite abhibhavād divā pradīpaprabhādau samānābhihārān
          nīrakṣīrādau yathāvad grahaṇaṃ nāstīty arthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Due to excessive distance, [as with] a tree situated on a mountain-peak; due to excessive proximity, [as with] eye-ointment; due to defect of the sense-faculty, [as with] lightning and the like; due to instability of mind, [as with] a pot in bright light for one whose mind is disturbed by desire and the like; due to subtlety, [as with] atoms and the like; due to interposition, [as with that which is] hidden behind a wall and the like; due to overshadowing, [as with] lamplight during the day; due to similarity of appearance, [as with] water and milk — proper apprehension does not occur. That is the meaning.

children.text:
bhavatu vā dharmabhedavādas tathāpi na kaścid doṣaḥ/ dharmipratiyogigrahaṇe sati paścāt
          tadghaṭitabhedagrahaṇopapatteḥ/ na ca parasparāśrayaprasaṅgaḥ/ parān anapekṣya
          prabhedaśālino vastuno grahaṇe sati dharmabhedabhānasaṃbhavāt/ na ca dharmabhedavāde tasya
          tasya bhedasya bhedāntarabhedyatvenānavasthā duravasthā syād ity āstheyam/
          bhedāntaraprasaktau mūlābhāvāt/ bhedabhedinau bhinnāv iti vyavahārādarśanāt/ na
          caikabhedabalenānyabhedānumānam/ dṛṣṭāntabhedāvighātenotthāne doṣābhāvāt/ so 'yaṃ
          piṇyākayācanārthaṃ gatasya khārikātailadātṛtvābhyupagama iva/ dṛṣṭāntabhedavimarde tv
          anutthānam eva/ na hi varavighātāya kanyodvāhaḥ/ tasmān mūlakṣayābhāvād anavasthā na
          doṣāya/
children.translated_text: Or, let the doctrine of property-difference stand; even so, there is no fault. Because, after the grasping of the property-bearer and counter-positive, the subsequent grasping of difference constituted by them is possible. And there is no undesirable consequence of mutual dependence — because, when a thing endowed with distinctions is grasped without reference to others, the appearance of property-difference is possible. Nor should it be maintained that, on the doctrine of property-difference, there would be a vicious infinite regress through each difference being differentiated by another difference. Because, when another difference is entailed, the foundation [i.e., the first difference] is not lost — since the conventional usage 'difference and differentiand are different' is not observed. And inference of another difference is not [made] by the force of one difference. Because, when the example-difference is not vitiated, there is no fault in its arising. This is like one who, having gone to beg for oil-cake, [is offered and] accepts a <s>khārikā</s>-measure of oil. But when the example-difference is challenged, [the inference] simply does not arise — for a wedding is not for the purpose of obstructing the bridegroom. Therefore, since the foundation is not destroyed, the infinite regress is not a fault.

children.text:
anumānenāpi bhedo 'vasīyate/ parameśvaro jīvād bhinnaḥ/ taṃ prati sevyatvāt/ yo yaṃ prati
          sevyaḥ sa tasmād bhinnaḥ/ yathā bhṛtyād rājā/ na hi sukhaṃ me syād duḥkhaṃ me na manāg api
          — iti puruṣārtham arthayamānāḥ puruṣāḥ sthapatipadaṃ kāmayamānāḥ satkārabhājo bhaveyuḥ/
          pratyuta sarvānarthabhājanaṃ bhavanti/ yaḥ svasyātmano hīnatvaṃ parasya guṇotkarṣaṃ ca
          kathayati sa stutyaḥ prītaḥ stāvakasya tasyābhīṣṭaṃ prayacchati/
children.translated_text: Difference is also ascertained through inference. The supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) is different from the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), because he is to be served by that [soul]. Whoever is to be served by someone is different from that one, like a king from a servant. For persons who desire the goal of human life, thinking 'Let there be happiness for me, let there not be the slightest suffering for me' — if they desire the position of master, they would not become recipients of honor. On the contrary, they become receptacles of all misfortune. One who declares the inferiority of one's own self and the superiority of qualities of another — he is praiseworthy; [the Lord], pleased, grants the desired [boon] to that praiser.
Thus it is said:

children.text: ghātayanti hi rājāno rājāham iti vādinaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Kings indeed strike down those who claim "I am king";

children.text: dadaty akhilam iṣṭaṃ ca svaguṇotkarṣavādinām// iti/
children.translated_text: but they give everything desired to those who declare the superiority of [the king's] qualities.' Thus.

children.text:
evaṃ ca parameśvarābhedatṛṣṇayā viṣṇor guṇotkarṣasya mṛgatṛṣṇikāsamatvābhidhānaṃ
          vipulakadalīphalalipsayā jihvācchedanam anusarati/ etādṛśaviṣṇuvidveṣaṇād
          andhatamasapraveśaprasaṅgāt/ tad etat pratipāditaṃ madhyamandireṇa
          mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaye —
children.translated_text: And thus, the declaration that, through the thirst for non-difference from the supreme Lord, the superiority of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s qualities is [reduced to] the level of a mirage — follows [the pattern of] cutting one's tongue out of desire for the fruit of a large plantain. Because from such enmity toward <s>Viṣṇu</s>, there would be the undesirable consequence of entering into blinding darkness. This has been demonstrated by <s>Madhyamandira</s> (<s>Madhva</s>) in the <s>Mahābhārata-tātparya-nirṇaya</s>:
'The <s>Daityas</s>, who have enmity from beginningless time, [their] enmity toward <s>Viṣṇu</s> has increased;

children.text: tamasy andhe pātayati daityān ante viniścayāt// iti/
children.translated_text: [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] assuredly casts the <s>Daityas</s> into blind darkness in the end.' Thus.

children.text:
sā ca sevā — aṅkananāmakaraṇabhajanabhedāt trividhā/ tatrāṅkanaṃ nārāyaṇāyudhādīnāṃ
          tadrūpasmaraṇārtham apekṣitārthasiddhyarthaṃ ca/ tathā ca śākalyasaṃhitāpariśiṣṭam —
children.translated_text: And that service is threefold, through the division of branding (<s>aṅkana</s>), naming (<s>nāmakaraṇa</s>), and worship (<s>bhajana</s>). Therein, branding is [the marking with] the weapons of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like, for the purpose of remembering his form and for the accomplishment of desired goals. And thus the appendix of the <s>Śākala Saṃhitā</s>:
'The person who bears the discus (<s>cakra</s>), heated [and branded],
the strength of the gods, of the immortal <s>Viṣṇu</s> —
he goes to heaven, having shaken off sins,
which the dispassionate sages enter.
By the arm on which that <s>Sudarśana</s> is held,
by which the gods have proceeded, to that they come.
Those <s>Manus</s>, marked by whom, spread forth the creation of the world —
the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> bear that.',

children.text: tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ yena gacchanti lāñchitāḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Those who are marked go to that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>;

children.text: urukramasya cihnair aṅkitā loke subhagā bhavāmaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: marked with the signs of <s>Urukrama</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), may we become fortunate in the world.' Thus.
and who bear [the marks] reach

children.text: / iti taittirīyakopaniṣac ca/ sthānaviśeṣaś cāgneyapurāṇe darśitaḥ —
children.translated_text: that' — thus the <s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> also [states]. And the specific location [for branding] has been shown in the <s>Āgneya Purāṇa</s>:
'One whose body is not heated does not attain that; only those who are heated

children.text: dakṣiṇe tu kare vipro bibhṛyāc ca sudarśanam/
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should bear the <s>Sudarśana</s> [discus] on the right hand,

children.text: savyena śaṅkhaṃ bibhṛyād iti brahmavido viduḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: and the conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>) on the left — thus the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> know.' Thus.
Elsewhere, a specific <s>mantra</s> for bearing the discus has also been shown:
'O <s>Sudarśana</s>, of great flame, equal in radiance to ten million suns!

children.text: ajñānāndhasya me nityaṃ viṣṇor mārgaṃ pradarśaya//
children.translated_text: For me, who is blind with ignorance, always show the path of <s>Viṣṇu</s>!

children.text: tvaṃ purā sāgarotpanno viṣṇunā vidhṛtaḥ kare/
children.translated_text: You were formerly born from the ocean, held in hand by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: namitaḥ sarvadevaiś ca pāñcajanya namo 'stu te// iti/
children.translated_text: saluted by all the gods — O <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, salutations to you!' Thus.

children.text: nāmakaraṇaṃ putrādīnāṃ keśavādināmnā vyavahāraḥ sarvadā tannāmānusmaraṇārtham/
children.translated_text: The naming ceremony (<s>nāmakaraṇa</s>) is the practice of naming sons and others with names such as <s>Keśava</s> and the like, for the purpose of constant remembrance of His names.
reference marker

children.text:
bhajanaṃ daśavidhaṃ vācā satyaṃ hitaṃ priyaṃ svādhyāyaḥ kāyena dānaṃ paritrāṇaṃ
          parirakṣaṇaṃ manasā dayā spṛhā śraddhā ceti/ atraikaikaṃ niṣpādya nārāyaṇe samarpaṇaṃ
          bhajanam/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: Worship (<s>bhajana</s>) is tenfold: by speech — truthfulness, beneficence, pleasantness, and self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>); by body — giving (<s>dāna</s>), protection (<s>paritrāṇa</s>), and safeguarding (<s>parirakṣaṇa</s>); by mind — compassion (<s>dayā</s>), longing (<s>spṛhā</s>), and faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). Here, having accomplished each one, offering it to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is worship. As stated —

children.text: aṅkanaṃ nāmakaraṇaṃ bhajanaṃ daśadhā ca tat/ iti/
children.translated_text: Branding (<s>aṅkana</s>), naming (<s>nāmakaraṇa</s>), and worship (<s>bhajana</s>) which is tenfold — thus.
In this way, difference is to be inferred also through knowability and the like.
reference marker

children.text:
tathā śrutyāpi bhedo 'vagantavyaḥ/ satyam enam anu viśve madanti rātiṃ devasya gṛṇato
          maghonaḥ/ satyaḥ so asya mahimā gṛṇe śavo yajñeṣu viprarājye/ satya ātmā satyo jīvaḥ
          satyaṃ bhidā satyaṃ bhidā satyaṃ bhidā maivāruvaṇyo maivāruvaṇyo maivāruvaṇya iti
          mokṣānandabhedapratipādakaśrutibhyaḥ/
children.translated_text: Likewise, difference is to be understood from <s>śruti</s> as well. 'Truly all beings rejoice in him; the bounty of the praiseworthy god <s>Maghon</s> (Indra). True is that greatness of his, I praise the mighty one, among the sacrifices, in the sovereignty of the wise.' 'True is the <s>ātman</s>, true is the <s>jīva</s>, true is difference, true is difference, true is difference — let there be no weeping, let there be no weeping, let there be no weeping' — from such <s>śrutis</s> that establish difference even in the bliss of liberation.

children.text: idaṃ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ/
children.translated_text: Having resorted to this knowledge, they have attained similarity of nature with Me;

children.text: sarge 'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca//
children.translated_text: even at the time of creation they are not born, nor do they suffer at the time of dissolution.

children.text:
jagadvyāpāravarjam/ prakaraṇād asaṃnihitatvāc ca ityādibhyaś ca/ na ca brahma veda
          brahmaiva bhavati iti śrutibalāj jīvasya pāramaiśvaryaṃ śakyaśaṅkam/
children.translated_text: Except for the activities of the world. From [the principle of] context, non-proximity, and so on. Nor can supreme lordship of the <s>jīva</s> be suspected on the strength of the <s>śruti</s> 'one who knows <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself.'

children.text: saṃpūjya brāhmaṇaṃ bhaktyā śūdro 'pi brāhmaṇo bhavet/
children.translated_text: Even a <s>śūdra</s>, by devoutly worshipping a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, becomes a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;
just as in that case, the meaning is that he becomes 'expanded' (<s>bṛṃhita</s>) — this being the intended sense.
reference marker
Now, [the objection:]

children.text: prapañco yadi vidyeta nivarteta na saṃśayaḥ/
children.translated_text: If the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) were to exist, it would certainly cease — there is no doubt;
all this duality is mere <s>māyā</s> (illusion); non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) alone is the ultimate reality.

children.text: iti vacanād dvaitasya kalpitatvam avagamyata iti cet —
children.translated_text: From this statement, it is understood that duality is merely imagined — if so, [we reply:]

children.text:
satyam/ bhāvam anabhisaṃdhāyābhidhānāt/ tathā hi yady ayam utpadyeta tarhi nivarteta na
          saṃśayaḥ/ tasmād anādir evāyaṃ prakṛṣṭaḥ pañcavidho bhedaprapañcaḥ/ na cāyam avidyamānaḥ/
          māyāmātratvāt/ māyeti bhagavadicchocyate/
children.translated_text: True. Because it is stated without intending [actual] existence. For thus: if this were produced, then it would certainly cease — there is no doubt. Therefore, this fivefold manifold of difference is beginningless and eminent. And it is not non-existent. Because it is mere <s>māyā</s>. By <s>māyā</s> is meant the will (<s>icchā</s>) of the Lord.
reference marker
Great <s>māyā</s>, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), destiny (<s>niyati</s>), the enchantress (<s>mohinī</s>),
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) — O Infinite One, Your will is called [by these names].
<s>Prakṛti</s> because of excellent making; <s>vāsanā</s> because it causes to dwell;

children.text: a ity ukto haris tasya māyāvidyeti saṃjñitā//
children.translated_text: 'a' denotes <s>Hari</s>, whose [power] is called <s>māyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: māyety uktā prakṛṣṭatvāt prakṛṣṭe hi mayābhidhā/
children.translated_text: Called <s>māyā</s> because of eminence, for in eminence the term <s>maya</s> is used;

children.text: viṣṇoḥ prajñaptir evaikā śabdair etair udīryate//
children.translated_text: the single designation of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is expressed by these words.

children.text: prajñaptirūpo hi hariḥ sā ca svānandalakṣaṇā//
children.translated_text: For <s>Hari</s> is of the nature of designation (<s>prajñapti</s>), and that is characterized by His own bliss.

children.text:
ityādivacananicayaprāmāṇyabalāt/ saiva prajñā mānatrāṇakartrī ca yasya tan māyāmātram/
          tataś ca parameśvareṇa jñātatvād rakṣitatvāc ca na dvaitaṃ bhrāntikalpitam/ na hīśvare
          sarvasya bhrāntiḥ saṃbhavati/ viśeṣādarśananibandhanatvād bhrānteḥ/ tarhi tadvyapadeśaḥ
          katham ity atrottaram advaitaṃ paramārthata iti/ paramārthata iti paramārthāpekṣayā/ tena
          sarvasmād uttamasya viṣṇutattvasya samābhyadhikaśūnyatvam uktaṃ bhavati/ tathā ca paramā
          śrutiḥ —
children.translated_text: By the force of the authority of such a collection of statements. That whose <s>māyā</s> is 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>) means: she who is that very wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is also the protector and maker. Therefore, since duality is known and protected by the Supreme Lord, it is not imagined through delusion. For delusion is impossible in the Lord of all. Because delusion depends on non-perception of distinctions. Then how is that designation [of 'mere illusion'] to be understood? The answer is: '<s>advaita</s> (non-duality) in the ultimate sense' (<s>paramārthataḥ</s>). '<s>Paramārthataḥ</s>' means 'with reference to the ultimate reality.' Thereby it is stated that the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-principle, being the highest of all, is devoid of equal or superior. And the supreme <s>śruti</s> states —
reference marker
The difference between <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord), and the difference between insentient matter (<s>jaḍa</s>) and <s>Īśvara</s>,
the mutual difference among <s>jīvas</s>, and the difference between insentient matter and <s>jīvas</s>,

children.text: mithaś ca jaḍabhedo yaḥ prapañco bhedapañcakaḥ/
children.translated_text: and the mutual difference among insentient things — the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) is this fivefold difference.

children.text: so 'yaṃ satyo' py anādiś ca sādiś cen nāśam āpnuyāt//
children.translated_text: This is real and beginningless; if it had a beginning, it would come to destruction.

children.text: na ca nāśaṃ prayāty eṣa na cāsau bhrāntikalpitaḥ/
children.translated_text: But it does not go to destruction, nor is it imagined through delusion;

children.text: kalpitaś cen nivarteta na cāsau vinivartate//
children.translated_text: if it were imagined, it would cease — but it does not cease.

children.text: dvaitaṃ na vidyata iti tasmād ajñānināṃ matam/
children.translated_text: That 'duality does not exist' — this is the view of the ignorant;

children.text: mataṃ hi jñāninām etan mitaṃ trātaṃ hi viṣṇunā//
children.translated_text: but the view of the wise is: this is 'measured' (<s>mita</s>) and 'protected' (<s>trāta</s>) by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tasmān mātram iti proktaṃ paramo harir eva tu/ ityādi/
children.translated_text: Therefore it is called 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>); the supreme [reality] is <s>Hari</s> alone. And so on.

children.text: tasmād viṣṇoḥ sarvotkarṣa eva tātparyaṃ sarvāgamānām/
children.translated_text: Therefore, the purport of all scriptures (<s>āgamas</s>) is the supreme excellence of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.
reference marker
With this very intention, the Lord has stated —

children.text: dvāv imau puruṣau loke kṣaraś cākṣara eva ca/
children.translated_text: There are two <s>puruṣas</s> (beings) in the world: the perishable (<s>kṣara</s>) and the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>);
the perishable comprises all beings; the unchanging (<s>kūṭastha</s>) is called the imperishable.

children.text: uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛtaḥ/
children.translated_text: But the Supreme Being (<s>Puruṣa</s>) is another, called the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>),

children.text: yo lokatrayam āviśya bibharty avyaya īśvaraḥ//
children.translated_text: who, pervading the three worlds, sustains them — the imperishable Lord.

children.text: yasmāt kṣaram atīto 'ham akṣarād api cottamaḥ/
children.translated_text: Since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable,

children.text: ato 'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ//
children.translated_text: therefore I am celebrated in the world and in the <s>Veda</s> as <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Being).

children.text: yo mām evam asaṃmūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam/
children.translated_text: He who, undeluded, thus knows Me as <s>Puruṣottama</s>,

children.text: sa sarvavid bhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena bhārata//
children.translated_text: he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being, O <s>Bhārata</s>.

children.text: iti guhyatamaṃ śāstram idam uktaṃ mayānagha/
children.translated_text: This most secret teaching (<s>śāstra</s>) has been declared by Me, O sinless one;

children.text: etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛtakṛtyaś ca bhārata// iti/
children.translated_text: understanding this, one becomes wise and fulfilled in all duties, O <s>Bhārata</s>. Thus.
reference marker
In the <s>Mahāvarāha</s> [Purāṇa] also —

children.text: mukhyaṃ ca sarvavedānāṃ tātparyaṃ śrīpatau pare/
children.translated_text: The chief purport of all the <s>Vedas</s> is in the supreme Lord of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Śrīpati</s>);

children.text: utkarṣe tu tadanyatra tātparyaṃ syād avāntaram// iti/
children.translated_text: the purport regarding the excellence of anything other than Him is secondary. Thus.

children.text: yuktaṃ ca viṣṇoḥ sarvotkarṣe mahātātparyam/ mokṣo hi sarvapuruṣārthottamaḥ/
children.translated_text: And it is fitting that the greatest purport lies in the supreme excellence of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. For <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is the highest of all human goals (<s>puruṣārthas</s>).

children.text: dharmārthakāmāḥ sarve 'pi na nityā mokṣa eva hi/
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (desire) — all these are not eternal; only <s>mokṣa</s> indeed

children.text: nityas tasmāt tadarthāya yateta matimān naraḥ//
children.translated_text: is eternal. Therefore, a wise person should strive for that purpose.

children.text: iti bhāllaveyaśruteḥ/ mokṣaś ca viṣṇuprasādam antareṇa na labhyate/
children.translated_text: Thus from the <s>Bhāllaveyaśruti</s>. And <s>mokṣa</s> cannot be obtained without the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: yasya prasādāt paramārtirūpād asmāt saṃsārān mucyate nāpareṇa/
children.translated_text: By whose grace one is freed from this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence), which is the form of supreme suffering — by no other [means];

children.text: nārāyaṇo 'sau paramo vicintyo mumukṣubhiḥ karmapāśād amuṣmāt//
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is to be contemplated as supreme by those desiring liberation from the bondage of <s>karma</s>.
Thus from the <s>Nārāyaṇaśruti</s>.
When He is pleased, what here is unattainable?
<s>Dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> are trivial compared to that;
from the infinite wish-fulfilling tree that is <s>Brahman</s>, which has been resorted to,
without doubt they attain the fruit of liberation (<s>mukti</s>).

children.text: iti viṣṇupurāṇokteś ca/ prasādaś ca guṇotkarṣajñānād eva nābhedajñānād ity uktam/
children.translated_text: Thus from the statement in the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>. And grace comes from knowledge of the excellence of His qualities alone, not from knowledge of non-difference — as stated.
reference marker

children.text: na ca tat tvam asyāditādātmyavyākopaḥ/ śrutitātparyāparijñānavijṛmbhaṇāt/
children.translated_text: Nor is there any contradiction with the identity statements such as 'tat tvam asi' ('That thou art'). Because of the failure to understand the purport of the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: āha nityaparokṣaṃ tu tacchabdo hy aviśeṣataḥ/
children.translated_text: He says: 'tat' ('That') refers to what is eternally beyond perception; the word 'tat' is without distinction;

children.text: tvaṃśabdaś cāparokṣārthaṃ tayor aikyaṃ kathaṃ bhavet//
children.translated_text: and the word 'tvam' ('thou') refers to what is directly perceived — how can there be identity of the two?

children.text: ādityo yūpa itivat sādṛśyārthā tu sā śrutiḥ/ iti/
children.translated_text: 'The sun is the sacrificial post' — like this, that <s>śruti</s> is intended to express similarity. Thus.
And the supreme <s>śruti</s> states —

children.text: jīvasya paramaikyaṃ tu buddhisārūpyam eva tu/
children.translated_text: The supreme oneness of the <s>jīva</s> is indeed similarity of intellect,
or dwelling in the same place — that [oneness] is with reference to the state of manifestation.
There is no identity of essential nature, even for the liberated soul, because of difference in form;
independence and fullness [belong to the Lord], while smallness and dependence are the different forms [of the soul]. Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
atha vā tat tvam asīty atra sa evātmā svātantryādiguṇopetatvāt/ atat tvam asi tvaṃ tan na
          bhavasi tadrahitatvād ity ekatvam atiśayena nirākṛtam/ tad āha —
children.translated_text: Alternatively, in 'tat tvam asi' (That thou art), [the meaning is:] He alone is the Self, because of possessing qualities such as independence. 'Atat tvam asi' — 'thou art not That' — because of being devoid of those [qualities]. Thus identity has been emphatically refuted. He says —

children.text: atat tvam iti vā chedas tenaikyaṃ sunirākṛtam/ iti/
children.translated_text: 'Atat tvam' — or by this alternative analysis, identity is thoroughly refuted. Thus.

children.text:
tasmād dṛṣṭāntanavake 'pi sa yathā śakuniḥ sūtreṇa prabaddhaḥ ityādinā bheda eva
          dṛṣṭāntābhidhānān nāyam abhedopadeśa iti tattvavādarahasyam/
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the new set of illustrations, since the illustration 'just as a bird bound by a string' and so on specifically expresses difference alone, this is not a teaching of non-difference — this is the secret of the <s>Tattvavāda</s> (Dvaita doctrine).
reference marker
And the <s>Mahopaniṣad</s> [states] —

children.text: yathā pakṣī ca sūtraṃ ca nānāvṛkṣarasā yathā/
children.translated_text: Just as a bird and its string, just as the saps of different trees,

children.text: yathā nadyaḥ samudrāś ca yathā jīvamahīruhau//
children.translated_text: just as rivers and oceans, just as a <s>jīva</s> and a great tree,

children.text: yathāṇimā ca dhānā ca śuddhodalavaṇe yathā/
children.translated_text: just as an atom and a grain, just as pure water and salt,

children.text: corāpahāryau ca yathā yathā puṃviṣayāv api//
children.translated_text: just as two things not stolen by a thief, and just as a male and his objects,

children.text: yathājño jīvasaṃghaś ca prāṇādeś ca niyāmakaḥ/
children.translated_text: just as an ignorant person and the community of souls, and the controller of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest —
so the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> are distinct, always of different nature.

children.text: tathāpi sūkṣmarūpatvān na jīvāt paramo hariḥ/
children.translated_text: Yet because of His subtle form, the supreme <s>Hari</s> is not [perceived as different] from the <s>jīva</s>;
by those of dull vision, the difference is not seen, even though He is the impeller.

children.text: vailakṣaṇyaṃ tayor jñātvā mucyate badhyate 'nyathā/ iti/
children.translated_text: Knowing the distinction between them, one is liberated; otherwise, one is bound. Thus.

children.text: brahmā śivaḥ surādyāś ca śarīrakṣaraṇāt kṣarāḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the gods and others are perishable (<s>kṣara</s>) because their bodies decay;
<s>Lakṣmī</s> is imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) because her body is imperishable; <s>Hari</s> is beyond her.
By all qualities such as independence, power, knowledge, bliss, and the rest,

children.text: niḥsīmatvena te sarve tadvaśāḥ sarvadaiva ca// iti
children.translated_text: being limitless — they are all forever under His control. Thus.
Knowing <s>Viṣṇu</s> as full of all qualities, one becomes free from <s>saṃsāra</s>,
enjoying bliss free from suffering, eternally rejoicing in His proximity.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the refuge of the liberated, their superior, and their overlord;

children.text: tadvaśā eva te sarve sarvadaiva sa īśvaraḥ// iti ca/
children.translated_text: they are all forever subject to Him — He alone is the Lord. Thus also.
reference marker

children.text:
ekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ ca pradhānatvakāraṇatvādinā yujyate na tu sarvamithyātvena/ na
          hi satyajñānena mithyājñānaṃ saṃbhavati/ yathā pradhānapuruṣāṇāṃ jñānājñānābhyāṃ grāmo
          jñāto 'jñāta ity evamādivyapadeśo dṛṣṭa eva/ yathā ca kāraṇe pitari jñāte jānāty asya
          putram iti/ yathā vā sādṛśyād ekastrījñānād anyastrījñānam iti/ tad eva sādṛśyam atrāpi
          vivakṣitaṃ yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛṇmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syād ityādinā/

anyathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛṇmayaṃ vijñātam ity atraikapiṇḍaśabdau
          vṛthā prasajyeyātām/ mṛdā vijñātam ity etāvataiva vākyasya pūrṇatvāt/ na ca vācārambhaṇaṃ
          vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam ity etat kāryasya mithyātvam ācaṣṭa ity eṣṭavyam/
          vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro yasya tad avikṛtaṃ nityaṃ nāmadheyaṃ mṛttiketyādikam ity etad vacanaṃ
          satyam ity arthasya svīkārāt/ aparathā nāmadheyamitiśabdayor vaiyarthyaṃ prasajyeta/ ato
          na kutrāpi jagato mithyātvasiddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: Otherwise, in 'just as, dear one, by one lump of clay, everything made of clay is known,' the words 'one' and 'lump' would become purposeless — since the sentence would be complete with merely 'by clay it is known.' Nor should one claim that 'the modification is a mere verbal designation; clay alone is the reality' teaches the unreality of effects. Because the accepted meaning is: 'that whose modification is a mere verbal designation — that is unmodified, eternal; the name such as "clay" — this statement is true.' Otherwise, the words 'name' and 'designation' (<s>nāmadheya</s>) would become purposeless. Therefore, nowhere is the unreality of the world established.

And 'by knowing one thing, everything is known' is consistent through [the relation of] principality and causality and the like, not through the unreality of everything. For true knowledge cannot produce false knowledge. Just as in the case of principal persons, by their being known or unknown, the village is said to be 'known' or 'unknown' — such usage is indeed observed. And just as when the father who is the cause is known, one says 'he knows his son.' Or just as from similarity, knowledge of one woman yields knowledge of another woman. That very similarity is intended here too: 'just as, dear one, by one lump of clay, everything made of clay becomes known' and so on.
reference marker

children.text:
kiṃ ca prapañco mithyety atra mithyātvaṃ tathyam atathyaṃ vā/ prathame
          satyādvaitabhaṅgaprasaṅgaḥ/ carame prapañcasatyatvāpātaḥ/
children.translated_text: Moreover, in [the claim] 'the phenomenal world is unreal' — is the unreality true or untrue? In the first case, the doctrine of true non-duality (<s>satyādvaita</s>) is contradicted. In the second case, the reality of the phenomenal world follows.

children.text:
nanv anityatvaṃ nityam anityaṃ vā/ ubhayathāpy anupapattir ity ākṣepavad ayam api
          nityasamajātibhedaḥ syāt/ tad uktaṃ nyāyanirmāṇavedhasā — nityam anityabhāvād anitye
          nityatvopapatter nityasamaḥ iti/ tārkikarakṣāyāṃ ca —
children.translated_text: Now, is impermanence itself permanent or impermanent? In either case there is a fallacy — just like this objection, there is also the [fallacy of] <s>nityasama</s> (eternality-equivalence). As stated by the author of the <s>Nyāyanirmāṇa</s>: 'Since the state of impermanence is permanent, or since permanence applies to what is impermanent — this is <s>nityasama</s> (the eternality-equivalence [fallacy]).' And in the <s>Tārkikarakṣā</s> —
Because the alternatives of a property being of such or not-such form are untenable,
the destruction of the property-bearer being qualified by that [property] would be <s>nityasama</s> (the eternality-equivalence [fallacy]). Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
asyāḥ saṃjñāyā upalakṣaṇatvam abhipretyābhihitaṃ prabodhasiddhāv anvarthitvāt
          tūparañjakadharmasameti/ tasmād asad uttaram etad iti cet —
children.translated_text: Intending this designation to be merely illustrative, it was stated in the <s>Prabodhasiddhi</s>: 'because it is fitting, it accompanies the qualifying property.' Therefore, if one says this is an invalid response —

children.text:
aśikṣitatrāsanam etat/ duṣṭatvamūlānirūpaṇāt/ tad dvividhaṃ sādhāraṇam asādhāraṇaṃ ca/
          tatrādyaṃ svavyāghātakam/ dvitīyaṃ trividhaṃ yuktāṅgahīnatvam ayuktāṅgādhikatvam
          aviṣayavṛttitvaṃ ceti/ tatra sādhāraṇam asaṃbhāvitam eva/ uktasyākṣepasya
          svātmavyāpanānupalambhāt/ evam asādhāraṇam api/ ghaṭasya nāstitāyāṃ nāstitoktāv astitvavat
          prakṛte 'py upapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: This is the fright of the untrained. Because the root of the defect has not been identified. That [defect] is twofold: common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) and uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>). Of these, the first is self-contradictory. The second is threefold: lacking a valid component, having an invalid additional component, and operating on a non-domain. Among these, the common [defect] is simply impossible — because the stated objection's applicability to itself is not perceived. Similarly, the uncommon [defect] is also [impossible] — because the reasoning applies here just as in the case of stating the non-existence of the non-existence of a pot, existence [applies].
reference marker

children.text:
nanu prapañcasya mithyātvam abhyupeyate nāsattvam iti cet tad etat so 'yaṃ śiraśchede 'pi
          śataṃ na dadāti viṃśatipañcakaṃ tu prayacchatīti śākaṭikavṛttāntam anuharet/
          mithyātvāsattvayoḥ paryāyatvād iti alam atiprapañcena/
children.translated_text: Now, if one says that the unreality of the phenomenal world is accepted, not its non-existence — that is like the story of the cart-driver who 'does not pay a hundred when his head is cut off, but gives twenty-five.' Because unreality and non-existence are synonymous. Thus, enough of this excessive elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>).
reference marker

children.text:
tatrāthāto brahmajijñāsā iti prathamasūtrasyāyam arthaḥ/ tatrāthaśabdo maṅgalārtho
          'dhikārānantaryārthaś ca svīkriyate/ ataḥśabdo hetvarthaḥ/ tad uktaṃ gāruḍe —
children.translated_text: Therein, the meaning of the first <s>sūtra</s>, 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>athāto brahmajijñāsā</s>), is as follows: therein, the word <s>atha</s> is accepted as denoting auspiciousness and the sequence after a prerequisite (<s>adhikārānantarya</s>). The word <s>ataḥ</s> denotes a reason. Thus stated in the <s>Gāruḍa</s> [Purāṇa]:
All <s>sūtras</s> without exception are invariably begun

children.text: prārabhyante niyatyaiva tat kim atra niyāmakam//
children.translated_text: preceded by the words <s>atha</s> and <s>ataḥ</s> -- what is the determining factor here?

children.text: kaś cārthas tu tayor vidvan katham uttamatā tayoḥ/
children.translated_text: What is the meaning of those two, O learned one? How do those two attain preeminence?

children.text: etad ākhyāhi me brahman yathā jñāsyāmi tattvataḥ//
children.translated_text: Tell me this, O <s>Brahman</s>, so that I may know it in truth.

children.text: evam ukto nāradena brahmā provāca sattamaḥ/
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the best of beings, spoke:
The word <s>atha</s> is for sequence and prerequisite, and likewise for auspiciousness;

children.text: athaśabdas tv ataḥśabdo hetvarthe samudīritaḥ/ iti/
children.translated_text: and the word <s>ataḥ</s> is uttered in the sense of reason.

children.text:
yato nārāyaṇaprasādam antareṇa na mokṣo labhyate prasādaś ca jñānam antareṇa ato
          brahmajijñāsā kartavyeti siddham/
children.translated_text: Since without the grace of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, liberation is not obtained, and since grace [is not obtained] without knowledge -- therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> is to be undertaken. This is established.
reference marker

children.text:
jijñāsyabrahmaṇo lakṣaṇam uktaṃ janmādy asya yataḥ iti/ sṛṣṭisthityādi yato bhavati tad
          brahmeti vākyārthaḥ/ tathā ca skāndaṃ vacaḥ —
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>Brahman</s> to be inquired into is stated [in the sūtra]: 'That from which the origin and so forth [of this universe proceed]' (<s>janmādy asya yataḥ</s>). The meaning of the sentence is: that from which creation, maintenance, and the like arise -- that is <s>Brahman</s>. And thus the statement from the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa]:
Creation, maintenance, destruction, regulation, knowledge, concealment,

children.text: bandhamokṣau ca puruṣād yasmāt sa harir ekarāṭ// iti/
children.translated_text: bondage and liberation -- since these [proceed] from the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person), He is <s>Hari</s>, the sole sovereign.
And from <s>Śruti</s> passages such as 'from which indeed these [beings are born]' and the like.
reference marker

children.text:
tatra pramāṇam apy uktaṃ śāstrayonitvāt iti/ nāvedavin manute taṃ bṛhantam taṃ tv
          aupaniṣadam ityādiśrutibhyas tasyānumānikatvaṃ nirākriyate/ na cānumānasya svātantryeṇa
          prāmāṇyam asti/ tad uktaṃ kaurme —
children.translated_text: Therein, the means of valid knowledge is also stated [in the sūtra]: 'because [<s>Brahman</s>] is the source of scripture' (<s>śāstrayonitvāt</s>). From <s>Śruti</s> passages such as 'one who does not know the <s>Veda</s> does not know that great one' and 'Him, the one of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>' -- His knowability through mere inference is rejected. Nor does inference have independent authority. Thus stated in the <s>Kaurma</s> [Purāṇa]:
Inference devoid of the support of <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation) can never

children.text: niścayāt sādhayed arthaṃ pramāṇāntaram eva ca//
children.translated_text: establish a thing with certainty; nor can any other means of knowledge.
That which is the supreme other means of knowledge, supported by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>,

children.text: pramāṇapadavīṃ gacchen nātra kāryā vicāraṇā// iti
children.translated_text: attains the status of a valid means of knowledge -- in this there need be no deliberation.
The nature of scripture is stated in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa]:
<s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, <s>Atharva</s>, the <s>Bhārata</s> (Mahābhārata), the <s>Pāñcarātrika</s>,
and the original <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> -- these are called scripture.

children.text: yac cānukūlam etasya tac ca śāstraṃ prakīrtitam/
children.translated_text: And whatever is in accord with these is also declared to be scripture;

children.text: ato 'nyo granthavistāro naiva śāstraṃ kuvartma tat// iti/
children.translated_text: any other expanse of texts is not scripture -- that is a wrong path.
reference marker

children.text:
tad anena ananyalabhyaḥ śāstrārtha iti nyāyena bhedasya prāptatvena tatra na tātparyaṃ
          kiṃ tv advaita eva vedavākyānāṃ tātparyam — ity advaitavādināṃ pratyāśā pratikṣiptā/
          anumānād īśvarasya siddhyabhāvena tadbhedasyāpi tataḥ siddhyabhāvāt/ tasmān na
          bhedānuvādakatvam iti tatparatvam avagamyate/ ata evoktam —
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the principle that 'the meaning of scripture is not obtainable from any other [source],' since difference [between the individual soul and Brahman] is already established, the purport [of Vedic statements] is not in that [difference]; rather, the purport of Vedic statements is in non-duality alone -- this expectation of the Advaitins is rejected. Because the Lord is not established through inference, the difference of that [Lord from souls] is also not established thereby. Therefore, since [the Vedic statements] do not merely reiterate difference, their purport in that [difference] is understood. Therefore it is stated:
Ever knowable through true scripture (<s>sadāgama</s>) alone, having transcended the perishable and imperishable,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, faultless and possessed of all good qualities -- Him I always worship.
reference marker

children.text:
śāstrasya tatra prāmāṇyam upapāditaṃ tat tu samanvayāt iti/ samanvaya upakramādiliṅgam/
          uktaṃ bṛhatsaṃhitāyām —
children.translated_text: The authority of scripture therein is established [by the sūtra]: 'But that [is known] through harmony' (<s>tat tu samanvayāt</s>). <s>Samanvaya</s> (harmony) is the indicator (<s>liṅga</s>) [established through] the opening statement (<s>upakrama</s>) and the like. Stated in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>:
Opening and closing statements (<s>upakramopasaṃhāra</s>), repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>), novelty (<s>apūrvatā</s>), result (<s>phala</s>),
laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), and reasoning (<s>upapatti</s>) -- these are the indicators for determining the purport [of a text].
reference marker

children.text:
evaṃ vedāntatātparyavaśāt tad eva brahma śāstragamyam ity uktaṃ bhavati/ diṅmātram atra
          prādarśi/ śiṣṭam ānandatīrthabhāṣyavyākhyānādau draṣṭavyam/ granthabahutvabhiyoparamyata
          iti/
children.translated_text: Thus, by the force of the purport of <s>Vedānta</s>, it is stated that that very <s>Brahman</s> is knowable through scripture. Only a brief indication has been shown here. The rest should be seen in the commentary of <s>Ānandatīrtha</s> (Madhva) and its sub-commentaries. We desist out of fear of excessive length of the work.
reference marker

children.text: etac ca rahasyaṃ pūrṇaprajñena madhyamandireṇa vāyos tṛtīyāvatāraṃmanyena nirūpitam/
children.translated_text: And this secret was expounded by <s>Pūrṇaprajña</s> (Madhva), the middle temple, who considered himself the third incarnation of <s>Vāyu</s> (the wind-god).

children.text: prathamas tu hanūmān syād dvitīyo bhīma eva ca/
children.translated_text: The first [incarnation] is <s>Hanumān</s>; the second is <s>Bhīma</s> himself;
<s>Pūrṇaprajña</s> (Madhva) is the third, the accomplisher of the Lord's purpose.

children.text: etad evābhipretya tatra tatra granthasamāptāv idaṃ padyaṃ likhyate —
children.translated_text: With this very intent, at the conclusion of the work here and there, this verse is written:

children.text: yasya trīṇy uditāni vedavacane divyāni rūpāṇy alaṃ
children.translated_text: He whose three divine forms have been proclaimed in the Vedic utterance --

children.text: baṭ tad darśatam ittham eva nihitaṃ devasya bhargo mahat/
children.translated_text: 'Behold! Thus indeed is placed the great splendor of the god!'

children.text: vāyo rāmavaconayaṃ prathamakaṃ pṛkṣo dvitīyaṃ vapur
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s>'s first body is the monkey [<s>Hanumān</s>], in <s>Rāma</s>'s command; the second body is the son of <s>Pṛkṣa</s> [<s>Bhīma</s>];

children.text: madhvo yat tu tṛtīyam etad amunā granthaḥ kṛtaḥ keśave//
children.translated_text: and <s>Madhva</s>'s, which is the third -- by him this work was composed for <s>Keśava</s>.

children.text:
baḻ itthā tad vapuṣe dhāyi darśataṃ
            devasya bhargaḥ sahaso yato jani
children.translated_text: is to be understood by contemplation of the <s>Śruti</s> beginning with 'Behold! Thus indeed was placed the splendor of the god of might, from whom was born...'

children.text:
ityādiśrutiparyālocanayāvagamyata iti/ tasmāt
          sarvasya śāstrasya viṣṇutattvaṃ sarvottamam ity atra tātparyam iti sarvaṃ niravadyam/
children.translated_text: and so on. Therefore, the purport of all scripture is that the truth of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the most supreme -- thus everything is faultless.
The meaning of this verse, however,
Thus concludes the <s>Pūrṇaprajñadarśana</s> (Madhva philosophy) in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṅgraha</s>.
Now the <s>Nakulīśa-Pāśupata</s> philosophy //6//
reference marker

children.text:
tad etad vaiṣṇavamataṃ dāsatvādipadavedanīyaṃ paratantratvaṃ duḥkhāvahatvān na
          duḥkhāntādīpsitāspadam ity arocayamānāḥ pāramaiśvaryaṃ kāmayamānāḥ parābhimatā muktā na
          bhavanti paratantratvāt pāramaiśvaryarahitatvād asmadādivat muktātmānaś ca
          parameśvaraguṇasaṃbandhinaḥ puruṣatve sati samastaduḥkhabījavidhuratvāt parameśvaravat —
          ityādy anumānaṃ pramāṇaṃ pratipadyamānāḥ kecana māheśvarāḥ paramapuruṣārthasādhanaṃ
          pañcārthaprapañcanaparaṃ pāśupataśāstram āśrayante/
children.translated_text: Considering that this <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> doctrine -- which teaches the dependence [on God] to be known through [concepts such as] servitude (<s>dāsatva</s>) and the like -- is the cause of suffering due to being subordinate, and is not the desired object of those who wish for the end of suffering; desiring supreme sovereignty (<s>pāramaiśvarya</s>); [arguing that] the liberated souls as conceived by the others are not [truly] liberated, because of being subordinate and because of lacking supreme sovereignty, just like us [ordinary souls]; and that the liberated selves, being related to the qualities of the Supreme Lord, being persons and being devoid of all seeds of suffering -- are like the Supreme Lord -- accepting such inference as the means of knowledge, certain <s>Māheśvaras</s> (devotees of <s>Maheśvara</s>) resort to the <s>Pāśupata</s> scripture, which is devoted to the elaboration of the five categories (<s>pañcārtha</s>) as the means of attaining the supreme goal of life.
reference marker

children.text:
tatredam ādisūtram — athātaḥ paśupateḥ pāśupatayogavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāma iti/ asyārthaḥ —
          atrāthaśabdaḥ pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣaḥ/ pūrvaprakṛtaś ca guruṃ prati śiṣyasya praśnaḥ/
          gurusvarūpaṃ gaṇakārikāyāṃ nirūpitam —
children.translated_text: Therein, this is the opening <s>sūtra</s>: 'Now, therefore, we shall explain the method of <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga from [the teaching of] <s>Paśupati</s>.' Its meaning: here the word <s>atha</s> depends on what was previously being discussed. And what was previously being discussed is the question of the disciple to the guru. The nature of the guru is defined in the <s>Gaṇakārikā</s>:

children.text: pañcakās tv aṣṭa vijñeyā gaṇaś caikas trikātmakaḥ/
children.translated_text: The pentads are to be known as eight, and the group (<s>gaṇa</s>) is one, having three aspects;

children.text: vettā navagaṇasyāsya saṃskartā gurur ucyate// iti/
children.translated_text: the knower of this nine-fold group, who is the consecrator, is called the guru.
Attainments (<s>lābha</s>), impurities (<s>mala</s>), means (<s>upāya</s>), places (<s>deśa</s>), stages (<s>avasthā</s>), purifications (<s>viśuddhi</s>),

children.text: dīkṣākāribalāny aṣṭau pañcakās trīṇi vṛttayaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: initiatory accessories (<s>dīkṣākāri</s>), and powers (<s>bala</s>) -- [these are] the eight pentads; [and] three [types of] livelihood (<s>vṛtti</s>).

children.text:
tisro vṛttaya iti prayoktavye trīṇi vṛttaya iti cchāndasaḥ prayogaḥ/ tatra vidhīyamānam
          upāyaphalaṃ lābhaḥ/ jñānatapodevanityatva

children.translated_text: It is fivefold, by the distinction of knowledge, austerity, permanence of the deity,

Where one should say 'three livelihoods' (<s>tisro vṛttayaḥ</s>), the Vedic usage 'three livelihoods' (<s>trīṇi vṛttayaḥ</s>) is employed. Therein, <s>lābha</s> (attainment) is the fruit of the means that is prescribed.
reference marker

children.text: jñanaṃ tapo 'tha nityatvaṃ sthitiḥ śuddhiś ca pañcamam// iti/
children.translated_text: stability, and purification -- [these are] the five. Thus states the teacher <s>Haradatta</s>:

children.text: ātmāśrito duṣṭabhāvo malaḥ/ sa mithyājñānādibhedāt pañcavidhaḥ/ tad apy āha —
children.translated_text: Knowledge, austerity, permanence, stability, and purification as the fifth.

children.text: mithyājñānam adharmaś ca saktihetuś cyutis tathā/
children.translated_text: Impurity (<s>mala</s>) is a defective condition residing in the self. It is fivefold, by the distinction of false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) and the like. He states that too:
and animality (<s>paśutva</s>) as the root -- these five in the <s>tantra</s> are to be abandoned through discrimination.
False knowledge, unrighteousness (<s>adharma</s>), attachment (<s>sakti</s>), causation (<s>hetu</s>), and falling (<s>cyuti</s>),

children.text: sādhakasya śuddhihetur upāyo vāsacaryādibhedāt pañcavidhaḥ/ tad apy āha —
children.translated_text: The means (<s>upāya</s>) is the cause of purification for the practitioner, fivefold by the distinction of dwelling in sacred ashes (<s>vāsa</s>), observance (<s>caryā</s>), and the like. He states that too:

children.text: vāsacaryā japo dhyānaṃ sadā rudrasmṛtis tathā/
children.translated_text: Dwelling [in sacred ashes] (<s>vāsa</s>), observance (<s>caryā</s>), recitation (<s>japa</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and constant remembrance of <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: prapattiś ceti lābhānām upāyāḥ pañca niścitāḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: and surrender (<s>prapatti</s>) -- these five are the established means for the attainments.
reference marker

children.text: yenārthānusaṃdhānapūrvakaṃ jñānatapovṛddhī prāpnoti sa deśo gurujanādiḥ/ yad āha —
children.translated_text: That place through which, preceded by purposeful investigation, one attains the growth of knowledge and austerity -- that is the place, [consisting of] the guru's presence and the like. As stated:

children.text: gurur jano guhādeśaḥ śmaśānaṃ rudra eva ca/ iti/
children.translated_text: The guru, the assembly of people, the cave, the cremation ground, and <s>Rudra</s> himself.

children.text: ā lābhaprāpter ekamaryādāvasthitasya yad avasthānaṃ sāvasthā vyaktādiviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭā/
children.translated_text: The stage (<s>avasthā</s>) is the state of one who abides within a single boundary until the attainment of the fruit, qualified by the specification of the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) and the like.
reference marker
Thus stated:
and completion (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) as the fifth.
The manifest (<s>vyakta</s>), the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), victory (<s>jaya</s>), cutting (<s>cheda</s>),

children.text: mithyājñānādīnām atyantavyapoho viśuddhiḥ/ sā pratiyogibhedāt pañcavidhā/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: Purification (<s>viśuddhi</s>) is the absolute removal of false knowledge and the like. It is fivefold by the distinction of the counter-correlate. Thus stated:
The removal of ignorance, of unrighteousness, of what causes attachment,

children.text: cyuter hāniḥ paśutvasya śuddhiḥ pañcavidhā smṛtā// iti/
children.translated_text: the removal of falling, and of animality (<s>paśutva</s>) -- purification is remembered as fivefold.
The pentad of initiatory accessories (<s>dīkṣākāri</s>) is also stated:

children.text: dravyaṃ kālaḥ kriyā mūrtir guruś caiva hi pañcamaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: Substance (<s>dravya</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), ritual action (<s>kriyā</s>), form (<s>mūrti</s>), and the guru as the fifth.
And the pentad of powers (<s>bala</s>):

children.text: gurubhaktiḥ prasādaś ca mater dvandvajayas tathā/
children.translated_text: Devotion to the guru, grace (<s>prasāda</s>), conquest of the pairs of opposites (<s>dvandvajaya</s>),

children.text: dharmaś caivāpramādaś ca balaṃ pañcavidhaṃ smṛtam// iti/
children.translated_text: righteousness (<s>dharma</s>), and vigilance (<s>apramāda</s>) -- power is remembered as fivefold.

children.text:
pañcamalalaghūkaraṇārtham āgamāvirodhino 'nnārjanopāyā vṛttayo
          bhaikṣyotsṛṣṭayathālabdhābhidhā iti/ śeṣam aśeṣam ākara evāvagantavyam/
children.translated_text: The livelihoods (<s>vṛtti</s>) are the means of acquiring food that do not contradict the scriptures, for the purpose of lightening the five impurities -- they are called begging (<s>bhaikṣya</s>), abandoned (<s>utsṛṣṭa</s>), and whatever is available (<s>yathālabdha</s>). The rest should be understood in its entirety from the source text itself.
reference marker

children.text:
ataḥśabdena duḥkhāntasya pratipādanam/ ādhyātmikādiduḥkhatrayavyapohapraśnārthatvāt
          tasya/ paśuśabdena kāryasya/ paratantravacanatvāt tasya/ patiśabdena kāraṇasya/ īśvaraḥ
          patir īśiteti jagatkāraṇībhūteśvaravacanatvāt tasya/ yogavidhī tu prasiddhau/
children.translated_text: By the word <s>ataḥ</s>, the end of suffering (<s>duḥkhānta</s>) is indicated -- because its [purpose] is to raise the question of the removal of the threefold suffering: <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), and the like. By the word <s>paśu</s> (animal/bound soul), the effect (<s>kārya</s>) [is indicated] -- because it is a word denoting what is dependent. By the word <s>pati</s> (lord), the cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>) [is indicated] -- because '<s>Īśvara</s> is <s>Pati</s>, He is the ruler' denotes <s>Īśvara</s> who has become the cause of the universe. And <s>yogavidhi</s> (method of yoga) is well-known.
reference marker

children.text:
tatra duḥkhānto dvividhaḥ — anātmakaḥ sātmakaś ceti/ tatrānātmakaḥ sarvaduḥkhānām
          atyantocchedarūpaḥ/ sātmakas tu dṛkkriyāśaktilakṣaṇam aiśvaryam/ tatra dṛkśaktir ekāpi
          viṣayabhedāt pañcavidhopacaryate darśanaṃ śravaṇaṃ mananaṃ vijñānaṃ sarvajñatvaṃ ceti/
          tatra sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭāśeṣacākṣuṣasparśādiviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ darśanam/
          aśeṣaśabdaviṣayaṃ siddhijñānaṃ śravaṇam/ samastacintāviṣayaṃ siddhijñānaṃ mananam/
          niravaśeṣaśāstraviṣayaṃ granthato ’rthataś ca siddhijñānaṃ vijñānam/ svaśāstraṃ yenocyate/
          uktānuktāśeṣārtheṣu samāsavistaravibhāgaviśeṣataś ca tattvavyāptasadoditasiddhijñānaṃ
          sarvajñatvam iti/ eṣā dhīśaktiḥ/
children.translated_text: Therein, the end of suffering (<s>duḥkhānta</s>) is twofold: without self (<s>anātmaka</s>) and with self (<s>sātmaka</s>). Among these, the 'without self' is the absolute cessation of all sufferings. The 'with self' is the sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) characterized by the powers of vision (<s>dṛk</s>) and action (<s>kriyā</s>). Therein, the power of vision (<s>dṛkśakti</s>), though one, is figuratively spoken of as fivefold according to the difference of objects: seeing (<s>darśana</s>), hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), reflection (<s>manana</s>), discernment (<s>vijñāna</s>), and omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>). Among these, knowledge of all visual and tactile objects -- subtle, concealed, and distant without remainder -- is seeing (<s>darśana</s>). Accomplished knowledge of all sounds without remainder is hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>). Accomplished knowledge of all objects of thought is reflection (<s>manana</s>). Accomplished knowledge of all scriptures without remainder, both in letter and in meaning, is discernment (<s>vijñāna</s>); by which one's own scripture is expounded. Accomplished knowledge that is pervaded by reality, regarding all stated and unstated meanings without remainder, in their summary, detail, and classification -- that is omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>). This is the power of intellect (<s>dhīśakti</s>).

children.text:
kriyāśaktir ekāpi trividhopacaryate manojavitvaṃ kāmarūpitvaṃ vikaraṇadharmitvaṃ ceti/
          tatra niratiśayaśīghrakāritvaṃ manojavitvam/ karmādinirapekṣasya
          svecchayaivānantasalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇasarūpakaraṇādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ kāmarūpitvam/
          upasaṃhṛtakaraṇasyāpi niratiśayaiśvaryasaṃbandhitvaṃ vikaraṇadharmitvam iti/ esā
          kriyāśaktiḥ/
children.translated_text: The power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>), though one, is figuratively spoken of as threefold: speed of mind (<s>manojavitva</s>), the ability to assume any form (<s>kāmarūpitva</s>), and the property of functioning without instruments (<s>vikaraṇadharmitva</s>). Among these, unsurpassed swiftness of operation is speed of mind. The capacity to preside over the production of innumerable forms, similar and dissimilar, by one's own will alone, independent of <s>karma</s> and the like, is the ability to assume any form (<s>kāmarūpitva</s>). Even with instruments withdrawn, the connection with unsurpassed sovereignty is the property of functioning without instruments (<s>vikaraṇadharmitva</s>). This is the power of action.
reference marker

children.text:
asvatantraṃ sarvaṃ kāryam/ tat trividhaṃ vidyā kalā paśuś ceti/ eteṣāṃ jñānāt
          saṃśayādinivṛttiḥ/
children.translated_text: Everything that is an effect (<s>kārya</s>) is dependent. That is threefold: <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>kalā</s> (art/power), and <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). From the knowledge of these, the removal of doubt and the like [is achieved].

children.text:
tatra paśuguṇo vidyā/ sāpi dvividhā bodhābodhasvabhāvabhedāt/ bodhasvabhāvā
          vivekāvivekapravṛttibhedād dvividhā/ sā cittam ity ucyate/ cittena hi sarvaḥ prāṇī
          bodhātmakaprakāśānugṛhītaṃ sāmānyena vivecitam avivecitaṃ cārthaṃ cetayata iti/ tatra
          vivekapravṛttiḥ pramāṇamātravyaṅgyā/
children.translated_text: Therein, <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is a quality of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>). It too is twofold, by the distinction of being of the nature of awareness and non-awareness. That of the nature of awareness is twofold, by the distinction of discriminating and non-discriminating activity. It is called <s>citta</s> (mind). For by means of <s>citta</s>, every living being cognizes objects -- illuminated by the light of awareness in general -- both discriminated and undiscriminated. Therein, the discriminating activity is indicated by the means of valid knowledge alone.

children.text:
paśvarthadharmādharmikā punar abodhātmikā vidyā/ cetanaparatantratve saty acetanā kalā/
          sāpi dvividhā — kāryākhā kāraṇākhyā ceti/ tatra kāryākhyā daśavidhā pṛthivyādīni pañca
          tattvāni rūpādayaḥ pañca guṇāś ceti/ kāraṇākhyā trayodaśavidhā — jñānendriyapañcakaṃ
          karmendriyapañcakam adhyavasāyābhimānasaṃkalpābhidhavṛttibhedād buddhyahaṃkāramanolakṣaṇam
          antaḥkaraṇatrayaṃ ceti/
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s> of the nature of non-awareness [pertains to] the properties of the bound soul such as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. <s>Kalā</s> (power) is that which is non-conscious while being dependent on the conscious being. It too is twofold: called effect (<s>kārya</s>) and called cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>). Among these, the effect-category is tenfold: the five principles (<s>tattvas</s>) beginning with earth, and the five qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) beginning with form (<s>rūpa</s>). The cause-category is thirteenfold: the pentad of knowledge-faculties (<s>jñānendriya</s>), the pentad of action-faculties (<s>karmendriya</s>), and the threefold inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) characterized as intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), and mind (<s>manas</s>), distinguished by the functions of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), self-appropriation (<s>abhimāna</s>), and conceptualization (<s>saṃkalpa</s>).

children.text:
paśutvasaṃbandhī paśuḥ/ so ’pi dvividhaḥ — sāñjano nirañjanaś ceti/ tatra sāñjanaḥ
          śarīrendriyasaṃbandhī/ nirañjanas tu tadrahitaḥ/ tatprapañcas tu pañcārthabhāṣyadīpikādau
          draṣṭavyaḥ/
children.translated_text: The <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) is that which is connected with animality (<s>paśutva</s>). It too is twofold: tainted (<s>sāñjana</s>) and untainted (<s>nirañjana</s>). Among these, the tainted [soul] is connected with body and sense-faculties. The untainted [soul] is devoid of those. The elaboration of this should be seen in the <s>Pañcārthabhāṣyadīpikā</s> and the like.
reference marker

children.text:
samastasṛṣṭisaṃhārānugrahakāri kāraṇam/ tasyaikasyāpi guṇakarmabhedāpekṣayā vibhāgaḥ
          uktaḥ patiḥ sann ādya

children.translated_text: and so on. Therein, lordship (<s>patitva</s>) is the unsurpassed power of vision and action. Existence (<s>sattva</s>) is

children.text:
tenaiśvaryeṇa nityasaṃbandhitvam/ ādyatvam anāgantukaiśvaryasaṃbandhitvam/ ity
          ādarśakārādibhis tīrthakarair nirūpitam/
children.translated_text: being eternally connected with that sovereignty. Primordiality (<s>ādyatva</s>) is being connected with sovereignty that is not adventitious. This has been determined by the <s>Tīrthaṅkaras</s> (preceptors of the tradition) such as <s>Ādarśakāra</s> (the mirror-maker) and others.

The cause that performs the creation, dissolution, and grace of the entire [universe]. Even of that single [cause], a division is stated with reference to the distinctions of qualities and actions: 'Being the Lord, the primal [one]' —

children.text:
cittadvāreṇātmeśvarasaṃbandhahetur yogaḥ/ sa ca dvividhaḥ kriyālakṣaṇaḥ
          kriyoparamalakṣaṇaś ceti/ tatra japadhyānādirūpaḥ kriyālakṣaṇaḥ/ kriyoparamalakṣaṇas tu
          niṣṭhāsaṃvidgatyādisaṃjñitaḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> is the cause of the connection between the self and the Lord through the medium of the mind (<s>citta</s>). And that is twofold: characterized by action (<s>kriyālakṣaṇa</s>) and characterized by the cessation of action (<s>kriyoparamalakṣaṇa</s>). Therein, that characterized by action has the form of <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and the like. That characterized by the cessation of action is designated by the names <s>niṣṭhā</s> (steadfastness), <s>saṃvid</s> (awareness), <s>gati</s> (attainment), and the like.

children.text:
dharmārthasādhakavyāpāro vidhiḥ/ sa ca dvividhaḥ — pradhānabhūto guṇabhūtaś ca/ tatra
          pradhānabhūtaḥ sākṣād dharmahetuś caryā/ sā dvividhā vrataṃ dvārāṇi ceti/ tatra
          bhasmasnānaśayanopahārajapapradakṣiṇāni vratam/ tad uktam bhagavatā nakulīśena — bhasmanā
          triṣavaṇaṃ snāyīta bhasmani śayīteti/
children.translated_text: <s>Vidhi</s> (injunction) is the activity that accomplishes <s>dharma</s> (religious merit). And that is twofold — primary (<s>pradhānabhūta</s>) and subsidiary (<s>guṇabhūta</s>). Therein, the primary [injunction], which is the direct cause of <s>dharma</s>, is <s>caryā</s> (observance). That is twofold: <s>vrata</s> (vow) and <s>dvāras</s> (gateways). Therein, bathing with ashes, sleeping [on ashes], offering, <s>japa</s> (recitation), and circumambulation constitute the <s>vrata</s>. As stated by the blessed <s>Nakulīśa</s>: 'One should bathe with ashes three times a day; one should sleep on ashes.'

children.text:
atropahāro niyamaḥ/ sa ca ṣaḍaṅgaḥ/ tad uktaṃ sūtrakāreṇa —
          hasitagītanṛtyahuḍukkāranamaskārajapyaṣaḍaṅgopahāreṇopatiṣṭheteti/ tatra hasitaṃ nāma
          kaṇṭhoṣṭhapuṭavisphūrjanapuraḥsaram ahahety aṭṭahāsaḥ/
children.translated_text: Therein, 'offering' (<s>upahāra</s>) is the observance (<s>niyama</s>). And that has six limbs. As stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras): 'One should worship with the sixfold offering consisting of laughter, song, dance, the <s>huḍukkāra</s> (bull-sound), obeisance, and recitation.' Therein, laughter is the loud guffaw preceded by the opening of the throat and lips [with the sound] 'aha!'

children.text:
gītaṃ gāndharvaśāstrasamayānusāreṇa maheśvarasaṃbandhiguṇadharmādinimittānāṃ cintanam/
          nṛtyam api nāṭyaśāstrānusāreṇa hastapādādīnām utkṣepaṇādikam aṅgapratyaṅgopāṅgasahitaṃ
          bhāvābhāvasametaṃ ca prayoktavyam/ huḍukkāro nāma jihvātālusaṃyogān niṣpādyamānaḥ puṇyo
          vṛṣanādasadṛśo nādaḥ/ huḍug iti śabdānukāro vaṣaḍ itivat/ yatra laukikā bhavanti tatraitat
          sarvaṃ gūḍhaṃ prayoktavyam/ śiṣṭaṃ prasiddham/ dvārāṇi tu
          krāthanaspandanamandanaśṛṅgāraṇāvitatkaraṇāvitadbhāṣaṇāni/ tatrāsuptasyaiva
          suptaliṅgapradarśanaṃ krāthanam/ vāyvabhibhūtasyeva śarīrāvayavānāṃ kampanaṃ spandanam/
          upahatapādendriyasyeva gamanaṃ mandanam/ rūpayauvanasaṃpannāṃ kāminīm avalokyātmānaṃ
          kāmukam iva yair vilāsaiḥ pradarśayati tac chṛṅgāraṇam/ kāryākāryavivekavikalasyeva
          lokaninditakarmakaraṇam avitatkaraṇam/ vyāhatāpārthakādiśabdoccāraṇam avitadbhāṣaṇam iti/
          guṇabhūtas tu vidhiś caryānugrāhako ’nusnānādir
          bhaikṣyocchiṣṭādinirmitāyogyatāpratyayanivṛttyarthaḥ/ tad apy uktaṃ sūtrakāreṇa —
          anusnānanirmālyaliṅgadhārīti/
children.translated_text: Song is the contemplation — in accordance with the principles of the science of music (<s>gāndharvaśāstra</s>) — of the qualities and attributes connected with <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord). Dance too is to be performed in accordance with the science of dramaturgy (<s>nāṭyaśāstra</s>), with the raising and the like of hands and feet, accompanied by major and minor limbs, and endowed with [the expression of] emotions and their absence. The <s>huḍukkāra</s> is a sacred sound resembling the bellowing of a bull, produced by the conjunction of tongue and palate. '<s>Huḍuk</s>' is an onomatopoeia, like '<s>vaṣaṭ</s>.' Where worldly [non-initiated] people are present, all this should be performed secretly. The rest is well known. The gateways (<s>dvāras</s>) are: feigning drowsiness (<s>krāthana</s>), trembling (<s>spandana</s>), limping (<s>mandana</s>), amorous display (<s>śṛṅgāraṇa</s>), acting without deliberation (<s>avitatkaraṇa</s>), and speaking incoherently (<s>avitadbhāṣaṇa</s>). Therein, feigning drowsiness is displaying the signs of sleep while actually awake. Trembling is the shaking of the limbs as if overpowered by wind. Limping is walking as if one's foot-organ is impaired. Amorous display is that by which, upon seeing a beautiful and youthful woman, one displays oneself as if amorous through various coquettish gestures. Acting without deliberation is performing actions condemned by the world, as if devoid of the discrimination between right and wrong. Speaking incoherently is uttering contradictory, meaningless, and similar words. The subsidiary injunction, which supports the observance, is the secondary bathing (<s>anusnāna</s>) and the like — for the purpose of removing the notion of unfitness produced by alms-food, leftovers, and the like. This too has been stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>: 'One who performs secondary bathing, [wears] the remnants [of worship], and bears the <s>liṅga</s> (mark [of <s>Śiva</s>]).'

children.text:
tatra samāso nāma dharmimātrābhidhānam/ tac ca prathamasūtra eva kṛtam/ pañcānāṃ
          padārthānāṃ pramāṇataḥ pañcābhidhānaṃ vistaraḥ/ sa khalu rāśīkarabhāṣye draṣṭavyaḥ/ eteṣāṃ
          yathāsaṃbhavaṃ lakṣaṇato ’saṃkareṇābhidhānaṃ vibhāgaḥ/ sa tu vihita eva/ śāstrāntarebhyo
          ’mīṣāṃ guṇātiśayena kathanaṃ viśeṣaḥ/ tathā hi — anyatra duḥkhanivṛttir eva duḥkhāntaḥ/
          iha tu pāramaiśvaryaprāptiś ca/ anyatrābhūtvā bhāvi kāryam/ iha tu nityaṃ paśvādi/ anyatra
          sāpekṣaṃ kāraṇam/ iha tu nirapekṣo bhagavān eva/ anyatra kaivalyādiphalako yogaḥ/ iha tu
          pāramaiśvaryaduḥkhāntaphalakaḥ/ anyatra punar āvṛttirūpasvargādiphalako vidhiḥ/ iha punar
          apunarāvṛttirūpasāmīpyādiphalakaḥ/
children.translated_text: Therein, the summary (<s>samāsa</s>) is the statement of the mere categories (<s>dharmin</s>). And that has been done in the very first <s>sūtra</s>. The detailed account (<s>vistara</s>) is the fivefold exposition of the five categories by means of valid knowledge. That should be seen in the <s>Rāśīkara</s> commentary.
