The division (<s>vibhāga</s>) is the non-confusing exposition of their definitions, as appropriate. And that has been duly presented. The distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>) is the statement of their superior qualities in comparison with other systems. Thus: in other [systems], the mere cessation of suffering is the end of suffering; but here, the attainment of supreme sovereignty (<s>pāramaiśvarya</s>) [is also included]. In other [systems], the effect is something that was previously non-existent; but here, the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) and the like are eternal. In other [systems], the cause requires auxiliary factors; but here, the blessed Lord alone [acts] without dependence. In other [systems], <s>yoga</s> has liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) and the like as its fruit; but here, it has supreme sovereignty and the end of suffering as its fruit. In other [systems], <s>vidhi</s> (injunction) has as its fruit heaven and the like, which involve return; but here, it has as its fruit proximity [to <s>Śiva</s>] and the like, which involve no return.

children.text:
nanu mahad etad indrajālaṃ yan nirapekṣaḥ parameśvaraḥ kāraṇam iti/ tathātve
          karmavaiphalyaṃ sarvakāryāṇāṃ samasamayasamutpādaś ceti doṣadvayaṃ prāduḥṣyāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'This is a great illusion — that the Supreme Lord is the cause without dependence [on anything]. If so, two faults would arise: the futility of <s>karma</s> (action) and the simultaneous origination of all effects.'
Do not think so! Because [the Lord and <s>karma</s>] have different spheres (<s>vyadhikaraṇatva</s>).

children.text:
yadi nirapekṣasya bhagavataḥ kāraṇatvaṃ syāt tarhi karmaṇo vaiphalye kim āyātam/
          prayojanābhāva iti cet — kasya prayojanābhāvaḥ karmavaiphalye kāraṇam/ kiṃ karmiṇaḥ kiṃ vā
          bhagavataḥ/ nādyaḥ/ īśvarecchānugṛhītasya karmaṇaḥ saphalatvopapatteḥ/ tadananugṛhītasya
          yayātiprabhṛtikarmavat kadācin niṣphalatvasaṃbhavāc ca/ na caitāvatā karmasv apravṛttiḥ/
          karṣakādivad upapatteḥ/ īśvarecchāyattatvāc ca paśūnāṃ pravṛtteḥ/ nāpi dvitīyaḥ/
          parameśvarasya paryāptakāmatvena karmasādhyaprayojanāpekṣāyā abhāvāt/ yad uktaṃ
          samasamayasamutpāda iti tad apy ayuktam/ acintyaśaktikasya parameśvarasyecchānuvidhāyinyā
          avyāhatakriyāśaktyā kāryakāritvābhyupagamāt/ tad uktaṃ saṃpradāyavidbhiḥ —
children.translated_text: If the blessed Lord's causality were without dependence, what would follow from the futility of <s>karma</s>? If [you say] 'the absence of purpose' — whose absence of purpose is the reason for the futility of <s>karma</s>? Is it of the agent of <s>karma</s>, or of the blessed Lord? Not the first — because <s>karma</s> that is favored by the Lord's will can indeed be fruitful, and [<s>karma</s>] not favored by Him may sometimes be fruitless, like the <s>karma</s> of <s>Yayāti</s> and others. Nor does this [occasional fruitlessness] cause non-engagement in <s>karmas</s> — because it is justified as with a farmer and the like. And because the activity of bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) is dependent on the Lord's will. Nor the second — because the Supreme Lord, being one whose desires are fulfilled (<s>paryāptakāma</s>), has no need for a purpose achievable through <s>karma</s>. As for the objection of simultaneous origination — that too is unjust. Because it is accepted that the Supreme Lord, who possesses inconceivable power, produces effects through His unobstructed power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>) that follows His will. As stated by the knowers of the tradition:

children.text: karmādinirapekṣas tu svecchācārī yato hy ayam/
children.translated_text: 'Since He acts according to His own will, independent of <s>karma</s> and the like,
therefore, from the [standpoint of] causation, [He is declared] in the scripture to be the cause of all causes.' Thus.

children.text:
nanu darśanāntare ’pīśvarajñānān mokṣo labhyata eveti kuto ’sya viśeṣa iti cet — maivaṃ
          vādīḥ/ vikalpānupapatteḥ/ kim īśvaraviṣayajñānamātraṃ nirvāṇakāraṇaṃ kiṃ vā sākṣātkāraḥ
          atha vā yathāvat tattvaniścayaḥ/ nādyaḥ/ śāstram antareṇāpi prākṛtajanavad devānām adhipo
          mahādeva iti jñānotpattimātreṇa mokṣasiddhau śāstrābhyāsavaiphalyaprasaṅgāt/ nāpi
          dvitīyaḥ/ anekamalapracayopacitānāṃ piśitalocanānāṃ paśūnāṃ
          parameśvarasākṣātkārānupapatteḥ/ tṛtīye ’smanmatāpātaḥ/ pāśupataśāstram antareṇa yathāvat
          tattvaniścayānupapatteḥ/ tad uktam ācāryaiḥ —
children.translated_text: Objection: 'In other systems too, liberation is obtained through knowledge of the Lord — so what is the distinction of this [system]?' Do not say so! Because [none of the] alternatives is tenable. Is mere knowledge pertaining to the Lord the cause of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation)? Or is it direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>)? Or is it correct ascertainment of reality? Not the first — because, even without scripture, if liberation were accomplished merely by the arising of the knowledge '<s>Mahādeva</s> is the overlord of the gods,' as with ordinary people, the study of scripture would be futile. Nor the second — because, for bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) whose eyes are covered with flesh, accumulated with heaps of many impurities, direct realization of the Supreme Lord is impossible. In the third case, one arrives at our own doctrine — because correct ascertainment of reality is impossible without the <s>Pāśupata</s> scripture. As stated by the <s>ācāryas</s> (masters):

children.text: jñānamātre vṛthā śāstraṃ sākṣāddṛṣṭis tu durlabhā/
children.translated_text: 'For mere knowledge, scripture would be in vain; direct vision is difficult to attain;

children.text: pañcārthād anyato nāsti yathāvat tattvaniścayaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: correct ascertainment of reality does not exist from [any source] other than the <s>pañcārtha</s> (five categories).' Thus.

children.text:
tasmāt puruṣārthakāmaiḥ puruṣadhaureyaiḥ pañcārthapratipādanaparaṃ pāśupataśāstram
          āśrayaṇīyam iti ramaṇīyam//
children.translated_text: Therefore, those who desire the highest human goal, who are foremost among men, should resort to the <s>Pāśupata</s> scripture, which teaches the five categories — this is delightful!
Thus concludes the <s>Nakulīśa-Pāśupata</s> philosophy in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Now the <s>Śaiva</s> (Śaiva Siddhānta) Philosophy

children.text:
tam imaṃ parameśvaraḥ karmādinirapekṣaḥ kāraṇam iti pakṣaṃ
          vaiṣamyanaighṛṇyadoṣadūṣitatvāt pratikṣipantaḥ kecana māheśvarāḥ śaivāgamasiddhāntatattvaṃ
          yathāvad īkṣamāṇāḥ karmādisāpekṣaḥ parameśvaraḥ kāraṇam iti pakṣaṃ kaṣīkurvāṇāḥ
          pakṣāntaram upakṣipanti patipaśupāśabhedāt trayaḥ padārthā iti/
children.translated_text: Certain <s>Māheśvaras</s> (Śaiva theologians), rejecting the position that 'the Supreme Lord is the cause independent of <s>karma</s> and the like' — because it is vitiated by the faults of partiality and cruelty — properly examining the truth of the <s>Śaivāgama</s> (Śaiva scriptural tradition), polishing the position that 'the Supreme Lord is the cause dependent on <s>karma</s> and the like,' introduce another thesis: 'There are three categories, distinguished as <s>pati</s> (lord), <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), and <s>pāśa</s> (bond).'
As stated by the knowers of the essence of the <s>Tantra</s>:
'The lord of the world, having condensed the great <s>Tantra</s> — which has three categories and four sections —

children.text: sūtreṇaikena saṃkṣipya prāha vistarataḥ punaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: into a single <s>sūtra</s>, then expounded it in detail.' Thus.

children.text:
asyārthaḥ/ uktās trayaḥ padārthā yasmin santi tat tripadārthaṃ vidyākriyāyogacaryākhāś
          catvāraḥ pādā yasmiṃs tac catuścaraṇaṃ mahātantram iti/ tatra paśūnām asvatantratvāt
          pāśānām acaitanyāt tadvilakṣaṇasya patyuḥ prathamam uddeśaḥ/ cetanatvasādharmyāt paśūnāṃ
          tadānantaryam/ avaśiṣṭānāṃ pāśānām ante viniveśa iti kramaniyamaḥ/ dīkṣāyāḥ
          paramapuruṣārthahetutvāt tasyāś ca paśupāśeśvarasvarūpanirṇayopāyabhūtena
          mantramantreśvarādimāhātmyaniścāyakena jñānena vinā niṣpādayitum aśakyatvāt
          tadavabodhakasya vidyāpādasya prāthamyam/ anekavidhasāṅgadīkṣāvidhipradarśakasya
          kriyāpādasya tadānantaryam/ yogena vinā nābhimataprāptir iti sāṅgayogajñāpakasya
          yogapādasya taduttaratvam/ vihitācaraṇaniṣiddhavarjanarūpāṃ caryāṃ vinā yogo ’pi na
          nirvahatīti tatpratipādakasya caryāpādasya caramatvam iti vivekaḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is: that in which the three categories are stated is '<s>tripadārtha</s>' (having three categories); that in which the four sections — named <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>kriyā</s> (ritual), <s>yoga</s>, and <s>caryā</s> (conduct) — are [contained] is '<s>catuṣpāda</s>' (having four sections) — this is the great <s>Tantra</s>. Therein, because the <s>paśus</s> (bound souls) lack independence, and because the <s>pāśas</s> (bonds) lack consciousness, the <s>pati</s> (Lord), who is different from both, is mentioned first. Because of the similarity with [the Lord] in being conscious, the <s>paśus</s> come next. The remaining <s>pāśas</s> are placed at the end — this is the fixed order. Because <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) is the cause of the supreme human goal, and because that [initiation] cannot be accomplished without the knowledge that determines the true nature of <s>paśu</s>, <s>pāśa</s>, and <s>Īśvara</s>, and that ascertains the greatness of <s>mantras</s>, <s>mantreśvaras</s>, and the like — the <s>vidyāpāda</s> (section on knowledge) that teaches that [knowledge] comes first. The <s>kriyāpāda</s> (section on ritual), which displays the manifold procedures of initiation with its auxiliaries, comes next. Since without <s>yoga</s> the desired [goal] is not attained, the <s>yogapāda</s> (section on yoga), which teaches <s>yoga</s> with its auxiliaries, follows that. Since even <s>yoga</s> does not succeed without <s>caryā</s> (conduct) — which consists in performing what is enjoined and avoiding what is prohibited — the <s>caryāpāda</s> (section on conduct) that teaches that comes last — this is the discernment.

children.text:
tatra patipadārthaḥ śivo ’bhimataḥ/ muktātmanāṃ vidyeśvarādīnāṃ ca yady api śivatvam asti
          tathāpi parameśvarapāratantryāt svātantryaṃ nāsti/ tataś ca tanukaraṇabhuvanādīnāṃ
          bhāvānāṃ saṃniveśaviśiṣṭatvena kāryatvam avagamyate/ tena ca kāryatvenaiṣāṃ
          buddhimatpūrvakatvam anumīyata ity anumānavaśāt parameśvaraprasiddhir upapadyate/
children.translated_text: Therein, the category of <s>pati</s> (Lord) is considered to be <s>Śiva</s>. Although liberated souls, <s>vidyeśvaras</s> (lords of knowledge), and the like also possess <s>Śiva</s>-hood, nevertheless, because of their dependence on the Supreme Lord, they lack independence. And thus, from the fact that entities such as bodies, instruments, worlds, and the like possess a specific configuration, their being effects is understood. And through that effecthood, their being preceded by an intelligent [cause] is inferred — thus the establishment of the Supreme Lord is justified through inference.

children.text:
nanu dehasyaiva tāvat kāryatvam asiddham/ na hi kvacit kenacit kadācid dehaḥ kriyamāṇo
          dṛṣṭacaraḥ/ satyam/ tathāpi na kenacit kriyamāṇatvaṃ dehasya dṛṣṭam iti
          kartṛdarśanāpahnavo na yujyate/ tasyānumeyatvenāpy upapatteḥ/ tathā hi/ dehādikaṃ kāryaṃ
          bhavitum arhati saṃniveśaviśiṣṭatvād vinaśvaratvād vā ghaṭādivat/ tena ca kāryatvena
          buddhimatpūrvakatvam anumātuṃ sukaram eva/ vimataṃ sakartṛkaṃ kāryatvād ghaṭavat/ yad
          uktasādhanaṃ tad uktasādhyaṃ yathā rathādi

/ na yad evaṃ na tad evaṃ yathātmādi/ parameśvarānumānaprāmāṇyasādhanam
          anyatrākārīty uparamyate/
children.translated_text: Whatever does not [possess] the former does not [possess] the latter — like the self and the like. The demonstration of the validity of inference for the Supreme Lord is set aside here [as having been treated] elsewhere.

Objection: 'But first, the effecthood of the body itself is unestablished! For nowhere has the body been observed being made by anyone at any time.' True. Nevertheless, the denial of the observation of a maker — [arguing that] the body has not been observed being made by anyone — is not justified. Because [the maker] can be established as inferable. For thus: the body and the like deserve to be effects — because they possess a specific configuration, or because they are perishable — like a pot and the like. And through that effecthood, it is easy to infer that they are preceded by an intelligent [being]. The subject of dispute possesses a maker, because it is an effect — like a pot. Whatever possesses the stated probans possesses the stated probandum — like a chariot and the like.
'This ignorant creature (<s>jantu</s>), powerless over its own happiness and sorrow,

children.text: īśvaraprerito gacchet svargaṃ vā śvabhram eva vā//
children.translated_text: impelled by the Lord, goes either to heaven or to the abyss' —

children.text:
iti nyāyena prāṇikṛtakarmāpekṣayā parameśvarasya kartṛtvopapatteḥ/ na ca
          svātantryavihatir iti vācyam/ karaṇāpekṣayā kartuḥ svātantryavihater anupalambhāt/
          koṣādhyakṣāpekṣasya rājñaḥ prasādādinā dānavat/
children.translated_text: by this principle, the agency of the Supreme Lord is justified with reference to the <s>karma</s> performed by living beings. Nor should it be said that [His] independence is violated — because no violation of the independence of an agent who depends on instruments is observed. Just as a king who depends on a treasurer [is not thereby rendered non-independent] in bestowing gifts and the like.
As stated by the <s>Siddha</s>-gurus (accomplished masters):
'That an independent [agent] cannot be caused to act [by another], and that he is the employer of instruments and the like —

children.text: kartuḥ svātantryam etad dhi na karmādyanapekṣatā// iti/
children.translated_text: this indeed is the independence of the agent, not [the claim of being] independent of <s>karma</s> and the like.' Thus.

children.text:
tathā ca tattatkarmāśayavaśād bhogatatsādhanatadupādānādiviśeṣajñaḥ kartānumānādisiddha
          iti siddham/ tad idam uktaṃ tatrabhavadbhir bṛhaspatibhiḥ —
children.translated_text: And thus, [the Lord], who knows — through the force of the accumulated <s>karma</s> of each [soul] — the particular enjoyments, the means of enjoyment, and the material causes thereof, is established as the agent through inference and the like. This has been stated by the revered <s>Bṛhaspati</s>:
'He who knows the enjoyments, the means of enjoyment, their material causes, and the like in this [world] —

children.text: tam ṛte bhaven na hīdaṃ puṃskarmāśayavipākajñam// iti/
children.translated_text: without Him, this [world] could not exist, [for He is] the one who knows the ripening of the <s>karma</s>-impressions of beings.' Thus.
And elsewhere too —
Everything that is the subject of dispute has an intelligent agent as its prior [cause],

children.text: kāryatvād āvayoḥ siddhaṃ kāryaṃ kumbhādikaṃ yathā// iti/
children.translated_text: because of being an effect — as is established for both of us — like a pot and the like.
Section 7.49

children.text: sarvakartṛtvād evāsya sarvajñatvaṃ siddham/ ajñasya karaṇāsaṃbhavāt/ uktaṃ ca śrīmanmṛgendre
A, ASS, IV. See also Torella 1980: 387.

children.translated_text: From his being the creator of all, his omniscience is also established, since it is impossible for an ignorant being to create. And it is stated in the glorious <s>Mṛgendra</s> [Āgama]:
"He is omniscient because of being the creator of all, together with means, auxiliaries, and fruits;

children.text: yo yaj jānāti kurute sa tad eveti susthitam// iti/
children.translated_text: whoever knows something does that very thing — this is well established."
Section 7.53

children.text:
astu tarhi svatantra īśvaraḥ kartā/ sa tu nāśarīraḥ/ ghaṭādikāryasya śarīravatā
          kulālādinā kriyamāṇatvadarśanāt/ śarīravattve cāsmadādivad īśvaraḥ kleśayukto ’sarvajñaḥ
          parimitaśaktiṃ prāpnuyād iti cet — maivaṃ maṃsthāḥ/ aśarīrasyāpy ātmanaḥ
          svaśarīraspandādau kartṛtvadarśanāt/ abhyupagamyāpi brūmahe/ śarīravattve ’pi bhagavato na
          prāguktadoṣānuṣaṅgaḥ/ parameśvarasya hi malakarmādipāśajālāsaṃbhavena prākṛtaṃ śarīraṃ na
          bhavati/ kiṃ tu śāktam/ śaktirūpair īśānādibhiḥ pañcabhir mantrair mastakādikalpanāyām
          īśānamastakas tatpuruṣavaktro ’ghorahṛdayo vāmadevaguhyaḥ sadyojātapāda īśvara iti
          prasiddhyā yathākramam anugrahatirobhāvādānarakṣaṇotpattilakṣaṇakṛtyapañcakakāraṇam
children.translated_text: Let the Lord then be an independent creator; but he cannot be bodiless. Because the effect, such as a pot, is seen to be made by an embodied [agent] such as a potter. And if [he is] embodied, then like us, the Lord would be afflicted by suffering, non-omniscient, and would attain limited power — if [one objects] thus — do not think so! Because agency is observed even for a bodiless Self, in the movement and the like of one's own body. And even accepting [embodiment], we say: Even if the Blessed Lord has a body, the previously stated defects do not attach [to him]. For the Supreme Lord, since the net of bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) such as <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>karma</s>, and the like is impossible [for him], his body is not material (<s>prākṛta</s>) but rather is made of <s>Śakti</s> (power). [His body], with the head and other [parts] fashioned by the five <s>mantras</s> of the form of power — <s>Īśāna</s> and the others — [<s>Śiva</s>] is well known as: <s>Īśāna</s>-headed, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>-faced, <s>Aghora</s>-hearted, <s>Vāmadeva</s>-[as his] secret part, <s>Sadyojāta</s>-[as his] feet — and is the cause of the fivefold activity (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>) characterized respectively by grace (<s>anugraha</s>), concealment (<s>tirobhāva</s>), withdrawal, protection, and creation;

children.text: svecchānirmitaṃ taccharīraṃ na cāsmaccharīrasadṛśam/ tad uktam śrīmanmṛgendraiḥ —
children.translated_text: that body, constructed by his own will, is not similar to our body. As stated in the glorious <s>Mṛgendra</s>:

children.text: malādyasaṃbhavāc chāktaṃ vapur naitādṛśaṃ prabhoḥ iti/
children.translated_text: "Because of the impossibility of <s>mala</s> (impurity) and the like, the body of the Lord is made of <s>Śakti</s>, not of this [material] kind."
Section 7.65
And elsewhere:
"That body, [composed] of the five <s>mantras</s> employed in the fivefold activity,
possesses the head and the other [parts]."
born from <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, and <s>Vāma</s>,
Section 7.68

children.text:
nanu pañcavaktras tripañcadṛg ityādināgameṣu parameśvarasya mukhyata eva
          śarīrendriyādiyogaḥ śrūyata iti cet — satyam/ nirākāre dhyānapūjādyasaṃbhavena
          bhaktānugrahakāraṇāya tattadākāragrahaṇāvirodhāt/ tad uktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare —
children.translated_text: Now, if [one argues]: In the <s>Āgamas</s>, by statements such as "five-faced, fifteen-eyed" and the like, the conjunction of the Supreme Lord with body, sense-organs, and the like is heard in the primary sense — truly so. Because, for a formless [being], meditation, worship, and the like being impossible, there is no contradiction in his assuming various forms for the purpose of gracing his devotees. As stated in the glorious <s>Pauṣkara</s>:

children.text: sādhakasya tu rakṣārthaṃ tasya rūpam idaṃ smṛtam/ iti/
children.translated_text: "For the protection of the practitioner, this form of his is remembered."
Section 7.73
And elsewhere:
"You are necessarily to be worshipped as having form,

children.text: na vastv anākāram upaiti buddhiḥ/ iti/
children.translated_text: for the intellect does not approach a formless reality."
Section 7.76
And the fivefold activity (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>) has been elaborated by King <s>Bhoja</s>:
"His fivefold activity is: creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>), dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>), concealment (<s>tirobhāva</s>),
and likewise the performance of grace (<s>anugraha</s>) — [these] are proclaimed for this one who is eternally risen."
Section 7.79

children.text:
etac ca kṛtyapañcakaṃ śuddhādhvaviṣaye sākṣāc chivakartṛkaṃ kṛcchrādhvaviṣaye tv
          anantādidvāreṇeti vivekaḥ/ tad uktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe —
children.translated_text: And this fivefold activity, in the domain of the pure path (<s>śuddhādhvan</s>), is directly performed by <s>Śiva</s>; but in the domain of the impure path (<s>kṛcchrādhvan</s>), it is performed through <s>Ananta</s> and the other [agents] — this is the distinction. As stated in the glorious <s>Kiraṇa</s> [Āgama]:
— thus.
"In the pure path, <s>Śiva</s> is declared to be the agent; <s>Ananta</s> is the lord in the impure [path]"
Section 7.82

children.text:
muktātmaśivānāṃ savācakānāṃ śivatvaprāptisādhanena dīkṣādinopāyakalāpena saha
          patipadārthe saṃgrahaḥ kṛta iti boddhavyam/ tad itthaṃ patipadārtho nirūpitaḥ/
children.translated_text: liberated souls, and <s>Śiva</s> himself — together with their designators and with the aggregate of means such as initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and the like for attaining <s>Śivatva</s>. This should be understood. Thus the meaning of the <s>pati</s> category has been determined.

And thus, by the word "<s>Śiva</s>," the summary is made of the meaning of the <s>pati</s> (lord) category: those who possess <s>Śivatva</s> (the nature of <s>Śiva</s>) — the <s>mantras</s>, <s>mantreśvaras</s> (lords of <s>mantras</s>), <s>mantramaheśvaras</s> (great lords of <s>mantras</s>),
Section 7.86

children.text:
kṣetrajñādipadavedaniyo jīvātmā paśuḥ/ na tu cārvākādivad dehādirūpaḥ/ nānyadṛṣṭaṃ
          smaraty anya iti nyāyena pratisaṃdhānānupapatteḥ/ nāpi naiyāyikādivat prakāśyaḥ/
          anavasthānaprasaṅgāt/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: atomic in size, knowable through the designations <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower) and the like, is the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). It is not of the form of the body and the like, as the <s>Cārvākas</s> and others [hold], because of the impossibility of recognition (<s>pratisaṃdhāna</s>), by the principle that "one who has not seen otherwise does not remember [what was not experienced]." Nor is it an object of illumination, as for the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others, because of the absurd consequence of infinite regress. As stated:
Now the meaning of the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) category is determined. The individual soul (<s>jīvātman</s>),

children.text: ātmā yadi bhaven meyas tasya mātā bhavet paraḥ/
children.translated_text: "If the Self were a knowable object, its knower would be another;

children.text: para ātmā tadānīṃ syāt sa paro yadi dṛśyate// iti/
children.translated_text: that other would then be the Self; and if it too is perceived [by yet another] —"
Section 7.92

children.text:
na ca jainavad avyāpakaḥ/ nāpi bauddhavat kṣaṇikaḥ/ deśakālābhyām anavacchinnatvāt/ tad
          apy uktam —
children.translated_text: Nor is it non-pervasive, as for the <s>Jainas</s>. Nor is it momentary, as for the Buddhists — because it is unlimited by place and time. This too has been stated:
"A reality whose existence is unlimited by place and time —

children.text: tan nityaṃ vibhu cecchantīty ātmano vibhunityatā iti/
children.translated_text: that is eternal and all-pervasive, they desire; thus the Self's all-pervasiveness and eternity."
Section 7.96

children.text:
nāpy advaitavādinām ivaikaḥ/ bhogapratiniyamasya puruṣabahutvajñāpakasya saṃbhavāt/ nāpi
          sāṃkhyānām ivākartā/ pāśajālāpohane
          nityaniratiśayadṛkkriyārūpacaitanyātmakaśivatvaśravaṇāt/ tad uktaṃ śrīmanmṛgendraiḥ —
          pāśānte śivatāśruteḥ — iti/
children.translated_text: Nor is it one, as for the Advaitins, because the restriction of experience to [specific individuals] — which indicates the multiplicity of persons — is possible. Nor is it a non-agent, as for the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, because it is heard that when the net of bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) is removed, [the soul attains] <s>Śivatva</s>, which is of the nature of consciousness in the form of eternal, unsurpassed cognition (<s>dṛk</s>) and action (<s>kriyā</s>). As stated in the glorious <s>Mṛgendra</s>: "Because <s>Śivatva</s> is heard at the end of the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>)" — thus.

children.text: caitanyaṃ dṛkkriyārūpaṃ tad asty ātmani sarvadā/
children.translated_text: "Consciousness, which is of the form of cognition and action, always exists in the Self

children.text: sarvataś ca yato muktau śrūyate sarvatomukham// iti/
children.translated_text: and in all directions; because in liberation it is heard to be all-faced."
Section 7.102
And in the <s>Tattvaprakāśa</s> as well:

children.text: muktātmāno ’pi śivāḥ kiṃ tv ete yatprasādato muktāḥ/
children.translated_text: "Liberated souls too are <s>Śivas</s>; but these have been liberated by whose grace —
he, the one beginninglessly liberated, should be known as having the body of the five <s>mantras</s>."
Section 7.105

children.text:
paśus trividhaḥ/ vijñānākalapralayākalasakalabhedāt/ tatra prathamo vijñānayogasaṃnyāsair
          bhogena vā karmakṣaye sati karmakṣayārthasya kalādibhogabandhasyābhāvāt
          kevalamalamātrayukto vijñānākala iti vyapadiśyate/ dvitīyas tu pralayena kalāder
          upasaṃhārān malakarmayuktaḥ pralayākala iti vyavahriyate/ tṛtīyas tu
          malamāyākarmātmakabandhatrayasahitaḥ sakala iti saṃlapyate/
children.translated_text: The <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) is threefold, through the division into <s>vijñānākala</s>, <s>pralayākala</s>, and <s>sakala</s>. Therein, the first — when <s>karma</s> has been exhausted through the yoga of knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>), renunciation, or through experience (<s>bhoga</s>), and since the bond of enjoyment beginning with <s>kalā</s> and the like, which serves the purpose of exhausting <s>karma</s>, is absent — being endowed with <s>mala</s> (impurity) alone, is designated as <s>vijñānākala</s>. The second, because of the withdrawal of <s>kalā</s> and the like through cosmic dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), is endowed with <s>mala</s> and <s>karma</s>, and is conventionally termed <s>pralayākala</s>. The third, accompanied by the threefold bond consisting of <s>mala</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>karma</s>, is called <s>sakala</s>.
Section 7.111

children.text:
tatra prathamo dviprakāro bhavati samāptakaluṣāsamāptakaluṣabhedāt/ tatrādyān
          kāluṣyaparipākavataḥ puruṣadhaureyān adhikārayogyān anugṛhyānantādividyeśvarāṣṭapadaṃ
          prāpayati/ tad vidyeśvarāṣṭakaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ bahudaivatye —
children.translated_text: Therein, the first is of two kinds, through the division of those whose impurity is ripe and those whose impurity is unripe. Of these, <s>Śiva</s> graces the first — those foremost persons whose impurity has matured, who are worthy of authority — and brings them to the eightfold station of <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> (Lords of Knowledge), such as <s>Ananta</s> and others. That group of eight <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> is specified in the <s>Bahudaivatya</s>:

children.text: anantaś caiva sūkṣmaś ca tathaiva ca śivottamaḥ/
children.translated_text: "<s>Ananta</s>, and <s>Sūkṣma</s>, and likewise <s>Śivottama</s>,
<s>Ekanetra</s>, and likewise <s>Ekarudra</s>, and <s>Trimūrtika</s>,

children.text: śrīkaṇṭhaś ca śikhaṇḍī ca proktā vidyeśvarā ime/ iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, and <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> — these are proclaimed as the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>."
Section 7.118

children.text:
antyān saptakoṭisaṃkhyātān mantrān anugrahakaraṇān vidhatte/ tad uktaṃ tattvaprakāśe
          —
children.translated_text: The latter — numbering seventy million — he appoints as <s>mantras</s> (divine agents) that perform the act of grace. As stated in the <s>Tattvaprakāśa</s>:
"Bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) are said to be threefold: <s>vijñānākala</s>, <s>pralayākala</s>, and <s>sakala</s>.
Of these, the first is endowed with <s>mala</s> alone; the second would be endowed with <s>mala</s> and <s>karma</s>.

children.text: malamāyākarmayutaḥ sakalas teṣu dvidhā bhaved ādyaḥ/
children.translated_text: The one endowed with <s>mala</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>karma</s> is the <s>sakala</s>. Of these, the first is of two kinds:
the first has mature impurity; the second would have immature impurity.

children.text: ādyān anugṛhya śivo vidyeśatve niyojayaty aṣṭau/
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, having graced the first [group], appoints eight as <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>;

children.text: mantrāṃś ca karoty aparāṃs te coktāḥ koṭayaḥ sapta// iti/
children.translated_text: and he makes the others into <s>mantras</s> — they are said to number seven <s>koṭis</s> (seventy million)."
Section 7.126
And <s>Somaśambhu</s> too has stated:
"The first is named <s>vijñānākala</s>; the second is the <s>pralayākala</s>;
the third, the <s>sakala</s> — in scripture, the one to be graced is considered threefold.
Of these, the first is endowed with <s>mala</s> alone; the other with <s>mala</s> and <s>karma</s>;
and the <s>sakala</s> is endowed with the principles (<s>tattvas</s>) from <s>kalā</s> down to earth."
Section 7.131

children.text:
pralayākalo ’pi dvividhaḥ — pakvapāśadvayas tadvilakṣaṇaś ca/ tatra prathamo mokṣaṃ
          prāpnoti/ dvitīyas tu puryaṣṭakayutaḥ karmavaśān nānāvidhajanmabhāg bhavati/ tad apy uktaṃ
          tattvaprakāśe —
children.translated_text: The <s>pralayākala</s> too is of two kinds: one whose twofold bond has ripened, and one different from that. Of these, the first attains liberation. But the second, endowed with the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), through the force of <s>karma</s>, partakes of various kinds of births. This too is stated in the <s>Tattvaprakāśa</s>:
travel [through births];
"Among the <s>pralayākalas</s>, those whose <s>mala</s> and <s>karma</s> are unripe
endowed with the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> body, [they wander] in all wombs through the force of <s>karma</s>."
Section 7.136
The <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (eightfold subtle body) is also specified therein:

children.text: syāt puryaṣṭakam antaḥkaraṇaṃ dhīkarma karaṇāni/ iti/
children.translated_text: "The <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> would be: the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), the intellect (<s>dhī</s>), <s>karma</s>, and the sense organs (<s>karaṇa</s>)."
Section 7.138

children.text:
vivṛtaṃ cāghoraśivācāryeṇa — puryaṣṭakaṃ nāma pratipuruṣaṃ niyataḥ sargād ārabhya
          kalpāntaṃ mokṣāntaṃ vā sthitaḥ pṛthivyādikalāparyantas triṃśattattvātmakaḥ sūkṣmo dehaḥ/
          tathā coktaṃ tattvasaṃgrahe —
children.translated_text: And <s>Aghoraśivācārya</s> has explained: The <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> is the subtle body, consisting of thirty principles (<s>tattvas</s>) from earth up to <s>kalā</s>, which is fixed for each individual person, existing from the [beginning of] creation until the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) or until liberation. And thus it is stated in the <s>Tattvasaṃgraha</s>:
"This group of principles (<s>tattvas</s>) beginning with earth, ending with <s>kalā</s>, fixed for each individual,

children.text: paryaṭati karmavaśād bhuvanajadeheṣv ayaṃ ca sarveṣu// iti/
children.translated_text: wanders through the force of <s>karma</s> in all world-bodies and insentient bodies."

children.text:
tathā cāyam arthaḥ samapadyata — antaḥkaraṇaśabdena manobuddhyahaṃkāravācinānyāny api
          puṃso bhogakriyāyām antaraṅgāṇi kalākālaniyatividyārāgaprakṛtiguṇākhyāni sapta tattvāny
          upalakṣyante/ dhīkarmaśabdena jñeyāni pañca bhūtāni tatkāraṇāni ca tanmātrāṇi vivakṣyante/
          karaṇaśabdena jñānakarmendriyadaśakaṃ saṃgṛhyate/ nanu śrīmatkālottare —
children.translated_text: And thus this meaning is explained: By the term "internal organ" (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), which denotes mind (<s>manas</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), and ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), seven other principles that are internal to a person's enjoyment and activity are also indicated — namely, <s>kalā</s> (limited agency), <s>kālaniyati</s> (temporal determination), <s>vidyā</s> (limited knowledge), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), and the qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) of <s>Prakṛti</s>. By the term "objects of intellect" (<s>dhīkarma</s>), the five gross elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) that are to be known and their causes, the five subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>), are intended. By the term "instruments" (<s>karaṇa</s>), the tenfold knowledge-and-action sense organs are included. Now, in the glorious <s>Kālottara</s>:

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśas tathā rūpaṃ raso gandhaś ca pañcakam/
children.translated_text: "Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — the five,

children.text: buddhir manas tv ahaṃkāraḥ puryaṣṭakam udāhṛtam//
children.translated_text: intellect, mind, and ego — [these] are declared as the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>" —

children.text: iti śrūyate/ tat katham anyathā kathyate/ addhā/ ata eva ca tatrabhavatā rāmakaṇṭhena
tat sūtraṃ triṃśattattvaparatayā vyākhyāyīty alam atiprapañcena/
children.translated_text: has explained that <s>sūtra</s> as referring to the thirty principles — enough with excessive elaboration.
thus it is heard. How then is it stated otherwise? Indeed! And for that very reason, the revered <s>Rāmakaṇṭha</s>
Section 7.152

children.text:
tathāpi kathaṃ punar asya puryaṣṭakatvam/
          bhūtatanmātrabuddhīndriyakarmendriyāntaḥkaraṇasaṃjñaiḥ pañcabhir vargais tatkāraṇena
          guṇatattvena tadāpūrakeṇa pradhānena kalādipañcakātmanā vargeṇa cārabdhatvād ity
          avirodhaḥ/ tatra puryaṣṭakayutān viśiṣṭapuṇyasaṃpannān kāṃścid anugṛhya bhuvanapatitvam
          atra maheśvaro ’nantaḥ prayacchati/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, how is this [called] <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> ("city of eight")? Because it is constituted by five groups designated as gross elements, subtle elements, knowledge sense-organs, action sense-organs, and internal organ — together with the <s>guṇa</s>-principle as their cause, <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) as their complement, and the group consisting of the fivefold <s>kalā</s> and so forth — there is no contradiction. Therein, the Great Lord <s>Ananta</s>, having graced certain [souls] endowed with the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> and possessing distinguished merit, grants them here the lordship of worlds. As stated:

children.text: kāṃścid anugṛhya vitarati bhuvanapatitvaṃ maheśvaras teṣām/ iti/
children.translated_text: "Having graced certain [souls], <s>Maheśvara</s> bestows upon them the lordship of worlds."
Section 7.158

children.text:
sakalo ’pi dvividhaḥ/ pakvakaluṣāpakvakaluṣabhedāt/ tatrādyān parameśvaras
          tatparipākaparipāṭyā tadanuguṇaśaktipātena maṇḍalyādyaṣṭādaśottaraśatamantreśvarapadaṃ
          prāpayati/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: The <s>sakala</s> too is of two kinds, through the division of those with mature and immature impurity. Of these, the first — the Supreme Lord, through the sequence of the maturation of their [impurity], with a descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) appropriate to that, brings them to the station of the one hundred and eighteen <s>Mantreśvaras</s> (Lords of <s>Mantras</s>) such as <s>Maṇḍalin</s> and others. As stated:

children.text: śeṣā bhavanti sakalāḥ kalādiyogād aharmukhe kāle/
children.translated_text: "The remaining <s>sakalas</s>, through their conjunction with <s>kalā</s> and the like, in the time facing day —

children.text: śatam aṣṭādaśa teṣāṃ kurute svayam eva mantreśān//
children.translated_text: one hundred and eighteen of them, he himself makes into <s>Mantreśvaras</s>.

children.text: tatrāṣṭau maṇḍalinaḥ krodhādyās tatsamāś ca vīreśaḥ/
children.translated_text: Of these, eight are <s>Maṇḍalins</s>, the <s>Krodhas</s> and others equal to them, and <s>Vīreśa</s>,

children.text: śrīkaṇṭhaḥ śatarudrāḥ śatam ity aṣṭādaśābhyadhikam// iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, the <s>Śatarudras</s> — one hundred, plus eighteen above."
Section 7.165

children.text:
tatparipākādhikyānurodhena śaktyupasaṃhāreṇa dīkṣākaraṇena mokṣaprado bhavaty
          ācāryamūrtim āsthāya parameśvaraḥ/ tad apy uktam —
children.translated_text: In accordance with the degree of maturation of their [impurity], the Supreme Lord — through the withdrawal of power (<s>śaktyupasaṃhāra</s>) and the performance of initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) — assuming the form of a preceptor (<s>ācārya</s>), becomes the bestower of liberation. This too has been stated:
"Those whose <s>mala</s> has matured, through the descent of power that is the cause of their eradication,

children.text: yojayati pare tattve sa dīkṣayācāryamūrtisthaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: he, standing in the form of the preceptor, joins them to the supreme principle through initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>)."
Section 7.169
And in the glorious <s>Mṛgendra</s> as well:
"He removes the net of bonds of the soul (<s>aṇu</s>) that was previously bound."
Section 7.171

children.text:
vyākṛtaṃ ca nārāyaṇkaṇṭhena/ tat sarvaṃ tata evāvadhāryam/ asmābhis tu vistarabhiyā na
          prastūyate/ apakvakaluṣān baddhān aṇūn bhogabhājo vidhatte parameśvaraḥ karmavaśāt/ tad
          apy uktam —
children.translated_text: And this has been explained by <s>Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha</s>; all that should be ascertained from that very [source]. But we do not elaborate, out of fear of prolixity. The Supreme Lord, through the force of <s>karma</s>, assigns the remaining bound souls (<s>aṇus</s>), whose impurity is immature, to the enjoyment of experience. This too has been stated:

children.text: baddhāñ śeṣān aparān viniyuṅkte bhogabhuktaye puṃsaḥ/
children.translated_text: "The remaining bound ones, he appoints for the enjoyment of experience of the person;

children.text: tatkarmaṇām anugamād ity evaṃ kīrtitāḥ paśavaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: following their <s>karmas</s> — thus the <s>paśus</s> (bound souls) have been described."
Section 7.176

children.text: atha pāśapadārthaḥ kathyate/ pāśaś caturvidhaḥ/ malakarmamāyārodhaśaktibhedāt/ nanu —
children.translated_text: Now the meaning of the <s>pāśa</s> (bond) category is stated. The <s>pāśa</s> is fourfold, through the division into <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>karma</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>rodhaśakti</s> (obstructing power). Now:

children.text: śaivāgameṣu mukhyaṃ patipaśupāśā iti kramāt tritayam/
children.translated_text: "In the <s>Śaiva Āgamas</s>, the primary triad is: <s>pati</s> (lord), <s>paśu</s> (soul), and <s>pāśa</s> (bond), in order.

children.text: tatra patiḥ śiva uktaḥ paśavo hy aṇavo ’rthapañcakaṃ pāśāḥ//
children.translated_text: Therein, <s>pati</s> is said to be <s>Śiva</s>; the <s>paśus</s> are the atomic [souls]; the <s>pāśas</s> are the fivefold [categories]."

children.text:
iti pāśaḥ pañcavidhaḥ kathyate/ tat kathaṃ caturvidha iti gaṇyate/ ucyate — bindor
          māyātmanaḥ śivatattvapadavedanīyasya śivapadaprāptilakṣaṇaparamamuktyapekṣayā pāśatve ’pi
          tadyogasya vidyeśvarādipadaprāptihetutvenāparamuktitvāt pāśatvenānupādānam ity avirodhaḥ/
          ata evoktaṃ tattvaprakāśe — pāśāś caturvidhāḥ syur iti/ śrīmanmṛgendre ’pi —
children.translated_text: Thus the bond (<s>pāśa</s>) is said to be fivefold. Then why is it counted as fourfold? It is explained: although <s>bindu</s>, which is of the nature of <s>Māyā</s> and cognizable as the <s>Śiva</s>-principle, has the nature of a bond in relation to supreme liberation characterized by the attainment of the <s>Śiva</s>-state, since its conjunction is the cause of attaining the station of <s>Vidyeśvara</s> and the like — constituting subordinate liberation — it is not taken as a bond [in this enumeration]. Thus there is no contradiction. For this very reason it is stated in the <s>Tattvaprakāśa</s>: 'The bonds are fourfold.' In the glorious <s>Mṛgendra</s> also:
'Covering (<s>prāvṛti</s>), power (<s>bala</s>), <s>karma</s>, and the product of <s>Māyā</s> — fourfold

children.text: pāśajālaṃ samāsena dharmā nāmnaiva kīrtitāḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: is the net of bonds, in brief, called by the name <s>dharmas</s>.' Thus.

children.text:
asyārthaḥ — prāvṛṇoti prakarṣeṇācchādayaty ātmanaḥ svābhāvikyau dṛkkriye iti prāvṛtir
          aśucir malaḥ/ sa ca īṣṭe svātantryeṇeti īśaḥ/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: The meaning of this: That which covers (<s>prāvṛṇoti</s>), i.e., intensely conceals the soul's own natural [powers of] seeing and acting, is the covering (<s>prāvṛti</s>) — the impure <s>mala</s> (impurity). And it 'rules' (<s>īṣṭe</s>) autonomously — hence [it is called] 'lord' (<s>īśa</s>). As stated:

children.text: eko hy anekaśaktir dṛkkriyayoś chādako malaḥ puṃsaḥ/
children.translated_text: '<s>Mala</s>, one yet of many powers, is the concealer of the soul's seeing and acting;
it should be understood like the husk on a grain of rice, or like the tarnish on copper.' Thus.

children.text:
balaṃ rodhaśaktiḥ/ asyāḥ śivaśakteḥ pāśādhiṣṭhānena puruṣatirodhāyakatvād upacāreṇa
          pāśatvam/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: <s>Bala</s> (power) is the obstructing power. Because this power of <s>Śiva</s>, through its presiding over the bonds, conceals the soul (<s>puruṣa</s>), it is figuratively called a bond. As stated:

children.text: tāsām ahaṃ varā śaktiḥ sarvānugrāhikā śivā/
children.translated_text: 'I am the supreme power among those, the auspicious one that bestows grace upon all;

children.text: dharmānuvartanād eva pāśa ity upacaryate// iti/
children.translated_text: merely from conforming to the [nature of] bonds, I am figuratively called a bond.' Thus.

children.text:
kriyate phalārthibhir iti karma dharmādharmātmakaṃ bījāṅkuravat pravāharūpeṇānādi/
          yathoktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe —
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> is that which is performed by those who desire fruits — consisting of merit and demerit (<s>dharmādharma</s>), beginningless in the form of a stream like seed and sprout. As stated in the glorious <s>Kiraṇa</s>:
beginningless;
'Just as <s>mala</s> is beginningless for him, <s>karma</s> too is likewise

children.text: yady anādi na saṃsiddhaṃ vaicitryaṃ kena hetunā// iti/
children.translated_text: if it is beginningless, then by what cause is [its] variety established?' Thus.

children.text:
māty asyām śaktyātmanā pralaye sarvaṃ jagat sṛṣṭau vyaktim āyātīti māyā yathoktaṃ
          śrīmatsaurabheye —
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> is that in which, in the form of power, the entire world is merged at dissolution and comes to manifestation at creation. As stated in the glorious <s>Saurabheya</s>:
'The effects merged therein in the form of power at the great dissolution

children.text: vikṛtau vyaktim āyāti sā kāryeṇa kalādinā// iti/
children.translated_text: come to manifestation in the transformation — she, through her effects such as <s>Kalā</s> and the rest.' Thus.

children.text:
yady apy atra bahu vaktavyam asti tathāpi granthabhūyastvabhayād uparamyate/ tad itthaṃ
          patipaśupāśapadārthās trayaḥ pradarśitāḥ/
children.translated_text: Although much remains to be said here, we desist for fear of the volume of the treatise. Thus, the three categories of <s>Pati</s> (Lord), <s>Paśu</s> (bound soul), and <s>Pāśa</s> (bond) have been set forth.

children.text: patividye tathāvidyā paśuḥ pāśaś ca kāraṇam/
children.translated_text: 'The Lord's knowledge, likewise ignorance, the bound soul, the bond, and causality,

children.text: tannivṛttāv iti proktāḥ padārthāḥ ṣaṭ samāsataḥ//
children.translated_text: and the cessation of that — thus six categories have been stated in brief.'

children.text:
ityādinā prakārāntaraṃ jñānaratnāvalyādau prasiddham/ sarvaṃ tata evāvagantavyam iti
          sarvaṃ samañjasam//
children.translated_text: By this and similar [verses], an alternative classification is well-known in the <s>Jñānaratnāvalī</s> and the like. Everything should be understood from that [source] itself. All is coherent.
Thus [ends] the Śaiva system in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Now, the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition) system. //8//

children.text:
atrāpekṣāvihīnānāṃ jaḍānāṃ kāraṇatvaṃ duṣyatīty aparituṣyanto matāntaram anviṣyantaḥ
          parameśvarecchāvaśād eva jagannirmāṇaṃ parighuṣyantaḥ svasaṃvedanopapattyāgamasiddhapratyagātmatādātmyo

nānāvidhamānameyādibhedābhedaśāliparameśvaro
          ’nanyamukhaprekṣitvalakṣaṇasvātantryabhāk svātmadarpaṇe bhāvān pratibimbavad
          avabhāsayatīti bhaṇanto bāhyābhyantaracaryāprāṇāyāmādikleśaprayāsakalāpavaidhuryeṇa
          sarvasulabham
children.translated_text: endowed with difference and non-difference of manifold knower, known, and means of knowledge — manifests entities in the mirror of his own Self like reflections, possessing autonomy characterized by not looking toward another's face [i.e., complete independence]; and proclaiming that, by doing away with the aggregate of external and internal observances, <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), and the troubles of arduous practices,
the novel

children.text:
pratyabhijñāmātraṃ
          parāparasiddhyupāyam abhyupagacchantaḥ pare māheśvarāḥ pratyabhijñāśāstram
          abhyasyanti/
children.translated_text: and universally accessible means of mere recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), which is the method for both the supreme and subordinate accomplishments — these other <s>Māheśvaras</s> (Śaivas) study the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> scripture.

Here, dissatisfied [with the view] that the causality of insentient things devoid of intentionality is defective, seeking an alternative doctrine, proclaiming that the construction of the world [occurs] solely by the will of the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), [asserting that] the supreme Lord — identical with the inner Self established through self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), reasoning, and scripture —
Its extent has also been delineated by the examiners:

children.text: sūtraṃ vṛttir vivṛtir laghvī bṛhatīty ubhe vimarśinyau/
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Sūtra</s>, the <s>Vṛtti</s>, the <s>Vivṛti</s>, and the two <s>Vimarśinīs</s> — the short and the long —
and the <s>Prakaraṇavivaraṇapañcaka</s> — this is the body of the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> scripture.'
Therein, the first <s>sūtra</s> is this:
'Having somehow attained the servanthood of <s>Maheśvara</s>,
wishing to benefit the people as well,
I shall demonstrate that recognition of him
which is the cause of the attainment of all prosperity.' Thus.

children.text:
kathaṃcid iti/ parameśvarābhinnagurucaraṇāravindayugalasamārādhanena
          parameśvaraghaṭitenaivety arthaḥ/ āsādyeti/ ā samantāt paripūrṇatayā sādayitvā
          svātmopabhogyatāṃ nirargalāṃ gamayitvā/ tad anena viditavedyatvena parārthaśāstrakaraṇe
          ’dhikāro darśitaḥ/ anyathā pratāraṇam eva prasajyeta/ māyottīrṇā api mahāmāyādhikṛtā
          viṣṇuviriñcyādyā yadīyaiśvaryaleśeneśvarībhūtāḥ sa bhagavān
          anavacchinnaprakāśānandasvātantryaparamārtho maheśvaraḥ/tasya dāsyam/ dīyate ’smai svāminā
          sarvaṃ yathābhilaṣitam iti dāsaḥ/ parameśvarasvarūpasvātantryapātram ity arthaḥ/
          janaśabdenādhikāriviṣayaniyamābhāvaḥ prādarśi/ yasya yasya hīdaṃ svarūpakathanaṃ tasya
          tasya mahāphalaṃ bhavati/ prajñānasyaiva paramārthaphalatvāt/ tathopadiṣṭaṃ śivadṛṣṭau
          paramagurubhir bhagavatsomānandanāthapādaiḥ —
children.translated_text: 'Somehow' (<s>kathaṃcit</s>) means: through the worship of the pair of lotus-feet of the guru who is non-different from the supreme Lord — that is, through an [act] effected by the supreme Lord himself. 'Having attained' (<s>āsādya</s>) means: having completely in all ways accomplished, having brought to a state of unrestricted enjoyability by one's own self. By this, the qualification for composing a treatise for others' benefit is shown through having known all that is to be known; otherwise, mere deception would follow. Those who have transcended <s>Māyā</s> yet preside over <s>Mahāmāyā</s> — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and others — who have become lords by a fraction of his sovereignty, that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the supreme reality of uninterrupted light, bliss, and autonomy, is <s>Maheśvara</s>. 'His servanthood' — <s>dāsa</s> means one to whom the master gives everything as desired; the meaning is: a receptacle for the autonomy that is the essential nature of the supreme Lord. By the word 'people' (<s>jana</s>), the absence of restriction regarding the qualified person is indicated — for whoever hears this teaching of essential nature, for each one it bears great fruit, since knowledge itself is the ultimate fruit. Thus it has been taught in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s> by the supreme guru, the blessed <s>Somānandanātha</s>:
'Once, through a means of knowledge — from scripture or from the guru's word —
the <s>Śiva</s>-nature present in all is known with firm conviction,

children.text: karaṇena nāsti kṛtyaṃ kvāpi bhāvanayāpi vā/
children.translated_text: there is nothing to be done anywhere by [any other] instrument or even by meditation.',

children.text: jñāte suvarṇe karaṇaṃ bhāvanāṃ vā parityajet// iti/
children.translated_text: 'Once gold is known [as gold], one should abandon [further] instruments and meditation [about it].' Thus.

children.text:
apiśabdena svātmanas tadabhinnatām āviṣkurvatā pūrṇatvena svātmani
          parārthasaṃpattyatiriktaprayojanāntarāvakāśaś ca parākṛtaḥ/ parārthaś ca prayojanaṃ
          bhavaty eva/ tallakṣaṇayogāt/ na hy ayaṃ devaśāpaḥ svārtha eva prayojanaṃ na parārtha iti/
          ata evoktam akṣapādena — yam artham adhikṛtya pravartate tat prayojanam iti/ upaśabdaḥ
          sāmīpyārthaḥ/ tena janasya parameśvarasamīpatākaraṇamātraṃ phalam/ ata evāha — samasteti/
          parameśvaratālābhe hi sarvāḥ saṃpadas tanniṣyandamayyaḥ saṃpannā eva rohaṇācalalābhe
          ratnasaṃpada iva/ evaṃ parameśvaratālābhe kim anyat prārthanīyam/ tad uktam utpalācāryaiḥ
          —
children.translated_text: By the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), revealing the non-difference of one's own self from that [Lord], and through fullness in one's own self, the possibility of any purpose other than the attainment of others' welfare is precluded. And benefit to others is indeed a purpose — because of possessing the defining characteristic [of purpose]. For this is not a divine curse that purpose be only self-interest and not other-interest. For this very reason <s>Akṣapāda</s> (<s>Gautama</s>) stated: 'That for the sake of which one engages — that is the purpose.' The prefix 'upa-' means 'proximity.' By that, the fruit is merely bringing people near to the supreme Lord. For this very reason, he says 'all' (<s>samasta</s>) — for when the nature of the supreme Lord is attained, all prosperities, being of his overflow, are already accomplished, like the prosperity of gems when the <s>Rohaṇa</s> mountain is obtained. When the nature of the supreme Lord is attained, what else remains to be sought? As stated by master <s>Utpala</s> (<s>Utpaladeva</s>):
'For those enriched with the wealth of devotion, what else is to be begged for?

children.text: etayā vā daridrāṇāṃ kim anyad apayācitam// iti/
children.translated_text: And for those impoverished of this [devotion], what else is to be begged away?' Thus.

children.text: itthaṃ ṣaṣṭhīsamāsapakṣe prayojanaṃ nirdiṣṭam/ bahuvrīhipakṣe tūpāyaḥ

/ samastasya bāhyābhyantarasya nityasukhāder yā saṃpat siddhis tathātvaprakāśas
          tasyāḥ samyag avāptir yasyāḥ pratyabhijñāyā hetuḥ sā tathoktā/ tasya maheśvarasya
          pratyabhijñā prati ābhimukhyena jñānam/ loke hi sa evāyam caitra iti
          pratisaṃdhānenābhimukhībhūte vastuni jñānaṃ pratyabhijñeti vyavahriyate/ ihāpi prasiddhapurāṇasiddhāgamānumānādiparijñāta
children.translated_text: The complete attainment of that prosperity — the manifestation of the true nature of all that is external and internal, [including] eternal bliss and the rest — that recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) of which is the cause, is so called. Recognition of that <s>Maheśvara</s> means knowledge directed toward [him] face-to-face (<s>abhimukhya</s>). For in the world, when an object is brought face-to-face through identification — 'This is that same <s>Caitra</s>' — the knowledge is conventionally called 'recognition.' Here too, when the supreme Lord, known [to be] of complete powers through well-known <s>Purāṇas</s>, established <s>āgamas</s>, inference, and the like, is [recognized as] present in one's own self, brought face-to-face,

children.text:
paripūrṇaśaktike parameśvare sati svātmany abhimukhībhūte tacchaktipratisaṃdhānena
          jñānam udeti nūnaṃ sa eveśvaro ’ham iti/ tām etāṃ pratyabhijñām upapādayāmi/ upapattiḥ
          saṃbhavaḥ/ saṃbhavatīti tatsamarthācaraṇena prayojaka
children.translated_text: through the identification of his powers, the knowledge arises: 'I am indeed that very Lord!' That very recognition I shall demonstrate (<s>upapādayāmi</s>). 'Demonstration' means possibility; [that which] is made possible — meaning:
I shall bring it about through a competent operation that accomplishes [it]. That is the meaning.
Thus, on the reading as a genitive compound (<s>ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa</s>), the purpose has been indicated. On the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> reading, however, the means [is indicated]:

children.text:
yadīśvarasvabhāva evātmā prakāśate tarhi kim anena pratyabhijñāpradarśanaprayāseneti cet
          — atrāyaṃ samādhiḥ/
children.translated_text: If the self, being of the nature of the Lord, shines forth [by itself], then what is the use of this effort to demonstrate recognition? — To this, here is the resolution:

children.text:
svaprakāśatayā satatam avabhāsamāne ’py ātmani māyāvaśād bhāgena prakāśamāne
          pūrṇatāvabhāsasiddhaye dṛkkriyātmakaśaktyāviṣkaraṇena pratyabhijñā pradarśyate/ tathā ca
          prayogaḥ —
children.translated_text: Although the self is perpetually manifest through self-luminosity, because of <s>Māyā</s> it manifests only partially; for the realization of [its] full manifestation, recognition is demonstrated through the disclosure of [its] power consisting of seeing (<s>dṛk</s>) and acting (<s>kriyā</s>). And thus the formal argument:
— This self is fit to be the supreme Lord;
— because of possessing the power of knowledge and action;

children.text: -yo yāvati jñātā kartā ca sa tāvatīśvaraḥ prasiddha īśvaravad

children.translated_text: or like a king;
— whoever is a knower and agent to whatever degree, is lord to that degree — as is well-known, like the Lord [himself],
— and the self is the knower and agent of the universe;
— therefore, this [self] is the Lord.
because of the adoption of the <s>Naiyāyika</s> position. As stated by the son of <s>Udayākara</s> [i.e., <s>Utpaladeva</s>]:
The resort to the five-membered [syllogism] is [necessary] only in the domain of <s>Māyā</s>,
'Regarding the self — the agent, knower, primordially established <s>Maheśvara</s> —

children.text: ajaḍātmā niṣedhaṃ vā siddhiṃ vā vidadhīta kaḥ//
children.translated_text: who, [the self being] non-inert, could perform either negation or proof?

children.text: kiṃ tu mohavaśād asmin dṛṣṭe ’py anupalakṣite/
children.translated_text: But due to delusion, though it is seen, it is not recognized;
therefore, through the disclosure of [its] powers, this recognition is demonstrated.'
For thus:
'Of all beings here, the foundation is that which depends on the living [soul];

children.text: jñānaṃ kriyā ca bhūtānāṃ jīvatāṃ jīvanaṃ matam//
children.translated_text: knowledge and action of beings are considered the life of the living.',

children.text: tatra jñānaṃ svataḥsiddhaṃ kriyā kāryāśritā satī/
children.translated_text: 'Therein, knowledge is self-established; action, being dependent on [its] effect,

children.text: parair apy upalakṣyeta tathānyajñānam ucyate// iti/
children.translated_text: could be recognized even by others; thus the knowledge of another is spoken of.' Thus.
'And the intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) of these [beings], shaped in the sequence of various objects —

children.text: akramānandacidrūpaḥ pramātā sa maheśvaraḥ// iti ca/
children.translated_text: the knower [who is] of the nature of non-sequential bliss and consciousness, he is <s>Maheśvara</s>.' And thus.
By the venerable <s>Somānandanāthapāda</s> also:

children.text: sadāśivātmanā vetti sadā vetti madātmanā/ ityādi/
children.translated_text: 'In the nature of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, he knows always; in my nature, he knows always' — and so on.
Even at the conclusion of the chapter on knowledge:

children.text: tad aikyena vinā nāsti saṃvidāṃ lokapaddhatiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Without the unity of those [cognitions], there is no worldly course of awarenesses;

children.text: prakāśaikyāt tadekatvaṃ mātaikaḥ sa iti sthitiḥ//
children.translated_text: from the unity of light, their oneness — the established position is that the knower is one.',
'He, by virtue of being a determinate reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), is <s>Maheśvara</s>;

children.text: vimarśa eva devasya śuddhe jñānakriye yataḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: for the Lord's pure knowledge and action are precisely reflective awareness.' Thus.

children.text:
vivṛtaṃ cābhinavaguptācāryaiḥ/ tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ
          vibhāti iti śrutyā prakāśacidrūpamahimnā sarvasya bhāvajātasya bhāsakatvam abhyupeyate/
          tataś ca viṣayaprakāśasya nīlaprakāśaḥ pītaprakāśa iti viṣayoparāgabhedād bhedaḥ/ vastutas
          tu deśakālākārasaṃkocavaikalyād abheda eva/ sa eva caitanyarūpaḥ prakāśaḥ pramātety
          ucyate/ tathā ca paṭhitaṃ śivasūtreṣu — caitanyam ātmeti/ tasya cidrūpatvam
          anavacchinnavimarśatvam ananyonmukhatvam ānandaikaghanatvaṃ māheśvaryam iti paryāyaḥ/ sa
          eva hy ahaṃbhāvātmā

vimarśaḥ śuddhe pāramārthikyau jñānakriye/ tatra prakāśarūpatā jñānam/ svato
          jagannirmātṛtvaṃ kriyā/ tac ca nirūpitaṃ kriyādhikāre —
children.translated_text: is the pure, ultimate knowledge and action. Therein, the nature of light (<s>prakāśa</s>) is knowledge; being the creator of the universe from oneself is action. And that has been determined in the chapter on action:

And it has been elucidated by the master <s>Abhinavagupta</s>: 'Him alone shining, everything shines after; by his light, all this shines' — by this <s>Śruti</s>, through the glory of the consciousness-light (<s>prakāśa</s>), the illumination of the entire class of entities is accepted. And therefore, the difference in the illumination of objects — 'blue-illumination,' 'yellow-illumination' — is due to the differentiation of object-coloring. But in reality, from the absence of contraction of place, time, and form, there is indeed non-difference. That very luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>), of the nature of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), is called the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>). And thus it is recited in the <s>Śiva Sūtras</s>: 'Consciousness is the self' (<s>caitanyam ātmā</s>). Its synonyms are: being of the nature of consciousness, being of unrestricted reflective awareness, not looking toward another, being a mass of bliss alone, and sovereignty (<s>māheśvarya</s>). For that very reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), whose nature is the sense of 'I',
'And this [Lord], because of possessing infinite powers, thus manifests these
this is action, his creatorship.' Thus.
entities by the force of will —
And in the conclusion as well:
'Thus, for one who stands with the universe as one's form — in the forms of pot, cloth, and the like —

children.text: tiṣṭhāsor evam icchaiva hetukartṛkṛtā kriyā// iti/
children.translated_text: this very will, produced by the agent-cause, is action.' Thus.
'When this exists, that exists' — the causality that [is asserted] —
that too is not tenable for insentient things devoid of intentionality.

children.text:
iti nyāyena yato jaḍasya na kāraṇatā na vānīśvarasya cetanasyāpi tasmāt tena tena
          jagadgatajanmasthityādibhāvavikāratattadbhedakriyāsahasrarūpeṇa sthātum icchoḥ
          svatantrasya bhagavato maheśvarasyecchaivottarottaram ucchūnasvabhāvā kriyā viśvakartṛtvaṃ
          vocyata iti/
children.translated_text: By the reasoning that neither insentient matter has causal agency, nor a non-sovereign conscious being, therefore the action (<s>kriyā</s>) of the independent Lord (<s>Bhagavān Maheśvara</s>), who desires to abide in the form of thousands of actions and their varieties — birth, persistence, and other transformations found in the world — that action, whose nature swells ever more, is called His universal agency.

children.text: icchāmātreṇa jagannirmāṇam ity atra dṛṣṭānto ’pi spaṣṭaṃ nirdiṣṭaḥ —
children.translated_text: That the creation of the world is by mere will — for this, an illustration is clearly indicated:
For <s>yogins</s> too, without clay, seed, and the like, by the power of will alone,
and productive of action. Thus.
pots and such things arise, each enduring, self-purposeful,

children.text:
yadi ghaṭādikaṃ prati mṛdādy eva paramārthataḥ kāraṇaṃ syāt tarhi kathaṃ yogīcchāmātreṇa
          ghaṭādijanma syāt/ athocyetānya eva mṛdbījādijanyā ghaṭāṅkurādayo yogīcchājanyās tv anya
          eveti tatrāpi bodhyase — sāmagrībhedāt tāvat kāryabheda iti sarvajanaprasiddham/
children.translated_text: If clay and such were truly the ultimate cause of pots and the like, then how could pots arise by the mere will of a <s>yogin</s>? And if one says that the pots and sprouts produced from clay, seeds, and the like are one thing, while those produced by the <s>yogin's</s> will are altogether different — then too, consider: that difference of effects arises from difference of causal conditions is well-known to all people.

children.text:
ye tu varṇayanti nopādānaṃ vinā ghaṭādyutpattir iti yogī tv icchayā paramāṇūn vyāpārayan
          saṃghaṭayatīti te ’pi bodhanīyāḥ/ yadi paridṛṣṭakāryakāraṇabhāvaviparyayo na labhyeta
          tarhi ghaṭe mṛddaṇḍacakrādi dehe strīpuruṣasaṃyogādi sarvam apekṣyeta/ tathā ca
          yogīcchāsamanantarasaṃjātaghaṭadehādisaṃbhavo duḥsamartha eva syāt/ cetana eva tu tathā
          bhāti bhagavān bhūribhago mahādevo niyatyanuvartanollaṅghanaghanatarasvātantrya iti pakṣe
          na kācid anupapattiḥ/ ata evoktaṃ vasuguptācāryaiḥ —
children.translated_text: Those who maintain that 'without a material cause, production of pots and the like is impossible' and that 'the <s>yogin</s> through his will sets atoms in motion and assembles them' — they too should be instructed: if the reversal of observed cause-effect relations were impossible, then for a pot, clay, rod, wheel, and the rest would all be required; for a body, the union of man and woman and all the rest would be required. And so the arising of pots, bodies, and the like immediately upon the <s>yogin's</s> will would be extremely difficult to explain. But in the position that the conscious Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), the greatly fortunate <s>Mahādeva</s>, who possesses dense independence to transcend and govern the laws [of nature], simply appears thus — there is no difficulty whatsoever. Therefore, the teacher <s>Vasugupta</s> has stated:
Without material cause or accessory, even on a non-surface, He paints

children.text: jagaccitraṃ namas tasmai kalānāthāya śūline// iti/
children.translated_text: the variegated picture of the world — homage to that Lord of digits (<s>Kalānātha</s>), the trident-bearer (<s>Śūlin</s>). Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu pratyagātmanaḥ parameśvarābhinnatve saṃsārasaṃbandhaḥ katham bhaved iti cet —
          tatroktam āgamādhikāre —
children.translated_text: Now, if the inner self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) is non-different from the Supreme Lord, how can the connection with <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) occur? To this it is stated in the section on scripture (<s>āgamādhikāra</s>):
This knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), blinded by <s>māyā</s>, is a <s>saṃsārin</s> (worldly being), bound by <s>karma</s>;
when his lordship is revealed through <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and the like, he is called liberated (<s>mukta</s>), being a mass of consciousness (<s>cidghana</s>). Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu prameyasya pramātrabhinnatve baddhamuktayoḥ prameyaṃ prati ko viśeṣaḥ/ atrāpy
          uttaram uktaṃ tattvārthasaṃgrahādhikāre —
children.translated_text: Now, if the object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>) is non-different from the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), what is the distinction regarding the object of knowledge for the bound and the liberated? To this too, the answer is stated in the section on the <s>Tattvārthasaṃgraha</s>:
The liberated one regards the object of knowledge as non-different from his own self,

children.text: maheśvaro yathā baddhaḥ punar atyantabhedavat// iti/
children.translated_text: as does <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord); but the bound one [regards it] as if completely different. Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
nanv ātmanaḥ parameśvaratvaṃ svābhāvikaṃ cen nārthaḥ pratyabhijñāprārthanayā/ na hi bījam
          apratyabhijñātaṃ sati sahakārisākalye ’ṅkuraṃ notpādayati/ tasmāt kasmād
          vātmapratyabhijñāne nirbandha iti cet — ucyate/ śṛṇu tāvad idaṃ rahasyam/ dvividhā hy
          arthakriyā bāhyāṅkurādikā pramātṛviśrānticamatkārasārā prītyādirūpā ca/ tatrādyā
          prayabhijñānaṃ nāpekṣate/ dvitīyā tu tad apekṣata eva/ ihāpy aham īśvara ity
          evaṃbhūtacamatkārasārā parāparasiddhilakṣaṇajīvātmaikatvaśaktivibhūtirūpārthakriyeti
          svarūpapratyabhijñānam apekṣaṇīyam/
children.translated_text: Now, if the self's supreme lordship is natural, then what need is there for the prayer of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>)? For a seed, even when not recognized, does not fail to produce a sprout when the full complement of auxiliaries is present. So why the insistence on self-recognition? The answer is: listen to this secret. For efficacious action (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is twofold: external, like sprouts and the like; and that whose essence is the repose-and-wonder of the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), having the form of delight (<s>prīti</s>) and so on. Of these, the first does not require recognition. But the second indeed requires it. Here too, the efficacious action whose essence is the wonder 'I am the Lord' — consisting in the powers and glories of the unity of the individual self with the supreme and subordinate <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) — requires self-recognition.
reference marker

children.text: nanu pramātṛviśrāntisārārthakriyā pratyabhijñānena vinā adṛṣṭā sati

tasmin dṛṣṭeti kva dṛṣṭam/ atrocyate/ nāyakaguṇagaṇasaṃśravaṇapravṛddhānurāgā
          kācana kāminī madanavihvalā virahakleśam asahamānā madanalekhāvalambanena
          svāvasthānivedanāni vidhatte/ tathā vegāt tannikaṭam aṭaty
children.translated_text: that [recognition] is present, it is seen — where is this seen? To this we reply: a certain woman (<s>kāminī</s>), whose passion has grown from hearing the aggregate of the hero's (<s>nāyaka</s>) qualities, agitated by love (<s>madana</s>), unable to bear the torment of separation, through the medium of a love-letter makes known her condition. And even when she hastily goes near him,

children.text:
api tasminn avalokite ’pi tadavalokanaṃ tadīyaguṇaparāmarśābhāve janasādhāraṇatvaṃ
          prāpte hṛdayaṃgamabhāvaṃ na labhate/ yadā tu dūtīvacanāt tadīyaguṇaparāmarśaṃ karoti tadā
          tatkṣaṇam eva pūrṇabhāvam abhyeti/ evaṃ svātmani viśveśvarātmanā bhāsamāne ’pi
          tannirbhāsanaṃ tadīyaguṇaparāmarśavirahasamaye pūrṇabhāvaṃ na saṃpādayati/
children.translated_text: and even when she sees him, that seeing of him — in the absence of the contemplation of his particular qualities — since it becomes like that of any common person, does not attain the state of touching the heart. But when, through the words of a messenger (<s>dūtī</s>), she engages in the contemplation of his qualities, then at that very moment it attains fullness. Similarly, even though the self shines as the Lord of the universe, that shining, at a time when there is absence of contemplation of His qualities, does not bring about fullness.
Now, [you say that] efficacious action whose essence is the knower's repose, without recognition, is unseen; but when

children.text:
yadā tu guruvacanādinā sarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvādilakṣaṇaparameśvarotkarṣaparāmarśo jāyate
          tadā tatkṣaṇam eva pūrṇātmatālābhaḥ/ tad uktaṃ caturthe vimarśe —
children.translated_text: But when, through the words of the guru and the like, the contemplation arises of the Supreme Lord's excellences such as omniscience, omnipotence, and the rest, then at that very moment the attainment of full selfhood occurs. As stated in the fourth <s>vimarśa</s> (reflection):

children.text: tais tair apy upayācitair upanatas tasyāḥ sthito ’py antike
children.translated_text: Even though brought near by all those entreaties, and standing close to her,

children.text: kānto lokasamāna evam aparijñāto na rantuṃ yathā/
children.translated_text: the beloved, being like any common person, unrecognized, is unable to delight [her];
similarly, for the world, even one's own self, which is the Lord of the universe, with its qualities unregarded,
for [manifesting] its own glory — therefore this <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition) has arisen. Thus.
is not sufficient
reference marker

children.text:
abhinavaguptādibhir ācāryair vihitapratāno ’py ayam arthaḥ saṃgraham upakramamāṇair
          asmābhir vistarabhiyā na pratānita iti sarvaṃ śivam//
children.translated_text: Though this subject was elaborated by masters such as <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, we who are undertaking a summary have not elaborated it out of fear of excessive length — thus all is auspicious (<s>śivam</s>).
Thus concludes the <s>Pratyabhijñādarśana</s> (Philosophy of Recognition) in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Now the <s>Raseśvaradarśana</s> (Philosophy of the Lord of Mercury) //9//
reference marker

children.text:
apare māheśvarāḥ parameśvaratādātmyavādino ’pi piṇḍasthairye sarvābhimatā jīvanmuktiḥ
          setsyatīty āsthāya piṇḍasthairyopāyaṃ pāradādipadavedanīyaṃ rasam eva saṃgirante/
children.translated_text: Other <s>Māheśvaras</s> (Śaiva adherents), though proponents of identity with the Supreme Lord, accepting that the universally desired <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living) will be achieved through the stability of the body (<s>piṇḍasthairya</s>), proclaim <s>rasa</s> (mercury), the means for bodily stability, known by the terms <s>pārada</s> (mercury) and the like.
reference marker
Mercury is called <s>pārada</s> because it causes one to cross to the far shore (<s>para-pāra</s>) of <s>saṃsāra</s>. As stated:

children.text: saṃsārasya paraṃ pāraṃ datte ’sau pāradaḥ smṛtaḥ/ iti/
children.translated_text: Because it grants (<s>datte</s>) the far shore (<s>paraṃ pāram</s>) of <s>saṃsāra</s>, it is called <s>pārada</s>. Thus.
In the <s>Rasārṇava</s> also —
Mercury is called [<s>pārada</s>] because the best practitioners use it for the supreme goal;
O <s>Devī</s>, equal to Me, born from My own limbs.
this <s>sūta</s> (mercury),

children.text: mama deharaso yasmād rasas tenāyam ucyate/ iti/
children.translated_text: Because it is the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of My body, therefore it is called <s>rasa</s>. Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu prakārāntareṇāpi jīvanmuktiyuktau neyaṃ vācoyuktir
            yuktimatīti cen na/ ṣaṭsv api darśaneṣu dehapātānantaraṃ mukter uktatayā tatra
            viśvāsānupapattyā nirvicikitsapravṛtter anupapatteḥ/ tad apy uktaṃ tatraiva —
children.translated_text: Now, if <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living) can be established by other means as well, this is not merely a verbal contrivance possessing reason — if so, no. Because in all six <s>darśanas</s> (philosophical systems), since liberation is stated to occur only after the fall of the body, confidence [in liberation] is impossible, and hence resolute engagement [in practice] is impossible. As stated there too —
In the six <s>darśanas</s> also, liberation is shown [to occur only] at the fall of the body;
like a fruit in the palm of the hand, it too is not perceived directly.

children.text: tasmāt taṃ rakṣayet piṇḍaṃ rasaiś caiva rasāyanaiḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: Therefore one should preserve the body through <s>rasas</s> (mercurial preparations) and <s>rasāyanas</s> (elixirs). Thus.
reference marker
The teacher <s>Govindabhagavatpāda</s> also [stated] —
Considering wealth, body, and enjoyments as always impermanent, one should always strive

children.text: muktau sā ca jñānāt tac cābhyāsāt sa ca sthire dehe// iti/
children.translated_text: for liberation; and that [comes] from knowledge, and that from practice, and that [practice requires] a stable body. Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu vinaśvaratayā dṛśyamānasya dehasya kathaṃ nityatvam avasīyata iti cet — maivaṃ
          maṃsthāḥ/ ṣāṭkauśikasya śarīrasyānityatve ’pi rasābhrakapadābhilapyaharagaurīsṛṣṭijātasya
          nityatvopapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, if the body is seen to be perishable, how can its permanence be established? Do not think so. For although the body composed of six sheaths (<s>ṣāṭkauśika</s>) is impermanent, permanence is consistent for a body born from the creation of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) and <s>Gaurī</s> (Pārvatī), designated by the terms <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and <s>abhraka</s> (mica).
reference marker
And in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s> —
Those who, without abandoning their bodies, have obtained a body born from the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>,

children.text: muktās te rasasiddhā mantragaṇaḥ kiṃkaro yeṣām// iti/
children.translated_text: they are liberated, accomplished through <s>rasa</s> (mercury), for whom the host of <s>mantras</s> are servants. Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
tasmāj jīvanmuktiṃ samīhamānena yoginā prathamaṃ divyatanur vidheyā/
          haragaurīsṛṣṭisaṃyogajanitatvaṃ ca rasasya harajatvenābhrakasya gaurīsaṃbhavatvena
          tattadātmakatvam uktam —
children.translated_text: Therefore, a <s>yogin</s> desiring <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living) must first create a divine body. And the fact that <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is born from the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s> is explained by <s>rasa</s> being born from <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) and <s>abhraka</s> (mica) being born from <s>Gaurī</s> (Pārvatī), making them of that nature. As stated —

children.text: abhrakas tava bījaṃ tu mama bījaṃ tu pāradaḥ/
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>abhraka</s>) is Your seed, and mercury (<s>pārada</s>) is My seed;
the fusion of these two, O <s>Devī</s>, destroys death and poverty. Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
atyalpam idam ucyate devadaityamunimānavādiṣu bahavo rasasāmarthyād divyaṃ deham āśritya
          jīvanmuktim āśritāḥ śrūyante raseśvarasiddhānte —
children.translated_text: This is but a small account. Among gods, demons, sages, and humans, many are heard to have attained divine bodies through the power of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and thus attained <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living). In the <s>Raseśvarasiddhānta</s> —
Among gods, some led by <s>Maheśa</s> (Śiva); among demons, those led by <s>Kāvya</s> (Śukrācārya);
among sages, <s>Vālakhilya</s> and others; among kings, <s>Someśvara</s> and others;
the teacher <s>Govindabhagavatpāda</s>, <s>Govindanāyaka</s>,
<s>Carvaṭi</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Vyāli</s>, <s>Kāpāli</s>, <s>Kandalāyana</s> —

children.text: etebhyo bahavaḥ siddhā jīvanmuktāś caranti hi/
children.translated_text: from among these, many <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings), liberated while living, wander about,
having obtained a body made of mercury, eagerly narrating accounts of that [mercury]. Thus.
reference marker

children.text: ayam evārthaḥ parameśvareṇa parameśvarīṃ prati prapañcitaḥ —
children.translated_text: This very meaning was elaborated by the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) to <s>Parameśvarī</s> (the Supreme Goddess):
O Goddess of the Gods, the preservation of the body is attained through <s>karmayoga</s> (yoga of action);

children.text: rasaś ca pavanaś ceti karmayogo dvidhā smṛtaḥ//
children.translated_text: <s>karmayoga</s> is remembered as twofold: through <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and through <s>pavana</s> (breath).

children.text: mūrchito harati vyādhīn mṛto jīvayati svayam/
children.translated_text: When swooned (<s>mūrchita</s>), it destroys diseases; when dead (<s>mṛta</s>), it revives by itself;

children.text: baddhaḥ khecaratāṃ kuryād raso vāyuś ca bhairavi// iti/
children.translated_text: when bound (<s>baddha</s>), it bestows the power of moving through the sky (<s>khecaratā</s>) — [such is] <s>rasa</s> and <s>vāyu</s> (breath), O <s>Bhairavī</s>. Thus.
reference marker
The nature of the swooned state (<s>mūrchita</s>) is described —
When mercury (<s>sūta</s>), abandoning its dense volatility, assumes various colors,

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ dṛśyate yasya mūrchitaṃ taṃ vadanti hi//
children.translated_text: and the [following] characteristics are seen — that they call the swooned state (<s>mūrchita</s>).
Moisture, density, luster, heaviness, and volatility —

children.text: yasyaitāni na dṛśyante taṃ vidyān mṛtasūtakam// iti/
children.translated_text: when these are not seen, one should know it as dead mercury (<s>mṛtasūtaka</s>). Thus.
reference marker
Elsewhere, the nature of the bound state (<s>baddha</s>) was also described —

children.text: akṣataś ca laghudrāvī tejasvī nirmalo guruḥ/
children.translated_text: Unbroken, light-flowing, lustrous, pure, and heavy;

children.text: sphoṭanaṃ punar āvṛttau baddhasūtasya lakṣaṇam/ iti/
children.translated_text: cracking upon re-heating — these are the characteristics of bound mercury (<s>baddhasūta</s>). Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu haragaurīsṛṣṭisiddhau piṇḍasthairyam āsthātuṃ pāryate/ tatsiddhir eva katham iti cet
          — na aṣṭādaśasaṃskāravaśāt tadupapatteḥ/ tad uktam ācāryaiḥ —
children.translated_text: Now, if the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s> is accomplished, bodily stability can be maintained. But how is that accomplishment itself achieved? It is through the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes), because through them it is possible. As stated by the teachers —
In the procedure for its purification, the wise person should first carefully learn
the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes), each of which purifies. Thus.
reference marker
And those <s>saṃskāras</s> have been specified —
Sweating (<s>svedana</s>), grinding (<s>mardana</s>), swooning (<s>mūrchana</s>), fixing (<s>sthāpana</s>), descending (<s>pātana</s>), restraining (<s>nirodhana</s>), regulation (<s>niyama</s>),
kindling (<s>dīpana</s>), sky-consumption (<s>gaganagrāsa</s>), measuring (<s>pramāṇa</s>), then digesting (<s>jāraṇa</s>), sealing (<s>pidhāna</s>),
internal liquefaction (<s>garbhadruti</s>), external liquefaction (<s>bāhyadruti</s>), alkaline dissolution (<s>kṣāraṇa</s>), coloring (<s>saṃrāga</s>), straining (<s>sāraṇa</s>),
progressive penetration (<s>krāmaṇa</s>), transmutation (<s>vedha</s>), and ingestion (<s>bhakṣaṇa</s>) — thus the eighteen operations of mercury (<s>rasakarma</s>). Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
tatprapañcas tu govindabhagavatpādācāryasarvajñarāmeśvarabhaṭṭārakaprabhṛtibhiḥ prācīnair
          ācāryair nirūpita iti granthabhūyastvabhayād udāsyate/ na ca rasaśāstraṃ dhātuvādārtham
          eveti mantavyam/ dehavedhadvārā mukter eva paramaprayojanatvāt/ tad uktaṃ rasārṇave —
children.translated_text: The elaboration of these has been expounded by ancient masters such as the teacher <s>Govindabhagavatpāda</s>, <s>Sarvajña Rāmeśvara Bhaṭṭāraka</s>, and others — therefore it is omitted here out of fear of excessive length. And the science of mercury (<s>rasaśāstra</s>) should not be thought of as meant only for metallurgy (<s>dhātuvāda</s>). Because the supreme purpose is liberation itself through the transmutation of the body (<s>dehavedha</s>). As stated in the <s>Rasārṇava</s> —
O Lord, the transmutation of metals which You have described —

children.text: taṃ dehavedham ācakṣva yena syāt khecarī gatiḥ//
