Therefore, by elimination, for a foremost person who has directly realized the truth of the Self through the sequence of hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and the like, by the grace of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), the absolute cessation of suffering is the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) — this is faultless.
Section 11.159

children.text:
nanv īśvarasadbhāve kiṃ pramāṇaṃ pratyakṣam anumānam āgamo vā/ na tāvad atra pratyakṣaṃ
          kramate/ rūpādirahitatvenātīndriyatvāt/ nāpy anumānam/ tadvyāptaliṅgābhāvāt/ nāgamaḥ/
          vikalpāsahatvāt/ kiṃ nityo 'vagamayaty anityo vā/ ādye 'pasiddhāntāpātaḥ/ dvitīye
          parasparāśrayāpātaḥ/ upamānādikam aśakyaśaṅkam/ niyataviṣayatvāt/ tasmād īśvaraḥ
          śaśaviṣāṇāyata iti cet —
children.translated_text: Now, what is the evidence for the existence of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>)? Perception, inference, or scripture? First, perception does not apply here, because he is beyond the senses, being devoid of form and the like. Nor inference, because of the absence of a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) pervaded by that [i.e., by his existence]. Nor scripture, because it does not withstand alternatives: Does [scripture] communicate [him] as eternal or as non-eternal? In the first case, there is the consequence of an unaccepted tenet. In the second case, the consequence of mutual dependence. Analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) and the like are beyond suspicion [i.e., irrelevant], because they have restricted scope. Therefore, the Lord is as [real as] the horn of a hare — if [one argues] thus,

children.text:
tad etan na caturacetasāṃ cetasi camatkāram āviṣkaroti/ vivādāspadaṃ nagasāgarādikaṃ
          sakartṛkaṃ kāryatvāt kumbhavat/ na cāyam asiddho hetuḥ/ sāvayavatvena tasya
          susādhanatvāt/
children.translated_text: This does not produce wonder in the minds of those who are not dull-witted. That which is the subject of dispute — mountains, oceans, and the like — has a creator, because of being an effect, like a pot. And this is not an unestablished reason, because it is well established through the having of parts (<s>sāvayavatva</s>).

children.text:
nanu kim idaṃ sāvayavatvam avayavasaṃyogitvam avayavasamavāyitvaṃ vā/ nādyaḥ/ gaganādau
          vyabhicārāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/ tantutvādāv anaikāntyāt/ tasmād anupapannam iti cet —
children.translated_text: Now, if [one asks]: What is this "having parts" — conjunction with parts, or inherence in parts? Not the first, because of deviation in space and the like. Not the second, because of inconclusiveness in thread-hood and the like. Therefore, [the inference] is untenable — if [one argues] thus,

children.text:
maivaṃ vādīḥ/ samavetadravyatvaṃ sāvayavatvam iti nirukter vaktuṃ śakyatvāt/
          avāntaramahattvena vā kāryatvānumānasya sukaratvāt/
children.translated_text: Do not argue so! Because the definition "having parts is being a substance in which [others] inhere" (<s>samavetadravyatva</s>) can be stated. Or because the inference of effect-hood is easily accomplished through subordinate magnitude.

children.text:
nāpi viruddho hetuḥ/ sādhyaviparyayavyāpter abhāvāt/ nāpy anaikāntikaḥ/ pakṣād anyatra
          vṛtter adarśanāt/ nāpi kālātyayāpadiṣṭaḥ/ bādhakānupalambhāt/ nāpi satpratipakṣaḥ/
          pratibhaṭādarśanāt/
children.translated_text: Nor is the reason contradictory, because of the absence of pervasion by the opposite of what is to be proved. Nor is it inconclusive, because [its] occurrence is not observed anywhere other than the thesis. Nor is it vitiated by temporal lapse (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>), because of the non-apprehension of a contradicting [cognition]. Nor does it have a valid counter-argument, because of the non-observation of a competitor.
Section 11.174

children.text: nanu nagādikam akartṛkaṃ śarīrājanyatvād gaganavad iti cet —
children.translated_text: Now, if [one argues]: Mountains and the like have no creator, because of not being produced from a body, like space —

children.text:
naitat parīkṣākṣamam īkṣyate/ na hi kaṭhorakaṇṭhīravasya kuraṅgaśāvaḥ pratibhaṭo bhavati/
          ajanyatvasyaiva samarthatayā śarīraviśeṣaṇavaiyarthyāt/
children.translated_text: This is not seen to withstand examination. For a deer fawn is not a competitor for a fierce lion. Since non-production (<s>ajanyatva</s>) alone is capable [of proving the conclusion], the qualification "from a body" is useless.

children.text: tarhy ajanyatvam eva sādhanam iti cet —
children.translated_text: Then, if [one says] non-production itself is the means of proof —

children.text:
na/ asiddheḥ/ nāpi sopādhikatvaśaṅkākalaṅkāṅkuraḥ saṃbhavī/ anukūlatarkasaṃbhavāt/ yady
          ayam akartṛkaḥ syāt kāryam api na syāt/ iha jagati nāsty eva tat kāryaṃ nāma
          yatkārakacakram avadhīryātmānam āsādayed ity etad avivādam/ tac ca sarvaṃ
          kartṛviśeṣopahitamaryādam/ kartṛtvaṃ cetarakārakāprayojyatve sati
          sakalakārakaprayoktṛtvalakṣaṇaṃ jñānacikīrṣāprayatnādhāratvam/ evaṃ ca kartṛvyāvṛttes
          tadupahitasamastakārakavyāvṛttāv akāraṇakakāryotpādaprasaṅga iti sthūlaḥ pramādaḥ/ tathā
          niraṭaṅki śaṃkarakiṃkareṇa —
children.translated_text: No, because of non-establishment. Nor is the sprout of the blemish of the suspicion of a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) possible, because of the possibility of a supporting argument. If this [world] were without a creator, it would not be an effect either. In this world, there is indeed no effect that, disregarding the circle of causal factors (<s>kāraka</s>), establishes itself — this is undisputed. And all of that follows the rules prescribed by the particular agent. And agency is defined as: being the employer of all causal factors, while not being employed by other causal factors — [it is] being the substrate of knowledge, desire to act, and effort. And thus, upon the exclusion of the agent, all the causal factors conditioned by it being excluded, the absurd consequence of the production of an effect without a cause would be a gross error. Thus <s>Niraṭaṅki</s>, the servant of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, [states]:
"When the means of proof has support through a favorable argument,
since the non-pervasion of what is to be proved is not broken, a limiting condition is not possible in the thesis."
Section 11.188

children.text: yadīśvaraḥ kartā syāt tarhi śarīrī syād ityādipratikūlatarkajātaṃ jāgartīti cet —
children.translated_text: If [one argues]: "If the Lord were a creator, then he would have a body" — and thus the class of unfavorable arguments awakens —
There is self-contradiction through both the establishment and non-establishment of the Lord. As stated by <s>Udayana</s>:
"If scripture and the like are valid means of knowledge, due to contradiction, there is no negation;

children.text: ābhāsatve tu saiva syād āśrayāsiddhir uddhatā/
children.translated_text: but if they are semblances, then that very rampant defect of the unestablished basis [applies to the opponent]."
And the objection of particular contradiction is not tenable, because it is defeated by the alternatives of known and unknown.
Section 11.194

children.text:
syād etat/ parameśvarasya jagannirmāṇe pravṛttiḥ kimarthā/ svārthā parārthā vā/ ādye
          'pīṣtaprāptyarthāniṣṭaparihārārthā vā/ nādyaḥ/ avāptasakalakāmasya tadanupapatteḥ/ ata eva
          na dvitīyaḥ/ dvitīye pravṛttyanupapattiḥ/ kaḥ khalu parārthaṃ pravartamānaṃ prekṣāvān ity
          ācakṣīta/ atha karuṇayā pravṛttyupapattir ity ācakṣīta kaścit taṃ pratyācakṣīta/ tarhi
          sarvān prāṇinaḥ sukhina eva sṛjed īśvaraḥ/ na duḥkhaśabalān/ karuṇāvirodhāt/ svārtham
          anapekṣya paraduḥkhaprahāṇecchā hi kāruṇyam/ tasmād īśvarasya jagatsarjanaṃ na
          yujyate/
children.translated_text: One might [object] thus: What is the Lord's purpose in the creation of the world? Is it for his own sake or for the sake of others? In the first case, is it for the attainment of what is desired or for the avoidance of what is undesired? Not the first, because that is untenable for one who has attained all desires. For the same reason, not the second either. In the second case [for others' sake], activity is untenable, for who indeed would call one acting for others' sake "discerning"? Now, if someone says that activity is tenable through compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), one would reply to him: Then the Lord should create all beings as happy alone, not mixed with suffering — because that would contradict compassion. For compassion is the desire to remove others' suffering without regard for one's own interest. Therefore, the Lord's creation of the world is not justified.
This has been stated by the <s>Bhaṭṭācāryas</s>:
Section 11.202
"Not even a fool acts without aiming at a purpose;
and for Him who created the world,

children.text:
jagac cāsṛjatas tasya ] ASS v.l., IV; jagac ca sṛjatas
                  tasya A.

children.translated_text: what desired [goal] is not [already] achieved?"

children.text:
nāmeṣṭaṃ na sidhyati ] Ślokavārttika; nāma na kṛtaṃ
                  bhavet ASS, IV, A.

children.translated_text: Section 11.204

children.text:
atrocyate/ nāstikaśiromaṇe tāvad īrṣyākaṣāyite cakṣuṣī nimīlya paribhāvayatu bhavān/
          karuṇayā pravṛttir asty eva/ na ca nisargataḥ sukhamayasargaprasaṅgaḥ/
          sṛjyaprāṇikṛtasukṛtaduṣkṛtaparipākaviśeṣād vaiṣamyopapatteḥ/ na ca svātantryabhaṅgaḥ
          śaṅkanīyaḥ/ svāṅgaṃ svavyavadhāyakaṃ na bhavatīti nyāyena pratyuta tannirvāhāt/ eka eva
          rudro na dvitīyo 'vatasthe ityādir āgamas tatra pramāṇam/ yady evaṃ tarhi
          parasparāśrayabādhavyādhiṃ samādhatsveti cet —
children.translated_text: Here it is replied: O crest-jewel of atheists! First, close your eyes stained with envy and reflect. Activity through compassion does exist. And there is no absurd consequence of a creation consisting solely of happiness by nature, because inequality is justified by the particular maturation of the merits and demerits done by the beings to be created. And no breaking of [the Lord's] independence should be suspected, because by the principle "one's own limb is not one's own obstruction," on the contrary, it sustains that [independence]. "There is only one <s>Rudra</s>; no second stood" — and similar scriptural passages are the evidence there. If this is so, then let [the opponent] set forth the disease of mutual dependence and contradiction — if [he objects] thus —

children.text:
tasyānutthānāt/ kim utpattau parasparāśrayaḥ śaṅkyate jñaptau vā/ nādyaḥ/
          āgamasyeśvarādhīnotpattikatve 'pi parameśvarasya nityatvenotpatter anupapatteḥ/ nāpi
          jñaptau/ parameśvarasyāgamādhīnajñaptikatve 'pi tasyānyato 'vagamāt/ nāpi
          tadanityatvajñaptau/ āgamānityatvasya tīvrādidharmopetatvādinā sugamatvāt/ tasmān
          nivartakadharmānuṣṭhānavaśād īśvaraprasādasiddhāv abhimateṣṭasiddhir iti sarvam
          avadātam//
children.translated_text: Because of its non-arising. Is mutual dependence (<s>parasparāśraya</s>) suspected in the origination [of scripture and God], or in the cognition [of them]? Not the first — because even though scripture's origination depends on <s>Īśvara</s>, since the Supreme Lord is eternal, origination [of Him] is impossible. Nor in cognition — because even though the Supreme Lord's cognizability depends on scripture, He can be known through other means. Nor in the cognition of its impermanence — because the impermanence of scripture is easily known through its possessing properties such as intensity and the like. Therefore, through the practice of the qualities that remove [obstacles], when the grace of <s>Īśvara</s> is attained, the desired goal is accomplished — thus everything is clear.
Thus concludes the <s>Ākṣapāda</s> (Nyāya) philosophy in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Now the <s>Jaimini</s> philosophy //12//
reference marker

children.text:
nanu dharmānuṣṭhānavaśād abhimatadharmasiddhir iti jegīyate bhavatā/ tatra dharmaḥ
          kiṃlakṣaṇaḥ kiṃpramāṇaka iti cet —
children.translated_text: Now, you maintain that the desired goal is accomplished through the practice of <s>dharma</s>. In that case, what is the definition of <s>dharma</s>, and what is its means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)? If so —

children.text:
ucyate/ śrūyatām avadhānena asya praśnasya prativacanaṃ prācyāṃ mīmāṃsāyāṃ prādarśi
          jaimininā muninā/ sā hi mīmāṃsā dvādaśalakṣaṇī/ tatra prathame 'dhyāye
          vidhyarthavādamantrasmṛtināmadheyārthakasya śabdarāśeḥ prāmāṇyam/ dvitīya
          upodghātakarmabhedapramāṇāpavādaprayogabhedarūpo 'rthaḥ/ tṛtīye
          śrutiliṅgavākyādivirodhapratipattikarmānārabhyādhītabahupradhānopakāraka-prayājādiyājamānacintanam/
          caturthe
          pradhānaprayojakatvāpradhānaprayojakatvajuhūparṇatādiphalarājasūyagata-jaghanyāṅgākṣadyūtādicintā/
          pañcame śrutyādikramatadviśeṣavṛddhyavardhanaprābalyacintā/ ṣaṣṭhe
          'dhikāritaddharmadravyapratinidhyarthalopanaprāyaścittasatradeyavahni-vicāraḥ/ saptame
          pratyakṣavacanātideśaśeṣanāmaliṅgātideśavicāraḥ/ aṣṭame
          spaṣṭāspaṣṭaprabalaliṅgātideśāpavādavicāraḥ/ navame
          ūhavicārārambhasāmohamantrohatatprasaṅgāgatavicāraḥ/ daśame
          bādhahetudvāralopavistārabādhakāraṇakāryaikatvasamuccayagrahādisāma-prakīrṇanañarthavicāraḥ/
          ekādaśe tantropodghātatantrāvāpatantraprapañcanāvāpaprapañcanacintanāni/ dvādaśe
          prasaṅgatantrinirṇayasamuccayavikalpavicāraḥ/
children.translated_text: It is said: listen attentively. The answer to this question was shown in the Pūrva Mīmāṃsā by the sage <s>Jaimini</s>. That <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> has twelve chapters. In the first chapter: the authority of the mass of words comprising injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), <s>mantra</s>, tradition (<s>smṛti</s>), and naming (<s>nāmadheya</s>). In the second: the subject matter in the form of introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>), distinction of rites (<s>karmabheda</s>), means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), exception (<s>apavāda</s>), and difference of application (<s>prayogabheda</s>). In the third: consideration of direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), indication (<s>liṅga</s>), sentence (<s>vākya</s>), and other conflicts; rites not undertaken; what is studied; the many and the principal; auxiliary considerations such as the preliminary offerings (<s>prayāja</s>) and the sacrificer. In the fourth: consideration of being productive of the principal, being productive of the non-principal, the <s>juhū</s> ladle, <s>parṇa</s> leaf, and the like; the fruit; the subsidiary rites of the <s>Rājasūya</s>; subordinate elements; games of dice, and the like. In the fifth: consideration of the order of direct statement and the like, its particularization, augmentation, non-augmentation, and predominance. In the sixth: examination of the qualified person (<s>adhikārin</s>), his properties, substance, substitution (<s>pratinidhi</s>), omission of purpose, expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>), sacrificial session (<s>satra</s>), what is to be given, and fire. In the seventh: consideration of direct perception, verbal extension (<s>atideśa</s>), remainder (<s>śeṣa</s>), name, and extension by indication. In the eighth: consideration of clear and unclear strong indications, extension, and exception. In the ninth: consideration of adaptation (<s>ūha</s>), commencement, <s>Sāman</s> hymns, <s>mantra</s> adaptation, and incidental matters. In the tenth: consideration of supersession (<s>bādha</s>), cause, door, omission, expansion, superseding cause, effect, unity, accumulation, inclusion, <s>Sāman</s> miscellany, and the meaning of the negative particle. In the eleventh: reflections on <s>tantra</s> (general rule), introduction to <s>tantra</s>, extension of <s>tantra</s>, elaboration of <s>tantra</s>, obtainment, and elaboration of obtainment. In the twelfth: consideration of incidental matters, <s>tantra</s> determination, accumulation, and alternatives.
reference marker

children.text:
tatrāthāto dharmajijñāsā iti prathamam adhikaraṇaṃ pūrvamīmāsārambhopapādanaparam/
          adhikaraṇaṃ ca pañcāvayavam ācakṣate parīkṣakāḥ/ te ca pañcāvayavā
          viṣayasaṃśayapūrvapakṣasiddhāntasaṃgatirūpāḥ/
children.translated_text: Among these, 'Now therefore the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>' — this is the first topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), aimed at justifying the commencement of the Pūrva Mīmāṃsā. The examiners describe a topic as having five parts. Those five parts consist of: subject (<s>viṣaya</s>), doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), prima facie view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>), established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), and consistency (<s>saṃgati</s>).
reference marker

children.text:
tatrācāryamatānusāreṇādhikaraṇaṃ nirūpyate/ svādhyāyo 'dhyetavya ity etad vākyaṃ viṣayaḥ/
          codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ ity ārabhyānvāhārye ca darśanāt ity etadantaṃ jaiminīyaṃ
          dharmaśāstram anārabhyam ārabhyaṃ veti saṃdehaḥ/ adhyayanavidher
          adṛṣṭārthatvadṛṣṭārthatvābhyāṃ tatrānārabhyam iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ/ adhyayanavidher
          arthāvabodhalakṣaṇadṛṣṭaphalakatvānupapatteḥ/ arthāvabodhārtham adhyayanavidhir iti vadan
          vādī praṣṭavyaḥ — kim atyantam aprāptam adhyayanaṃ vidhīyate kiṃ vā pākṣikam avaghātavan
          niyamyata iti/ na tāvad ādyaḥ/ vivādapadaṃ vedādhyayanam arthāvabodhahetur adhyayanatvād
          bhāratādhyayanavad ity anumānena vidhyanapekṣatayā prāptatvāt/ astu tarhi dvitīyo yathā
          nakhavidalanādinā taṇḍulaniṣpattisaṃbhavāt pākṣiko 'vaghāto 'vaśyam kartavya iti vidhinā
          niyamyate tathā likhitapāṭhenārthajñānasaṃbhavāt pākṣikam adhyayanaṃ vidhinā niyamyata iti
          cet —
children.translated_text: Among these, the topic is explained according to the teacher's view. 'One's own Vedic text should be studied' — this sentence is the subject. The <s>Jaiminīya</s> <s>dharmaśāstra</s>, beginning with '<s>dharma</s> is that purpose which is indicated by injunction (<s>codanā</s>)' and ending with 'because it is seen in the <s>anvāhārya</s>' — is it not to be commenced, or is it to be commenced? This is the doubt. Because the injunction to study may have an unseen or a seen purpose — the prima facie view is that it is not to be commenced. Because the injunction to study cannot have the seen result of understanding meaning. One who argues that the injunction to study is for the purpose of understanding meaning should be asked: is study enjoined as something absolutely unattained, or is it, like threshing, regulated as something optionally [attainable]? Not the first — because 'Vedic study, the subject of dispute, is a cause of understanding meaning, because it is study, like the study of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>' — by this inference, since it is already attained without needing an injunction. Then let it be the second: just as threshing, since rice can optionally be obtained by splitting with nails and so on, is necessarily regulated by injunction, so too study, since knowledge of meaning is optionally possible through reading a written text, is regulated by injunction — if so,

children.text:
naitac caturasram/ dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭānikayor vaidharmyasaṃbhavāt/ avaghātaniṣpannair eva
          taṇḍulaiḥ piṣṭapuroḍāśādikaraṇe 'vāntarāpūrvadvārā darśapūrṇamāsau paramāpūrvam utpādayato
          nāparathā/ ato 'pūrvam avaghātasya niyamahetuḥ/ prakṛte likhitapāṭhajanyenādhyayanajanyena
          vārthāvabodhena kratvanuṣṭhānasiddher adhyayanasya niyamahetur nāsty eva/ tasmād
          arthāvabodhahetuvicāraśāstrasya vaidhatvaṃ nāstīti/
children.translated_text: This is not well-reasoned. Because there may be dissimilarity between the example and the exemplified. The <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifice generates the supreme <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit) through the intermediate <s>apūrva</s> produced only from rice obtained by threshing, not otherwise. Therefore <s>apūrva</s> is the reason for the restriction of threshing. In the present case, since the performance of sacrificial rites is accomplished equally by understanding meaning derived from reading a written text or from study, there is simply no reason for restricting study. Therefore, the science of inquiry into the means of understanding meaning does not have the character of being enjoined.

children.text:
tarhi śrūyamāṇasya vidheḥ kā gatir iti cet svargaphalako 'kṣaragrahaṇamātravidhir iti
          bhavān parituṣyatu/ viśvajinnyāyenāśrutasyāpi svargasya kalpayituṃ śakyatvāt/ yathā sa
          svargaḥ sarvān praty aviśiṣṭatvāt iti viśvajity aśrutam apy adhikāriṇaṃ saṃpādayatā
          tadviśeṣaṇaṃ svargaḥ phalaṃ yuktyā niraṇāyi tadvad adhyayane 'py astu/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: Then what is the scope of the injunction that is heard? You should be satisfied that it is merely an injunction for grasping syllables, with heaven as its fruit. Because by the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle, even an unheard [fruit such as] heaven can be supplied. Just as in the <s>Viśvajit</s> [sacrifice], because heaven is common to all, one who supplies even an unmentioned qualified person determines heaven as the fruit by reasoning based on its qualification — similarly let it be in the case of study. As stated —
reference marker

children.text: vināpi vidhinā dṛṣṭalābhān na hi tadarthatā/
children.translated_text: Since the seen result is obtained even without an injunction, the injunction is not for that purpose;

children.text: kalpyas tu vidhisāmarthyāt svargo viśvajidādivat// iti/
children.translated_text: but heaven should be supplied by the force of the injunction, as in the case of the <s>Viśvajit</s> and the like. Thus.

children.text:
evaṃ ca sati vedam adhītya snāyād iti smṛtir anugṛhītā bhavati/ atra hi
          vedādhyayanasamāvartanayor avyavadhānam avagamyate/ tāvake mate tv adhīte 'pi vede
          dharmavicārāya gurukule vastavyam/ tathā saty avyavadhānaṃ bādhyeta/ tasmād
          vicāraśāstrasya vaidhatvābhāvāt pāṭhamātreṇa svargasiddheḥ samāvartanaśāstrāc ca
          dharmavicāraśāstram anārambhaṇīyam iti pūrvapakṣasaṃkṣepaḥ/
children.translated_text: And in this case, the <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) 'having studied the <s>Veda</s>, one should perform the bath [of graduation]' is supported. For here, the absence of interruption between Vedic study and the graduation ceremony (<s>samāvartana</s>) is understood. But in your view, even after studying the <s>Veda</s>, one must remain in the guru's house for the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>. In that case, the absence of interruption would be contradicted. Therefore, because the science of inquiry is not enjoined, since heaven is accomplished by mere recitation, and because of the injunction for the graduation ceremony, the science of <s>dharma</s>-inquiry is not to be commenced — this is the summary of the prima facie view.
reference marker

children.text:
siddhāntas tv anyataḥ prāptatvād aprāptavidhitvaṃ māstu/ niyamavidhitvapakṣas tu
          vajrahastenāpi nāpahastayituṃ pāryate/ tathā hi svādhyāyo 'dhyetavya iti tavyapratyayaḥ
          preraṇāparaparyāyāṃ puruṣapravṛttirūpārthabhāvanābhāvyām abhidhābhāvanāṃ pratyāyayati/ sā
          hy arthabhāvanā bhāvyam ākāṅkṣati/ na tāvat samānapadopāttam adhyayanaṃ bhāvyatvena
          pariramate/ adhyayanaśabdārthasya svādhīnoccāraṇakṣamatvasya vāṅmanasavyāpārasya
          kleśārthakasya bhāvyatvāsaṃbhavāt/ nāpi samānavākyopāttaḥ svādhyāyaḥ/
          svādhyāyaśabdārthasya varṇarāśer nityatvena vibhutvena cotpattyādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ
          kriyāphalānām asaṃbhavāt/ tasmāt sāmarthyaprāpto 'vabodho bhāvyatvenāvatiṣṭhate/ arthī
          samartho vidvān adhikriyata iti nyāyena darśapūrṇamāsādividhayaḥ svaviṣayāvabodham
          apekṣamāṇāḥ svārthabodhe svādhyāyaṃ viniyuñjate/ adhyayanavidhiś ca
          likhitapāṭhādivyāvṛttādhyayanasaṃskṛtatvaṃ svādhyāyasyāvagamayati/ tathā ca yathā
          darśapūrṇamāsādijanyaṃ paramāpūrvam avaghātādijanyasyāvāntarāpūrvasya kalpakaṃ tathā
          samastakratujanyam apūrvajātaṃ kratujñānasādhanādhyayananiyamajanyam apūrvaṃ kalpayiṣyati/
          niyamādṛṣṭāniṣṭau vidhiśravaṇavaiphalyam āpadyeta/ na ca viśvajinnyāyena
          phalakalpanāvakalpyate/ arthāvabodhe dṛṣṭe phale sati phalāntarakalpanāyā ayogāt/
children.translated_text: But the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) is: since it is attained from another source, let it not be an injunction of the unattained; but the position that it is a restrictive injunction (<s>niyamavidhi</s>) cannot be dislodged even by a vajra-hand (diamond-fist). For thus: in 'one's own Vedic text should be studied,' the suffix '-tavya' (denoting obligation) conveys the linguistic expression (<s>abhidhābhāvanā</s>), which is to be expressed through <s>arthabhāvanā</s> (effectuation of meaning), which is synonymous with impulsion and has the form of human activity. That <s>arthabhāvanā</s> seeks something to be effectuated (<s>bhāvya</s>). Now, study mentioned in the same word does not satisfy the role of being the thing to be effectuated — because the meaning of the word 'study,' namely the vocal and mental activity capable of self-directed utterance, being laborious, cannot be what is to be effectuated. Nor is <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic text) mentioned in the same sentence [the thing to be effectuated] — because the meaning of the word <s>svādhyāya</s>, being a collection of phonemes that is eternal and all-pervading, is incompatible with the four action-results [of origination and the like]. Therefore, understanding, which is arrived at through capacity, remains as what is to be effectuated. By the principle 'one who desires, is capable, and is learned is qualified,' the injunctions of <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and other [sacrifices], requiring understanding of their own subject matter, employ Vedic study for the comprehension of their own meaning. And the injunction of study conveys that <s>svādhyāya</s> has the character of being refined by study as distinct from reading a written text and the like. And just as the supreme <s>apūrva</s> generated by <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and other [rites] is the determinant of the intermediate <s>apūrva</s> generated by threshing and the like, so too the <s>apūrva</s> arising from all sacrificial rites will determine the <s>apūrva</s> generated by the restriction of study as the means of knowledge of those rites. Otherwise, if the restriction had no unseen result, hearing the injunction would become fruitless. Nor is the supplying of a fruit possible by the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle — because when a seen fruit such as understanding of meaning exists, the supplying of another fruit is inappropriate.
reference marker
As stated —
When a seen fruit is obtainable, one should not supply an unseen fruit;

children.text: vidhes tu niyamārthatvān nānarthakyaṃ bhaviṣyati// iti/
children.translated_text: since the injunction has the purpose of restriction, it will not be purposeless. Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu vedamātrādhyāyino 'rthāvabodhānudaye 'pi sāṅgavedādhyāyinaḥ
          puruṣasyārthāvabodhasaṃbhavād vicāraśāstrasya vaiphalyam iti cet —
children.translated_text: Now, even if understanding of meaning does not arise for one who studies the <s>Veda</s> alone, since understanding of meaning is possible for a person who studies the <s>Veda</s> with its auxiliaries (<s>aṅgas</s>), the science of inquiry is futile — if so,

children.text:
tad asamañjasam/ bodhamātrasaṃbhave 'pi nirṇayasya vicārādhīnatvāt/ tad yathā — aktāḥ
          śarkarā upadadhāti ity atra ghṛtenaiva na tailādinety ayaṃ nirṇayo vyākaraṇena nigamena
          niruktena vā na labhyate/ vicāraśāstreṇa tu tejo vai ghṛtam iti vākyaśeṣavaśād
          arthanirṇayo labhyate/ tasmād vicāraśāstrasya vaidhatvaṃ siddham/ na ca vedam adhītya
          snāyād iti śāstraṃ gurukulanivṛttiparaṃ vyavadhānapratibandhakaṃ bādhyeteti mantavyam/
          snātvā bhuṅkta itivat pūrvāparībhāvasamānakartṛkatvamātrapratipattyādhyayanasamāvartanayor
          nairantaryāpratipatteḥ/ tasmād vidhisāmarthyād evādhikaraṇasahasrātmakaṃ
          pūrvamīmāṃsāśāstram ārambhaṇīyam/
children.translated_text: That is not valid. Because even though mere understanding is possible, definitive determination (<s>nirṇaya</s>) depends on inquiry. For example, in 'he places anointed sugar-pieces,' the definitive determination that it is with ghee alone and not with sesame oil and the like is not obtained through grammar (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>), the Vedic text (<s>nigama</s>), or etymology (<s>nirukta</s>). But through the science of inquiry, the determination of meaning is obtained from the remainder of the sentence 'brilliance indeed is ghee.' Therefore, the enjoined character of the science of inquiry is established. Nor should one think that the scripture 'having studied the <s>Veda</s>, one should bathe' — which concerns departure from the guru's house — is contradicted by an interruption. Because, just as in 'having bathed, he eats,' one understands merely the same agent performing actions in sequence, not the uninterruptedness of study and the graduation ceremony. Therefore, by the very force of the injunction, the science of Pūrva Mīmāṃsā, consisting of a thousand topics, is to be commenced.
reference marker

children.text: idaṃ cādhikaraṇaṃ śāstreṇopodghātatvena saṃbadhyate/ tad āha —
children.translated_text: And this topic is connected with the <s>śāstra</s> as an introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>). He says —
They call the inquiry aimed at establishing the main subject an introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>). Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
idam evādhikaraṇaṃ gurumatam anusṛtyopanyasyate/ aṣṭavarṣaṃ brāhmaṇam upanayīta tam
          adhyāpayītety atrādhyāpanaṃ niyogaviṣayaḥ pratibhāsate/ niyogaś ca niyojyam apekṣate/ kaś
          cātra niyojya iti cet — ācāryakakāma eva/ saṃmānana ityādinā pāṇinyanuśāsanenācāryake
          gamyamāne nayater dhātor ātmanepadasya vidhānāt/ upanayane yo niyojyaḥ sa evādhyāpane 'pi/
          tayor ekaprayojanatvāt/ ata evoktaṃ manunā muninā —
children.translated_text: This very topic is presented following the teacher's view. In 'one should initiate a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> at eight years of age; one should teach him' — here, teaching appears as the object of injunction (<s>niyoga</s>). And injunction requires someone to be enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>). Who is the person enjoined here? It is the one who desires the status of teacher (<s>ācāryaka</s>). Because in the designation [of this meaning], since the status of teacher is understood through <s>Pāṇini's</s> rule beginning with '<s>saṃmānana</s>' (honoring) and the like, the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) of the root 'nay' (to lead) is prescribed. The one who is enjoined in initiation (<s>upanayana</s>) is the same one in teaching as well — because both have a single purpose. Therefore, the sage <s>Manu</s> stated —

children.text: upanīya tu yaḥ śiṣyaṃ vedam adhyāpayed dvijaḥ/
children.translated_text: A twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) who, having initiated a student, teaches him the <s>Veda</s>

children.text: sāṅgaṃ ca sarahasyaṃ ca tam ācāryaṃ pracakṣate// iti/
children.translated_text: with its auxiliaries (<s>aṅgas</s>) and its secret doctrines (<s>rahasya</s>) — him they call the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>). Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
tataś cācāryakartṛkam adhyāpanaṃ māṇavakakartṛkeṇādhyayanena vinā na sidhyatīty
          adhyāpanavidhiprayuktyaivādhyayanānuṣṭhānaṃ setsyati/ prayojyavyāpāram antareṇa
          prayojakavyāpārasyānirvāhāt/ tarhy adhyetavyaḥ ity asya vidhitvaṃ na sidhyatīti cet — mā
          saitsīt kā no hāniḥ/ pṛthag adhyayanavidher abhyupagame prayojanābhāvāt/ vidhivākyasya
          nityānuvādatvenāpy upapatteḥ/ tasmād adhyayanavidhim upajīvya pūrvam upanyastau
          pūrvottarapakṣau prakārāntareṇa pradarśanīyau/
children.translated_text: Therefore, the teaching performed by the teacher is not accomplished without the study performed by the student — hence the performance of study will be established by the very impetus of the injunction to teach. Because the activity of the instigator cannot be accomplished without the activity of the instigated. Then, if one objects that the injunctive character of 'one should study' is not established — let it not be established; what is our loss? Because there is no purpose in accepting a separate injunction of study, and because the injunctive sentence can be explained as merely reiterating what is already established (<s>nityānuvāda</s>). Therefore, relying on the injunction of study, the prima facie and conclusive views previously presented should be demonstrated in another manner.
reference marker

children.text:
vicāraśāstram avaidhatvenānārabdhavyam iti pūrvapakṣo vaidhatvenārabdhavyam iti
          rādhāntaḥ/ tatra vaidhatvaṃ vadatā vaditavyaṃ kim adhyāpanavidhir māṇavakasyārthāvabodham
          api prayuṅkte kiṃ vā pāṭhamātram/ nādyaḥ/ vināpy arthāvabodhenādhyāpanasiddheḥ/ na
          dvitīyaḥ/ pāṭhamātre vicārasya viṣayaprayojanayor asaṃbhavāt/ āpātataḥ pratibhātaḥ
          saṃdigdho 'rtho vicāraśāstrasya viṣayo bhavati/ tathā sati yatrārthāvagatir eva nāsti
          tatra saṃdehasya kā kathā/ vicāraphalasya nirṇayasya pratyāśā dūrata eva/ tathā ca yad
          asaṃdigdham prayojanaṃ

tat prekṣāvatpratipatsāgocaraḥ/ yathā samanaskendriyasaṃnikṛṣṭaḥ spaṣṭālokamadhyam
          adhyāsīno ghaṭa iti nyāyena viṣayaprayojanayor asaṃbhavena vicāraśāstram anārabhyam iti
          pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: falls within the scope of the engagement of a discerning person — as illustrated by the maxim: 'A pot sitting in the midst of clear light, in contact with the sense-organs of one whose mind is attentive' — thus, because of the impossibility of subject-matter and purpose, the science of inquiry should not be undertaken — this is the prima facie view.

The prima facie view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) is that the science of inquiry (<s>vicāraśāstra</s>) should not be undertaken since it is not enjoined; the established conclusion (<s>rādhānta</s>) is that it should be undertaken since it is enjoined. Therein, the one who asserts that it is enjoined must state: does the injunction to teach cause the student (<s>māṇavaka</s>) to comprehend the meaning also, or merely to recite? Not the first — because teaching is accomplished even without comprehension of the meaning. Not the second — because, in mere recitation, the subject-matter and purpose of the science of inquiry would be impossible. An object that is prima facie apparent and then [becomes] doubtful is the subject-matter of the science of inquiry. That being so, where there is no comprehension of meaning at all, what question can there be of doubt? The expectation of the result of inquiry, namely ascertainment, is far removed. And thus, an undoubted purpose

children.text:
adhyāpanavidhinārthāvabodho mā prayoji/ tathāpi sāṅgavedādhyāyino
          gṛhītapadapadārthasaṃgatikasya puruṣasya pauruṣeyeṣv iva prabandheṣv āmnāye 'py
          arthāvabodhaḥ prāpnoty eva/
children.translated_text: Let the injunction to teach not require comprehension of meaning. Even so, for a person who has studied the <s>Veda</s> with its auxiliary sciences and has grasped the meaning of words and their syntactic connections, comprehension of meaning in the Vedic text arises naturally, just as in compositions of human authorship.

children.text:
nanu yathā viṣaṃ bhuṅkṣvety atra pratīyamāno 'py artho na vivakṣyate māsya gṛhe bhukthā
          iti bhojanapratiṣedhasya mātṛvākyatātparyaviṣayatvāt/ tathāmnāyārthasyāvivakṣāyāṃ
          viṣayādyabhāvadoṣaḥ prācīnaḥ prāduṣyād iti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Just as in the statement "Eat poison!" the meaning, though understood, is not intended — because the purport of a mother's words is the prohibition of eating [at someone's house], "Do not eat at his house" — so too, if the meaning of the Vedic text is not intended, the previously stated fault of absence of subject-matter and the like would arise.'

children.text:
maivaṃ vocaḥ/ dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayor vaiṣamyasaṃbhavāt/
          viṣabhojanavākyasyāptapraṇītatvena mukhyārthaparigrahe bādhaḥ syād iti vivakṣā nāśrīyate/
          apauruṣeye tu vede pratīyamāno 'rthaḥ kuto na vivakṣyate/ vivakṣite ca vedārthe yatra
          yatra puruṣasya saṃdehaḥ sa sarvo 'pi vicāraśāstrasya viṣayo bhaviṣyati/ tan nirṇayasya
          prayojanam/ tasmād adhyāpanavidhiprayuktenādhyayanenāvagamyamānasyārthasya vicārārhatvād
          vicāraśāstrasya vaidhatvena vicāraśāstram ārambhaṇīyam iti rādhāntasaṃgrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: Do not say so — because there is a possibility of dissimilarity between the illustration and the illustrated. In the statement about eating poison, since it was composed by a trustworthy person, accepting the primary meaning would lead to contradiction — therefore [the primary meaning] is not intended. But in the <s>Veda</s>, which is not of human origin (<s>apauruṣeya</s>), why should the understood meaning not be intended? And when the Vedic meaning is intended, wherever a person has doubt, all of that will become the subject-matter of the science of inquiry; the ascertainment of that will be the purpose. Therefore, since the meaning apprehended through study impelled by the injunction to teach is worthy of inquiry, the science of inquiry should be undertaken because it is enjoined — this is the summary of the established conclusion.

children.text:
syād etat/ vedasya katham apauruṣeyatvam abhidhīyate/ tatpratipādakapramāṇābhāvāt/ atha
          manyethā apauruṣeyā vedāḥ saṃpradāyāvicchede saty asmaryamāṇakartṛkatvād ātmavad iti/ tad
          etan mandam/ viśeṣaṇāsiddheḥ/ pauruṣeyavedavādibhiḥ pralaye saṃpradāyavicchedasya
          kakṣīkaraṇāt/ kiṃ ca kim idam asmaryamāṇakartṛkatvaṃ nāmāpramīyamāṇakartṛkatvam
          asmaraṇagocarakartṛkatvaṃ vā/ na prathamaḥ kalpaḥ/ parameśvarasya kartuḥ pramiter
          abhyupagamāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ tathā hi/ kim ekenāsmaraṇam abhipretya sarvair
          vā/ nādyaḥ/ yo dharmaśīlo jitamānaroṣa ityādiṣu muktakoktiṣu vyabhicārāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/
          sarvāsmaraṇasyāsarvajñadurjñānatvāt/ pauruṣeyatve pramāṇasaṃbhavāc ca/ vedavākyāni
          pauruṣeyāṇi vākyatvāt kālidāsādivākyavat/ vedavākyāny āptapraṇītāni pramāṇatve sati
          vākyatvān manvādivākyavad iti/ nanu
children.translated_text: One might [object]: 'How can the <s>Veda</s> be declared to be not of human origin (<s>apauruṣeya</s>)? Because there is no means of knowledge that establishes this.' Now, if you think [to argue]: 'The <s>Vedas</s> are not of human origin because, when the tradition is unbroken, no author is remembered — like the self (<s>ātman</s>)' — that is weak. Because of the non-establishment of the qualifier. Since proponents of a human-authored <s>Veda</s> maintain that the tradition was broken during <s>pralaya</s> (cosmic dissolution). Moreover, what is this 'having no remembered author'? Is it 'having an author who is not cognized by any means of knowledge' or 'having an author who is not within the scope of memory'? Not the first alternative — because the Supreme Lord is accepted as the author who is cognized [by valid means]. Not the second — because of the inability to withstand the alternatives. For consider: is the non-remembering intended by one person or by all? Not the first — because there is deviation in independent verses (<s>muktaka</s>) such as 'He who is virtuous, who has conquered pride and anger' and the like. Not the second — because universal non-remembering is difficult to know for one who is not omniscient. And because a means of knowledge for [the <s>Veda</s>'s] human authorship is possible: 'Vedic statements are of human origin, because they are statements — like the statements of <s>Kālidāsa</s> and others.' 'Vedic statements are composed by a trustworthy person, because they are authoritative statements — like the statements of <s>Manu</s> and others.' Objection:
'All study of the <s>Veda</s> is preceded by study from a teacher;
the current study too [is so], because of the common feature of being study of the <s>Veda</s>' —

children.text: ity anumānaṃ pratisādhanaṃ pragalbhata iti cet —
children.translated_text: this inference presumes to be a counter-proof, [one might say].

children.text: tad api na pramāṇakoṭiṃ praveṣṭum īṣṭe/
children.translated_text: That too does not manage to enter the category of valid means of knowledge.
'All study of the <s>Mahābhārata</s> is preceded by study from a teacher;
the current study too [is so], because of being study of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>' —

children.text: ity ābhāsasamānayogakṣematvāt/ nanu tatra vyāsaḥ karteti smaryate/
children.translated_text: because it shares the same fate as this fallacious [inference]. Objection: 'But there, <s>Vyāsa</s> is remembered as the author —

children.text: ko hy anyaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣān mahābhāratakṛd bhavet/
children.translated_text: "Who other than the lotus-eyed [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>/<s>Vyāsa</s>] could be the composer of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>?"
and so on.' If so —

children.text:
tad asāram/ ṛcaḥ sāmāni jajñire/ chandāṃsi jajñire tasmād yajus tasmād ajāyata iti
          puruṣasūkte vedasya sakartṛkatāpratipādanāt/ kiṃ cānityaḥ śabdaḥ sāmānyavattve saty
          asmadādibāhyendriyagrāhyatvād ghaṭavat/
children.translated_text: that is groundless. Because in the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, the <s>Veda</s>'s having an author is taught: 'From Him the <s>Ṛks</s> were born, the <s>Sāmans</s> were born; the metres were born from Him, from Him the <s>Yajus</s> was born.' Furthermore, sound is non-eternal, because, while possessing universals, it is graspable by our external sense-organs — like a pot.

children.text: nanv idam anumānaṃ sa evāyaṃ gakāra iti pratyabhijñāpramāṇapratihatam iti cet —
children.translated_text: Objection: 'But this inference is struck down by the means of knowledge that is recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>): "This is the very same letter <s>ga</s>."'

children.text:
tad atiphalgu/ lūnapunarjātakeśadalitakundādāv iva pratyabhijñāyāḥ sāmānyaviṣayatvena
          bādhakatvābhāvāt/
children.translated_text: That is exceedingly flimsy — because recognition, having universals as its object (as in the case of hair that is cut and regrown, or a crushed <s>kunda</s> flower and the like), is not a defeater.

children.text:
nanv aśarīrasya parameśvarasya tālvādisthānābhāvena varṇoccāraṇāsaṃbhavāt kathaṃ
          tatpraṇītatvaṃ vedasya syād iti cet —
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Since the Supreme Lord is bodiless and lacks the vocal positions such as palate and the like, the utterance of phonemes is impossible — so how can the <s>Veda</s> be composed by Him?'

children.text:
na tad bhadram/ svabhāvato 'śarīrasyāpi tasya bhaktānugrahārthaṃ līlāvigrahaṇasaṃbhavāt/
          tasmād vedasyāpauruṣeyatvavācoyuktir na yukteti cet —
children.translated_text: That is not sound — because even for Him who is by nature bodiless, the assumption of a playful body (<s>līlāvigraha</s>) for the sake of gracing His devotees is possible. Therefore, if [you say] the verbal formulation of the <s>Veda</s>'s not being of human origin is not justified —

children.text:
tatra samādhānam abhidhīyate/ kim idaṃ pauruṣeyatvaṃ sisādhayiṣitam/ puruṣād
          utpannatvamātraṃ yathāsmadādibhir ahar ahar uccāryamāṇasya vedasya/ pramāṇāntareṇārtham
          upalabhya tatprakāśanāya racitatvaṃ vā yathāsmadādibhir eva nibadhyamānasya prabandhasya/
          prathame na vipratipattiḥ/ carame kim anumānabalāt tatsādhanam āgamabalād vā/ nādyaḥ/
          mālatīmādhavādivākyeṣu savyabhicāratvāt/ atha pramāṇatve satīti viśiṣyata iti cet — tad
          api na vipaścito manasi vaiśadyam āpadyate/ pramāṇāntarāgocarārthapratipādakaṃ hi vākyaṃ
          vedavākyam/ tat pramāṇāntaragocarārthapratipādakam iti sādhyamāne mama mātā vandhyetivad
          vyāghātāpātāt/
children.translated_text: Therein, the resolution is stated. What is this human authorship that you wish to prove? Is it merely having been produced from a person — as with the <s>Veda</s> uttered by us and others day after day? Or is it having been composed in order to illuminate a meaning apprehended through another means of knowledge — as with literary compositions authored by us and others? In the first case, there is no disagreement. In the latter case, is its establishment through the force of inference or through the force of scripture? Not the first — because there is deviation in statements such as those of [the play] <s>Mālatīmādhava</s> and the like. Now, if [one qualifies it] by [adding] 'while being authoritative' — even that does not produce clarity in the mind of the wise. For a Vedic statement is one that conveys a meaning not accessible to other means of knowledge. If it is to be proved that it conveys a meaning accessible to other means of knowledge, the absurd consequence would arise — like [saying] 'my mother is barren.'

children.text:
kiṃ ca parameśvarasya līlāvigrahaparigrahābhyupagame 'py atīndriyārthadarśanaṃ na
          saṃjāghaṭīti/ deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭārthagrahaṇopāyābhāvāt/ na ca taccakṣurādikam eva
          tādṛkpratītijananakṣamam iti mantavyam/ dṛṣṭānusāreṇaiva kalpanāyā āśrayaṇīyatvāt/ tad
          uktaṃ gurubhiḥ sarvajñanirākaraṇavelāyām —
children.translated_text: Moreover, even if the Supreme Lord's assumption of a playful body is accepted, the perception of supersensible objects does not come together [with it]. Because there is no means for grasping objects that are remote in space, time, and essential nature. Nor should it be thought that His eyes and other [sense-organs] alone are capable of producing such cognition — because hypothetical construction should be adopted only in conformity with what is observed. As stated by the teachers at the time of refuting omniscience:
'Where an extraordinary [capacity] is observed, it pertains — because of not transgressing its own object-domain —

children.text: dūrasūkṣmādidṛṣṭau syān na rūpe śrotravṛttitā// iti/
children.translated_text: to the vision of the distant, the subtle, and the like; not [to] the activity of the ear with respect to form.' Thus.

children.text:
ata eva nāgamabalāt tatsādhanam/ yathā tena proktam iti pāṇinyanuśāsane jāgraty api
          kāṭhakakālāpataittirīyam ityādisamākhyādhyayanasaṃpradāyapravartakaviṣayatvenopapadyate
          tadvad atrāpi saṃpradāyapravartakaviṣayatvenāpy upapadyate/
children.translated_text: For this very reason, that [human authorship] is not established through the force of scripture either. Just as in the <s>Pāṇinīya</s> grammar, [the statement] 'as spoken by Him' — though it remains valid even while the [grammatical tradition names like] <s>Kāṭhaka</s>, <s>Kālāpa</s>, <s>Taittirīya</s>, and the like are current — is justified as having as its scope the initiator of the tradition of study, so too here also it can be justified as having as its scope [merely] the initiator of the tradition.

children.text:
na cānumānabalāc chabdasyānityatvasiddhiḥ/ pratyabhijñavirodhāt/ na cāsaty apy ekatve
          sāmānyanibandhanaṃ tad iti sāṃpratam/ sāmānyanibandhanatvam asya balavadbādhakopanipātād
          āsthīyate kvacid vyabhicāradarśanād vā/ tatra kvacid vyabhicāradarśane tadutprekṣāyām
          uktaṃ svataḥprāmāṇyavādibhiḥ —
children.translated_text: Nor is the non-eternality of sound established through the force of inference — because of the contradiction with recognition. Nor is it currently tenable [to say] that [recognition] is grounded in the universal even without identity. The grounding in universals is maintained [only] when a powerful defeater strikes, or when deviation is observed in some cases. In the case of observing occasional deviation, those who hold the doctrine of intrinsic validity (<s>svataḥprāmāṇya</s>) have stated, when such a hypothesis [of grounding in universals] is raised:

children.text: utprekṣeta hi yo mohād ajñātam api bādhakam/
children.translated_text: 'He who, out of delusion, would hypothesize a defeater even when none is known —
he, being of doubting nature, would perish in all practical dealings.' Thus.

children.text:
nanv idaṃ pratyabhijñānaṃ gatvādijātiviṣayaṃ na gādivyaktiviṣayam/ tāsāṃ pratipuruṣaṃ
          bhedopalambhāt/ anyathā somaśarmādhīta iti vibhāgo na syād iti cet —
children.translated_text: Objection: 'This recognition has as its object the universal of <s>ga</s>-ness and the like, not the individual instance of <s>ga</s> and the like — because a difference [in individual instances] is perceived for each speaker. Otherwise, the distinction "<s>Somaśarman</s> has studied" would not be possible.'

children.text:
tad api śobhāṃ na bibharti/ gādivyaktibhede pramāṇābhāvena gatvādijātiviṣayakalpanāyāṃ
          pramāṇābhāvāt/ yathā gotvam ajānata ekam eva
          bhinnadeśaparimāṇasaṃsthānavyaktyupadhānavaśād bhinnadeśam ivālpam iva mahad iva dīrgham
          iva vāmanam iva prathate tathā gavyaktim ajānata ekāpi vyañjakabhedāt
          tattaddharmānubandhinī pratibhāsate/ etena viruddhadharmādhyāsād bhedasiddhir iti
          pratyuktam/ tatra kiṃ svābhāviko viruddhadharmādhyāso bhedasādhakatvenābhimataḥ prātītiko
          vā/ prathame 'siddhiḥ/ aparathā svābhāvikabhedābhyupagame daśa gakārān udacārayac caitra
          iti pratipattiḥ syān na tu daśakṛtvo gakāra iti/ dvitīye tu na svābhāvikabhedasiddhiḥ/ na
          hi paropādhibhedena svābhāvikam aikyaṃ vihanyate/ mā bhūn nabhaso 'pi kumbhādyupādhibhedāt
          svābhāviko bhedaḥ/ tatra vyāvṛttavyavahāro nādanidānaḥ/ tad uktaṃ ācāryaiḥ —
children.translated_text: That too does not bear beauty [i.e., is not convincing]. Because there is no means of knowledge for hypothesizing that [recognition] pertains to the universal of <s>ga</s>-ness and the like, when there is no means of knowledge for the difference of individual instances of <s>ga</s> and the like. Just as one who does not know cowness perceives the same [cow] as if in different locations, as if small, as if large, as if long, as if short — due to the imposition of individual instances differing in location, dimension, and configuration — so too, one who does not know the individual sound-instance: even though it is one, it appears as endowed with various properties due to the difference of manifesters. By this, the [argument that] 'difference is established through the superimposition of contradictory properties' is answered. Therein, is the superimposition of contradictory properties that is claimed to establish difference essential (<s>svābhāvika</s>) or conventional (<s>prātītika</s>)? In the first case, non-establishment — because otherwise, if essential difference were accepted, the cognition would be '<s>Caitra</s> uttered ten <s>ga</s>-letters,' not 'uttered the <s>ga</s>-letter ten times.' In the second case, essential difference is not established — for the unity that is essential is not destroyed by difference due to an extrinsic condition (<s>upādhi</s>). Otherwise, even of ether (<s>nabhas</s>), essential difference would [follow] from the difference of conditions such as pots and the like. Therein, the [alleged need for] distinctive practical usage is not grounded in sound — as stated by the <s>ācāryas</s> (masters):

children.text: prayojanaṃ tu yaj jātes tad varṇād eva lapsyate/
children.translated_text: 'Whatever purpose the universal serves — that can be obtained from the phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>) itself;

children.text: vyaktilabhyaṃ tu nādebhya iti gatvādidhīr vṛthā// iti/
children.translated_text: but what is obtained from individual instances — that [comes] from sounds, so [the postulation of] <s>ga</s>-ness and the like is in vain.' Thus.
And thus:
'When recognition with regard to sound stands firm, irresistible,
that very [recognition] refutes all inferences for non-eternality.'

children.text:
etenedam apāstaṃ yad avādi vāgīśvareṇa mānamanohare anityaḥ śabda
          indriyagrāhyaviśeṣaguṇatvāc cakṣūrūpavad iti/ śabdadravyatvavādinaṃ praty asiddheḥ
          dhvanyaṃśe siddhasādhanatvāc ca/ aśrāvaṇatvopādhibādhitatvāc ca/ udayanas tu
          āśrayāpratyakṣatve 'py abhāvasya pratyakṣatāṃ mahatā prabandhena pratipādayan nivṛttaḥ
          kolahala utpannaḥ śabda iti vyavahārācaraṇe kāraṇaṃ pratyakṣaṃ śabdānityatve pramāṇayati
          sma/ so 'pi viruddhadharmasaṃsargasyaupādhikatvopapādananyāyena dattaraktabalivetālasamaḥ/
          yo hi nityatve sarvadopalabdhyanupalabdhiprasaṅgo nyāyabhūṣaṇakāroktaḥ so 'pi
          dhvanisaṃskṛtasvopalambhābhyupagamāt pratikṣiptaḥ/ yat tu yugapad indriyasaṃbandhitvena
          pratiniyatasaṃskārakasaṃskāryatvābhāvānumānaṃ tad ātmany anaikāntikam ity alam
          atikalahena/ tataś ca vedasyāpauruṣeyatayā nirastasamastaśaṅkākalaṅkāṅkuratvena
          svataḥsiddhaṃ dharme prāmāṇyam iti susthitam/
children.translated_text: By this, what was stated by <s>Vāgīśvara</s> (<s>Bhartṛhari</s>?) in [his work] 'Charming to the Mind of the Proud' — 'Sound is non-eternal, because it is a particular quality graspable by the sense-organs — like form [grasped] by the eye' — is set aside. Because it is unestablished for one who holds that sound is a substance; and because, with respect to the <s>dhvani</s> (manifested sound) aspect, it proves what is already established. And because it is vitiated by the limiting condition of non-audibility. <s>Udayana</s>, however, demonstrating at great length the perceptibility of absence even when the substratum is imperceptible, established perception as the means of knowledge for the non-eternality of sound through the practical usage 'the commotion has ceased, the sound has arisen.' But even he is [like] a <s>vetāla</s> (vampire) appeased by an offering of blood — [i.e., disposed of] by the method of demonstrating that the superimposition of contradictory properties is due to extrinsic conditions. And the [argument] stated by the author of the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> — that if [sound were] eternal, the absurd consequence would arise of its being perceived and not-perceived at all times — that too has been rejected through the acceptance that [sound's] manifestation is [produced] by <s>dhvani</s> (articulate sound) and its latent impression. As for the inference that, because [sounds uttered simultaneously] are simultaneously connected with the sense-organ, there is no specific latent-impression and its specific product — that is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) with respect to the self. Enough with excessive quarrelling! Therefore, since the <s>Veda</s> is not of human origin, and since the sprouts of all objections and blemishes are completely removed, its authority regarding <s>dharma</s> is self-established — this is well established.
One might [object]:
'The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> have adopted that validity and invalidity [of knowledge] are both intrinsic (<s>svataḥ</s>);

children.text: naiyāyikās te parataḥ saugatāś caramaṃ svataḥ//
children.translated_text: the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> [say] both are extrinsic (<s>parataḥ</s>); the <s>Bauddhas</s> [say] the latter [invalidity] is intrinsic.'
First, the <s>Vedavādins</s> (Vedic proponents) declare validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) to be extrinsic (<s>parataḥ</s>);
they declare the status of being a valid means of knowledge to be intrinsic (<s>svataḥ</s>), and invalidity to be extrinsic.

children.text:
iti vādivivādadarśanāt kathaṃkāraṃ svataḥ dharme prāmāṇyam iti siddhavatkṛtya
          svīkriyate/
children.translated_text: Since there is the observation of dispute in the <s>Vādavivāda</s> [treatise], how can intrinsic validity in <s>dharma</s> be accepted as established?
reference marker

children.text:
kiṃ ca kim idaṃ svataḥ prāmāṇyaṃ nāma/ kiṃ svata eva prāmāṇyasya janma/ āhosvit
          svāśrayajñānajanyatvam/ kim uta svāśrayajñānasāmagrījanyatvam/ utāho
          jñānasāmānyasāmagrījanyajñānaviśeṣāśritatvam/ kiṃ vā
          jñānasāmānyasāmagrīmātrajanyajñānaviśeṣāśritatvam/
children.translated_text: Moreover, what is this 'intrinsic validity' (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>)? Is it (1) that validity itself is self-produced? Or (2) that it is produced by the cognition that is its own substratum? Or (3) that it is produced by the causal aggregate of the cognition that is its own substratum? Or (4) that it resides in a particular cognition produced by the causal aggregate of cognition in general? Or (5) that it resides in a particular cognition produced by the mere causal aggregate of cognition in general?
Among these, the first is faulty -- because the relation of cause and effect, being one of difference, cannot reside in a single [entity] as having the same locus.

children.text:
nāpi dvitīyaḥ/ guṇasya sato jñānasya prāmāṇyaṃ prati samavāyikāraṇatayā
          dravyatvāpātāt/
children.translated_text: Nor is the second [acceptable] -- because a cognition that is an existent quality would, as the inherent cause of its own validity, absurdly become a substance.

children.text:
nāpi tṛtīyaḥ/ prāmāṇyasyopādhitve jātitve vā janmāyogāt/ smṛtitvānadhikaraṇasya jñānasya
          bādhātyantābhāvaḥ prāmāṇyopādhiḥ/ na ca tasyotpattisaṃbhavaḥ/ atyantābhāvasya
          nityatvābhyupagamāt/ ata eva na jāter api janir yujyate/
children.translated_text: Nor is the third [acceptable] -- because of the impossibility of the production [of validity] whether it is a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) or a universal (<s>jāti</s>). The limiting adjunct of validity is the absolute absence of sublation in a cognition that is not the locus of memory-hood (<s>smṛtitva</s>). And the production of that [absolute absence] is impossible, because absolute absence is accepted as eternal. For this very reason, the production of the universal [of validity] too is not possible.

children.text:
nāpi caturthaḥ/ jñānaviśeṣo hy apramā/ viśeṣasāmagryāṃ ca sāmānyasāmagry anupraviśati
          śiṃśapāsāmagryām iva vṛkṣasāmagrī/ aparathā tasyākasmikatvaṃ prasajyeta/ tasmāt
          paratastvena svīkṛtāprāmāṇyaṃ vijñānasāmānyasāmagrījanyāśritam ity ativyāptir
          āpadyeta/
children.translated_text: Nor is the fourth [acceptable] -- for a particular cognition is an invalid cognition (<s>apramā</s>). And in the causal aggregate of a particular, the causal aggregate of the general enters, as the causal aggregate of the <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree [enters] that of the tree [in general]. Otherwise, [invalidity] would be uncaused. Therefore, invalidity -- accepted as extrinsic -- being produced by and residing in the causal aggregate of cognition in general, the defect of over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) would arise.

children.text:
pañcamavikalpaṃ vikalpayāmaḥ/ kiṃ doṣābhāvasahakṛtajñānasāmagrījanyatvam eva
          jñānasāmagrīmātrajanyatvaṃ kiṃ vā doṣābhāvāsahakṛtajñānasāmagrījanyatvam/
children.translated_text: We consider the fifth alternative. Is 'being produced by the mere causal aggregate of cognition' the same as 'being produced by the causal aggregate of cognition cooperating with the absence of defects'? Or is it 'being produced by the causal aggregate of cognition not cooperating with the absence of defects'?

children.text:
nādyaḥ/ doṣābhāvasahakṛtajñānasāmagrījanyatvam eva parataḥprāmāṇyam iti
          parataḥprāmāṇyavādibhir urarīkaraṇāt/
children.translated_text: Not the first -- because the proponents of extrinsic validity (<s>parataḥprāmāṇyavādin</s>) accept that 'being produced by the causal aggregate of cognition cooperating with the absence of defects' is precisely extrinsic validity.
reference marker

children.text:
nāpi dvitīyaḥ/ doṣābhāvasahakṛtatvena sāmagryāṃ sahakṛtatve siddhe
          'nanyathāsiddhānvayavyatirekasiddhatayā doṣābhāvasya kāraṇatāyā vajralepāyamānatvāt/
          abhāvaḥ kāraṇam eva na bhavatīti cet
children.translated_text: Nor the second -- because, when the cooperation of the absence of defects with the causal aggregate is established, the causality of the absence of defects is cemented like adamantine plaster through the positive and negative concomitance that is not otherwise explicable. Objection: 'Absence can never be a cause!' --

children.text:
tadā vaktavyam abhāvasya kāryatvam asti na vā/ yadi nāsti tadā ghaṭapradhvaṃsānutpattyā
          ghaṭasya nityatāprasaṅgaḥ/ athāsti kim aparāddhaṃ kāraṇatveneti seyam ubhayataspāśā
          rajjuḥ/ tad uditam udayanena —
children.translated_text: Then one must state: does absence have the status of being an effect or not? If not, then from the non-production of the posterior absence of a pot, the permanence of the pot would absurdly follow. If it does, then what fault is there in [absence] being a cause? -- thus this is a rope that binds from both sides. As stated by <s>Udayana</s>:
reference marker

children.text: bhāvo yathā tathābhāvaḥ kāraṇaṃ kāryavan mataḥ/ iti/
children.translated_text: Just as a positive entity, so too absence is considered to be both a cause and an effect.

children.text:
tathā ca prayogaḥ — vimataṃ prāmāṇyaṃ jñānahetvatiriktahetvadhīnaṃ kāryatve sati
          tadviśeṣāśritatvād aprāmāṇyavat/
children.translated_text: And thus the formal argument: the disputed validity is dependent on a cause other than the cause of cognition -- because, being an effect, it resides in a particular [cognition] of that [cognition] -- like invalidity.

children.text: prāmāṇyaṃ parato jñāyate anabhyāsadaśāyāṃ sāṃśayikatvād aprāmāṇyavat/
children.translated_text: [Another argument:] validity is known extrinsically -- because in the state of non-familiarity, it is subject to doubt -- like invalidity.

children.text:
tasmād utpattau jñaptau ca paratastve pramāṇasaṃbhavāt svataḥsiddhaṃ prāmāṇyam ity etat
          pūtikūṣmāṇḍāyata iti cet —
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Therefore, since there is a valid means of knowledge for the extrinsic [view] regarding both production and apprehension, the [claim of] intrinsically established validity amounts to a rotten pumpkin!' --
reference marker

children.text:
tad etad ākāśamuṣṭihananāyate/ vijñānasāmagrījanyatve sati tadatiriktahetvajanyatvaṃ
          pramāyāḥ svatastvam iti niruktisaṃbhavāt/
children.translated_text: That amounts to punching the sky with one's fist! Because it is possible to define [intrinsic validity] as: being produced by the mere causal aggregate of cognition [means] that, while being produced by the causal aggregate of cognition, [validity] is not produced by a cause additional to that.
And there is an inference here:

children.text: -vimatā pramā vijñānasāmagrījanyatve sati tadatiriktajanyā na bhavati/
children.translated_text: The disputed valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>), while being produced by the causal aggregate of cognition, is not produced by anything additional to that,
because it is not the locus of invalidity (<s>apramātva</s>),
like the valid cognition of a pot and the like.

children.text: na caudayanam anumānaṃ paratastvasādhakam iti śaṅkanīyam/
children.translated_text: Nor should it be suspected that <s>Udayana</s>'s inference establishes the extrinsic [view],
[for the counter-argument is:] a valid cognition is not produced by anything additional to the cause of cognition other than defects,
because it is a cognition,
like an invalid cognition --

children.text:
iti pratisādhanagrahagrastatvāt/ jñānasāmagrīmātrād eva pramotpattisaṃbhave
          tadatiriktasya guṇasya doṣābhāvasya vā kāraṇatvakalpanāyāṃ kalpanāgauravaprasaṅgāc ca/
          nanu doṣasyāpramāhetutvena tadabhāvasya pramāṃ prati hetutvaṃ durnivāram iti cet —
children.translated_text: because [<s>Udayana</s>'s argument] is seized by [this] counter-proof. And because, when the production of valid cognition is possible from the mere causal aggregate of cognition alone, postulating the causality of an additional quality or of the absence of defects would lead to the fault of excessive postulation (<s>kalpanāgaurava</s>). Objection: 'Since defect is the cause of invalid cognition, the causality of the absence of defect with respect to valid cognition is irresistible!' --
No -- because the absence of defects, being the preventer of invalid cognition, is otherwise explicable [without being a cause of valid cognition].
reference marker
Therefore, [Mīmāṃsā holds:] from the absence of defects [arising] from [the presence of] qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), from the absence of those [defects],
the non-existence of the two [types of] invalidity [follows]; therefore the general presumption [of validity] is unrefuted.
reference marker

children.text:
tathā pramājñaptir api jñānajñāpakasāmagrīta eva jāyate/ na ca saṃśayānudayaprasaṅgo
          bādhaka iti yuktaṃ vaktum/ saty api pratibhāsapuṣkalakāraṇe
          pratibandhakadoṣādisamavadhānāt tadupapatteḥ/ kiṃ ca tāvakam anumānaṃ svataḥpramāṇaṃ na
          vā/ ādye 'naikāntikatā/ dvitīye tasyāpi parataḥprāmāṇyam evaṃ tasya tasyāpīty anavasthā
          duravasthā syāt/
children.translated_text: Likewise, the apprehension of a valid cognition also arises from the causal aggregate that makes cognition known. Nor is it correct to say that the absurd consequence of the non-arising of doubt is a defeater -- because, even when the sufficient cause of appearance is present, [doubt] is explicable from the presence of obstructing defects and the like. Moreover, is your inference itself intrinsically valid or not? In the first case, there is inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>). In the second case, the extrinsic validity of that [inference] too, and of that [which establishes the extrinsic validity] too -- would lead to an undesirable infinite regress.
reference marker

children.text:
yad atra kusumāñjalāv udayanena jhaṭ iti pracurapravṛtteḥ prāmāṇyaniścayādhīnatvābhāvam
          āpādayatā praṇyagādi/
children.translated_text: To this, <s>Udayana</s> immediately argued in the <s>Kusumāñjali</s>, establishing the absence of dependence on the ascertainment of validity for the abundance of purposive activity:

children.text:
pravṛttir hīcchām apekṣate/ tatprācuryaṃ cecchāprācuryam/ icchā ceṣṭasādhanatājñānam/
            tac ceṣṭajātīyatvaliṅgānubhavam/ so 'pīndriyārthasaṃnikarṣam/ prāmāṇyagrahaṇaṃ tu na
            kvacid upayujyata iti/
children.translated_text: For activity depends on desire; the abundance of that [activity depends on] the abundance of desire; desire [depends on] the knowledge that [the object] is the means to the desired [end]; that [knowledge depends on] the experience of the inferential mark of being of the same kind as the desired; and that [experience depends on] sense-object contact. But the apprehension of validity is not useful anywhere [in this chain].

children.text:
tad api taskarasya purastāt kakṣe suvarṇam upetya sarvāṅgodghāṭanam iva pratibhāti/ yataḥ
          samīhitasādhanatājñānam eva pramāṇatayāvagamyamānam icchāṃ janayatīty atraiva sphuṭa eva
          prāmāṇyagrahaṇasyopayogaḥ/ kiṃ ca kvacid api cen nirvicikitsā pravṛttiḥ saṃśayād
          upapadyeta tarhi sarvatra tathābhāvasaṃbhavāt prāmāṇyaniścayo nirarthakaḥ syāt/ tathoktam
          — aniścitasya sattvam eva durlabham iti/ yadi sattvaṃ sulabhaṃ bhavet tadā prāmāṇyaṃ
          dattajalāñjalikaṃ bhaved ity alam atiprapañcena/ yasmād uktam —
children.translated_text: That too appears like stripping one's whole body naked upon finding gold in a thicket in front of a thief. Because the knowledge that [the object] is the means to the desired [end], apprehended precisely as a valid cognition, generates desire -- in this very [statement], the usefulness of the apprehension of validity is quite clear. Moreover, if at any point unhesitating activity were explicable from doubt, then since such [a possibility] would exist everywhere, the ascertainment of validity would be purposeless. As stated: 'The very existence of what is unascertained is difficult to obtain.' If existence were easy to obtain, then validity would be offered with libations of water [i.e., abandoned]! Enough with excessive elaboration. Since it is stated:
Therefore, the status of being a valid means of knowledge is obtained for cognition through the capacity to make known what is real;
it is removed by the knowledge of defects that arise from the cause of the object's being otherwise.
reference marker

children.text:
tasmād dharme svataḥsiddhapramāṇabhāve jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo
          yajetetyādividhyarthavādamantranāmadheyātmake vede yajetety atra tapratyayaḥ
          prakṛtyarthoparaktāṃ bhāvanām abhidhatta iti siddhe vyutpattim abhyupagacchatām
          abhihitānvayavādināṃ bhaṭṭācāryāṇaṃ siddhāntaḥ/ yāgaviṣayaṃ niyogam iti kārye vyutpattim
          anusaratām anvitābhidhānavādināṃ prabhākaragurūṇāṃ siddhānta iti sarvam avadātam//
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the intrinsic validity of the means of knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s> is established -- in the <s>Veda</s>, which consists of injunctive statements (<s>vidhi</s>), laudatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>), <s>mantras</s>, and proper names (<s>nāmadheya</s>), [exemplified by] 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' -- 'one should sacrifice': here the suffix <s>ta</s> (optative) denotes <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation) colored by the meaning of the root -- this is the established doctrine of the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> school of <s>Abhihitānvayavādins</s> (proponents of stated-relation), who accept derivation in what is established. The established doctrine of the <s>Prābhākara</s> school of <s>Anvitābhidhānavādins</s> (proponents of contextual-denotation), who follow the derivation in the injunction (<s>kārya</s>) -- [holding that] it denotes an obligation (<s>niyoga</s>) directed toward sacrifice -- thus everything is clear.
Thus concludes the <s>Jaimini</s> philosophy (Mīmāṃsā) in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Now the <s>Pāṇini</s> philosophy (Grammarian philosophy).
reference marker

children.text:
nanv ayaṃ prakṛtibhāgo ’yaṃ pratyayabhāga iti prakṛtipratyayavibhāgaḥ katham avagamyata
          iti cet:
children.translated_text: Objection: 'How is the division into base (<s>prakṛti</s>) and suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>) -- "this is the base portion, this is the suffix portion" -- ascertained?'

children.text:
pītapātañjalajalānām etac codyaṃ camatkāraṃ na karoti/ vyākaraṇaśāstrasya
          prakṛtiprayayavibhāgapratipādanaparatāyāḥ prasiddhatvāt/ tathā hi patañjaler bhagavato
          mahābhāṣyakārasyedam ādimaṃ vākyam: atha śabdānuśāsanam iti/ asyārthaḥ: athety ayaṃ śabdo
          ’dhikārārthaḥ prayujyate/ adhikāraḥ prastāvaḥ/ prārambha iti yāvat/ śabdānuśāsanaśabdena
          ca pāṇinipraṇītaṃ vyākaraṇaśāstraṃ vivakṣyate/ śabdānuśāsanam ity etāvaty abhidhīyamāne
          saṃdehaḥ syāt/ kiṃ śabdānuśāsanaṃ prastūyate na veti/ tathā mā prasāṅkṣīd ity athaśabdaṃ
          prāyuṅkta/ athaśabdaprayogabalenārthāntaravyudāsena prastūyata ity asyābhidhīyamānatvāt/
          anena hi vaidikāḥ śabdāḥ śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaye ityādayas tadupakāriṇo laukikāḥ śabdā gaur
          aśvaḥ puruṣo hastī śakunir ityādayaś cānuśiṣyante vyutpādya saṃskriyante
          prakṛtipratyayavibhāgavattayā bodhyanta iti śabdānuśāsanam/
children.translated_text: For those who have drunk the waters of <s>Patañjali</s>, this objection produces no wonder -- because it is well known that the science of grammar (<s>vyākaraṇaśāstra</s>) is devoted to teaching the division of base and suffix. For thus, the opening statement of the blessed <s>Patañjali</s>, the author of the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s>, is: 'Now, the instruction of words' (<s>atha śabdānuśāsanam</s>). Its meaning: the word <s>atha</s> is used in the sense of commencement (<s>adhikāra</s>). Commencement means beginning; that is to say, a starting point. By the compound <s>śabdānuśāsana</s>, the science of grammar composed by <s>Pāṇini</s> is intended. If merely <s>śabdānuśāsanam</s> were said, there would be doubt whether the instruction of words is being commenced or not. Lest such [doubt arise], he employed the word <s>atha</s>. Because, by the force of using the word <s>atha</s>, through the exclusion of other meanings, [the sense] 'it is being commenced' is conveyed. For by this [grammar], Vedic words such as '<s>śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaye</s>' and the like, and worldly words that serve those -- such as 'cow,' 'horse,' 'man,' 'elephant,' 'bird,' and the like -- are instructed, that is, derived and refined, made known as possessing the division of base and suffix. This is <s>śabdānuśāsana</s> (instruction of words).
reference marker

children.text:
atra kecit paryanuyuñjate: anuśāsikriyāyāḥ sakarmakatvāt karmabhūtasya śabdasya
          kartṛbhūtasyācāryasya prāptau satyām ubhayaprāptau karmaṇi ity anuśāsanabalāt karmaṇy eṣā
          ṣaṣṭhī vidhātavyā/ tathā ca karmaṇi ca iti samāsapratiṣedhasaṃbhavāc chabdānuśāsanaśabdo
          na pramāṇapatham avataratīti/ atrāyaṃ samādhir abhidhīyate yasmin kṛtpratyaye
          kartṛkarmaṇor ubhayoḥ prāptir asti tatra karmaṇy eva ṣaṣṭhīvibhaktir bhavati na kartarīti
          bahuvrīhivijñānabalān niyamyate/ tad yathāścaryo gavāṃ doho ’śikṣitena gopālakeneti/
          śabdānuśāsanam ity atra tu śabdānām anuśāsanaṃ nārthānām ity etāvato
          vivakṣitasyārthasyācāryasya kartur upādānena vināpi supratipādyatvād

ācāryopādānam akiṃcitkaram/ tasmād ubhayaprāpter abhāvād ubhayaprāptau karmaṇīty
          eṣā ṣaṣṭhī na bhavati/ kiṃ tu kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti (Pā° sū° 2.3.65) iti kṛdyoge kartari
          karmaṇi ca ṣaṣṭhī vibhaktir bhavatīti kṛdyogalakṣaṇā ṣaṣṭhī bhaviṣyati/ tathā
          cedhmapravraścanapalāśaśātanādivat samāso bhaviṣyati/ kartary api ṣaṣṭhī bhavatīti kecid
          bruvate/ ata eva evoktaṃ kāśikāvṛttau: kecid aviśeṣeṇaiva vibhāṣām icchanti śabdānām
          anuśāsanam ācāryeṇācāryasya veti/ atha vā śeṣalakṣaṇeyaṃ ṣaṣṭhī/ tatra kim api codyaṃ
          nāvataraty eva/ yady evaṃ tarhi śeṣalakṣaṇāyāḥ ṣaṣṭhyāḥ sarvatra suvacatvāt
          ṣaṣṭḥīsamāsapratiṣedhasūtrāṇām ānarthakyaṃ prāpnuyād iti cet,
children.translated_text: the mention of the teacher is superfluous. Therefore, since there is no availability of both [agent and object], the genitive [assigned] by the rule 'in the objective case when both are available' does not apply. Rather, the genitive will be by the rule '<s>kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 2.3.65) -- in a <s>kṛt</s>-suffix [formation], the sixth case applies to both agent and object. And thus the compound will be formed like <s>idhma-pravraścana</s>, <s>palāśa-śātana</s>, and the like. Some say the sixth case applies to the agent as well. Therefore it is stated in the <s>Kāśikāvṛtti</s>: 'Some desire the option without distinction -- instruction of words, by the teacher, or of the teacher.' Or alternatively, this genitive is by the residual (<s>śeṣa</s>) [relation]. In that case, no objection descends at all. 'If so, then since the genitive by residual relation would be easily applicable everywhere, the <s>sūtras</s> that prohibit genitive compounds would become purposeless' -- if [so objected],

Here some raise an objection: since the verb 'to instruct' (<s>anuśāsiḥ</s>) is transitive, when the object -- the word -- and the agent -- the teacher -- are both available, given the availability of both, by the force of the [rule] '<s>anuśāsana</s>' [being in the objective case], this sixth case-ending (genitive) should be assigned to the object [<s>śabda</s>]. And thus, since the prohibition of compounding in the objective case [by the rule] 'and in the objective case' is possible, the compound <s>śabdānuśāsana</s> would not be grammatically valid. The resolution is stated here: when, in a <s>kṛt</s>-suffix [formation], both agent and object are available, the sixth case-ending applies only to the object, not to the agent -- this is restricted by the force of the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> interpretation. For example: 'Wonderful is the milking of cows by an untrained cowherd.' In <s>śabdānuśāsanam</s> here, since the intended meaning -- 'instruction of words, not of meanings' -- is perfectly communicable even without mentioning the teacher as agent,

children.text:
satyam/ teṣāṃ svaracintāyām upayogo vākyapadīye hariṇā prādarśi/ tad āha
          mahopādhyāyavardhamānaḥ:
children.translated_text: True. The use of those [prohibitory sūtras] in accent-analysis (<s>svaracintā</s>) has been shown by <s>Hari</s> (Bhartṛhari) in the <s>Vākyapadīya</s>. Thus states the great teacher <s>Vardhamāna</s>:
In worldly usage, let people act as they wish;
but in Vedic paths, let specific [grammatical] expression prevail.
Since thereby the meaningfulness of <s>Pāṇini</s>'s <s>sūtras</s> [is preserved],

children.text: janikartur iti brūte tatprayojaka ity api// iti/
children.translated_text: he says '<s>janikartuḥ</s>' (of the agent of production) and also '<s>tatprayojakaḥ</s>' (the instigator of that).

children.text:
tathā ca śabdānuśāsanāparanāmadheyaṃ vyākaraṇaśāstram ārabdhaṃ veditavyam iti vākyārthaḥ
          saṃpadyate/
children.translated_text: And thus the sentence-meaning is achieved: the science of grammar, whose other name is 'instruction of words' (<s>śabdānuśāsana</s>), has been commenced -- this is to be understood.
reference marker

children.text:
tasyārthasya jhaṭ iti pratipattaye atha vyākaraṇam ity evābhidhīyatām/ atha
          śabdānuśāsanam ity adhikākṣaraṃ mudhābhidhīyata iti/ maivam/ śabdānuśāsanam ity
          anvarthasamākhyopādāne tadīyavedāṅgatvapratipādakaprayojanānvākhyānasiddheḥ/ anyathā
          prayojanānabhidhāne vyākaraṇādhyayane ’dhyetṝṇāṃ pravṛttir eva na prasajyet/ nanu
          niṣkāraṇo dharmaḥ ṣaḍaṅgo vedo ’dhyetavya ity adhyetavyatvavidhānād eva pravṛttiḥ
          setsyatīti cet,
children.translated_text: For the swift comprehension of that meaning, let it be called "grammar" (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>). But [you say] "instruction of words" (<s>śabdānuśāsana</s>) is uselessly stated with extra syllables — do not say so! Because by adopting the meaningful name "instruction of words" (<s>śabdānuśāsana</s>), the purpose-explanatory statement (<s>prayojanānvākhyāna</s>), which conveys its status as a <s>Vedāṅga</s> (auxiliary of the <s>Veda</s>), is accomplished. Otherwise, if the purpose were not stated, the activity of students in studying grammar would simply not arise. Now, if [one says]: "<s>Dharma</s> is without [external] reason; the sixfold <s>Veda</s> is to be studied — activity will be established by the very injunction to study" —

children.text:
maivam/ tathā vidhāne ’pi tadīyavedāṅgatvapratipādakaprayojanānabhidhāne teṣāṃ pravṛtter
          anupapatteḥ/ tathā hi purā kila vedam adhītyādhyetāras tvaritaṃ vaktāro bhavanti/
children.translated_text: Do not say so! Because even in such an injunction, if the purpose-explanatory statement conveying its status as a <s>Vedāṅga</s> is not stated, their activity is untenable. For thus: formerly, having studied the <s>Veda</s>, students indeed quickly became [competent] speakers.

children.text: vedān no vaidikāḥ śabdāḥ siddhā lokāc ca laukikāḥ/
children.translated_text: "Vedic words are established from the <s>Vedas</s>, and worldly words from common usage;

children.text:
tasmād anarthakaṃ vyākaraṇam iti/ tasmād vedāṅgatvaṃ manyamānās tadadhyayane pravṛttim
          akārṣuḥ/ tataś cedānīṃtanānām api tatra pravṛttir na sidhyet/ sā mā prasāṅkṣīd iti
          tadīyavedāṅgatvapratipādakaṃ prayojanam anvākhyeyam eva/ yady anvākhyāte ’pi prayojane na
          pravarteraṃs tarhi laukikaśabdasaṃskārajñānarahitās te yājñe karmaṇi pratyavāyabhājo
          bhaveyuḥ/ dharmād dhīyeran/ ata eva yājñikāḥ paṭhanti: āhitāgnir apaśabdaṃ prayujya
          prāyaścittīyāṃ sārasvatīm iṣṭiṃ nirvaped iti/ atas
          tadīyavedāṅgatvapratipādakaprayojanānvākhyānārtham atha śabdānuśāsanam ity eva kathyate
          nātha vyākaraṇam iti/ bhavati ca śabdasaṃskāro vyākaraṇaśāstrasya prayojanam/ tasya
          taduddeśena pravrtteḥ/ yathā svargoddeśena pravṛttasya yāgasya svargaḥ prayojanam/ tasmāc
          chabdānuśiṣṭiḥ saṃskārapadavedanīyā śabdānuśāsanasya prayojanam/
children.translated_text: therefore grammar is purposeless." Hence, thinking of it as a <s>Vedāṅga</s>, they engaged in its study.
