          brahmajijñāsā ity atra tu brahmajijñāsāyā anadhikāryatvenādhikārārthatvaṃ parityajya
          sādhanacatuṣṭayasaṃpattiviśiṣṭādhikārisamarpaṇāya śamadamādivākyavihitāc chamāder
          ānantaryam athaśabdārtha iti śaṃkarācāryair niraṭaṅki/
children.translated_text: and from this <s>Smṛti</s>. For this very reason, succession from a student's question, the practice of austerities, the use of elixirs, and the like is also rejected. In '<s>athāto brahmajijñāsā</s>' (Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>), however, since the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> is one for which [one might be] unqualified (<s>anadhikārin</s>), abandoning the interpretation of commencement, [<s>atha</s>] in the sense of succession from tranquility and the like — enjoined by the passage on tranquility, self-restraint, and the like — for the purpose of specifying the qualified student who possesses the fourfold prerequisite (<s>sādhanacatuṣṭaya</s>), is maintained without hesitation by <s>Śaṃkarācārya</s>.

children.text:
atha mā nāma bhūd ānantaryārtho 'thaśabdaḥ/ maṅgalārthaḥ kiṃ na syāt/ na syāt/ maṅgalasya
          vākyārthe samanvayābhāvāt/ agarhitābhīṣṭāvāptir maṅgalam/ abhīṣṭaṃ ca
          sukhāvāptiduḥkhaparihārarūpatayeṣṭam/ yogānuśāsanasya ca sukhaduḥkhanivṛttyor
          anyataratvābhāvān na maṅgalatā/ tathā ca yogānuśāsanaṃ maṅgalam iti na saṃpanīpadyate/
          mṛdaṅgadhvaner ivāthaśabdaśravaṇasya kāryatayā maṅgalasya vācyatvalakṣyatvayor asaṃbhavāc
          ca/ yathārthikārtho vākyārthe na niviśate tathā kāryam api na niviśeta/
          apadārthatvāviśeṣāt/ padārtha eva hi vākyārthe samanvīyate/ anyathā śabdapramāṇakānāṃ
          śābdī hy ākāṅkṣā śabdenaiva pūryata iti mudrābhaṅgaḥ kṛto bhavet/
children.translated_text: Now, let <s>atha</s> not be in the sense of succession. Why should it not be in the sense of auspiciousness (<s>maṅgala</s>)? It should not — because auspiciousness has no syntactic connection with the sentence-meaning. Auspiciousness is the attainment of a blameless desired [object]. And the desired [object] is what is wished for in the form of obtaining happiness and removing suffering. And since <s>yoga</s> instruction is neither the obtaining of happiness nor the removal of suffering, it does not qualify as auspiciousness. And thus, '<s>yoga</s> instruction is auspicious' does not hold together. And because, since the hearing of the word '<s>atha</s>' is an effect — like the sound of a drum — neither the denotation nor the indication of auspiciousness is possible [for the word <s>atha</s>]. Just as the meaning of '<s>arthika</s>' (one who desires wealth) does not enter into the sentence-meaning, so too an effect should not enter [as sentence-meaning] — because there is no distinction in their being non-word-meanings. For only word-meanings are syntactically connected in sentence-meaning. Otherwise, for those for whom scripture is the means of knowledge, [since] verbal expectation is fulfilled by words alone — their seal would be broken.

children.text:
nanu prāripsitaprabandhaparisamāptiparipanthipratyūhavyūhapraśamanāya
          śiṣṭācāraparipālanāya ca śāstrārambhe maṅgalācaraṇam anuṣṭheyam/ maṅgalādīni
          maṅgalamadhyāni maṅgalāntāni ca śāstrāṇi prathante āyuṣmatpuruṣakāṇi vīrapuruṣakāṇi ca
          bhavanti ity abhiyuktokteḥ/ bhavati ca maṅgalārtho 'thaśabdaḥ —
children.translated_text: Objection: 'At the beginning of a treatise, the performance of an auspicious invocation (<s>maṅgalācaraṇa</s>) should be undertaken -- for the pacification of the array of obstacles that impede the completion of the intended composition, and for the preservation of the practice of the learned. For it is stated by authorities: "Treatises that have auspicious beginnings, auspicious middles, and auspicious ends flourish, and are productive of long-lived and heroic persons." And the word <s>atha</s> does serve an auspicious purpose --',
reference marker

children.text: oṃkāraś cāthaśabdaś ca dvāv etau brahmaṇaḥ purā/
children.translated_text: The syllable <s>Oṃ</s> and the word <s>atha</s> -- these two of old

children.text: kaṇṭhaṃ bhittvā viniryātau tasmān māṅgalikāv ubhau//
children.translated_text: burst forth from the throat of <s>Brahman</s>; therefore both are auspicious.

children.text:
iti smṛtisaṃbhavāt/ tathā ca vṛddhir ādaic ityādau vṛddhyādiśabdavad athaśabdo
          maṅgalārthaḥ syād iti cet — maivaṃ bhāṣiṣṭhāḥ/ arthāntarābhidhānāya prayuktasyāthaśabdasya
          vīṇāveṇvādidhvanivad chravaṇamātreṇa maṅgalaphalatvopapatteḥ/
          athārthāntarārambhavākyārthadhīphalakasyāthaśabdasya katham anyaphalakateti cen na/
          anyārthaṃ nīyamānodakumbhopalambhavat tatsaṃbhavāt/ na ca smṛtivyākopaḥ/ māṅgalikāv iti
          maṅgalaprayojanatvavivakṣayā pravṛtteḥ/
children.translated_text: -- because of the support of such a <s>Smṛti</s> text. And thus, just as the word <s>vṛddhi</s> in '<s>vṛddhir ādaic</s>' and the like [serves an auspicious purpose], so too the word <s>atha</s> would serve an auspicious purpose.' Do not speak thus! Because the word <s>atha</s>, employed to denote another meaning, produces the fruit of auspiciousness through mere hearing alone, like the sound of the <s>vīṇā</s>, flute, and the like. Objection: 'How can the word <s>atha</s>, whose fruit is the apprehension of the sentence-meaning of a commencement-statement directed at another purpose, have a different fruit?' -- Not so, because that is possible, like the perception of a water-pot being carried for another purpose. Nor is there any violation of the <s>Smṛti</s>, because [the word] 'auspicious' (<s>māṅgalika</s>) is used with the intention of [expressing] that it has auspiciousness as its purpose.
reference marker

children.text:
nāpi pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣo 'thaśabdaḥ/ phalata ānantaryāvyatirekeṇa prāg uktadūṣaṇānuṣaṅgāt/
          kim ayam athaśabdo 'dhikārārtho 'thānantaryārtha ityādivimarśavākye pakṣāntaropanyāse
          tatsaṃbhave 'pi prakṛte tadasaṃbhavāc ca/
children.translated_text: Nor is the word <s>atha</s> used in the sense of dependence on what was previously discussed -- because, in result, since there is no difference from sequentiality (<s>ānantarya</s>), the previously stated refutation would follow. And because, in the deliberative statement 'Is this word <s>atha</s> in the sense of commencement or in the sense of sequentiality?' -- when an alternative position is presented, even though that [sequentiality] is possible [in general], it is not possible in the present context.
reference marker

children.text:
tasmāt pāriśeṣyād adhikārapadavedanīyaprārambhārtho 'thaśabda iti viśeṣo bhāṣyate/
          yathāthaiṣa jyotir athaiṣa viśvajyotir ity atrāthaśabdaḥ kratuviśeṣaprārambhārthaḥ
          parigṛhīto yathā cātha śabdānuśāsanam ity atrāthaśabdo vyākaraṇaśāstrādhikārārthas tadvat/
          tad abhāṣi vyāsabhāṣye yogasūtravivaraṇapare athety ayam adhikārārthaḥ prayujyata iti/ tad
          vyācakhyau vācaspatiḥ/ tad ittham — amuṣyāthaśabdasyādhikārārthatvapakṣe śāstreṇa
          prastūyamānasya yogasyopavartanāt samastaśāstratātparyārthavyākhyānena śiṣyasya
          sukhāvabodhapravṛttir bhavatīty athaśabdasyādhikārārthatvam upapannam/
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the method of elimination, the word <s>atha</s> is used in the sense of commencement, to be understood by the word denoting 'commencement' -- this distinction is stated [in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>]. Just as in 'Now this is the light; now this is the universal light,' the word <s>atha</s> is understood as denoting the commencement of a particular ritual; and just as in 'Now, the instruction of words,' the word <s>atha</s> is used for the commencement of the science of grammar -- so too [here]. This was stated in the <s>Vyāsabhāṣya</s>, which is devoted to the elucidation of the <s>Yoga Sūtras</s>: 'The word <s>atha</s> is used in the sense of commencement.' <s>Vācaspati</s> explained this. Thus: when the commencement-meaning of this word <s>atha</s> is accepted, since yoga, which is being commenced by the scripture, is introduced, and through the explanation of the purport-meaning of the entire scripture, the disciple's easy comprehension is facilitated -- the commencement-meaning of the word <s>atha</s> is well-established.
reference marker
Objection:
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Golden Embryo) is the teacher of <s>yoga</s>; no other ancient [teacher exists] --

children.text:
iti yājñavalkyasmṛteḥ patañjaliḥ kathaṃ yogasya śāsiteti cet — addhā/ ata eva tatra tatra
          purāṇādau viśiṣya yogasya viprakīrṇatayā durgrāhyārthatvaṃ manyamānena bhagavatā
          kṛpāsindhunā phaṇipatinā sāraṃ saṃjighṛkṣuṇānuśāsanam ārabdhaṃ na tu sākṣāc chāsanam/
          yadāyam athaśabdo 'dhikārārthas tadaivaṃ vākyārthaḥ saṃpadyate — yogānuśāsanaṃ śāstram
          adhikṛtaṃ veditavyam iti/

tasmād ayam athaśabdo 'dhikāradyotako
                maṅgalārthaś ceti siddham
"It is therefore established that this word

suggests ‘beginning’ and means
              ‘auspicious’". Since it is absent from IV (p. 158) and contradicts the preceding
              discussion, it has here been dropped.

children.translated_text: since this is [stated in] the <s>Yājñavalkya Smṛti</s>, how is <s>Patañjali</s> the instructor of <s>yoga</s>? -- Indeed! Therefore, the blessed Serpent-King (<s>Phaṇipati</s>, i.e., <s>Patañjali</s> as <s>Śeṣa</s>), who is an ocean of compassion, considering that the meaning [of yoga], being scattered here and there in various <s>Purāṇas</s> and the like, is difficult to grasp in its dispersed state, began an instruction (<s>anuśāsana</s>), wishing to gather the essence -- but not a direct teaching (<s>śāsana</s>) [which belongs to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>]. When this word <s>atha</s> is in the sense of commencement, the sentence-meaning is achieved thus: the treatise called 'instruction on yoga' (<s>yogānuśāsana</s>) has been commenced -- this is to be understood.
reference marker

children.text:
tatra śāstre vyutpādyamānatayā yogaḥ sasādhanaḥ saphalo viṣayaḥ/ tadvyutpādanam
          avāntaraphalam/ vyutpāditasya yogasya kaivalyaṃ paramaprayojanam/ śāstrayogayoḥ
          pratipādyapratipādakabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandhaḥ/ yogasya kaivalyasya ca
          sādhyasādhanabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandhaḥ/ sa ca śrutyādiprasiddha iti prāg evāvādiṣam/ mokṣam
          apekṣamāṇā evādhikāriṇa ity arthasiddham/ na cāthāto brahmajijñāsā ityādāv adhikāriṇo
          'rthataḥ siddhir āśaṅkanīyā/
          tatrāthaśabdenānantaryābhidhānapraṇāḍikayādhikārisamarpaṇasiddhāv ārthikatvaśaṅkānudayāt/
          ata evoktaṃ śrutiprāpte prakaraṇādīnām anavakāśa iti/ asyārthaḥ — yatra hi śrutyārtho na
          labhyate tatraiva prakaraṇādayo 'rthaṃ samarpayanti netaratra/ yatra tu śabdād
          evārthasyopalambhas tatra netarasya saṃbhavaḥ/ śīghrabodhinyā śrutyā viniyogasya bodhanena
          nirākāṅkṣatayetareṣām anavakāśāt/ kiṃ ca śrutyā bodhite 'rthe tadviruddhārthaṃ prakaraṇādi
          samarpayaty aviruddhaṃ vā/ na prathamaḥ/ viruddhārthabodhakasya tasya bādhitatvāt/ na
          caramaḥ/ vaiyarthyāt/ tad āha — śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāṃ samavāye
          pāradaurbalyam arthaviprakarṣāt iti/
children.translated_text: In that treatise, yoga together with its means and its fruit, being what is to be expounded, is the subject. Its exposition is the secondary fruit. <s>Kaivalya</s> (liberation/isolation) of the yoga that has been expounded is the supreme purpose. The relation between the scripture and yoga is characterized by the nature of what is to be presented and what presents [it]. The relation between yoga and <s>kaivalya</s> is characterized by the nature of means and end. And that [relation] is well-known through <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation) and the like, as I have stated previously. Those who desire <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) are the qualified students -- this is self-evident. Nor should it be suspected that in 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>' and the like, the [determination of] qualified students is accomplished implicitly [rather than by statement]. Because there, through the channel of the word <s>atha</s> denoting sequentiality, the qualified student is indicated -- so the suspicion of implicitness does not arise. Therefore it is stated: 'When [something] is obtained through <s>Śruti</s> (direct statement), context and the like have no scope.' The meaning of this is: where the meaning is not obtained through direct statement, there alone do context and the like convey meaning, not elsewhere. But where the meaning is obtained from the word itself, there is no possibility of the other [means]. Because, since direct statement swiftly communicates the connection, the others have no scope due to the absence of any need. Moreover, when the direct statement has communicated a meaning, does the context convey a meaning contradicting that, or a non-contradicting one? Not the first -- because that [context], conveying a contradictory meaning, would be sublated. Not the last -- because it would be purposeless. Therefore it is stated: 'Among direct statement (<s>śruti</s>), indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), sentence (<s>vākya</s>), context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), position (<s>sthāna</s>), and designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) -- when they converge, there is gradation from strength to weakness, due to remoteness from the object.'

children.text: bādhikaiva śrutir nityaṃ samākhyā bādhyate sadā/
children.translated_text: Direct statement (<s>Śruti</s>) is always the defeater; designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) is always defeated;

children.text: madhyamānāṃ tu bādhyatvaṃ bādhakatvam apekṣayā// iti ca/
children.translated_text: the status of the intermediate ones as defeated or defeating depends on the [relative] context.

children.text:
tasmād viṣayādimattvād brahmavicārakaśāstravad yogānuśāsanaṃ śāstram ārambhaṇīyam iti
          sthitam/
children.translated_text: Therefore, since [this scripture] possesses a subject-matter and the like, like the treatise on the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>, the treatise called 'instruction on yoga' deserves to be commenced. This is established.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu vyutpādyamānatayā yoga evātra prastuto na śāstram iti cet — satyam/ pratipādyatayā
          yogaḥ prādhānyena prastutaḥ/ sa ca tadviṣayeṇa śāstreṇa pratipādyata iti tatpratipādane
          karaṇaṃ śāstram/ karaṇagocaraś ca kartṛvyāpāro na karmagocaratām ācarati/ yathā chettur
          devadattasya vyāpārabhūtam udyamananipātanādikarma karaṇabhūtaparaśugocaraṃ na
          karmabhūtavṛkṣādigocaram/ tathā ca vaktuḥ patañjaleḥ pravacanavyāpārāpekṣayā
          yogaviṣayasyādhikṛtatā karaṇasya śāstrasya/ abhidhānavyāpārāpekṣayā tu yogasyaiveti
          vibhāgaḥ/ tataś ca yogaśāstrasyārambhaḥ saṃbhāvanāṃ bhajate/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Since yoga is the subject being expounded, it is yoga that is being commenced here, not the treatise.' True. Yoga, as what is to be presented, is commenced primarily. And that [yoga] is presented through the treatise that has it as its subject. Therefore the treatise is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) in that presentation. And the operation of the instrument falls within the domain of the agent, not the domain of the object. Just as the action of lifting and striking and the like, which is the operation of the cutter <s>Devadatta</s>, falls within the domain of the instrument -- the axe -- not within the domain of the object -- the tree and the like. Similarly, with reference to the activity of utterance by <s>Patañjali</s> the speaker, the treatise as instrument is what is commenced, whose subject is yoga. But with reference to the activity of designation, it is yoga itself [that is commenced]. This is the distinction. And thus the commencement of the yoga-scripture is plausible.
reference marker

children.text:
atra cānuśāsanīyo yogaś cittavṛttinirodha ity ucyate/ nanu yujir yoga iti saṃyogārthatayā
          paripaṭhitād yujer niṣpanno yogaśabdaḥ saṃyogavacana eva syān na tu nirodhavacanaḥ/ ata
          evoktaṃ yājñavalkyena —
children.translated_text: And here, the yoga to be instructed is said to be the cessation of the modifications of the mind (<s>cittavṛttinirodha</s>). Objection: 'The word <s>yoga</s>, derived from the root <s>yuj</s> listed as having the meaning of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) in "<s>yujir yoge</s>," should mean conjunction alone, not cessation.' Therefore <s>Yājñavalkya</s> stated:

children.text: saṃyogo yoga ity ukto jīvātmaparamātmanoḥ/ iti/
children.translated_text: Conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is said to be yoga -- of the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) and the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>).
reference marker

children.text:
/ jīvaparayoḥ saṃyoge kāraṇasyānyatarakarmāder asaṃbhavāt/ ajasaṃyogasya
          kaṇabhakṣākṣacaraṇādibhiḥ pratikṣepāc ca/ mīmāṃsakamatānusāreṇa tadaṅgīkāre 'pi
          nityasiddhasya tasya sādhyatvābhāvena śāstravaiphalyāpatteś ca/ dhātūnām anekārthatvena
          yujeḥ samādhyarthatvopapatteś ca/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: because a cause -- whether action or something else -- for the conjunction of the <s>jīva</s> and the Supreme is impossible. And because the conjunction of the soul (<s>aja</s>) has been rejected by <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> (<s>Kaṇāda</s>), <s>Akṣacaraṇa</s> (<s>Gautama</s>), and others. And because, even if it were accepted following the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> view, since that [conjunction] is eternally established, [yoga] would lack the status of something to be accomplished, resulting in the futility of the scripture. And because, since verbal roots have multiple meanings, it is possible that <s>yuj</s> has the meaning of <s>samādhi</s> (absorption). As stated:
That is not correct,

children.text: nipātāś copasargāś ca dhātavaś ceti te trayaḥ/
children.translated_text: Particles (<s>nipāta</s>), prefixes (<s>upasarga</s>), and verbal roots (<s>dhātu</s>) -- these three

children.text: anekārthāḥ smṛtāḥ sarve pāṭhas teṣāṃ nidarśanam// iti/
children.translated_text: are all known to have multiple meanings; their listing is [merely] illustrative.
reference marker

children.text:
ata eva kecana yujiṃ samādhāv api paṭhanti yuja samādhāv iti/ nāpi
          yājñavalkyavacanavyākopaḥ/ tatrasthasyāpi yogaśabdasya samādhyarthatvāt/
children.translated_text: Therefore, some list <s>yuj</s> as also having the meaning of <s>samādhi</s>: '<s>yuja samādhau</s>' (the root <s>yuj</s> in the sense of absorption). Nor is there any violation of <s>Yājñavalkya</s>'s statement, because the word <s>yoga</s> occurring there also has the meaning of <s>samādhi</s>.
<s>Samādhi</s> (absorption) is the state of equality of the individual self and the supreme self;

children.text: brahmaṇy eva sthitir yā sā samādhiḥ pratyagātmanaḥ//
children.translated_text: the abiding in <s>Brahman</s> alone -- that is the <s>samādhi</s> of the inner self.

children.text: iti tenaivoktatvāc ca/ tad uktaṃ bhagavatā vyāsena yogaḥ samādhir iti/
children.translated_text: -- because this too has been stated by him (<s>Yājñavalkya</s>) himself. As stated by the blessed <s>Vyāsa</s>: 'Yoga is <s>samādhi</s>.'
reference marker

children.text:
nanv evam aṣṭāṅgayoge caramasyāṅgasya samādhitvam uktaṃ patañjalinā
          yamaniyamāsanaprāṇāyāmapratyāhāradhāraṇādhyānasamādhayo 'ṣṭāv aṅgāni yogasyeti/ na cāṅgy
          evāṅgatām gantum utsahate/ upakāryopakārakabhāvasya darśapūrṇamāsaprayājādau
          bhinnāyatanatvenātyantabhedāt/ ataḥ samādhir api na yogaśabdārtho yujyata iti cet — tan na
          yujyate/ vyutpattimātrābhidhitsayā tad evārthamātranirbhāsaṃ svarūpaśūnyam iva samādhiḥ
          iti nirūpitacaramāṅgavācakena samādhiśabdenāṅgino yogasyābhedavivakṣayā vyapadeśopapatteḥ/
          na ca vyutpattibalād eva sarvatra śabdaḥ pravartate/ tathātve gacchatīti gaur iti
          vyutpattes tiṣṭhan gaur na syāt/ gacchan devadattaś ca gauḥ syāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'If so, then in the eightfold yoga, the last limb is stated to be <s>samādhi</s> by <s>Patañjali</s>: "Restraint (<s>yama</s>), observance (<s>niyama</s>), posture (<s>āsana</s>), breath-control (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>), withdrawal (<s>pratyāhāra</s>), concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and absorption (<s>samādhi</s>) are the eight limbs of yoga." And a limb cannot presume to become the [whole] limbed [entity]. Because the relationship of means and end (<s>upakārya-upakāraka</s>), like that of the <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifice and the <s>prayāja</s> and the like, involves completely different substrata and thus absolute difference.' Therefore, <s>samādhi</s> too is not appropriate as the meaning of the word yoga.' -- That is not correct. Because, by the word <s>samādhi</s>, which denotes the last limb determined as 'that [state] which, by the mere intention of expressing the etymological meaning, shines forth as the mere [reflected] meaning, as if devoid of its own form -- that is <s>samādhi</s>' -- the designation of the possessor of the limb (<s>aṅgin</s>) -- yoga -- is explicable through the intention of [expressing] non-difference [between the chief limb and the whole]. And a word does not operate everywhere merely by the force of etymology. If so, since [a cow] is etymologically derived as 'one who goes,' a standing [cow] would not be a <s>go</s> (cow). And a walking <s>Devadatta</s> would be a <s>go</s>.
reference marker

children.text:
pravṛttinimittaṃ ca prāg uktam eva cittavṛttinirodha iti/ tad uktaṃ yogaś
          cittavṛttinirodhaḥ iti/
children.translated_text: And the reason for [the word's] application is precisely what was stated earlier -- the cessation of the modifications of the mind. As stated: 'Yoga is the cessation of the modifications of the mind' (<s>yogaś cittavṛttinirodhaḥ</s>).
reference marker

children.text:
nanu vṛttīnaṃ nirodhaś ced yogo 'bhimatas tāsāṃ jñānatvenātmāśrayatayā tannirodho 'pi
          pradhvaṃsapadavedanīyas tadāśrayo bhavet/ prāgabhāvapradhvaṃsayoḥ
          pratiyogisamānāśrayatvaniyamāt/ tataś ca
children.translated_text: Objection: 'If yoga is accepted as the cessation of the modifications, then since those [modifications] are of the nature of knowledge and thus have the self as their substratum, their cessation too, being a posterior absence (<s>pradhvaṃsa</s>), would have the same substratum. Because of the rule that prior absence and posterior absence share the same substratum as their counter-correlate. And thus,

children.text: upayann apayan dharmo vikaroti hi dharmiṇam/
children.translated_text: a property arising and departing modifies the property-bearer --

children.text:
iti nyāyenātmanaḥ kauṭasthyaṃ vihanyeteti cet — tad api na ghaṭate/
          nirodhapratiyogibhūtānāṃ pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtisvarūpāṇāṃ vṛttīnām
          antaḥkaraṇādyaparaparyāyacittadharmatvāṅgīkārāt/ kūṭasthanityā cicchaktir apariṇāminī
          vijñānadharmāśrayo bhavituṃ nārhaty eva/ na ca citiśakter apariṇāmitvam asiddham iti
          mantavyam/ citiśaktir apariṇāminī sadā jñātṛtvāt/ na yad evaṃ na tad evaṃ yathā cittādi —
          ityādyanumānasaṃbhavāt/ tathā yady asau puruṣaḥ pariṇāmī syāt tadā pariṇāmasya
          kādācitkatvāt tāsāṃ cittavṛttīnāṃ sadā jñātatvaṃ nopapadyeta/ cidrūpasya puruṣasya
          sadaivādhiṣṭhātṛtvenāvasthitasya yad antaraṅgaṃ nirmalaṃ sattvaṃ tasyāpi sadaiva
          sthitatvāt yena yenārthenoparaktaṃ bhavati tasya dṛśyasya sadaiva cicchāyāpattyā
          bhānopapattyā puruṣasya niḥsaṅgatvaṃ saṃbhavati/ tataś ca siddhaṃ tasya sadā jñātṛtvam iti
          na kadācit pariṇāmitvaśaṅkāvatarati/ cittaṃ punar yena viṣayeṇoparaktaṃ bhavati sa viṣayo
          jñātaḥ yenoparaktaṃ na bhavati tad ajñātam iti vastuno 'yaskāntamaṇikalpasya
          jñānājñānakāraṇabhūtoparāgānuparāgadharmitvād ayaḥsadharmakaṃ cittaṃ pariṇāmīty
          ucyate/
children.translated_text: by this principle, the immutability (<s>kūṭasthya</s>) of the self would be undermined.' -- That too does not work. Because it is accepted that the modifications -- whose forms are valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), sleep (<s>nidrā</s>), and memory (<s>smṛti</s>), which are the counter-correlates of cessation -- are properties of the mind (<s>citta</s>), otherwise known as the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) and the like. The power of consciousness (<s>cicchakti</s>), which is eternally immutable (<s>kūṭasthanitya</s>) and non-transforming, cannot possibly be the substratum of the properties of cognition. Nor should it be thought that the non-transforming nature of the power of consciousness is unestablished. Because the inference is possible: the power of consciousness is non-transforming, because it is always a knower -- what is not so is not so, like the mind and the like. Moreover, if that <s>Puruṣa</s> were subject to transformation, then since transformation is occasional, the perpetual knowness of those mental modifications would be inexplicable. Since the <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose nature is consciousness, is always established as the presider, and since the inner pure <s>sattva</s> too is always present -- whatever object colors [the sattva], that seen [object], through the perpetual falling of the shadow of consciousness upon it, is explicable as illuminated, and the detachment of <s>Puruṣa</s> is possible. Therefore, his perpetual knower-hood is established, and the suspicion of transformability never arises. But the mind (<s>citta</s>), by whatever object it is colored, that object is known; by what it is not colored, that is unknown. Since the thing [i.e., the mind], being like a lodestone, has the property of being colored or not colored, which is the cause of knowledge and ignorance, the mind, being analogous to iron, is said to be subject to transformation.

          yatra śarīre vṛttimat tena śarīreṇa saha saṃbandho yeṣāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ teṣv evāsya jñānaṃ

parañjayantīty uktam/ tasmāc cittasya dharmā vṛttayo nātmanaḥ/ tathā ca śrutiḥ —
          kāmaḥ saṃkalpo vicikitsā śraddhāśraddhā dhṛtir adhṛtir hrīr dhīr bhīr ity etat sarvaṃ mana
          eva iti/ cicchakter apariṇāmitvaṃ pañcaśikhācāryair ākhyāyi — apariṇāminī bhoktṛśaktir
          iti/ patañjalināpi sadā jñātāś cittavṛttayas tatprabhoḥ puruṣasyāpariṇāmitvāt iti/
          cittapariṇāmitve 'numānam ucyate — cittaṃ pariṇāmi jñātājñātaviṣayatvāt śrotrādivad
          iti/
children.translated_text: conquer [the mind]. Therefore, mental modifications (<s>vṛttis</s>) are properties of the mind, not of the <s>ātman</s> (self). And the <s>śruti</s> states: 'Desire, resolution, doubt, faith and unfaith, steadfastness and unsteadfastness, modesty, intelligence, fear — all this is mind alone.' The unchangeability of the conscious power (<s>cicchakti</s>) was declared by the teacher <s>Pañcaśikha</s>: 'The power of the experiencer is unchanging.' And by <s>Patañjali</s> also: 'The modifications of the mind are always known [by] <s>puruṣa</s>, its lord, because of His unchanging nature.' The inference for the changeability of the mind is stated: 'The mind is changeable, because it has objects both known and unknown, like the ear and the like.'

Now, since the mind (<s>citta</s>) and the sense organs (<s>indriyas</s>), which arise from <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, are all-pervading, they are always connected with all objects. And thus, knowledge of everything at all times and everywhere would absurdly follow — if so, no. Although all-pervading, the mind has cognition only of those objects that are connected with the body in which it functions, and not of others — because there is no such absurd consequence. Therefore, it has been said that objects, like the lodestone, and the mind, like iron, become connected through the channel of the sense organs and

children.text:
dharmiṇaś cittasya nīlādyālocanaṃ dharmapariṇāmaḥ/ yathā kanakasya
          kaṭakamukuṭakeyūrādi/ dharmasya vartamānatvādir lakṣaṇapariṇāmaḥ/ nīlādyālocanasya
          sphuṭatvādir avasthāpariṇāmaḥ/ kaṭakādes tu navapurāṇatvādir avasthāpariṇāmaḥ/ evam
          anyatrāpi yathāsaṃbhavaṃ pariṇāmatritayam ūhanīyam/ tathā ca pramāṇādivṛttīnaṃ
          cittadharmatvāt tannirodho 'pi tadāśraya eveti na kiṃcid anupapannam/
children.translated_text: The apprehension of blue and the like by the mind, the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), is property-transformation (<s>dharmapariṇāma</s>) — just as a bracelet, crown, armlet, and the like [are transformations] of gold. The present-ness and the like of a property is character-transformation (<s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s>). The clarity and the like of the apprehension of blue and so on is state-transformation (<s>avasthāpariṇāma</s>). And for a bracelet and the like, newness, oldness, and the like is state-transformation. Similarly, in other cases too, the triad of transformations should be inferred as applicable. And since the modifications such as valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and the like are properties of the mind, their cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) too pertains to the mind alone — thus nothing is inconsistent.
And transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) is well known to be threefold, by the distinction of property (<s>dharma</s>), character (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and state (<s>avasthā</s>).

children.text:
nanu vṛttinirodho yoga ity aṅgīkāre suṣuptyādau kṣiptamūḍhādicittavṛttīnāṃ
          nirodhasaṃbhavād yogatvaprasaṅgaḥ/ na caitad yujyate/ kṣiptādyavasthāsu kleśaprahāṇāder
          asaṃbhavān niḥśreyasaparipanthitvāc ca/ tathā hi — kṣiptaṃ nāma teṣu teṣu viṣayeṣu
          kṣipyamāṇam asthiraṃ cittam ucyate/ tamaḥsamudre magnaṃ nidrāvṛttibhāvitaṃ mūḍham iti
          gīyate/ kṣiptād viśiṣṭaṃ cittaṃ vikṣiptam iti gīyate/ viśeṣo nāma
children.translated_text: Now, if the cessation of modifications is accepted as <s>yoga</s>, then in deep sleep and the like, since cessation of the mental modifications in the scattered (<s>kṣipta</s>), stupefied (<s>mūḍha</s>), and other states is possible, the absurd consequence of them being <s>yoga</s> would follow. And this is not proper — because in the scattered and other states, the elimination of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) and the like is impossible, and because they obstruct the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). For thus: the scattered (<s>kṣipta</s>) state is said to be the unstable mind being tossed about among various objects. Submerged in the ocean of <s>tamas</s> (darkness), conditioned by the activity of sleep, it is called stupefied (<s>mūḍha</s>). The mind that is distinguished from the scattered state is called distracted (<s>vikṣipta</s>). The distinction is:

children.text: cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham/
children.translated_text: For the mind is restless, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, turbulent, powerful, and obstinate —

children.text:
iti nyāyenāsthirasyāpi manasaḥ kādācitkasamudbhūtaviṣayasthairyasaṃbhavena sthairyam/
          asthiratvaṃ ca svābhāvikaṃ vyādhyādyanuśayajanitaṃ vā/ tad āha —
          vyādhistyānasaṃśayapramādālasyāviratibhrāntidarśanālabdha-bhūmikatvānavasthitatvāni
          cittavikṣepās te 'ntarāyāḥ iti/ tatra doṣatrayavaiṣamyanimitto jvarādir vyādhiḥ/
          cittasyākarmaṇyatvaṃ styānam/ viruddhakoṭidvayāvagāhi jñānaṃ saṃśayaḥ/ samādhisādhanānām
          abhāvanaṃ pramādaḥ/ śarīravākcittagurutvād apravṛttir ālasyam/ viṣayābhilāṣo 'viratiḥ/
          atasmiṃs tadbuddhir bhrāntidarśanam/ kutaścin nimittāt samādhibhūmer alābho
          'labdhabhūmikatvam/ labdhāyām api tasyām cittasyāpratiṣṭhānavasthitatvam ity arthaḥ/
          tasmān na vṛttinirodho yogapakṣanikṣepam arhatīti cet — maivaṃ vocaḥ/
          heyabhūtakṣiptādyavasthātraye vṛttinirodhasya yogatvāsaṃbhave 'py upādeyayor
          ekāgraniruddhāvasthayor vṛttinirodhasya yogatvasaṃbhavāt/ ekatānaṃ cittam ekāgram ucyate/
          niruddhasakalavṛttikaṃ saṃskāramātraśeṣaṃ cittaṃ niruddham iti bhaṇyate/
children.translated_text: by this reasoning, although the mind is unstable, stability is possible through the occasional arising of steadiness regarding objects. And the instability is either natural or produced by the latent impressions (<s>anuśaya</s>) of disease and the like. He states: 'Disease, dullness, doubt, carelessness, laziness, non-abstention, erroneous perception, non-attainment of a stage, and instability — these are the distractions of the mind; they are the obstacles.' Among these: disease (<s>vyādhi</s>) is fever and the like, caused by the imbalance of the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors). Dullness (<s>styāna</s>) is the unfitness of the mind for action. Doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) is knowledge that grasps two contradictory alternatives. Carelessness (<s>pramāda</s>) is the non-cultivation of the means of <s>samādhi</s>. Laziness (<s>ālasya</s>) is non-engagement due to heaviness of body, speech, and mind. Non-abstention (<s>avirati</s>) is desire for sense objects. Erroneous perception (<s>bhrāntidarśana</s>) is the cognition 'that' in what is 'not-that.' Non-attainment of a stage (<s>alabdhabhūmikatva</s>) is the failure to reach the ground of <s>samādhi</s> due to some cause. Instability (<s>anavasthitatva</s>) is the mind's non-establishment even when that ground has been reached. Therefore, the cessation of modifications does not deserve to be placed in the category of <s>yoga</s> — if so, do not say that. Although the cessation of modifications cannot be <s>yoga</s> in the three states of the scattered, stupefied, and distracted — which are to be rejected — it can be <s>yoga</s> in the two states that are to be embraced: the one-pointed (<s>ekāgra</s>) and the arrested (<s>niruddha</s>). The mind that flows in a single stream is called one-pointed. The mind whose all modifications are arrested, with only latent impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) remaining, is called arrested.

children.text:
sa ca samādhir dvividhaḥ/ saṃprajñātāsaṃprajñātabhedāt/ tatraikāgracetasi yaḥ
          pramāṇādivṛttīnāṃ bāhyaviṣayāṇāṃ nirodhaḥ sa saṃprajñātaḥ samādhiḥ/ samyak prajñāyate
          'smin prakṛter viviktatayā dhyeyam iti vyutpatteḥ/ sa caturvidhaḥ/ savitarkādibhedāt/
          samādhir nāma bhāvanā/ sā ca bhāvyasya viṣayāntaraparihāreṇa cetasi punaḥ punar niveśanam/
          bhāvyaṃ ca dvividham — īśvaras tattvāni ca/ tāny api dvividhāni jaḍājaḍabhedāt/ jaḍāni
          prakṛtimahadahaṃkārādīni caturviṃśatiḥ/ ajaḍaḥ puruṣaḥ/ tatra yadā pṛthivyādīni sthūlāni
          viṣayatvenādāya pūrvāparānusaṃdhānena śabdārthollekhasaṃbhedena ca bhāvanā pravartate sa
          samādhiḥ savitarkaḥ/ yadā tanmātrāntaḥkaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ viṣayam ālambya
          deśādyavacchedena bhāvanā pravartate tadā savicāraḥ/ yadā rajastamoleśānuviddhaṃ cittaṃ
          bhāvyate tadā sukhaprakāśamayasya sattvasyodrekāt sānandaḥ/ yadā rajastamoleśānabhibhūtaṃ
          śuddhaṃ sattvam ālambanīkṛtya yā pravartate bhāvanā tadā tasyāṃ sattvasya nyagbhāvāc
          citiśakter udrekāc ca sattāmātrāvaśeṣatvena sāsmitaḥ samādhiḥ/ tad uktaṃ patañjalinā —
          vitarkavicārānandāsmitārūpānugamāt saṃprajñātaḥ iti/ sarvavṛttinirodhe tv asaṃprajñātaḥ
          samādhiḥ/ nanu sarvavṛttinirodho yoga ity ukte saṃprajñāte vyāptir na syāt/ tatra
          sattvapradhānāyāḥ sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātilakṣaṇāyā vṛtter anirodhād iti cet — tad etad
          vārtam/ kleśakarmavipākāśayaparipanthicittavṛttinirodho yoga ity aṅgīkārāt/
children.translated_text: And that <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) is twofold, by the distinction of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> (cognitive) and <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> (non-cognitive). Among these, in the one-pointed mind, the cessation of modifications such as valid cognition and the like that have external objects is <s>saṃprajñāta samādhi</s> — from the etymology: 'in which the object of meditation is rightly known (<s>samyak prajñāyate</s>) as distinct from <s>prakṛti</s>.' It is fourfold, by the distinction of <s>savitarka</s> (with deliberation) and the like. <s>Samādhi</s> is meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), and that is the repeated placing of the object of meditation in the mind, to the exclusion of other objects. The object of meditation is twofold: <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) and the <s>tattvas</s> (principles). Those too are twofold, by the distinction of insentient and sentient. The insentient are the twenty-four [principles] — <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, and the rest. The sentient is <s>puruṣa</s>. Among these, when meditation proceeds by taking gross objects such as earth and the like as its content, with sequential connection of before and after and with the blending of word, meaning, and concept — that <s>samādhi</s> is <s>savitarka</s> (with deliberation). When meditation proceeds by taking a subtle object characterized by the <s>tanmātras</s> and the inner instrument as its support, with delimitation by place and the like — then it is <s>savicāra</s> (with reflection). When the mind tinged with a trace of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> is meditated upon, then, because of the predominance of <s>sattva</s> whose nature is pleasure and illumination, it is <s>sānanda</s> (with bliss). When meditation proceeds by taking as its support pure <s>sattva</s> not overcome by traces of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, then in that [meditation], because of the subordination of <s>sattva</s> and the predominance of the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>), with only bare existence remaining, it is <s>sāsmita</s> (with I-am-ness) <s>samādhi</s>. As stated by <s>Patañjali</s>: '<s>saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi] is accompanied by deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>), reflection (<s>vicāra</s>), bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), and I-am-ness (<s>asmitā</s>).' But when all modifications cease, it is <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>. Now, if 'cessation of all modifications is <s>yoga</s>' is stated, there would be no pervasion in <s>saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi] — because in that state the modification characterized by the discriminative knowledge of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> (<s>sattvapuruṣānyatākhyāti</s>) is not ceased — if so, that is ill-considered. Because it is accepted that <s>yoga</s> is the cessation of mental modifications that are obstacles to afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), <s>karma</s>, fruition (<s>vipāka</s>), and latent deposits (<s>āśaya</s>).

children.text: kleśāḥ punaḥ pañcadhā prasiddhā avidyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśāḥ kleśāḥ iti/
children.translated_text: The afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) are well known to be fivefold: 'Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), I-am-ness (<s>asmitā</s>), attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and clinging to life (<s>abhiniveśa</s>) are the afflictions.'

children.text:
nanv avidyety atra kim āśrīyate pūrvapadārthaprādhānyam amakṣikaṃ vartata itivat/
          uttarapadārthaprādhānyaṃ vā rājapuruṣa itivat/

anyapadārthaprādhānyaṃ vā amakṣiko deśa itivat/ tatra na pūrvaḥ/
          pūrvapadārthaprādhānye avidyāyāṃ prasajyapratiṣedhopapattau kleśādikārakatvānupapatteḥ/
          avidyāśabdasya strīliṅgatvābhāvāpatteś ca/ na dvitīyaḥ/ kasyacid abhāvena viśiṣṭāyā
          vidyāyāḥ kleśādiparipanthitvena tadbījatvānupapatteḥ/ na tṛtīyaḥ/ naño 'styarthānāṃ
          bahuvrīhir vā cottarapadalopaś ceti vṛttikāravacanānusāreṇāvidyamānā vidyā yasyāḥ sā
          avidyā buddhir iti samāsārthasiddhau tasyā avidyāyāḥ kleśādibījatvānupapatteḥ/
          vivekakhyātipūrvakasarvavṛttinirodhasaṃpannāyās tasyās tathātvaprasaṅgāc ca/ uktaṃ
          cāsmitādīnāṃ kleśānām avidyānidānatvam — avidyā kṣetram
children.translated_text: Or is another word-meaning predominant, as in '<s>amakṣiko deśaḥ</s>' (a flyless region)? Among these, not the first — because if the prior word-meaning were predominant, then since in <s>avidyā</s> the negation would function as a simple denial (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>), the role of being the cause of afflictions and the like would be impossible; and because the word <s>avidyā</s> would absurdly fail to be feminine gender. Not the second — because a particular kind of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) characterized by the absence of something cannot be the seed of afflictions and the like, since it would oppose them. Not the third — because, following the statement of the <s>vṛttikāra</s> (commentator): 'the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound with the negative particle applied to existing things, with deletion of the latter member' — the meaning of the compound being 'that intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) in which <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is absent is <s>avidyā</s>' — such <s>avidyā</s> cannot be the seed of afflictions and the like; and because there would be the absurd consequence of that characterization applying to one who has accomplished the cessation of all modifications preceded by discriminative knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>). And it has been stated that <s>avidyā</s> is the ground of the remaining afflictions: '<s>avidyā</s> is the field

children.text:
uttareṣāṃ prasuptatanuvicchinnodārāṇām iti/ tatra prasuptatvaṃ
          prabodhasahakāryabhāvenānabhivyaktiḥ/ tanutvaṃ pratipakṣabhāvanayā śithilīkaraṇam/
          vicchinnatvaṃ balavatā kleśenābhibhavaḥ/ udāratvaṃ sahakārisaṃnidhivaśāt kāryakāritvam/
          tad uktaṃ vācaspatimiśreṇa vyāsabhāṣyavyākhyāyām —
children.translated_text: of the subsequent ones, whether dormant, attenuated, intermittent, or fully active.' Among these: dormancy is non-manifestation due to the absence of a cooperating cause for awakening. Attenuation is weakening through cultivation of the antidote. Intermittence is being overpowered by a stronger affliction. Full activity is producing effects due to the presence of cooperating causes. As stated by <s>Vācaspatimiśra</s> in his commentary on <s>Vyāsa's</s> <s>bhāṣya</s> —

Now, in '<s>avidyā</s>' (ignorance), what is intended? Is the prior word-meaning predominant, as in '<s>amakṣikam vartate</s>' (it exists without flies)? Or is the latter word-meaning predominant, as in '<s>rājapuruṣa</s>' (king's man)?
Dormant in those who are absorbed in the <s>tattvas</s>; attenuated in <s>yogins</s>;
intermittent and fully active — such are the afflictions in those attached to sense objects. Thus.

children.text:
dvandvavat svatantrapadārthadvayānavagamād ubhayapadārthapradhānatvaṃ nāśaṅkitam/ tasmāt
          pakṣatraye 'pi kleśādinidānatvam avidyāyāḥ prasiddhaṃ hīyeteti cet —
children.translated_text: Since from a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative) compound, two independent word-meanings cannot be ascertained, the predominance of both word-meanings should not be suspected. Therefore, if [one objects that] in all three alternatives, the well-known fact that <s>avidyā</s> is the cause of afflictions and the like would be undermined —

children.text:
tad api na śobhanaṃ vibhāti/ paryudāsaśaktim āśrityāvidyāśabdena vidyāviruddhasya
          viparyayajñānasyābhidhānam iti vṛddhair aṅgīkārāt/ tad āha —
children.translated_text: That too does not appear well-founded. Because the elders have accepted that, relying on the function of <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion-negation), the word <s>avidyā</s> denotes erroneous knowledge (<s>viparyayajñāna</s>) that is contrary to [true] knowledge. He states —
When the negative particle is joined with a nominal stem or verbal root meaning, it is not a simple negation;
it expresses non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s> and non-<s>dharma</s> as merely contrary to the other [i.e., to <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>dharma</s>]. Thus.

children.text: vṛddhaprayogagamyo hi śabdārthaḥ sarva eva naḥ/
children.translated_text: The meaning of words is entirely understood by us through the usage of the learned;

children.text: tena yatra prayukto yo na tasmād apanīyate// iti/
children.translated_text: therefore, wherever a word is used, it cannot be displaced from that [meaning]. Thus.

children.text:
vācaspatimiśrair apy uktaṃ lokādhīnāvadhāraṇo hi śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhaḥ/ loke
          cottarapadārthapradhānasyāpi naña uttarapadābhidheyopamardakasya tadviruddhatayā tatra
          tatropalabdher ihāpi tadviruddhe pravṛttir iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Vācaspatimiśra</s> also stated: 'For the connection between words and meanings is determined by common usage. And in common usage, even for the negative particle with predominance of the latter word-meaning, since it is observed here and there as destroying the denotation of the latter member and applying to what is contrary to it, here too it applies to what is contrary.'

children.text:
etad evābhipretyoktam — anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmakhyātir avidyā iti/
          atasmiṃs tadbuddhir viparyaya ity uktaṃ bhavati/ tad yathā — anitye ghaṭādau
          nityatvābhimānaḥ/ aśucau kāyādau śucitvapratyayaḥ —
children.translated_text: With this very intention it was stated: '<s>Avidyā</s> is the cognition of the permanent, pure, pleasant, and self in what is impermanent, impure, painful, and not-self.' Thus it amounts to saying: erroneous knowledge (<s>viparyaya</s>) is the cognition 'that' in what is 'not-that.' For example: the conceit of permanence in the impermanent, such as a pot. The notion of purity in the impure, such as the body —

children.text: sthānād bījād upaṣṭambhān niṣyandān nidhanād api/
children.translated_text: By reason of its origin, seed, sustenance, secretion, and decay,

children.text: kāyam ādheyaśaucatvāt paṇḍitā hy aśuciṃ viduḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: and because it is receptacle-pure [only], the wise know the body to be impure. Thus.

children.text:
ca duḥkham eva sarvaṃ vivekinaḥ iti nyāyena duḥkhe srakcandanavanitādau
          sukhatvāropaḥ/ anātmani dehādāv ātmabuddhiḥ/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: everything is indeed pain for the discerning one' — the superimposition of pleasure on what is painful, such as garlands, sandalwood, and butter. The cognition of self in what is not-self, such as the body. As stated —
By the reasoning: 'due to the pain of transformation, torment, latent impressions, and the conflict of the <s>guṇa</s>-activities,

children.text: anātmani ca dehādāv ātmabuddhis tu dehinām/
children.translated_text: The cognition of self in what is not-self, such as the body, by embodied beings —

children.text: avidyā tatkṛto bandhas tannāśo mokṣa ucyate// iti/
children.translated_text: that is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); the bondage caused by it; and its destruction is called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). Thus.

children.text:
evam iyam avidyā catuṣpadā bhavati/ nanv eteṣv avidyāviśeṣeṣu kiṃcid anugataṃ
          sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ varṇanīyam/ anyathā viśeṣasyāsiddheḥ/ tathā coktaṃ bhaṭṭācāryaiḥ —
children.translated_text: Thus this <s>avidyā</s> has four aspects. Now, among these particular forms of <s>avidyā</s>, some common general characteristic should be described. Otherwise, the particular would be unestablished. And the <s>Bhaṭṭācāryas</s> have stated —
Setting aside the general characteristic, the characteristic of the particular alone

children.text: na śakyaṃ kevalaṃ vaktum ato 'py asya na vācyatā// iti/
children.translated_text: cannot be stated independently — therefore it too is inexpressible. Thus.

children.text: tad api na vācyam/ atasmiṃs tadbuddhir iti sāmānyalakṣaṇābhidhānena dattottaratvāt/
children.translated_text: That too need not be said — because the answer has been given by stating the general characteristic: 'the cognition of "that" in what is "not-that."'
reference marker

children.text:
sattvapuruṣayor aham asmīty ekatābhimāno 'smitā/ tad apy uktaṃ — dṛgdarśanaśaktyor
          ekātmatevāsmitā iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Asmitā</s> (I-am-ness) is the conceit of identity — 'I am' — between <s>sattva</s> (the intellect) and <s>puruṣa</s> (consciousness). As stated: '<s>asmitā</s> is, as it were, the identity of the power of seeing (<s>dṛk</s>) and the power of what is seen (<s>darśana</s>).'
reference marker

children.text:
sukhābhijñasya sukhānusmṛtipūrvakaḥ sukhasādhaneṣu tṛṣṇārūpo gardho rāgaḥ/
          duḥkhābhijñasya tadanusmṛtipurassaraṃ tatsādhaneṣu nivṛttir dveṣaḥ/ tad uktaṃ —
          sukhānuśayī rāgaḥ duḥkhānuśayī dveṣaḥ iti/
children.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) is the craving in the form of thirst (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) for the means of pleasure, preceded by the recollection of pleasure, in one who has experienced pleasure. <s>Dveṣa</s> (aversion) is the turning away from the means of pain, preceded by the recollection of pain, in one who has experienced pain. As stated: '<s>rāga</s> follows upon pleasure; <s>dveṣa</s> follows upon pain.'
reference marker

children.text:
kim atrānuśayiśabde tācchīlyārthe ṇinir inir vā matvarthīyo 'bhimataḥ/ nādyaḥ/ supy
          ajātau ṇinis tācchīlye ity atra supīti vartamāne punaḥ
          subgrahaṇasyopasarganivṛttyarthatvena sopasargād dhātor ṇiner anutpatteḥ/ yathākathaṃcit
          tadaṅgīkāre 'py aco ñṇiti iti vṛddhiprasaktāv atiśāyyādipadavad anuśāyipadasya
          prayogaprasaṅgāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/
children.translated_text: What is intended by the suffix in the word <s>anuśayin</s> — is it the <s>ṇin</s> suffix in the sense of habitual tendency (<s>tācchīlya</s>), or the <s>in</s> suffix in the possessive sense (<s>matvarthīya</s>)? Not the first — because in the rule 'the <s>ṇin</s> suffix is used after a verbal form with a case-ending (<s>sup</s>) in the sense of habitual tendency,' since the word <s>sup</s> is operative [in the rule], the repeated mention of <s>sub</s> serves the purpose of excluding [derivation] from a root with a prefix (<s>upasarga</s>); therefore, the <s>ṇin</s> suffix does not arise from a root with a prefix. Even if it were somehow accepted, since the <s>vṛddhi</s> [vowel strengthening] would be entailed by the rule 'for a stem ending in a vowel before <s>ñ</s> or <s>ṇ</s>-initial [suffixes],' the form <s>anuśāyin</s> would have to be used, like the word <s>atiśāyyin</s> and the like. Nor the second —

children.text: ekākṣarāt kṛto jāteḥ saptamyāṃ ca na tau smṛtau/
children.translated_text: 'After a monosyllabic [stem] and a <s>kṛt</s>-derivative, in the locative case, those two [suffixes <s>ṇin</s> and <s>in</s>] are not recorded' —

children.text:
iti tatpratiṣedhāt/ atra cānuśayaśabdasyājantatvena kṛdantatvāt/ tasmād anuśayiśabdo
          durupapāda iti cet — naitad bhadram/ bhāvānavabodhāt/ prāyikābhiprāyam idaṃ vacanam/ ata
          evoktaṃ vṛttikāreṇa — itikaraṇo vivakṣārthaḥ sarvatrābhisaṃbadhyate iti/ tena kvacid
          bhavati kāryī kāryikas taṇḍulī taṇḍulika iti/ tathā ca kṛdantāj jāteś ca pratiṣedhasya
          prāyikatvam/ anuśayaśabdasya kṛdantatayener upapattir iti siddham/
children.translated_text: because of their prohibition there. And here, the word <s>anuśaya</s>, not ending in a case-suffix, is a <s>kṛt</s>-derivative. Therefore, the word <s>anuśayin</s> is difficult to justify — if [one argues] thus — that is not right, good sir! Because of failure to understand the intention. This statement is meant to express the general [rule]. For this very reason the <s>Vṛttikāra</s> stated: 'The word <s>iti</s> is intended to convey the speaker's intention and applies everywhere.' By that [principle], in some cases there occurs: <s>kāryī</s>/<s>kāryikaḥ</s>, <s>taṇḍulī</s>/<s>taṇ��ulikaḥ</s>. And thus, the prohibition after <s>kṛt</s>-derivatives and universals (<s>jāti</s>) is [merely] a general [rule]. The justification of the <s>in</s> suffix for the word <s>anuśaya</s>, it being a <s>kṛt</s>-derivative, is established.

children.text:
pūrvajanmānubhūtamaraṇaduḥkhānubhavavāsanābalāt sarvasya prāṇabhṛnmātrasyā kṛmer ā ca
          viduṣaḥ saṃjāyamānaḥ śarīraviṣayāder mama viyogo mā bhūd iti pratyahaṃ nimittaṃ vinā
          pravartamāno bhayarūpo 'bhiniveśaḥ pañcamaḥ kleśaḥ/ mā na bhūvaṃ hi bhūyāsaṃ iti
          prārthanāyāḥ pratyātmam anubhavasiddhatvāt/ tad āha — svarasavāhī viduṣo 'pi tathā rūḍho
          'bhiniveśaḥ iti/
children.translated_text: By the force of the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the experience of the suffering of death experienced in previous births, the <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life), which has the nature of fear and arises daily without any [specific] cause in every breathing creature, from a worm to a learned person, [taking the form of] 'May separation from my body, sense-objects, and the like not occur!' — this is the fifth <s>kleśa</s> (affliction). Because the prayer 'May I not cease to exist! May I continue to be!' is experientially established for each individual. Thus he says: '<s>Abhiniveśa</s> is [that which] flows by its own momentum, established even in the learned.'

children.text:
te cāvidyādayaḥ pañca sāṃsārikavividhaduḥkhopahārahetutvena puruṣaṃ kliśnantīti kleśāḥ
          prasiddhāḥ/
children.translated_text: And these five, beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), being the cause of bringing about the manifold sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>, torment the <s>puruṣa</s> (soul) — hence they are well known as <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).

children.text:
karmāṇi vihitapratiṣiddharūpāṇi jyotiṣṭomabrahmahatyādīni/ vipākāḥ karmaphalāni
          jātyāyurbhogāḥ/ ā phalavipākāc cittabhūmau śerata ity āśayā dharmādharmasaṃskārāḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Karmas</s> (actions) are of the nature of prescribed and prohibited [acts] — such as the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice and <s>Brahma</s>-cide, and the like. <s>Vipākas</s> (ripening) are the fruits of action — species of birth (<s>jāti</s>), lifespan (<s>āyus</s>), and experience (<s>bhoga</s>). <s>Āśayas</s> (deposits) are the impressions of merit and demerit that sleep (<s>śerate</s>) in the ground of the mind (<s>citta</s>) until the fruition of the result.

children.text:
tatparipanthicittavṛttinirodho yogaḥ/ nirodho nābhāvamātram abhimatam/ tasya tucchatvena
          bhāvarūpasākṣātkārajananakṣamatvāsaṃbhavāt/ kiṃ tu tadāśrayo
          madhumatīmadhupratīkāviśokāsaṃskāraśeṣāvyapadeśyaś cittasyāvasthāviśeṣaḥ/ nirudhyante
          'smin pramāṇādyāś cittavṛtaya iti vyutpatter upapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> is the cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) of the mental modifications (<s>cittavṛtti</s>) that are the adversary of those [afflictions]. Cessation is not intended as mere non-existence — because, being void, it would be incapable of producing the direct realization of reality. Rather, it is a specific state of the mind (<s>citta</s>) that is the locus of [those states called] <s>madhumatī</s> (honey-like), <s>madhupratīkā</s> (facing honey), <s>viśokā</s> (sorrowless), <s>saṃskāraśeṣā</s> (with only residual impressions), and <s>avyapadeśya</s> (indescribable) — because the etymological derivation 'that in which the mental modifications such as valid cognition and the like are restrained' is appropriate.

children.text:
abhyāsavairāgyābhyāṃ vṛttinirodhaḥ/ tatra sthitau yatno 'bhyāsaḥ/ vṛttirahitasya cittasya
          svarūpaniṣṭhaḥ praśāntavāhitārūpaḥ pariṇāmaviśeṣaḥ sthitiḥ/ taṃ nimittīkṛtya yatnaḥ punaḥ
          punas tathātvena cetasi niveśanam abhyāsaḥ/ carmaṇi dvīpinam hantītivan nimittārtheyaṃ
          saptamīty uktaṃ bhavati/ dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayavitṛṣṇasya vaśīkārasaṃjñā vairāgyam/
          aihikapāratrikaviṣayādau doṣadarśanān nirabhilāṣasya mamaite viṣayā vaśyā nāham eteṣāṃ
          vaśya iti vimarśo vairāgyam ity uktaṃ bhavati/
children.translated_text: The cessation of mental modifications [is achieved] through practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). Therein, effort for stability is practice. 'Stability' is a particular transformation consisting of the state of tranquil flow, abiding in the essential nature of the mind freed from modifications. The effort directed toward that — the repeated establishment of the mind in that state — is practice. 'One who kills a leopard on the hide' — just as there [the locative indicates] the occasion, so this locative [in the sūtra] is explained as indicating the occasion. Dispassion is the mastery-state (<s>vaśīkārasaṃjñā</s>) of one who is free from craving toward seen and heard objects. [That is to say:] for one who, from perceiving faults in worldly and other-worldly objects and the like, is free from desire, the reflective judgment 'These objects are under my control; I am not under their control' — is said to be dispassion.

children.text:
samādhiparipanthikleśatanūkaraṇārthaṃ samādhilābhārthaṃ ca prathamaṃ
          kriyāyogavidhānapareṇa yoginā bhavitavyam/ kriyāyogasaṃpādane 'bhyāsavairāgyayoḥ
          saṃbhavāt/ tad uktaṃ bhagavatā —
children.translated_text: For the purpose of attenuating the afflictions that obstruct <s>samādhi</s>, and for the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, the yogin must first engage in <s>kriyāyoga</s> (yoga of action) — because the accomplishment of <s>kriyāyoga</s> [leads to] the possibility of practice and dispassion. Thus the Blessed Lord stated:

children.text: ārurukṣor muner yogaṃ karma kāraṇam ucyate/
children.translated_text: 'For the sage who wishes to ascend to <s>yoga</s>, action is said to be the means;

children.text: yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇam ucyate// iti/
children.translated_text: for that very one who has ascended to <s>yoga</s>, tranquility is said to be the means.' Thus.

children.text:
kriyāyogaś copadiṣṭaḥ patañjalinā — tapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni kriyāyogaḥ iti/
          tapaḥsvarūpaṃ nirūpitaṃ yājñavalkyena —
children.translated_text: And <s>kriyāyoga</s> has been taught by <s>Patañjali</s>: '<s>Kriyāyoga</s> consists of austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and devotion to the Lord (<s>īśvarapraṇidhāna</s>).' The nature of austerity has been determined by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>:
'Through the method prescribed by the rules, through <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, and other [vows],

children.text: śarīraśoṣaṇaṃ prāhus tapasāṃ tapa uttamam// iti/
children.translated_text: the emaciation of the body — they call that the supreme among austerities.' Thus.
Self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is the recitation of <s>mantras</s> such as <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and the like.

children.text:
te ca mantrā dvividhā vaidikās tāntrikāś ca/ vaidikāś ca dvividhāḥ pragītā apragītāś ca/
          tatra pragītāḥ sāmāni/ apragītāś ca dvividhāḥ/ chandobaddhās tadvilakṣaṇāś ca/ tatra
          prathamā ṛco dvitīyā yajūṃṣi/ tad uktaṃ jaimininā — teṣām ṛg yatrārthavaśena
          pādavyavasthā/ gītiṣu sāmākhyā/ śeṣe yajuḥśabdaḥ iti/ tantreṣu
          kāmikakāraṇaprapañcādyāgameṣu ye ye varṇitās te tāntrikāḥ/ te punar mantrās trividhāḥ
          strīpuṃnapuṃsakabhedāt/ tad āha —
children.translated_text: And those <s>mantras</s> are twofold: Vedic and Tantric. Vedic [mantras] are also twofold: chanted and unchanted. Therein, the chanted ones are the <s>Sāmans</s>. The unchanted too are twofold: metrically bound and different from those. The first are the <s>Ṛcs</s> (verses), the second are the <s>Yajus</s>-formulas. As stated by <s>Jaimini</s>: 'Among those, the <s>Ṛk</s> is that in which the arrangement of verse-quarters (<s>pāda</s>) is determined by the meaning; in songs, the designation is <s>Sāman</s>; the remainder is called <s>Yajus</s>.' Those described in the <s>tantras</s> — the <s>āgamas</s> such as <s>Kāmika</s>, <s>Kāraṇa</s>, <s>Prapañca</s>, and the like — are Tantric. Those <s>mantras</s> are again threefold, through the division of feminine, masculine, and neuter. Thus it is said:
'The classes of <s>mantras</s> are threefold by being feminine, masculine, and neuter;
feminine <s>mantras</s> end in <s>vahnijāyā</s> (svāhā); those ending in <s>namaḥ</s> are neuter;

children.text: śeṣāḥ pumāṃsas te śastāḥ siddhā vaśyādikarmaṇi/ iti/
children.translated_text: the rest are masculine — they are praised as perfected (<s>siddha</s>) for the rites of subjugation and the like.' Thus.

Their being 'perfected' (<s>siddha</s>) [means that] even without the [preliminary] rites beginning with 'enlivening' (<s>janana</s>), they are causes of accomplishment because of being free from all faults.

children.text: sa ca saṃskāro daśavidhaḥ kathitaḥ śāradātilake —
children.translated_text: And that [mantra-]purification (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is stated as tenfold in the <s>Śāradātilaka</s>:
'Ten purificatory rites of <s>mantras</s> are declared, which bestow accomplishment;

children.text: nirdoṣatāṃ prayānty āśu te mantrāḥ sādhu saṃskṛtāḥ//
children.translated_text: those <s>mantras</s>, well-purified, quickly become free from faults.',

children.text: jananaṃ jīvanaṃ caiva tāḍanaṃ bodhanaṃ tathā/
children.translated_text: 'Enlivening (<s>janana</s>), vivifying (<s>jīvana</s>), striking (<s>tāḍana</s>), awakening (<s>bodhana</s>),
anointing (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), then purifying (<s>vimalīkaraṇa</s>) and nourishing (<s>āpyāyana</s>),
sating (<s>tarpaṇa</s>), illuminating (<s>dīpana</s>), and concealing (<s>gupti</s>) — these ten are the mantra-rites.',
'The extraction of the mantra from the <s>mātṛkā</s>-diagram (<s>yantra</s>) is considered enlivening (<s>janana</s>).',
'The wise one should recite the mantra-syllables interspersed with <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ);
they call that vivifying (<s>jīvana</s>), [done] the number of times equal to the mantra-syllables.',
'Having inscribed the mantra-syllables, one should strike them with sandalwood-water,
each one with the wind-seed (<s>vāyubīja</s>) — that is called striking (<s>tāḍana</s>).',
'Having inscribed the mantra-syllables, with oleander (<s>karavīra</s>) flowers
one should strike them — that is considered awakening (<s>bodhana</s>).',
numbering equal to the mantra-syllables,
'According to the procedure stated in the <s>Svatantra</s>, the mantra-practitioner, by the number of mantra-syllables,
should sprinkle the <s>mantra</s> with <s>aśvattha</s>-leaves for purification.',

children.text: saṃcintya manasā mantraṃ jyotir mantreṇa nirdahet/
children.translated_text: 'Having mentally contemplated the <s>mantra</s>, one should burn the three impurities (<s>malatrayam</s>) in the <s>mantra</s> with the <s>jyotir mantra</s> (fire-mantra) —

children.text: mantre malatrayaṃ mantrī vimalīkaraṇaṃ hi tat//
children.translated_text: that is indeed purifying (<s>vimalīkaraṇa</s>).',
'The <s>jyotir mantra</s> is declared as [consisting of] <s>tāra</s> (Oṃ), <s>vyoma</s> (space-seed), <s>agni</s> (fire-seed), and <s>manu</s> (Svāhā).',
'The sprinkling of the <s>mantra</s> syllable by syllable with <s>kuśa</s>-water recited [with a mantra],
with the water-seed (<s>vāribīja</s>) according to the prescribed method — that is considered nourishing (<s>āpyāyana</s>).',

children.text: mantreṇa vāriṇā mantre tarpaṇaṃ tarpaṇaṃ smṛtam//
children.translated_text: 'Sating the <s>mantra</s> with water [consecrated by] the <s>mantra</s> — that is considered sating (<s>tarpaṇa</s>).',
'The conjunction of <s>tāra</s> (Oṃ), <s>māyā</s>-seed, <s>rama</s>-seed, and <s>māyā</s>-seed is called the illumination (<s>dīpana</s>) of the <s>mantra</s>.',
'Concealing (<s>gopana</s>) is the non-disclosure of the <s>mantra</s> while it is being recited.',
'These ten purificatory rites of <s>mantras</s> are kept secret in all <s>tantras</s>;

children.text: yat kṛtvā saṃpradāyena mantrī vāñchitam aśnute//
children.translated_text: having performed them according to tradition, the mantra-practitioner obtains what is desired.',
'Obstructed, blocked, interrupted, dormant, cursed, and other

children.text: mantradoṣāḥ praṇaśyanti saṃskārair ebhir uttamaiḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: mantra-defects are destroyed by these supreme purificatory rites.' Thus.
But enough of this proclamation of the secrets of mantra-science, which resembles an untimely dance!

children.text:
īśvarapraṇidhānaṃ nāmābhihitānām anabhihitānāṃ ca sarvāsāṃ kriyāṇāṃ parameśvare
          paramagurau phalānapekṣayā samarpaṇam/ yatredam uktam —
children.translated_text: Devotion to the Lord (<s>īśvarapraṇidhāna</s>) means the offering of all actions — both those mentioned [in scripture] and those not mentioned — to the supreme Lord, the supreme Guru, without regard for their fruits. As it is stated:
'Whatever I do, whether by desire or without desire, whether auspicious or inauspicious —

children.text: tat sarvaṃ tvayi vinyastaṃ tvatprayuktaḥ karomy aham// iti/
children.translated_text: all that is deposited in You; impelled by You, I act.' Thus.

children.text:
kriyāphalasaṃnyāso 'pi bhaktiviśeṣāparaparyāyaṃ praṇidhānam eva/ phalānabhisaṃdhānena
          karmakaraṇāt/ tathā ca gīyate gītāsu bhagavatā —
children.translated_text: The renunciation of the fruits of action, which is synonymous with a special kind of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), is indeed devotion (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) — because of performing action without intending its fruit. And thus the Blessed Lord sings in the <s>Gītā</s>:

children.text: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana/
children.translated_text: 'Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits;

children.text: mā karmaphalahetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi// iti/
children.translated_text: do not be the cause of the fruit of action; let there not be attachment to inaction for you.' Thus.
The destructive nature of the desire for fruit has been stated by the blessed <s>Nīlakaṇṭha Bhāratī</s>:
'Even austerity endowed with effort, when tainted by desire,

children.text: na tuṣṭaye maheśasya śvalīḍham iva pāyasam// iti/
children.translated_text: does not please <s>Maheśvara</s> — like milk-rice licked by a dog.' Thus.

children.text:
sā ca tapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānātmikā kriyā yogasādhanatvād yoga iti
          śuddhasāropalakṣaṇāvṛttyāśrayaṇena nirūpyate yathāyur ghṛtam iti/
children.translated_text: And this practice consisting of austerity, self-study, and devotion to the Lord, being a means of <s>yoga</s>, is designated '<s>yoga</s>' by resort to the <s>śuddhasāropalakṣaṇā</s> (pure-essence indicative designation) — just as '<s>��yus</s> (life) is ghee.'

children.text:
śuddhasāropalakṣaṇā nāma lakṣaṇāprabhedaḥ/ mukhyārthabādhatadyogābhyām
          arthāntarapratipādanaṃ lakṣaṇā/ sā dvividhā/ rūḍhimūlā prayojanamūlā ca/ tad uktam
          kāvyaprakāśe —
children.translated_text: <s>Śuddhasāropalakṣaṇā</s> (pure-essence indicative designation) is a sub-type of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary/figurative meaning). <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> is the indication of a different meaning through the obstruction of the primary meaning and its connection [with the secondary]. It is twofold: based on established usage (<s>rūḍhimūlā</s>) and based on a purpose (<s>prayojanamūlā</s>). As stated in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>:
'When the primary meaning is obstructed, through its connection, another meaning

children.text: anyo 'rtho lakṣyate yat sā lakṣaṇāropitā kriyā// iti/
children.translated_text: is indicated — from established usage or from a purpose — that is <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, an attributed operation.' Thus.

children.text:
yacchabdena lakṣyata ity ākhyāte guṇībhūtaṃ pratipādanamātraṃ parāmṛśyate/ sā lakṣaṇeti
          pratinirdiśyamānāpekṣayā tacchabdasya strīliṅgatopapattiḥ/ tad uktaṃ kaiyaṭaiḥ —
          nirdiśyamānapratinirdiśyamānayor aikyam āpādayanti sarvanāmāni paryāyeṇa tattalliṅgam
          upādadata iti/ tatra karmaṇi kuśala ityādi rūḍhilakṣaṇāyā udāharaṇam/ kuśāṃl lātīti
          vyutpattyā darbhādānakartari yaugikaṃ kuśalapadaṃ vivecakatvasārūpyāt pravīṇe
          pravartamānam anādivṛddhavyavahāraparamparānupātitvenābhidhānavat prayojanam anapekṣya
          pravartate/ tad āha —
children.translated_text: By the word 'that' (<s>yat</s>), the mere conveying [of meaning], which is subordinate, is referred to in the verbal form 'is indicated.' The feminine gender of the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) is justified by its agreement with the [feminine] word <s>lakṣaṇā</s> being pointed to. As stated by <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>: 'The pronouns bring about the identity of the referred-to and the referring terms, adopting the gender of the respective [term] in alternation.' Therein, '<s>kuśala</s> (skilled) in action' and the like are examples of established-usage <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. The word <s>kuśala</s>, etymologically 'one who takes <s>kuśa</s>-grass,' applied to one who gathers <s>darbha</s>-grass, operates for the skilled person due to similarity with discernment, proceeding — like denotation — without depending on a purpose, by following the succession of beginningless, established conventional usage. Thus it is said:

children.text: nirūḍhā lakṣaṇāḥ kāścit sāmarthyād abhidhānavat/ iti/
children.translated_text: 'Some <s>lakṣaṇās</s> are established; by their capacity, they operate like denotation.' Thus.

children.text:
tasmād rūḍhilakṣaṇāyāḥ prayojanāpekṣā nāsti/ yady api prayuktaḥ śabdaḥ prathamaṃ
          mukhyārthaṃ pratipādayati tenārthenārthāntaraṃ lakṣyata ity arthadharmo 'yaṃ lakṣaṇā
          tathāpi tatpratipādake śabde samāropitaḥ sañ śabdavyāpāra iti vyapadiśyate/ etad
          evābhipretyoktaṃ lakṣaṇāropitā kriyeti/ prayojanalakṣaṇā tu ṣaḍvidhā/ upadānalakṣaṇā
          lakṣaṇalakṣaṇā gauṇasāropā gauṇasādhyavasānā śuddhasāropā śuddhasādhyavasānā ceti/ kuntāḥ
          praviśanti mañcāḥ krośanti gaur vāhīkaḥ gaur ayam āyur ghṛtam āyur evedam — iti
          yathākramam udāharaṇāni draṣṭavyāni/ tad uktam —
children.translated_text: Therefore, established-usage <s>lakṣaṇā</s> does not depend on a purpose. Although a used word first conveys the primary meaning and another meaning is indicated by that meaning — this <s>lakṣaṇā</s> being a property of meaning — nevertheless, having been attributed to the word that conveys it, it is designated a verbal operation. This very point is intended by the statement 'an attributed operation' (<s>lakṣaṇāropitā kriyā</s>). But purpose-based <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is sixfold: <s>upadāna-lakṣaṇā</s> (mention-indication), <s>lakṣaṇa-lakṣaṇā</s> (mark-indication), <s>gauṇa-sāropā</s> (figurative-with-superimposition), <s>gauṇa-sādhyavasānā</s> (figurative-with-identification), <s>śuddha-sāropā</s> (pure-with-superimposition), and <s>śuddha-sādhyavasānā</s> (pure-with-identification). 'The spears enter,' 'the platforms cry out,' 'the cow is a <s>Vāhīka</s>,' 'this is a cow' [said of a man], 'life is ghee,' 'this is life itself' — these should be seen as examples in order. As stated:
'For one's own establishment, the attribution of another; for another's sake, the offering of oneself —

children.text: upādānaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cety uktā śuddhaiva sā dvidhā//
children.translated_text: mention and indication — thus the pure [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] is said to be twofold.',

children.text: sāropānyā tu yatroktau viṣayī viṣayas tathā/
children.translated_text: 'Another [type] is with-superimposition, where both the referent and the object are stated;
[where] the [primary] referent is subsumed in another — that is with-identification.',

children.text: bhedāv imau ca sādṛśyāt saṃbandhāntaratas tathā/
children.translated_text: 'And these two divisions should be understood as figurative — from similarity — and pure — from another relation;

children.text: gauṇau śudhau ca vijñeyau lakṣaṇā tena ṣaḍvidhā// iti/
children.translated_text: <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is thus sixfold.' Thus.
But enough of this churning of the vital points of poetic theory!

children.text:
sa ca yogo yamādibhedavaśād aṣṭāṅga iti nirdiṣṭaḥ/ tatra yamā ahiṃsādayaḥ/ tad āha
          patañjaliḥ — ahiṃsāsatyāsteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ/ iti/ niyamāḥ śaucādayaḥ/ tad apy
          āha — śaucasaṃtoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ iti/ ete ca yamaniyamā
          viṣṇupurāṇe darśitāḥ —
children.translated_text: And that <s>yoga</s>, due to the distinction of <s>yama</s> (restraints) and the like, is declared to be eightfold (<s>aṣṭāṅga</s>). Therein, the <s>yamas</s> are non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) and the rest. As <s>Patañjali</s> states: 'Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possessiveness are the <s>yamas</s>.' The <s>niyamas</s> (observances) are purity (<s>śauca</s>) and the rest. As he also states: 'Purity, contentment, austerity, self-study, and surrender to God are the <s>niyamas</s>.' And these <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> are shown in the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>:
'A <s>yogin</s>, desireless, should practice celibacy, non-violence,

children.text: seveta yogī niṣkāmo yogyatāṃ svaṃ mano nayan//
children.translated_text: truthfulness, non-stealing, and non-possessiveness, directing his own mind toward fitness [for yoga].
Self-controlled, he should practice self-study, purity, contentment,

children.text: kurvīta brahmaṇi tathā parasmin pravaṇaṃ manaḥ//
children.translated_text: and austerities, and likewise incline his mind toward the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ete yamāḥ saniyamāḥ pañca pañca prakīrtitāḥ/
children.translated_text: These <s>yamas</s> together with <s>niyamas</s> are proclaimed as five and five;
they grant specific fruits to those with desires, and liberation to the desireless.' Thus.

<s>Āsana</s> (posture) is steady and comfortable — it is tenfold, by the distinction of <s>padmāsana</s> (lotus posture), <s>bhadrāsana</s> (auspicious posture), <s>vīrāsana</s> (hero posture), <s>svastikāsana</s> (auspicious-mark posture), <s>daṇḍakāsana</s> (staff posture), <s>sopāśraya</s> (supported posture), <s>paryaṅka</s> (couch posture), <s>krauñcaniṣadana</s> (heron-sitting posture), <s>uṣṭraniṣadana</s> (camel-sitting posture), and <s>samasaṃsthāna</s> (even-position posture).
'One should bind one's big toes with the hands in reverse order,

children.text: ūrvor upari viprendra kṛtvā pādatale ubhe//
children.translated_text: placing both soles of the feet upon the thighs, O chief of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> —
this would be <s>padmāsana</s> (lotus posture), honored by all' —

children.text:
ityādinā yājñavalkyaḥ padmāsanādisvarūpaṃ nirūpitavān/ tat sarvaṃ tata
          evāvagantavyam/
children.translated_text: by such [descriptions] <s>Yājñavalkya</s> has described the nature of <s>padmāsana</s> and the rest. All of that should be learned from that [source] itself.

children.text:
tasminn āsanasthairye sati prāṇāyāmaḥ pratiṣṭhito bhavati/ sa ca śvāsapraśvāsayor
          gativicchedasvarūpaḥ/ tatra śvāso nāma bāhyasya vāyor antarānayanam/ praśvāsaḥ punaḥ
          koṣṭhyasya bahirniḥsāraṇam/ tayor ubhayor api saṃcaraṇābhāvaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ/ nanu nedaṃ
          prāṇāyāmasāmānyalakṣaṇam/ tadviśeṣeṣu recakapūrakakumbhakaprakāreṣu tadanugater ayogād iti
          cet — naiṣa doṣaḥ/ sarvatrāpi śvāsapraśvāsagativicchedasaṃbhavāt/ tathā hi/ koṣṭhyasya
          vāyor bahirniḥsaraṇaṃ recekaḥ prāṇāyāmo yaḥ praśvāsatvena prāg uktaḥ/ bāhyasya vāyor
          antardhāraṇaṃ pūrako yaḥ śvāsarūpaḥ/ antaḥstambhavṛttiḥ kumbhakaḥ/ yasmiñ jalam iva kumbhe
          niścalatayā prāṇākhyo vāyur avasthāpyate/ tatra sarvatra śvāsapraśvāsadvayagativicchedo
          'sty eveti nāsti śaṅkāvakāśaḥ/ tad uktaṃ tasmin sati śvāsapraśvāsayor gativicchedaḥ
          prāṇāyāmaḥ iti/
children.translated_text: When steadiness in that <s>āsana</s> (posture) has been attained, <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) becomes established. And its nature is the interruption of the movement of inhalation and exhalation. Therein,

children.text:
sa ca vāyuḥ sūryodayam ārabhya sārdhaghaṭikādvayaṃ
          ghaṭīyantrasthitaghaṭabhramaṇanyāyenaikasyāṃ nāḍyāṃ bhavati/ evaṃ saty aharniśaṃ
          śvāsapraśvāsayoḥ ṣaṭśatādhikaikaviṃśatisahasrāṇi jāyante/ ata evoktaṃ
          mantrasamarpaṇarahasyavedibhir ajapāmantrasamarpaṇe —
children.translated_text: That <s>vāyu</s> (breath), beginning from sunrise, remains in one <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) for two and a half <s>ghaṭikās</s> (one hour), by the principle of the rotation of pots on a water-wheel,
'Six hundred [repetitions] to <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, six thousand to <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>),
six thousand to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and six thousand to <s>Pinākin</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
one thousand to the <s>Guru</s>, one thousand to the Supreme Self,

children.text: sahasram ātmane caivam arpayāmi kṛtaṃ japam// iti/
children.translated_text: and one thousand to the individual self — thus I offer the completed recitation.' Thus.

children.text:
tathā nāḍīsaṃcāraṇadaśāyāṃ vāyoḥ saṃcaraṇe pṛthivyādīni tattvāni varṇaviśeṣavaśāt
          puruṣārthābhilāṣukaiḥ puruṣair avagantavyāni/ tad uktam abhiyuktaiḥ —
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the state of the movement through the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels), when the <s>vāyu</s> (breath) is moving, the <s>tattvas</s> (elements) such as earth and the like, according to their specific colors, should be identified by those who desire the human goals,
'The breath flows in each of the two <s>nāḍīs</s> for two and a half <s>ghaṭīs</s> (one hour) from sunrise;
the principle of the rotation of pots on a water-wheel [applies] to the two <s>nāḍīs</s> again and again.
Nine hundred inhalations and exhalations occur therein;
in the complete day and night, the number is twenty-one thousand six hundred.
The time it takes to utter thirty-six long syllables —

children.text: sā velā maruto nāḍyantare saṃcarato bhavet//
children.translated_text: that is the time [of transition] when the breath moves from one <s>nāḍī</s> to the other.

children.text: pratyekaṃ pañca tattvāni nāḍyoś ca vahamānayoḥ/
children.translated_text: Five <s>tattvas</s> (elements) each flow in the two <s>nāḍīs</s> as they operate;
they flow day and night and should be known by the self-controlled.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ vahnir adhas toyaṃ tiraścīnaḥ samīraṇaḥ/
children.translated_text: Fire [flows] upward, water downward, wind horizontally,

children.text: bhūmim ardhapuṭe vyoma sarvagaṃ pravahet punaḥ//
children.translated_text: earth in a half-arch, and space, being all-pervading, flows [everywhere].

children.text: vāyor vahner apāṃ pṛthvyā vyomnas tattvaṃ vahet kramāt/
children.translated_text: The <s>tattvas</s> of air, fire, water, earth, and space flow in sequence

children.text: vahantyor ubhayor nāḍyor jñātavyo 'yam kramaḥ sadā//
children.translated_text: in both <s>nāḍīs</s> as they operate — this sequence should always be known.
Fifty <s>palas</s> (units of time) for earth, forty for water,

children.text: agnes triṃśat punar vāyor viṃśatir nabhaso daśa//
children.translated_text: thirty for fire, twenty for air, and ten for space —
this is the count of the duration of flow; the reason [for this sequence] is shown here:
Earth has five qualities, water four, then fire

children.text: triguṇo dviguṇo vāyur viyad ekaguṇaṃ bhavet/
children.translated_text: has three, air two, and space has one quality;

children.text: guṇaṃ prati daśa palāny urvyāṃ pañcāśad ity ataḥ//
children.translated_text: ten <s>palas</s> per quality — hence fifty for earth.

children.text: ekaikahānis toyādes tathā pañca guṇāḥ kṣiteḥ/
children.translated_text: A reduction of one [quality] each from water onward, and thus five qualities for earth;

children.text: gandho rasaś ca rūpaṃ ca sparśaḥ śabdaḥ kramād amī//
children.translated_text: smell, taste, form, touch, and sound — these in order [are the qualities].

children.text: tattvābhyāṃ bhūjalābhyāṃ syāc chāntiḥ kārye phalonnatiḥ/
children.translated_text: By the two <s>tattvas</s> of earth and water, there is peace in [one's] undertakings and increase of results;
in fire, air, and space, [the result is] blazing, instability, and dispersal.
The signs of the <s>tattvas</s> of earth, water, fire, air, and space are stated:

children.text: ādye sthairyaṃ svacittasya śaitye kāmodbhavo bhavet//
children.translated_text: in the first [earth], steadiness of one's mind; in the cold [water], the arising of desire;
in the third [fire], anger and burning; in the fourth [air], restlessness;
in the fifth [space], there is voidness alone, or alternatively, the latent tendency toward <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
One should place the thumbs of the hearing [organs] and the middle fingers on the two nostrils,
the ring fingers and the fingers next to the ring fingers at the corners of the mouth, and the remaining [index fingers] at the corners of the eyes —
knowledge of the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with earth, which are located within, arises in sequence
through dots of yellow, white, red, and dark [colors]; space is without limiting condition.' And so on.

children.text:
