yathāvad vāyutattvam avagamya tanniyamane vidhīyamāne vivekajñānāvaraṇakarmakṣayo
          bhavati/ tapo na paraṃ prāṇāyāmād iti/
children.translated_text: Having properly understood the <s>tattva</s> of <s>vāyu</s> (breath/air), when its regulation is practiced, the destruction of the <s>karma</s> that covers discriminative knowledge takes place. 'There is no austerity higher than <s>prāṇāyāma</s>' —

children.text: dahyante dhmāyamānānāṃ dhātūnāṃ hi yathā malāḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Just as the impurities of metals being smelted are burned away,

children.text: prāṇāyāmais tu dahyante tadvad indriyajā malāḥ// iti ca/
children.translated_text: so too the impurities born of the senses are burned away by <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.' And also.

children.text:
tad evaṃ yamādibhiḥ saṃskṛtamanaskasya yoginaḥ saṃyamāya pratyāhāraḥ kartavyaḥ/
          cakṣurādīnām indriyāṇāṃ
          pratiniyatarañjanīyakopanīyamohanīyapravaṇatvaprahāṇenāvikṛtasvarūpa-pravaṇacittānukāraḥ
          pratyāhāraḥ/ indriyāṇi viṣayebhyaḥ pratīpam āhriyante 'sminn iti vyutpatteḥ/ nanu tadā
          cittam abhiniviśate nendriyāṇi/ teṣāṃ bāhyaviṣayatvena tatra sāmarthyābhāvāt/ ataḥ kathaṃ
          cittānukāraḥ/ addhā/ ata eva vastutas tasyāsaṃbhavam abhisaṃdhāya sādṛśyārtham ivaśabdaṃ
          cakāra sūtrakāraḥ — svaviṣayāsaṃprayoge cittasvarūpānukāra ivendriyāṇāṃ pratyāhāraḥ iti/
          sādṛśyaṃ ca cittānukāranimittaṃ viṣayāsaṃprayogaḥ/ yadā cittaṃ nirudhyate tadā
          cakṣurādīnāṃ nirodhe prayatnāntaraṃ nāpekṣaṇīyam/ yathā madhukararājaṃ madhumakṣikā
          anuvartate tathendriyāṇi cittam iti/ tad uktaṃ viṣṇupūrāṇe —
children.translated_text: Thus, for the <s>yogin</s> whose mind has been refined by <s>yama</s> and the rest, <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses) is to be performed for the sake of <s>saṃyama</s> (constraint). [It is] the withdrawal of the senses such as sight and the like from the sense-objects,
'The knower of <s>yoga</s>, devoted to <s>pratyāhāra</s>, restraining the senses
that are attached to sound and the like, should make them follow the mind.
Thereby arises the supreme mastery over the extremely restless

children.text: indriyāṇām avaśyais tair na yogī yogasādhakaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: senses; without those [controlled senses], a <s>yogin</s> is not an accomplisher of <s>yoga</s>.' Thus.

children.text:
nābhicakrahṛdayapuṇḍarīkanāsāgrādāv ādhyātmike hiraṇyagarbhavāsavaprajāpatiprabhṛtike
          bāhye vā deśe cittasya viṣayāntaraparihāreṇa sthirīkaraṇaṃ dhāraṇā/ tad āha — deśabandhaś
          cittasya dhāraṇā iti/ paurāṇikāś ca —
children.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is the binding of the mind to an internal location such as the navel-<s>cakra</s>, the heart-lotus, the tip of the nose, and the like, or to an external [location] such as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the rest.
'Having brought the breath under control through <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, and the senses through <s>pratyāhāra</s>,

children.text: vaśīkṛtya tataḥ kuryāc cittasthānaṃ śubhāśraye// iti/
children.translated_text: one should then fix the mind upon an auspicious support.' Thus.

children.text:
tasmin deśe dhyeyāvalambanasya pratyayasya visadṛśapratyayaprahāṇena pravāho dhyānam/ tad
          uktaṃ — tatra pratyayaikatānatā dhyānam iti/ anyair apy uktam —
children.translated_text: <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is the flow of the cognition pertaining to the object of meditation in that [chosen] location, through the elimination of dissimilar cognitions. As stated: 'The continuation of cognition directed toward that form' —
'the unbroken stream focused on that form alone, free from desire for anything else —

children.text: tad dhyānaṃ prathamair aṅgaiḥ ṣaḍbhir niṣpādyate nṛpa// iti/
children.translated_text: that is <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), accomplished through the preceding six limbs, O king.' Thus.

children.text: prasaṅgāc caramam aṅgaṃ prāg eva pratyapīpadāma/
children.translated_text: Incidentally, we have already explained the last limb [<s>samādhi</s>] earlier.

Thus, through this practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s>, cultivated with reverence, without interruption, and for a long time — when the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) that oppose <s>samādhi</s> are destroyed, through the force of practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>),

children.text:
atha kim evam akasmād asmān ativikaṭābhir atyantāprasiddhābhiḥ karṇāṭagauḍalāṭabhāṣābhir
          bhīṣayate bhavān/ na hi vayaṃ bhavantaṃ bhīṣayāmahe/ kiṃ tu
          madhumatyādipadārthavyutpādanena toṣayāmaḥ/ tataś cākutobhayena bhavatā śrūyatām
          avadhānena/
children.translated_text: 'But why do you suddenly frighten us with such exceedingly harsh, utterly unfamiliar <s>Karṇāṭa</s>, <s>Gauḍa</s>, and <s>Lāṭa</s> languages?' No,

children.text:
tatra madhumatī nāmābhyāsavairāgyādivaśād
          apāstarajastamoleśasukhaprakāśamayasattvabhāvanayānavadyavaiśāradyavidyotanarūpaṛtaṃbharaprajñākhyā
          samādhisiddhiḥ/ tad uktam ṛtaṃbharā tatra prajñā iti/ ṛtaṃ satyaṃ bibharti kadācid api na
          viparyayeṇācchādyate/ tatra sthitau dārḍhye sati dvitīyasya yoginaḥ sā prajñā bhavatīty
          arthaḥ/
children.translated_text: therein, the [stage] called <s>Madhumatī</s> (honey-laden) — through the force of practice, dispassion, and the like, [the mind attains] a cultivation of <s>sattva</s> (purity) characterized by [the predominance of] happiness and luminosity, with the traces of <s>rajas</s> (activity) and <s>tamas</s> (inertia) removed — [endowed with] faultless lucidity —

children.text:
catvāraḥ khalu yoginaḥ prasiddhāḥ prāthamakalpiko madhubhūmikaḥ prajñājyotir
          atikrāntabhāvanīyaś ceti/ tatrābhyāsī pravṛttamātrajyotiḥ prathamaḥ/ na tv anena
          paracittādigocarajñānarūpaṃ jyotir vaśīkṛtam ity uktaṃ bhavati/ ṛtaṃbharaprajño dvitīyaḥ/
          bhūtendriyajayī tṛtīyaḥ/ paravairāgyasaṃpannaś caturthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Indeed, four [types of] <s>yogins</s> are well known: the <s>prāthamakalpika</s> (beginner), the <s>madhubhūmika</s> (one established in the honey-stage), the <s>prajñājyotis</s> (light of wisdom), and the <s>atikrāntabhāvanīya</s> (one who has transcended all cultivation). Therein,

children.text:
manojavitvādayo madhupratīkasiddhayaḥ/ tad uktaṃ — manojavitvaṃ vikaraṇabhāvaḥ
          pradhānajayaś ca iti/ manojavitvaṃ nāma kāyasya manovad anuttamo gatilābhaḥ/
          vikaraṇabhāvaḥ kāyanirapekṣāṇām indriyāṇām abhimatadeśakālaviṣayāpekṣavṛttilābhaḥ/
          pradhānajayaḥ prakṛtivikāreṣu sarveṣu vaśitvam/ etāś ca siddhayaḥ karaṇapañcakarūpajayāt
          tṛtīyasya yoginaḥ prādurbhavanti/ yathā madhuna ekadeśo 'pi svadate tathā pratyekam eva
          tāḥ siddhayaḥ svadanta iti madhupratīkāḥ/ sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvādirūpā viśokā siddhiḥ/ tad
          āha — sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ sarvajñatvaṃ ca iti/
          sarveṣāṃ vyavasāyāvyavasāyātmakānāṃ guṇapariṇāmarūpāṇāṃ bhāvanānāṃ svāmivad ākramaṇaṃ
          sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvam/ teṣām eva śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmitvena sthitānāṃ vivekajñānaṃ
          sarvajñātṛtvam/ tad uktaṃ — viśokā vā jyotiṣmatī iti/ sarvavṛttipratyastamaye paraṃ
          vairāgyam āśritya jātyādibījānāṃ kleśānāṃ nirodhasamartho nirbījaḥ samādhir
          asaṃprajñātapadavedanīyaḥ saṃskāraśeṣatāvyapadeśyaś cittasyāvasthāviśeṣaḥ/ tad uktaṃ —
          virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrvaḥ saṃskāraśeṣo 'nyaḥ iti/ evaṃ ca sarvato virajyamānasya tasya
          puruṣadhaureyasya kleśabījāni nirdagdhaśālibījakalpāni prasavasāmarthyavidhurāṇi manasā
          sārdhaṃ pratyastaṃ gacchanti/
children.translated_text: Speed of mind (<s>manojavitva</s>) and the like are the attainments symbolized by honey (<s>madhupratīka siddhis</s>). As stated: "Speed of mind, freedom from the sense-organs (<s>vikaraṇabhāva</s>), and mastery over <s>pradhāna</s>." Speed of mind means the body's acquisition of supreme movement like that of the mind. Freedom from the sense-organs means the sense-organs' acquisition of functioning with regard to desired places, times, and objects, independent of the body. Mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> means lordship over all the modifications of <s>prakṛti</s>. And these attainments arise for the third type of <s>yogin</s> from the conquest of the fivefold instrument (<s>karaṇapañcaka</s>). Just as even a portion of honey is savored, so each of those attainments is savored individually — hence [they are called] "honey-symbolized" (<s>madhupratīka</s>). The sorrowless (<s>viśokā</s>) attainment has the form of lordship over all states of existence and the like. As stated: "For one who has merely the discernment of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, there is lordship over all states of existence and omniscience." The mastery, like an owner, over all states — which are modifications of the <s>guṇas</s> in the form of determinate and indeterminate cognitions — is lordship over all states of existence. The discriminative knowledge of those very [states], characterized by quiescent, arisen, and indeterminate properties, is omniscience. As stated: "[The mind is] sorrowless or luminous (<s>jyotiṣmatī</s>)." Upon the cessation of all mental modifications, relying on supreme dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), the seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>) <s>samādhi</s> — capable of suppressing the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) whose seeds are birth and the like, to be experienced as the state of <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> (non-cognitive [absorption]), designated as "having a residue of impressions" (<s>saṃskāraśeṣa</s>) — is a special state of mind. As stated: "The other [<s>samādhi</s>] is preceded by the practice of cessation, having a residue of impressions." And thus, for that foremost among <s>puruṣas</s> who becomes completely dispassionate in every respect, the seeds of <s>kleśas</s> — like burnt rice-seeds — deprived of the capacity to germinate, sink along with the mind.
reference marker

children.text:
tad eteṣu pralīneṣu nirupaplavavivekakhyātiparipākavaśāt kāryakāraṇātmakānāṃ pradhāne
          layaḥ citiśaktiḥ svarūpapratiṣṭhā punarbuddhisattvābhisaṃbandhavidhurā vā kaivalyaṃ
          labhata iti siddham/
children.translated_text: When those [afflictions] have dissolved, through the force of the maturation of unimpeded discriminative knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>), the dissolution of [all things] consisting of cause and effect into <s>pradhāna</s> [occurs], and the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>), established in its own nature, or devoid of any further connection with the <s>sattva</s> of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), attains <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) — this is established.

children.text:
dvayī ca muktir uktā patañjalinā — puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ
          svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktiḥ iti/ na cāsmin saty api kasmān na jāyate jantur iti
          vaditavyam/ kāraṇābhāvāt kāryābhāva iti pramāṇasiddhārthe niyogānuyogayor ayogāt/ aparathā
          kāraṇābhāve 'pi kāryasaṃbhave maṇivedhādayo 'ndhādibhyo bhaveyuḥ/ tathā
          cānupapannārthatāyām ābhāṇako laukika upapannārtho bhavet/ tathā ca śrutiḥ — andho maṇim
          avindat/ tam anaṅgulir āvayat/ agrīvaḥ pratyamuñcat/ tam ajihvā asaścata/ avindad
          avidhyata/ āvayat gṛhītavān/ pratyamuñcat pinaddhavān/ asaścatābhyapūjayat stutavān iti
          yāvat/ evaṃ ca cikitsāśāstravad yogaśāstraṃ caturvyūham/ yathā cikitsāśāstraṃ rogo
          rogahetur ārogyaṃ bheṣajam iti tathedam api saṃsāraḥ saṃsārahetur mokṣo mokṣopāya iti/
          tatra duḥkhamayaḥ saṃsāro heyaḥ/ pradhānapuruṣayoḥ saṃyogo heyabhogahetuḥ/ tasyātyantikī
          nivṛttir hānam/ tadupāyaḥ samyagdarśanam/ evam anyad api śāstraṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ
          caturvyūham ūhanīyaṃ iti sarvam avadātam/ (itaḥ paraṃ sarvadarśanaśiromaṇibhūtaṃ
          śāṃkaradarśanam anyatra likhitam ity atropekṣitam)
children.translated_text: And a twofold liberation is stated by <s>Patañjali</s>: "The counter-involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>, devoid of the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>, is <s>kaivalya</s>; or the power of consciousness established in its own nature." And one should not say: "If this [<s>puruṣa</s>] exists [as eternally free], why is the creature not [always] liberated?" — because in a conclusion established by valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that the absence of the effect follows from the absence of the cause, there is no room for objection. Otherwise, if effects could arise even in the absence of causes, then the piercing of gems and the like would be possible for blind men and others. And thus, when [we have] a position with untenable meaning, the folk proverb with tenable meaning would be vindicated. And thus the <s>Śruti</s>: "A blind man found a gem. A fingerless man strung it. A neckless man put it on. A tongueless man praised it." "Found" — obtained it. "Strung" — grasped it. "Put on" — bound it. "Praised" — honored, i.e., extolled [it]. And thus, like the science of medicine, the <s>Yoga</s> scripture has a fourfold structure. Just as the science of medicine [treats] disease, cause of disease, health, and remedy — so too this [treats] <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), and the means to liberation. Therein, <s>saṃsāra</s>, consisting of suffering, is what is to be abandoned. The conjunction of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> is the cause of the experience that is to be abandoned. The absolute cessation of that is abandonment. The means thereto is right knowledge. Thus, every other scripture too should be inferred to have a fourfold structure as applicable — this is all established. (Henceforth the <s>Śāṅkara</s> philosophy, which is the crest-jewel of all philosophical systems, has been written elsewhere, hence it is omitted here.)
reference marker
Thus concludes the <s>Pātañjala</s> philosophy in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Now the <s>Śāṅkara</s> (Advaita Vedānta) Philosophy //16//
reference marker

children.text:
so ’yaṃ pariṇāmavādaḥ prāmāṇikagarhaṇam arhati/ na hy acetanaṃ pradhānaṃ
          cetanānadhiṣṭhitaṃ pravartate/ suvarṇādau rucakādyupādāne
          hemakārādicetanādhiṣṭhānopalambhena nityatvasādhakakṛtakatvavat/
          sukhaduḥkhamohātmanā'nvitatvādeḥ sādhanasya sādhyaviparyayavyāptatayā viruddhatvāt/
          svarūpasiddhatvāc ca/ āntarāḥ khalv amī sukhaduḥkhamohā bāhyebhyaś candanādibhyo
          vibhinnaprat thatyayavedanīyebhyo vyatiriktā adhyakṣam īkṣyante/ yady amī sukhādisvabhāvā
          bhaveyus tadā hemante ’pi candanaḥ sukhaḥ syāt/ na hi candanaḥ kadācid acandanaḥ/ tathā
          nidāgheṣv api kuṅkumapaṅkaḥ sukho bhavet/ na hy asau kadācid akuṅkumapaṅka iti/ evaṃ
          kaṇṭakaḥ kramelakasyeva manuṣyādīnām api prāṇabhṛtāṃ sukhaḥ syāt/ na hy asau kāṃścit praty
          eva kaṇṭaka iti/ tasmāc candanakuṅkumādayo viśeṣāḥ kālaviśeṣādyapekṣayā sukhādihetavo na
          tu sukhādisvabhāvā iti ramaṇīyam/ tasmād dhetur asiddha iti siddham/
children.translated_text: This doctrine of transformation (<s>pariṇāmavāda</s>) deserves censure by authoritative thinkers. For the non-conscious <s>pradhāna</s>, not governed by a conscious being, does not engage in activity — because in the case of gold and the like being fashioned into bracelets and the like, the governance of a conscious agent such as a goldsmith is observed — like the property of being produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) that establishes permanence. Because the proof — namely, being endowed with the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion — is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), since the means of proof is pervaded by the opposite of what is to be proved. And because [the proof] is self-established (<s>svarūpasiddha</s>). For indeed, these internal [states of] pleasure, pain, and delusion — distinct from external things like sandalwood and the like, which are experienced differently [by different beings] — are directly perceived. If these [external things] were of the nature of pleasure and the like, then sandalwood would be pleasant even in winter. For sandalwood is never non-sandalwood. Likewise, saffron paste would be pleasant even in the hot season. For it is never non-saffron-paste. Similarly, a thorn would be pleasant for human beings and other creatures, just as for a camel. For it is never a thorn only for some [beings]. Therefore, it is agreeable that the special things such as sandalwood, saffron, and the like are causes of pleasure and the like in dependence on specific times and the like — but they are not of the nature of pleasure and the like. Therefore, the proof is unestablished — this is settled.
reference marker

children.text:
nāpi śrutiḥ pradhānakāraṇatvavāde pramāṇam/ yataḥ: yad agne rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad
          rūpaṃ yac chuklaṃ tad apām yat kṛṣṇaṃ tad annasya iti cchāndogyaśākhāyāṃ tejobannātmikāyāḥ
          prakṛter lohitaśuklakṛṣṇarūpāṇi samāmnātāni tāny evātra pratyabhijñāyante/ tatra
          śrautapratyabhijñāyāḥ prābalyāl lohitādiśabdānāṃ mukhyārthasaṃbhavāc ca tejobannātmikā
          jarāyujāṇḍajasvedajodbhijjacatuṣṭayasya bhūtagrāmasya prakṛtir avasīyate/ yady api
          tejobannānāṃ prakṛter jātatvena yogavṛttyā na jāyata ity ajatvaṃ na sidhyati tathāpi
          rūḍhivṛttyāvagatam ajātatvam uktaprakṛtau sukhāvabodhāya prakalpyate/ yathā asau vādityo
          devamadhu ityādivākyenādityasya madhutvaṃ parikalpyate tathā tejobannātmikā prakṛtir
          evājeti/ ato ’jām ekām ityādikā śrutir api na pradhānapratipādikā/
children.translated_text: Nor is <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) a valid authority for the doctrine that <s>pradhāna</s> is the cause. Because: "That form of fire which is red is the form of heat (<s>tejas</s>); that which is white is [the form] of water; that which is dark is [the form] of food" — in this passage of the <s>Chāndogya</s> branch, the red, white, and dark forms of <s>prakṛti</s> consisting of heat, water, and food are remembered, and those very [forms] are recognized here. Therein, because of the strength of the scriptural recognition, and because a primary meaning of the words "red" and the like is possible, the <s>prakṛti</s> consisting of heat, water, and food is ascertained as the material cause of the fourfold group of living beings — those born from a womb, from an egg, from moisture, and from a sprout. Even though, since heat, water, and food are produced from <s>prakṛti</s>, their unborn nature cannot be established through the derivative usage [of the word <s>ajā</s>, "unborn"], nevertheless, the unborn nature understood through conventional usage is attributed to the aforementioned <s>prakṛti</s> for ease of comprehension. Just as by the passage "That sun yonder is the honey of the gods" and the like, the nature of honey is attributed to the sun, so too, the <s>prakṛti</s> consisting of heat, water, and food is itself the "unborn" (<s>ajā</s>). Therefore, the <s>Śruti</s> passage "the one unborn" (<s>ajām ekām</s>) and the like also does not teach <s>pradhāna</s>.
reference marker

children.text:
yad avādi nidarśanaṃ pūrvavādinā kṣīrādikam acetanaṃ cetanānadhiṣṭhitam eva
          vatsavivṛddhyarthaṃ pravartata iti/ naitad ramaṇīyam/ buddhiviśeṣaśālinaḥ parameśvarasya
          tatrāpy adhiṣṭhātṛtvābhyupagamāt/ na ca parameśvarasya karuṇayā pravṛttyaṅgīkāre
          prāguktavikalpāvasaraḥ/ sṛṣṭeḥ prāk prāṇināṃ duḥkhasaṃbandhāsaṃbhave ’pi
          tannidānādṛṣṭasaṃbandhasaṃbhavena tatprahāṇecchayā pravṛttyupapatteḥ/ kiṃ ca
          puruṣārthaprayuktā pradhānapravṛttir ity uktaṃ tad vivektavyam/ kiṃ pradhānaṃ kevalaṃ
          bhogārthaṃ pravartate kiṃ vā kevalamokṣārtham āhosvid ubhayārtham/ na tāvad ādyaḥ kalpo
          ’vakalpate/ anādheyātiśayasya kūṭasthanityasya puruṣasya tāttvikabhogāsaṃbhavāt/
          anirmokṣaprasaṅgāc ca/ yena hi prayojanena pradhānaṃ pravartitaṃ tad anena vidhātavyam/
          bhogena caitat pravartitam iti tam eva vidadhyān na mokṣam iti/ nāpi dvitīyaḥ/ ciddhātor
          nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvatayā karmānubhavavāsanānām asaṃbhavena pradhānapravṛtteḥ
          prāg api muktatayā tadarthaṃ pravṛttyanupapatteḥ/ śabdādyupabhogārtham apravṛttatvena
          pradhānasya tadajanakatvaprasaṅgāc ca/ nāpi tṛtīyaḥ/ prāguktadūṣaṇalaṅghanālaṅghitatvāt/
          pravṛttisvabhāvāyāḥ prakṛter audāsinyāyogāc ca/
children.translated_text: As for the illustration cited by the earlier disputant — that insentient [substances] like milk and the like, not governed by a conscious being, act for the growth of the calf — this is not agreeable. Because the governance of the Supreme Lord, who possesses supreme intelligence, is accepted even there. And when the activity of the Supreme Lord through compassion is accepted, there is no occasion for the alternatives raised earlier. Even though before creation there is no connection of living beings with suffering, since there is the possibility of a connection with <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit and demerit) that is the cause of that [suffering], the activity [of the Lord] through the desire to remove that is justified. Moreover, it was said that the activity of <s>pradhāna</s> is motivated by the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> — that needs to be examined. Does <s>pradhāna</s> act solely for the purpose of enjoyment, or solely for the purpose of liberation, or for both purposes? The first alternative is not viable — because for <s>puruṣa</s>, who is of an unsurpassable nature and eternally immutable, genuine enjoyment is impossible. And because there would be the consequence of non-liberation — for that by whose purpose <s>pradhāna</s> was set in motion, that [purpose] must be accomplished by it. And since it was set in motion by [the purpose of] enjoyment, it would accomplish only that, not liberation. Nor is the second [alternative viable] — because for the conscious principle (<s>cidddhātu</s>), whose nature is eternally pure, awakened, and liberated, since the latent impressions of the experience of <s>karma</s> are impossible, and since [<s>puruṣa</s>] is already liberated even before the activity of <s>pradhāna</s>, activity for that purpose is unjustified. And because, since [<s>pradhāna</s>] would not have acted for the purpose of enjoying sound and the like, there would be the consequence that <s>pradhāna</s> does not produce them. Nor is the third [alternative viable] — because the objections stated above cannot be overcome. And because indifference is impossible for <s>prakṛti</s>, whose nature is activity.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātiḥ puruṣārthaḥ/ tasyām jātāyāṃ sā nivartate kṛtakāryatvād iti
          cet
children.translated_text: Objection: "The discernment of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> (<s>sattvapuruṣānyatākhyāti</s>) is the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>. When that has arisen, <s>prakṛti</s> ceases, having accomplished its purpose" — if so,

children.text:
tad asamañjasam/ acetanāyāḥ prakṛter vicārya kāryakāritvāyogāt/ yatheyaṃ kṛte ’pi
          śabdādyupalambhe tadarthaṃ punaḥ pravartata evam atrāpi punaḥ pravarteta/
          svabhāvasyānapāyāt/
children.translated_text: that is untenable. Because for <s>prakṛti</s>, which is non-conscious, deliberative action directed toward a goal is impossible. Just as she continues to act for the purpose of perception of sound and the like even after that has been accomplished, so too she would continue to act again in this case as well — because her nature cannot be lost.
reference marker

children.text:
kiṃ ca sā prakṛtir vivekakhyātivaśād ucchidyate na vā/ ucchede sarvasya saṃprati saṃsāro
          ’stam iyāt/ anucchede na kasya cin mokṣaḥ/
children.translated_text: Moreover, is that <s>prakṛti</s> annihilated through the force of discriminative knowledge, or not? If annihilated, then the <s>saṃsāra</s> of all [beings] would come to an end at once. If not annihilated, then no one would attain liberation.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu pradhānābhede ’pi tattatpuruṣāvivekakhyātilakṣaṇāvidyāsadasattvanibandhanau
          bandhamokṣāv upapadyeyātām iti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: "Even though <s>pradhāna</s> is not destroyed, bondage and liberation can be accounted for through the existence and non-existence of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) characterized by the non-discriminative knowledge of each respective <s>puruṣa</s>" — if so,

children.text: hanta tarhi kṛtaṃ prakṛtyā/ avidyāsadasadbhāvābhyām eva tadupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: well then, <s>prakṛti</s> is rendered superfluous! Because [bondage and liberation] can be accounted for simply by the existence and non-existence of <s>avidyā</s>.
reference marker

children.text: nanv avidyāpakṣe ’py eṣa doṣaḥ prāduḥṣyād iti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: "This fault would arise even in the position of <s>avidyā</s> [i.e., in Advaita]" — if so,

children.text:
tad etat pratyavasthānam asthāne/ na hi vayaṃ pradhānavad avidyāṃ sarveṣu jīveṣv ekām
          ācakṣmahe yenaivam upālabhyemahi/ api tv iyaṃ pratijīvaṃ bhidyate/ tena yasyaiva jīvasya
          vidyotpadyate tasyaivāvidyā samucchidyate nānyasya/ bhinnāyatanayos tayor virodhābhāvāt/
          ato na samastasaṃsārocchedaprasaṅgadoṣaḥ/ tasmāt pariṇāmaḥ parityaktavyaḥ/ svīkartavyaś ca
          vivartavādaḥ/
children.translated_text: this counter-objection is misplaced. For we do not maintain that <s>avidyā</s> is one [and the same] for all <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls), as [is maintained regarding] <s>pradhāna</s>, such that we could be criticized in this way. Rather, <s>avidyā</s> differs for each <s>jīva</s>. Therefore, for whichever <s>jīva</s> knowledge arises, the <s>avidyā</s> of that very [<s>jīva</s>] is destroyed, not of another — because there is no contradiction between the two [knowledge and ignorance] that have different loci. Hence, there is no fault of the consequence that the entire <s>saṃsāra</s> would be annihilated. Therefore, the [doctrine of] transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) should be abandoned. And the doctrine of apparent transformation (<s>vivartavāda</s>) should be accepted.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu jīvajaḍayoḥ sārūpyābhāvena cidvivartatvaṃ prapañcasya na saṃparipadyata iti prāg
          avādiṣmeti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: "We stated earlier that the phenomenal world cannot be an apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of consciousness, because of the absence of similarity between the conscious (<s>jīva</s>) and the insentient (<s>jaḍa</s>)" — if so,

children.text:
naitat sādhu/ na hi sārūpyanibandhanāḥ sarve vibhramā iti vyāptir asti/ asarūpād api
          kāmādeḥ kāntāliṅganādiṣv iva svapnavibhramasyopalambhāt/ kiṃ ca kādācitke vibhrame
          sārūpyāpekṣā nānādyavidyānibandhane prapañce/ tad avocad ācāryavācaspatiḥ :
children.translated_text: this is not sound. For there is no invariable rule (<s>vyāpti</s>) that all errors are grounded in similarity. Because error is observed even from a dissimilar [cause], as in the case of experiencing the embrace of a lover and the like in dreams arising from desire and the like. Moreover, [the requirement of] similarity applies to occasional error, not to the phenomenal world, which is grounded in beginningless <s>avidyā</s>. Thus stated the master <s>Vācaspati</s>:
This phenomenal world is indeed an apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, who is without [real] transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>);
arising from beginningless latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), it does not require similarity. Thus.

children.text: tad etat sarvaṃ vedāntaśāstrapariśramaśālināṃ sugamaṃ sughaṭaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: All this is easily accessible and readily comprehensible for those who have labored in the study of <s>Vedānta</s> scripture.
reference marker

children.text:
tac ca vedāntaśāstraṃ caturlakṣaṇam/ bhagavatā bādarāyaṇena praṇītasya vedāntaśāstrasya
          pratyagbrahmaikyaṃ viṣaya iti śaṃkarācāryāḥ pratyapīpadan/ tatra prathame samanvayādhyāye
          sarveṣāṃ vedāntānāṃ brahmaṇi tātparyeṇa paryavasānam/ dvitīye ’virodhādhyāye
          sāṃkhyāditarkavirodhanirākaraṇam/ tṛtīye sādhanādhyāye brahmavidyāsādhanam/ caturthe
          phalādhyāye vidyāphalam/ tatra pratyadhyāyaṃ pādacatuṣṭayam/ tatra prathamasyādhyāyasya
          prathame pāde spaṣṭabrahmaliṅgaṃ vākyajātaṃ mīmāṃsyate/ dvitīye ’spaṣṭabrahmaliṅgam
          upāsyaviṣayam/ tṛtīye tādṛśaṃ jñeyaviṣayam/ caturthe ’vyaktājāpadādi saṃdigdhaṃ padajātam
          iti/ avirodhasya dvitīyasya prathame sāṃkhyayogakaṇādādismṛtivirodhaparihāraḥ/ dvitīye
          sāṃkhyādimatānāṃ duṣṭatvam/ tṛtīye pañcamahābhūtaśrutīnāṃ jīvaśrutīnāṃ ca
          parasparavirodhaparihāraḥ/ caturthe liṅgaśarīraśrutīnāṃ virodhaparihāraḥ/
children.translated_text: And that <s>Vedānta</s> scripture has four characteristics [i.e., four chapters]. The <s>Śaṅkarācāryas</s> established that the subject of the <s>Vedānta</s> scripture composed by the blessed <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> is the identity of the inner self and <s>Brahman</s>. Therein, in the first chapter, the <s>Samanvaya</s> (Harmony) chapter, all <s>Vedānta</s> passages conclude with their purport in <s>Brahman</s>. In the second, the <s>Avirodha</s> (Non-contradiction) chapter, the removal of the contradiction of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other logical objections. In the third, the <s>Sādhana</s> (Means) chapter, the means of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. In the fourth, the <s>Phala</s> (Fruit) chapter, the fruit of knowledge. Therein, each chapter has four sections (<s>pāda</s>). In the first section of the first chapter, the group of passages with clear indicators of <s>Brahman</s> is examined. In the second, [passages with] unclear indicators of <s>Brahman</s> pertaining to objects of meditation. In the third, similar [passages] pertaining to objects of knowledge. In the fourth, ambiguous terms like <s>avyakta</s>, <s>aja</s>, and the like. Of the second [chapter on] non-contradiction: in the first [section], the removal of the contradiction of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, <s>Kaṇāda</s>, and other <s>Smṛtis</s>. In the second, the defectiveness of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other doctrines. In the third, the removal of mutual contradiction among the <s>Śruti</s> passages on the five great elements and on the individual soul. In the fourth, the removal of the contradiction among <s>Śruti</s> passages on the subtle body.
reference marker

children.text:
tṛtīyasya prathame jīvasya paralokagamanāgamanavicārapuraḥsaraṃ vairāgyam/ dvitīye
          tvaṃpadatatpadārthapariśodhanam/ tṛtīye saguṇavidyāsu guṇopasaṃhāraḥ/ caturthe
          nirguṇabrahmavidyāyā bahiraṅgāntaraṅgāśramayajñaśamādisādhanajātam/ caturthasya prathame
          brahmasākṣātkāreṇa jīvataḥ pāpapuṇyakleśavaidhuryalakṣaṇā muktiḥ/ dvitīye
          maraṇotkramaṇaprakāraḥ/ tṛtīye saguṇabrahmopāsakasyottaramārgaḥ/ caturthe
          nirguṇasaguṇabrahmavido videhakaivalyabrahmalokāvasthānāni/ tad itthaṃ
          brahmavicāraśāstrādhyāyapādārthasaṃgrahaḥ/
children.translated_text: Of the third [chapter]: in the first [section], dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) preceded by the consideration of the soul's going to and coming from the other world. In the second, the purification of the meanings of the words 'thou' (<s>tvam</s>) and 'that' (<s>tat</s>). In the third, the gathering of attributes in meditations on <s>Brahman</s> with qualities (<s>saguṇa</s>). In the fourth, the group of means -- external and internal, such as the <s>āśrama</s> duties, sacrifices, tranquility (<s>śama</s>), and the like -- for the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>). Of the fourth [chapter]: in the first [section], liberation characterized by freedom from sin, merit, and afflictions while still alive, through the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s>. In the second, the manner of departure at death. In the third, the northern path (<s>uttaramārga</s>) for the worshipper of <s>Brahman</s> with qualities. In the fourth, the states of <s>videhakaivalya</s> (disembodied liberation) and abiding in <s>Brahmaloka</s> for the knower of <s>Brahman</s> with and without qualities. Thus is the summary of the chapters and sections of the treatise on the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>.
reference marker

children.text:
tatra prathamam adhikaraṇam athāto brahmajijñāsā iti brahmamīmāṃsārambhopapādanaparam/
          adhikaraṇaṃ ca pañcāvayavaṃ prasiddham/ te ca viṣayādayaḥ pañcāvayavā nirūpyante/ ātmā vā are

draṣṭavyaḥ ity etad vākyaṃ viṣayaḥ/ brahma jijñāsitavyaṃ na veti saṃdehaḥ/
          jijñāsyatvavyāpakayoḥ saṃdehaprayojanayoḥ saṃbhavāsaṃbhavābhyām/
children.translated_text: The sentence 'The Self, O dear one, should be seen' is the subject (<s>viṣaya</s>). 'Whether <s>Brahman</s> is to be inquired into or not' is the doubt (<s>saṃdeha</s>). Since [both] doubt and purpose, which pervade what is to be inquired into, [must be established]...

Therein, the first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) -- 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>' -- is devoted to establishing the commencement of the <s>Brahman</s> investigation. And the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is well-known as having five components. And those five components -- beginning with the subject (<s>viṣaya</s>) -- are determined.
reference marker

children.text: tatra kasyedaṃ jijñāsyatvam avagamyate/ ahamanubhavagamyasya śrutigamyasya vā/
children.translated_text: Now, of what is this 'to-be-inquired-into-ness' understood? Of what is known through the 'I'-experience, or of what is known through <s>Śruti</s>?
Not the first -- because through the universal 'I'-experience, the self clearly appears as distinguished from the body and the like, which are the referent of 'this.'

children.text:
nanu sthūlo ’haṃ kṛśo ’ham ityādidehadharmasāmānādhikaraṇyānubhavād
          adhyastātmabhāvadehālambano ’yam ahaṃkāra iti cen na/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Since in the experience "I am stout, I am thin" and the like, there is the experience of co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of the properties of the body, this ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) is based on the body upon which self-hood has been superimposed.'

children.text:
bālyādyavasthāsu bhinnaparimāṇatayā badarāmalakādivat parasparabhedena śarīrasya
          pratyabhijñānānupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: Because, due to different dimensions in the stages of childhood and the like, the body, like a jujube and a gooseberry, cannot be recognized as the same across mutual differences.

children.text:
athocyeta yathā pīlupākapakṣe piṭharapākapakṣe vā kālabhedenaikasmin vastuni pākajabhedo
          yujyate tathaikasmiñ śarīrābhidhe vastuni kālabhedena parimāṇabhedaḥ/ ata eva laukikāḥ
          śarīram ātmanaḥ sakāśād abhinnaṃ pratipadyamānāḥ pratyabhijānate ceti/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Just as, whether in the <s>pīlupāka</s> (atomic transformation) theory or the <s>piṭharapāka</s> (pot-baking) theory, difference through heat-transformation (<s>pākajabheda</s>) in a single entity at different times is possible, so too in a single body...'

children.text:
na tad bhadram/ maṇimantrauṣadhādyupāyabhedena bhūmikādhānavan nānāvidhān dehān
          pratipadyamānasyāhamālambanasya bhinnasyātmanaḥ śarīrād bhedena bhāsamānatvāt/ ata eva
          cakṣurādīnām apy ahamālambanatvam aśakyaśaṅkam/ nānyadṛṣṭam smaraty anyaḥ iti nyāyena
          cakṣurādau naṣṭe ’pi rūpādipratisaṃdhānānupapatteḥ/ nāpy antaḥkaraṇasyāhamālambanatvam
          āstheyam/ ayam eva bhedo bhedahetur vā yad viruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ kāraṇabhedaś ceti nyāyena
          kartṛkaraṇabhūtayor ātmāntaḥkaraṇayos takṣavāsivat saṃbhedāsaṃbhavāt/ yady abheda eva
          nādriyate tarhi sthūlo ’haṃ kṛśo ’haṃ kṛṣṇo ’ham ityādi saṃkhyānam utsannasaṃkathaṃ
          syāt/
children.translated_text: That is not fortunate. Because, for the one who assumes various bodies through different means such as gems, <s>mantras</s>, herbs, and the like -- like the construction of different stages -- the 'I'-based [self-recognition would not persist]...

children.text:
na syāt/ evaṃ loke śāstre cobhayathā śabdaprayogadarśanena mukhyārthatvānupapattau mañcāḥ
          krośantītyādivad aupacārikatvenopapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: it would not be. Thus, since in both worldly and scriptural usage the usage of words is observed in both ways, when the primary meaning is untenable, the figurative [usage] -- like 'the platforms are shouting' -- [is to be understood]...

children.text:
-na dvitīyaḥ/ ahamanubhavagamyasyaiva śrutigamyatvāt/ satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma
          ityādiśrutibhyo hi brahmāvagamyate/ brahmabhāvaś cāham ātmā brahma tat tvam asi
          ityādiśrutiṣv ahaṃpratyayagamyasyaiva bodhyate/ tathā cedam anumānaṃ samasūci/ vimatam
          ajijñāsyam asaṃdigdhatvāt karatalāmalakavat/
children.translated_text: Not the second -- because what is known through the 'I'-experience is itself what is known through <s>Śruti</s>. For from <s>Śruti</s> passages such as '<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite' (<s>satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma</s>), <s>Brahman</s> is understood...
reference marker

children.text:
tathā phalaṃ na phalabhāvam īkṣate/ puruṣair arthyata iti vyutpattyā
          niḥśeṣaduḥkhopaśamalakṣitaṃ paramānandaikarasaṃ ca puruṣārthaśabdasyārthaḥ
          sakalapuruṣadhaureyaiḥ prepsyate naitat sāṃsārikaṃ sukhajātam/ tasyaihikasya
          pāralaukikasya ca sātiśayatayā ca sadṛkṣatayā ca prekṣāvadbhir arthyamānatvānupapatteḥ/
          yat tatparipanthi duḥkhajātaṃ taj jihāsyate/ tac cāvidyāparaparyāyasaṃsāra eva/
          kartṛtvādisakalānarthakaratvād avidyāyāḥ/ sam ity ekīkaraṇe vartate/ saṃbhedādau tathā
          copalambhāt/ tathā cātmānaṃ dehenaikīkṛtya svarganarakamārgayoḥ sarati yena puruṣaḥ sa
          saṃsāro ’vidyāśabdārthaḥ/ tannivṛttiḥ phalaṃ phalavatām abhimatam/ tathā kathitam :
children.translated_text: Likewise, the fruit does not see fruit-hood [in itself]. By the derivation '<s>puruṣa</s> = that which is desired by persons,' [the fruit is] characterized by the complete cessation of all suffering and consisting solely of supreme bliss...

children.text: avidyāstamayo mokṣaḥ sā ca bandha udāhṛtaḥ/ iti
children.translated_text: The cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); and that [<s>avidyā</s>] is called bondage.
reference marker

children.text:
tac ca kāśakuśāvalambanakalpam/ ātmayāthātmyānubhavena saha vartamānasya saṃsārasya
          rūparasavad virodhābhāvena nivartyanivartakabhāvābhāvāt/
children.translated_text: And that [coexistence of bondage and knowledge] is like grasping <s>kāśa</s> grass and <s>kuśa</s> grass [simultaneously]. Because of the absence of contradiction -- like form and taste -- of <s>saṃsāra</s> continuing together with the experience of the true nature of the self...

children.text:
nanu sahānuvartamāno bodhaḥ saṃsāraṃ mā bādhiṣṭa/ sahāvartamānas tu bodhaḥ prakāśas
          tamovad bādhiṣyata iti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Let the knowledge that coexists [with saṃsāra] not sublate <s>saṃsāra</s>. But knowledge that does not coexist would sublate [it], as light does darkness.'

children.text: tad etad riktaṃ vacaḥ/ ahamanubhavād anyasyātmajñānasya mūṣikaviṣāṇāyamānatvāt/
children.translated_text: That is empty talk -- because any knowledge of the self other than the 'I'-experience would be like the horn of a mouse [i.e., non-existent].
reference marker

children.text:
nanv anyo ’yam anubhavaḥ pāmarāṇāṃ mā sma bhavan nāma/
          vedāntavacananicayaparyālocanakṣamāṇāṃ parīkṣakāṇāṃ saṃbhavaty evety api na vaktavyam/
          abādhitānubhavavirodhena vedāntavākyānāṃ grāvaplavanādivākyakalpatvāt/ na hy āgamāḥ
          paraḥśataṃ ghaṭaṃ paṭayitum utsahante/ na cādhyayanavidhivyākopaḥ/ gurumatānusāreṇa
          huṃphaḍādivākyavaj japamātropayogitvenācāryamatānusāreṇa vā yajamānaḥ prastara
          ityādivākyavat stāvakatvena vedāntasiddhāntasyādhyetavyatvasaṃbhavāt/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Let this be the experience of the common people -- may it not exist! But for the examiners who are capable of thoroughly considering the collection of <s>Vedānta</s> statements...'
And thus the formal argument:

children.text:
vivādāspadaṃ brahma vicāryapadaṃ na bhavaty aphalatvāt kākadantavad iti/ tad āhur
          ācāryāḥ:
children.translated_text: 'The disputed <s>Brahman</s> does not deserve to be investigated, because of being fruitless -- like the teeth of a crow.' Thus the teachers state:
Since the self is established through the 'I'-cognition, and since that [self] itself is <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: tajjñānān muktyabhāvāc ca jijñāsā nāvakalpate// iti/
children.translated_text: and since from the knowledge of that there is no [additional] liberation -- the inquiry [into <s>Brahman</s>] is not warranted.
reference marker

children.text:
na ca bhedenādhyastadehādinivṛttiḥ phalam ity aphalahetur asiddha iti veditavyam/
          bhedagraho hi vyāpakanivṛttyā vyāpyanivṛttir iti nyāyena bhedāgrahaparipathinaṃ
          bhedasaṃskāram apekṣate/ anākalitakaladhautasya śuktiśakale tatsamāropānupalambhāt/
          saṃskāraś ca pramitim ākāṅkṣati/ ananubhūte saṃskārānudayāt/ na ca bhrāntirūpo ’nubhavas
          tatkaraṇam iti bhaṇitavyam/ bhrānter abhrāntipūrvakatvena kvacit pramiter
          avaśyābhyupagamayitavyatvāt/ prayogaś ca: vimatāv ātmānātmānau bhedena pramitāv
          abhedāyogyatvāt/ tamaḥprakāśavat/ na cātmānātmanor abhedāyogyatvalakṣaṇo hetur asiddha iti
          śaṅkanīyam/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ tathā hi: anātmātmapariśeṣaḥ syād ātmānātmapariśeṣo vā/ ādye
          muktidaśāyām iva paridṛśyamānaṃ jagad astam iyāt/ dvitīye jagadāndhyaṃ prasajyeta/
          tamaḥprakāśavad viruddhasvabhāvatvāc ca dṛgdṛśyayor ātmānātmanor abhedāyogyatvam
          avadheyam/ tataś cārthādhyāsānupapattau tatpūrvakasya jñānādhyāsasyāsaṃbhavena brahmaṇo
          vicāryatvāsaṃbhavād vicārātmikā caturlakṣaṇaśārīrakamīmāṃsā nārambhaṇīyeti pūrvapakṣe
          prāpte siddhānto ’bhidhīyate/
children.translated_text: Nor should it be understood that the removal of the superimposed body and the like through [the knowledge of] difference is the fruit, and therefore the reason 'fruitlessness' is unestablished. For the apprehension of difference, through the cessation of the pervader...
reference marker

children.text:
ahaṃpadādhigamyād anyad ātmatattvaṃ nāstīti na vaktavyam/
          nirastasamastopādhikasyātmatattvasya śrutyādiṣu prasiddhatvāt/ na ca teṣām
          upacaritārthatā/ upakramopasaṃhārādiṣaḍvidhatātparyaliṅgavattayā tattvaṃ bodhayatām
          upacaritārthatvānupapatteḥ/ liṅgaṣaṭkaṃ ca pūrvācāryair darśitam:
children.translated_text: It should not be said that there is no reality of the self other than what is ascertained through the word 'I.' Because the reality of the self, divested of all limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), is well-established in <s>Śruti</s> and the like...
Opening and closing statements (<s>upakramopasaṃhāra</s>), repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>), novelty (<s>apūrvatā</s>), fruit (<s>phala</s>),
laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), and reasoning (<s>upapatti</s>) -- these are the indicators for determining the purport.
reference marker

children.text:
tatra sad eva saumyedam agra āsīd ity upakramaḥ/ aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ tat satyaṃ sa
          ātmā tat tvam asi śvetaketo ity upasaṃhāraḥ/ tayor brahmaviṣayatvenaikarūpyam

ekaliṅgam/ asakṛt tat tvam asīty uktir abhyāsaḥ/ mānāntarāgamyatvam apūrvatvam/
          ekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ phalam/ sṛṣṭisthitipralayapraveśaniyamanāni pañcārthavādāḥ/
          mṛdādidṛṣṭāntā upapattayaḥ/ tasmād etair liṅgair vedāntānāṃ
          nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvabrahmātmaparatvaṃ niścetavyam/ tad ittham
          aupaniṣadasyātmatattvasyāhamanubhave ’navabhāsamānatvāt
          tasyānubhavasyādhyastātmaviṣayatvaṃ siddham/
children.translated_text: This is the single indicator (<s>ekaliṅga</s>). The repeated utterance 'that thou art' (<s>tat tvam asi</s>) is repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>). Not being obtainable by any other means of knowledge is novelty (<s>apūrvatva</s>). 'Through one cognition, all is cognized' is the fruit (<s>phala</s>)...

Therein, 'Being alone, O dear one, this was in the beginning' is the opening statement (<s>upakrama</s>). 'All this has that as its self; that is the truth; that is the self; that thou art, O <s>Śvetaketu</s>' -- this is the closing statement (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>).
reference marker

children.text:
kaṇabhakṣākṣacaraṇādikakṣīkṛtasyātmano bhānābhāvād ahamanubhavasyādhyastātmaviṣayatvam
          eṣitavyam/ na tāvad ahamanubhavaḥ sarvagatatvam ātmano ’vagamayitum īṣṭe/ aham ihāsmi
          sadane jānāna iti prādeśikatvagrahaṇāt/ na cedaṃ dehasya prādeśikatvaṃ pratibhāsata iti
          veditavyam/ aham ity ullekhāyogāt/
children.translated_text: Since the self, as apprehended by <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> (Kaṇāda), <s>Akṣacaraṇa</s> (Gautama), and others, cannot shine [in experience], the I-experience (<s>ahamanubhava</s>) must be understood as having a superimposed self as its object. To begin with, the I-experience is unable to reveal the all-pervasiveness of the self — because of the apprehension of a limited location, as in 'I am here, in this house, I know.' Nor should one think that this limitation pertains to the body — because it cannot be expressed as 'I' [if it were merely the body].

children.text:
nanu yathā rājñaḥ sarvaprayojanavidhātari bhṛtye mamātmā bhadrasena ity upacāras tadvad
          ātmavacanasyāhaṃśabdasya deha upacāra iti cet
children.translated_text: Now, just as with regard to a king, there is a figurative usage 'my servant <s>Bhadrasena</s> is my self,' directed toward his servant who fulfills all purposes — similarly, the word 'I' (<s>aham</s>), which denotes the self, is figuratively applied to the body — if so,

children.text:
maivaṃ vocaḥ/ upacaritātmabhāvasya dehādeḥ svasamānākṛtiśilāputrakādivaj
          jñātṛtvāyogāt/
children.translated_text: do not say this. Because the body and the like, to which selfhood is figuratively attributed, cannot be the knower, just as a stone doll of similar shape [cannot be].

children.text:
na ca jñātṛtvam apy upacaritam/ prayoktuḥ svapratipattiprakāśake prayoge
          pratipattṛtvopacārānupapatteḥ/ atha dehadharmaḥ prādeśikatvam ātmany upacaryeta tadā
          dehātmanor bhedena bhavitavyam/ prasiddhabhede māṇavake siṃhaśabdavat sāṃpratikagauṇatve
          tirohitabhedena sārṣapādau rase tailaśabdavan nirūḍhagauṇatve vā gauṇamukhyayor
          bhedādhyavasāyasya niyatatvāt/
children.translated_text: Nor is the knower-hood itself figurative — because in a usage that reveals the speaker's own cognition, the figurative attribution of knower-hood is impossible. Now, if the bodily property of limited location were figuratively attributed to the self, then there must be a difference between body and self. Because the ascertainment of difference between the figurative and the literal is invariable — as in the case of the word 'lion' applied to a boy where the difference is well-known (contemporary figurative usage), or as in the case of the word 'oil' (<s>taila</s>) applied to mustard and other extracts where the [original] difference is obscured (established figurative usage).

children.text:
atha mama śarīram iti bhedabhānasaṃbhavād gauṇatvaṃ manyethās tad ayuktam/
          ahaṃśabdārthasya dehādibhyo niṣkṛṣyāsādhāraṇadharmavattvena pratibhāsamānatvābhāvāt/
          aparathā lokāyatikamataṃ nodayam āsādayet/ mama śarīram ity uktis tu rāhoḥ śira itivad
          aupacārikī/ mama śarīram iti bruvāṇenāpi kas tvam iti pṛṣṭena vakṣasthalanyastahastena
          śṛṅgagrāhikayāyam aham iti prativacanasya dīyamānatvena dehātmapratyayasya
          sakalānubhavasiddhatvāt/ tad uktam :
children.translated_text: Now, if you think that the figurative usage is possible because of the apprehension of difference in 'my body' — that is not right. Because the meaning of the word 'I' is not experienced as being extracted from the body and the like and as possessing a distinctive property. Otherwise, the materialist (<s>Lokāyatika</s>) view would not even arise. The expression 'my body' is figurative, like '<s>Rāhu's</s> head.' Because even one who says 'my body,' when asked 'who are you?', places his hand on his chest and gives the answer 'this is I' — using the superficial [identification] — thus the cognition of identity between body and self is established by universal experience. As stated:
reference marker
Just as the cognition of body-self identity is assumed to be a valid means of knowledge,

children.text: laukikaṃ tadvad evedaṃ pramāṇaṃ tv ātmaniścayāt// iti//
children.translated_text: similarly this worldly [cognition] is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), but from the determination of the [true] self. Thus.

children.text:
tathā ca vyāpakasya bhedabhānasya nivṛtter vyāpyasya gauṇatvasya nivṛttir iti
          niravadyam/
children.translated_text: And thus, since the pervasive apprehension of difference is negated, the negation of the pervaded figurative usage follows — this is flawless.
reference marker

children.text:
nanv abhijñayā bhedasiddhir mā saṃbhūn nāma/ pratyabhijñayā tu so ’ham ity evaṃrūpayā
          tatsiddhiḥ saṃbhaviṣyatīti cen
children.translated_text: Now, even if the establishment of difference through direct cognition (<s>abhijñā</s>) may not occur, through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) — 'that [I was then] is [the same as] this I [now]' — the establishment of that [difference from the body] will be possible — if so,

children.text:
na/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ kim iyaṃ pratyabhijñā pāmarāṇāṃ syāt parīkṣakāṇāṃ vā/ nādyaḥ/
          dehavyatiriktātmaikyam avagāhamānāyāḥ pratyabhijñāyā anudayāt/ pratyuta śyāmasya
          lauhityavat kāraṇaviśeṣād alpasyāpi mahāparimāṇatvam aviruddham anubhavatāṃ taddeha eva
          tasyāḥ saṃbhavāc ca/ na dvitīyaḥ/ vyavahārasamaye pāmarasāmyānatirekāt/ aparokṣabhramasya
          parokṣajñānavināśyatvānupapatteś ca/ yad uktaṃ bhagavatā bhāṣyakāreṇa paśvādibhiś
          cāviśeṣāt iti/ bhāmatīkārair apy uktaṃ śāstracintakāḥ khalv evaṃ vicārayanti na
          pratipattāra iti/ tathā cātmagocarasyādhyāsātmarūpatvaṃ sustham/
children.translated_text: no. Because it does not withstand analysis. Would this recognition belong to ordinary people or to critical examiners? Not the first — because recognition that grasps the unity of a self distinct from the body does not arise [for ordinary people]. On the contrary, since those who experience that even slight [things] can have great dimensions due to particular causes — just as darkness can have redness — find such recognition possible with respect to the body itself. Not the second — because at the time of practical engagement, there is no difference from ordinary people. And because a direct error cannot be destroyed by indirect knowledge. As stated by the blessed commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>): 'because there is no distinction from animals and the like.' And the <s>Bhāmatī</s> author also stated: 'It is the philosophical investigators who analyze thus, not the ordinary perceivers.' And thus, the fact that what is apprehended as the self has the nature of superimposition is well-established.
reference marker

children.text:
na cārhatamatānusāreṇāhaṃpratyayaprāmāṇyāyātmano dehaparimāṇatvam aṅgīkaraṇīyam iti
          sāṃpratam/ madhyamaparimāṇasya sāvayavatvena dehādivad anityatve
          kṛtahānākṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgāt/ athaitaddoṣaparijihīrṣayāvayavasamudāya ātmety
          abhyupagamyeta tadā vaktavyam/ kiṃ pratyekam avayavānāṃ caitanyaṃ saṃghātasya vā/ nādyaḥ/
          bahūnāṃ cetanānām ahamahamikayā pradhānabhāvam anubhavatām aikamatyābhāvena samasamayaṃ
          viruddhadikkriyatayā śarīrasyāpi viśaraṇaniṣkriyatvayor anyatarāpātāt/ dvitīye ’pi
          saṃghātāpattiḥ kiṃ śarīropādhikī svābhāvikī yādṛcchikī vā/ nādyaḥ/ ekasminn avayave chinne
          cidātmano ’py avayavaś chinna ity acetanatvāpātāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/ anekeṣām avayavānām
          anyonyasāhityaniyamādarśanāt/ na tṛtīyaḥ/ saṃśleṣavad viśleṣasyāpi yādṛcchikatvena sukhena
          vasatām akasmād acetanatvaprasaṅgāt/
children.translated_text: Nor is it right to accept, following the Jaina view, that the self has the dimensions of the body on the authority of the I-cognition. Because something of medium dimensions, being possessed of parts, would be impermanent like the body and the like — leading to the absurdity of the loss of what is done and the accrual of what is not done. If, to avoid this defect, one accepts that the self is the aggregate of parts — then one must say: does consciousness belong to each individual part or to the aggregate? Not the first — because when many conscious entities compete with each other, each experiencing itself as primary, due to the absence of unanimity, since they would simultaneously act in contradictory directions, the body would face one of two consequences: disintegration or inactivity. In the second case too: is the advent of aggregation conditioned by the body, natural, or accidental? Not the first — because when one part is severed, a part of the conscious self would also be severed, leading to the absurdity of unconsciousness. Not the second — because no rule is observed that multiple parts must necessarily accompany each other. Not the third — because just as aggregation would be accidental, disintegration too would be accidental, leading to the absurdity that those living comfortably would suddenly become unconscious.
reference marker

children.text:
na cāṇuparimāṇatvam ātmanaḥ śaṅkanīyam/ sthūlo ’haṃ dīrgho ’ham iti
          pratyayānupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: Nor should atomic dimensions be suspected for the self — because the cognitions 'I am stout,' 'I am tall,' and the like would be impossible.
reference marker

children.text:
na ca vijñānātmabhāṣiṇāṃ naiṣa doṣaḥ/ viśuddhasāvayavatvābhāvād iti gaṇanīyam/ yaḥ
          suṣuptaḥ so ’haṃ jāgarmīti sthiragocarasyāhamullekhasya kṣaṇabhaṅgivijñānagocaratve
          atasmiṃstadbuddhirūpamithyādhyāsasya tadavasthānāt/ tad anena kṛśo ’haṃ kṛṣṇo ’ham
          ityādīnāṃ prakhyātānānāṃ buddhyā sarūpatākhyānenaupacārikatvaṃ pratyākhyātam/
          tadvyāpakabhedabhānāsaṃbhavasya prāg eva prapañcitatvāt/ tathā ca prayogaḥ:
children.translated_text: Nor should those who speak of the self as [mere] consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) consider themselves free of this defect [by claiming] the absence of pure partedness. Because the I-reference (<s>ahamullekha</s>) that has a stable object — as in 'I who was asleep am now awake' — if it had momentarily perishing consciousness as its object, would be a false superimposition of the form 'that in what is not that' — and that is the very state [of superimposition, which Advaitins acknowledge]. By this, [the objection that] well-known [cognitions] such as 'I am thin,' 'I am dark,' and the like show similarity with the intellect and hence are figurative — is refuted. Because the impossibility of the apprehension of difference, which pervades [figurative usage], was already elaborated. And the inference is:
The disputed <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) has a subject and a purpose,
because it removes the bondage produced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),
like the awareness upon waking from sleep.

children.text:
yathā svapnāvasthāyāṃ māyāparikalpitayoṣādikṛtabandhanivartakasya suptotthitabodhasya
          mandiramadhye sukhena śayyāyām avatiṣṭhamāno deho viṣayaḥ/ tasya suptabodhenāniścayāt/
          svapnamāyāvijṛmbhitānarthanivṛttiḥ prayojanam/ evaṃ
          mananādijanyaparokṣajñānadvāreṇādhyāsikakartṛtva-bhoktṛtvādyanarthaniṣedhakasya śāstrasya
          saccidānandaikarasaṃ pratyagātmabhūtaṃ brahma viṣayaḥ/ tasyāhamanubhavenāniścayāt/
          adhyāsanivṛttiḥ prayojanam/ tathā cāphalatvād iti hetur asiddha iti siddham/ tad
          uktam :
children.translated_text: Just as the awareness upon waking from sleep — which removes the bondage caused by women and the like imagined by <s>māyā</s> (illusion) in the dream state — has as its subject the body comfortably resting on a bed in a mansion, since it was not ascertained by the sleeping cognition, and has as its purpose the removal of the calamities manifested in the dream-illusion — similarly, the <s>śāstra</s>, which through indirect knowledge produced by reflection (<s>manana</s>) and the like negates the calamities of superimposed agentship, enjoyership, and the rest, has as its subject <s>Brahman</s>, which is the inner self (<s>pratyagātman</s>), of the nature of being-consciousness-bliss (<s>saccidānanda</s>) alone, since it is not ascertained by the I-experience. And its purpose is the removal of superimposition. And thus the reason 'because it is fruitless' is unestablished — this is proven. As stated:
reference marker
The nature of the self (<s>ātmatattva</s>) accessible through <s>śruti</s> (scripture) is not grasped by the I-cognition;

children.text: api khe kāmato mohā nātmany astaviparyaye// iti/
children.translated_text: even in the sky, from desire and delusion, no — in the self, there should not be the eightfold error. Thus.

children.text: ito ’yam asaṃdigdhatvād iti hetur apy asiddha iti siddham/
children.translated_text: From this, the reason 'because it is free from doubt' is also unestablished — this is proven.
reference marker

children.text:
yady api sarvaḥ prāṇī pratyagātmāstitvaṃ pratyety aham asmīti/ na hi kaścid api nāham
          asmīti vipratipadyate/ pratyagātmaiva brahma tat tvam asi iti sāmānādhikaraṇyāt/ tasmād
          ātmatattvam asaṃdigdhaṃ siddham/ tathāpi dharmaṃ prati vipratipannā bahuvidhā iti nyāyena
          viśeṣapratipattir upapadyata eva/ tathā hi/ caitanyaviśiṣṭaṃ deham ātmeti lokāyatā
          manyante/ indriyāṇy ātmety anye/ antaḥkaraṇam ātmety apare/ kṣaṇabhaṅguraṃ saṃtanyamānaṃ
          vijñānam ātmeti bauddhā budhyante/ dehaparimāṇa ātmeti jainā jināḥ pratijānate/
          kartṛtvādiviśiṣṭaḥ parameśvarād bhinno jīvātmeti naiyāyikādayo varṇayanti/
          dravyabodhasvabhāvam ātmety ācāryāḥ paricakṣate/ bhoktaiva kevalaṃ na karteti sāṃkhyāḥ
          saṃgirante/ cidrūpaḥ kartṛtvādirahitaḥ parasmād abhinnaḥ pratyagātmety aupaniṣadā
          bhāṣante/ evaṃ prasiddhe dharmiṇi viśeṣato vipratipattau tadviśeṣasaṃśayo yujyate/ tathā
          ca saṃdehasaṃbhavāj jijñāsyatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ siddham/ tad itthaṃ brahmaṇo
          vicāryatvasaṃbhavena tadvicārātmakaṃ brahmamīmāṃsāśāstram āraṃbhaṇīyam iti yuktam/ janmādy
          asya yataḥ ityādisarvasya śāstrasyaitadvicārāpekṣatvāc chāstraprathamādhyāyasaṃgatam idam
          adhikaraṇam/
children.translated_text: Although every living being cognizes the existence of the inner self — 'I am' — for indeed no one disagrees [thinking] 'I am not' — and although the inner self is <s>Brahman</s>, as established by the co-referentiality of '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art) — and thus the reality of the self is established as free from doubt — nevertheless, by the principle 'the disputants are manifold regarding [its] nature (<s>dharma</s>),' disagreement regarding particular attributes is entirely possible. For thus: the materialists (<s>Lokāyatas</s>) think the self is the body endowed with consciousness. Others [think] the sense organs are the self. Still others [think] the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is the self. The Buddhists (<s>Bauddhas</s>) understand the self to be momentarily perishing consciousness that continues in a stream. The Jainas (<s>Jainas</s>) declare the self to be of the dimensions of the body. The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others describe the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) as endowed with agentship and the like, different from the Supreme Lord. The [Bhāṭṭa-Mīmāṃsā] teachers describe the self as having the nature of substance and cognition. The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> maintain that the self is merely an experiencer, not an agent. The <s>Aupaniṣadas</s> (Vedāntins) say the inner self is of the form of consciousness, devoid of agentship and the like, non-different from the Supreme. Thus, when there is disagreement regarding the particular attributes of a well-known property-bearer, doubt regarding those attributes is justified. And thus, since doubt is possible, the fact that <s>Brahman</s> is to be inquired into is established. Thus, since the possibility of inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> is [demonstrated], it is proper that the <s>Brahmamīmāṃsā</s> scripture, whose nature is that inquiry, should be commenced. Since 'that from which the origin [etc. of this world arise]' and the entire rest of the <s>śāstra</s> depends on this inquiry, this topic has its connection with the first chapter of the <s>śāstra</s>.
reference marker

children.text:
nanv itthaṃbhūte brahmaṇi kiṃ pramāṇaṃ pratyakṣam anumānam āgamo vā/ na kadācit tatra
          pratyakṣaṃ śramate/ atīndriyatvāt/ nāpy anumānam/ vyāptasya liṅgasyābhāvāt/ nāpy āgamaḥ/
          yato vāco nivartante iti śrutyaivāgamagamyatvaniṣedhāt/ upamānādikam aśakyaśaṅkam/
          niyataviṣayatvāt/ tasmād brahmaṇi pramāṇaṃ na saṃbhavatīti cet
children.translated_text: Now, regarding such a <s>Brahman</s>, what is the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)? Perception, inference, or scripture? Perception never succeeds there — because [<s>Brahman</s>] is beyond the senses. Nor does inference — because of the absence of a pervaded inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Nor scripture — because the <s>śruti</s> itself denies accessibility through scripture with 'from which words return.' Analogy and the like cannot even be suspected — because they have a limited domain. Therefore, no means of valid knowledge is possible regarding <s>Brahman</s> — if so,
do not say this. Because even though perception and the like are impossible, scripture is available.

children.text: yato vāco nivartante iti vāggocaratvaniṣedhāt katham etad iti cet
children.translated_text: 'From which words return' — since accessibility through words is denied, how is this [possible]? If so —

children.text:
śrutir eva niṣedhati vedāntavedyatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ śrutir eva vidhatte/ na hi
          vedapratipādite ’rthe ’nupapanne vaidikānāṃ buddhiḥ khidyate/ api tu tadupapādanamārgam
          eva vicārayati/ tasmād ubhayam api pratipādanīyam/ viṣayatvaniṣedhakāni vākyāni/
          vākyajanyavṛttivyaktasphuraṇalakṣaṇaphalāsaṃbhavavivakṣayā pravṛttāni/ viṣayatvabodhakāni
          tu vṛttijanyāvaraṇabhaṅgalakṣaṇaphalasaṃbhavavivakṣayā/ tad uktaṃ bhagavadbhiḥ :
children.translated_text: <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) itself denies, and <s>śruti</s> itself establishes that <s>Brahman</s> is to be known through <s>Vedānta</s>. For the intellect of the followers of the <s>Veda</s> is not troubled when the object taught by the <s>Veda</s> proves difficult [to understand]; rather, it investigates the very path of its elucidation. Therefore, both must be explained. The statements that deny [<s>Brahman's</s>] being an object [of knowledge] are uttered with the intention that the result characterized by the manifest shining of a mental modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) born from the sentence is impossible. But the statements that teach [<s>Brahman</s> as] an object are [uttered] with the intention that the result characterized by the destruction of the veil (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) produced by the mental modification is possible. As stated by the blessed [teacher]:
Because it is not a conferrer of an unattainable fruit, <s>Brahman</s> is not the object of <s>śruti</s>;

children.text: prameyaṃ pramitau tu syād ātmākārasamarpaṇāt// iti/
children.translated_text: but it is the object of cognition (<s>prameya</s>), through [the <s>vṛtti's</s>] offering the form of the self. Thus.

children.text: na prakāśyaṃ pramāṇena prakāśo brahmaṇaḥ svayam/
children.translated_text: The luminosity of <s>Brahman</s> is not to be illuminated by a means of knowledge; it is self-luminous;

children.text: tajjanyāvṛtibhaṅgatvāt prameyam iti gīyate// iti ca/
children.translated_text: it is called an object of cognition because [the means of knowledge] destroys the veil produced by it. Thus also.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu syād eṣa manoratho yadi siddhe ’rthe vedasya prāmāṇyaṃ sidhyet/
          saṃgatigrahaṇāyattatvāt/ vṛddhavyavahārasya ca loke kāryaikaniyatatvāt/ na hy asti
          saṃbhavaḥ śabdānāṃ kārye ’rthe saṃgatigrahe

siddhārthābhidhāyakatvaṃ tatra vā prāmāṇyam iti/ na hi turaṅgatve gṛhītasaṃgatikaṃ
          turaṅgapadaṃ gotvam ācaṣṭe tatra vā prāmāṇyaṃ bhajate/ tasmāt kāryagṛhītasaṃgatikānāṃ
          śabdānāṃ kārya eva prāmāṇyam/
children.translated_text: would denote an already-established entity or have authoritativeness regarding it. For the word 'horse,' whose connection has been apprehended with respect to horse-ness, does not denote cow-ness or have authoritativeness regarding it. Therefore, for words whose connection is apprehended with respect to what is to be done, authoritativeness pertains only to what is to be done.

Now, this might be wishful thinking, if the authoritativeness of the <s>Veda</s> were established regarding an already-established entity. Because [authoritativeness] depends on the apprehension of a connection [between words and their meanings]. And the practical usage of the learned in the world is invariably restricted to [words denoting] what is to be done (<s>kārya</s>). For there is no possibility that words whose connection is apprehended with respect to an object to be done

children.text:
nanu mukhavikāsādiliṅgād dharṣahetuṃ prasiddhārtham anumāya yatra śabdasya saṃgatigraho
          yathā putras te jāta ityādiṣu tatrāvaśyaṃ kāryam antareṇaiva śabdasya siddhe ’rthe
          prāmāṇyam āśrīyata iti cen
children.translated_text: Now, [in cases] where the connection of a word is apprehended through inferring a well-known meaning as the cause of delight from signs such as facial expressions and the like — as in 'a son is born to you' and the like — there, the authoritativeness of the word regarding an already-established entity must necessarily be resorted to, without [reference to] what is to be done — if so,

children.text:
na/ putrajanmavad eva priyāsukhaprasavāder anekasya harṣahetor upasthīyamānatvena
          pariśeṣāvadhāraṇānupapatteḥ/ putras te jāta ityādiṣu siddhārthapareṣu prayogeṣu dvāraṃ
          dvāram ityādivat kāryādhyāhāreṇa prayogopapatteś ca/ śāstratvaprasiddhyā ca na vedāntānāṃ
          siddhārthatvaparatvam/ pravṛttinivṛttiparāṇām eva vākyānāṃ śāstratvaprasiddheḥ/ tad uktaṃ
          bhaṭṭācāryaiḥ :
children.translated_text: No — because, since many causes of joy such as the birth of a son, the pleasure of a beloved, and the like are [all] available, determination by elimination is untenable. And because, in usages pertaining to established facts such as 'a son has been born to you' and the like, the usage is justified by supplying an implied action, like [the expression] 'a door, a door!' And because, by the well-known nature of being a scripture, the <s>Vedānta</s> [passages] are not oriented toward established facts. For only sentences oriented toward engagement or withdrawal are well known as scripture. As stated by the <s>Bhaṭṭācāryas</s> (the followers of <s>Kumārila Bhaṭṭa</s>):

children.text: pravṛttir vā nivṛttir vā nityena kṛtakena vā/
children.translated_text: 'That by which engagement or withdrawal, whether eternal or produced,

children.text: puṃsāṃ yenopadiśyeta tac chāstram abhidhīyate// iti/
children.translated_text: is taught to people — that is called a scripture.' Thus.

children.text:
na caiteṣāṃ svarūpaparatve prayojanam asti/ śrutavedāntārthasyāpi puṃsaḥ
          sāṃsārikadharmāṇām anivṛtteḥ/ tasmād vedāntānām apy ātmā jñātavya iti samāmnātena
          vidhinaikavākyatām āśritya kāryaparataivāśrayaṇīyeti siddham/ tataś ca kevalasiddharūpe
          brahmaṇi vedāntānāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ na sidhyatīti cet/
children.translated_text: Nor is there any purpose in [the <s>Vedānta</s> passages'] being oriented toward [describing] the essential nature [of <s>Brahman</s>]. Because, even for a person who has heard the meaning of the <s>Vedānta</s>, the worldly properties [of bondage] do not cease. Therefore, even for the <s>Vedānta</s> [passages], it is established that their orientation toward injunction (<s>kārya</s>) should be accepted, through syntactic unity with the injunction found in '<s>ātmā jñātavyaḥ</s>' ('the Self should be known'). If [you object] that therefore the authority of the <s>Vedānta</s> with regard to <s>Brahman</s>, which is purely of an established nature, cannot be established —

children.text:
atra pratividhīyate: na tāvad siddhe vyutpattyasiddhiḥ/ prāg unnītayā nītyā putras te
          jāta iti vākyāt siddhaparād api vyutpattisiddheḥ/ na ca pariśeṣāvadhāraṇānupapattiḥ/
          priyāsukhaprasavāder api saṃbhavād iti bhaṇitavyam/ putrapadāṅkitapaṭapradarśanavat
          priyāsukhaprasavādisūcakābhāvāt/ putrajanmaiva tatsūcakam iti cen na
children.translated_text: Here the counter-resolution is stated. First, it is not the case that there is no semantic competence (<s>vyutpatti</s>) with regard to established facts. Because semantic competence is established even from a sentence oriented toward established facts, such as 'a son has been born to you,' by the procedure previously raised. Nor is determination by elimination untenable — because [the objection] that causes of pleasure such as happiness, and the like are also possible, should not be made. Because there is no indicator (<s>sūcaka</s>) of the pleasure of a beloved, happiness, and the like — unlike the display of a cloth marked with a footprint of a son. If [you say] 'the birth of a son itself is the indicator of those [other joys]' — no,
because there is no reason to abandon the primarily understood birth of a son; and because the birth of a son itself is the cause of the greatest joy.
'Through the birth and misfortune of a son, there is no other [cause]
of happiness and sorrow' — because this is observed. And thus <s>Citsukhācārya</s> has said:
'When, having directly seen the birth of <s>Caitra</s>'s son,
one who has gone [away] is informed through a cloth marked with [the son's] footprint — [the ascertainment] by elimination [is justified].'

children.text:
yad uktaṃ siddhārthapareṣu kāryādhyāhāra iti tad ayuktam/ mukhyārthaviṣayatayā siddhe ’pi
          prayogasiddhāv adhyāhārānupapatteḥ/ yad uktaṃ śāstratvaprasiddhyā ca na svarūpaparatvam
          iti tad apy ayuktam/ hitaśāsanād api śāstratvopapatteḥ/ na ca prayojanābhāvaḥ/
          śrutamatavedāntajanyādvitīyātmavijñānābhyāsena vidyodaye
          saṃsāranidānāvidyānivṛttyupalakṣitabrahmātmatālakṣaṇaparamapuruṣārtha-siddheḥ/ na cātra
          vidhiḥ saṃbhavati/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ tathā hi : kiṃ śābdajñānaṃ vidheyaṃ kiṃ vā
          bhāvanātmakam āhosvit sākṣātkārarūpam/ nādyaḥ/
          viditapadārthasaṃgatikasyādhītaśabdanyāyatattvasyāntareṇāpi vidhiṃ śabdād evopapatteḥ/
          nāpi dvitīyaḥ/ bhāvanāyā jñānaprakarṣahetubhāvasyānvayavyatirekasiddhatayā
          prāptatvenāvidheyatvāt/ aprāptaprāpakasyaiva vidhitvāṅgīkārāt/ tṛtīye sākṣātkāraḥ kiṃ
          brahmasvarūpaḥ kiṃ vāntaḥkaraṇapariṇāmabhedaḥ/ nādyaḥ/ tasya nityatvenāvidheyatvāt/ nāpi
          dvitīyaḥ/ ānandasākṣātkārarūpatayā phalatvenāvidheyatvāt/ tasmāj jñātavya ityādīnām
          avidhāyakatvād arhe kṛtyatṛcaś ca iti kṛtyapratyayānām arhārthe vidhānād arhārthataiva
          vyākhyeyā/ tathā ca sarveṣāṃ vedāntavākyānām upakramopasaṃhārādiṣaḍvidhatātparyopetatvān
          nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvabrahmātmaparatvam āstheyam/
children.translated_text: What was said — that an implied action should be supplied in [sentences] oriented toward established facts — that is unjust. Because, when usage is established through the primary meaning, the supplying of something implied is untenable. What was said — that by the well-known nature of being a scripture, [the <s>Vedānta</s> passages] are not oriented toward essential nature — that too is unjust. Because scripture-hood is justified even from beneficent instruction (<s>hitaśāsana</s>). Nor is there absence of purpose — because, through the repeated practice of the non-dual knowledge of the self generated by the <s>Vedānta</s> whose meaning has been heard and reflected upon, when knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) arises, the attainment of the supreme human goal in the form of identity with <s>Brahman</s> — characterized by the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which is the root cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> — is achieved. Nor is an injunction possible here — because of the inability to withstand the alternatives. For consider: is the enjoined [thing] verbal knowledge, or is it of the nature of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), or is it of the form of direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>)? Not the first — because, for one who has studied the words and reasoning and knows the meaning and syntactic connections, [verbal knowledge] arises from the words themselves even without an injunction. Nor the second — because meditation, its being the cause of the intensification of knowledge being established through positive and negative concomitance, is already obtained (<s>prāpta</s>) and hence not a proper object of injunction — since only what brings about what has not been obtained is accepted as an injunction. In the third case: is the direct realization of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, or is it a modification of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>)? Not the first — because, being eternal, it cannot be enjoined. Nor the second — because, being of the nature of the direct realization of bliss, it is a result (<s>phala</s>) and hence not enjoinable. Therefore, since [passages like] '<s>jñātavyaḥ</s>' ('should be known') and the like are not injunctive, and since the <s>kṛtya</s> suffixes (potential suffixes) are ordained in the sense of fitness (<s>arha</s>) by the rule '<s>arhe kṛtyatṛcaś ca</s>', they should be interpreted as denoting fitness. And thus, since all <s>Vedānta</s> statements possess the sixfold criteria of purport (<s>tātparya</s>) such as introductory statement, conclusion, and the like, their orientation toward the identity of the self with <s>Brahman</s> — which is by nature eternally pure, awakened, and free — should be maintained.

children.text:
niṣpradeśe paramāṇau pradeśavṛttitvenābhimatasya saṃyogasya durupapādanatayā
          tannibandhanasya dvyaṇukasyāsiddhau dvyaṇukādikrameṇārambhavādāsaṃbhavād acetanāyāḥ
          prakṛter mahadādirūpeṇa pariṇāmavādāsaṃbhavāc ca khyātibādhānyathānupapattyānirvacanīyaḥ
          prapañcaś cidvivarta iti siddham/ svarūpāparityāgena rūpāntarāpattir vivarta iti
          satyamithyākhyāvabhāsa iti/ avabhāso ’dhyāsa iti paryāyaḥ/ sa cādhyāso dvividhaḥ :
          arthādhyāso jñānādhyāsaś ceti/ tad uktam :
children.translated_text: Since conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) — which is assumed to operate in a part-possessing [entity] — is difficult to establish in a partless atom, the dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) grounded in that [conjunction] is unestablished, and hence the theory of origination through the sequence of dyads and the like (<s>ārambhavāda</s>) is impossible. And since the theory of transformation (<s>pariṇāmavāda</s>) — in the form of the non-conscious <s>Prakṛti</s> transforming into <s>Mahat</s> and the like — is also impossible; and since what is perceived (<s>khyāti</s>), its sublation (<s>bādha</s>), and its being otherwise inexplicable (<s>anyathānupapatti</s>) [all converge] — it is established that the phenomenal world is an indeterminable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) <s>vivarta</s> (apparent transformation) of consciousness (<s>cit</s>). <s>Vivarta</s> is the assumption of another form without abandoning one's own essential nature. [Alternatively expressed as:] the appearance of the real and the unreal. And 'appearance' (<s>avabhāsa</s>) is a synonym for 'superimposition' (<s>adhyāsa</s>). And that superimposition is twofold: superimposition of an object (<s>arthādhyāsa</s>) and superimposition of cognition (<s>jñānādhyāsa</s>). As stated:
'The [appearance of an] other [thing] upon the self (<s>parātmatā</s>), born from the defect, latent impression, and means of knowledge;

children.text: taddhīś cādhyāsa iti hi dvayam iṣṭaṃ manīṣibhiḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: and the cognition thereof — this twofold [superimposition] is accepted by the wise.' Thus.

children.text: punar api dvividho ’dhyāsaḥ/ nirupādhikasopādhikabhedāt/ tad apy uktam :
children.translated_text: Superimposition is again twofold — by the distinction of unconditioned (<s>nirupādhika</s>) and conditioned (<s>sopādhika</s>). That too is stated:
'That which arises from ignorance agitated by a defect or by <s>karma</s>,
and which is opposed to the knowledge of reality — this error is unconditioned.
That which is the unfolding of ignorance — [its] agitation acquired through the proximity of a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) —
and which is removable by the departure of the limiting condition — that is called conditioned error.' Thus.

children.text: tatra svarūpeṇa kalpitāhamādyadhyāso nirupādhikaḥ/ tad apy uktam :
children.translated_text: Therein, the superimposition of 'I' (<s>aham</s>) and the like, imagined as [the self's] own essential nature, is unconditioned. As stated:

children.text: nīlimeva viyaty eṣā bhrāntyā brahmaṇi saṃsṛtiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Like the blue [appearance] in the sky, this <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) [exists] in <s>Brahman</s> through error;

children.text: ghaṭavyomeva bhoktāyaṃ bhrānto bhedena na svataḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: like pot-space, this enjoyer is deluded through [the appearance of] difference, not through its own nature.' Thus.

children.text:
ata eva bhāṣyakāraḥ śuktikā rajatavad avabhāsata ekaś candraḥ sadvitīyavad iti
          nidarśanadvayam udājahāra/ śiṣṭaṃ śāstra eva spaṣṭam iti vistarabhiyoparamyate/ evaṃ ca
          dṛgdṛśyau dvāv eva padārthāv iti vedāntināṃ siddhānta iti sarvam avadātam/
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (<s>Śaṅkarācārya</s>) adduced two illustrations: 'nacre appears like silver' and 'the one moon appears as if accompanied [by a second].' The rest is clear in the scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) itself — [we] desist out of fear of prolixity. And thus, [the doctrine that] the seer (<s>dṛk</s>) and the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) are the only two categories — this is the established doctrine of the <s>Vedāntins</s>. Thus everything is clear.

children.text:
atra prabhākaraḥ : śuktikā rajatavad avabhāsata iti dṛṣṭānto neṣṭaḥ/ rajatapratyayasya
          śuktikālambanatvānupapatteḥ/ tathā hi : idaṃ rajatam iti pratītau śukter ālambanatvaṃ
          purodeśasattāmātreṇāvalambyate kāraṇatvena bhāsamānatvena vā/ nādyaḥ/ purovartināṃ
          loṣṭādīnām apy ālambanatvaprasaṅgāt/ atha kaladhautabodhakaraṇasaṃskārodbodhakāraṇatvena
          taddvārā rajatajñānakāraṇatvād ālambanatvaṃ manyase/ tad api na saṃgacchate/ cakṣurādīnām
          api kāraṇatvena viṣayatvāpātāt/ atha bhāsamānatayā viṣayatvam iṣyate tad apy aśliṣṭam/
          rajatanirbhāsasya śuktikālambanatvānupapatteḥ/ yasmin vijñāne yad avabhāsate tat
          tadālambanam/ atra ca kaladhautānubhavaḥ śuktikālambanatvakalpanāyāṃ virudhyate/ tathā
          cācakathan nyāyavīthyāṃ śālikanāthaḥ :
children.translated_text: Here, [the objection of] <s>Prabhākara</s>: The illustration 'nacre appears like silver' is not acceptable — because it is untenable that the silver-cognition has nacre as its object (<s>ālambana</s>). For consider: in the cognition 'this is silver,' is the object-hood of nacre maintained merely through its being present before [the perceiver], or through its appearing [as nacre]? Not the first — because clods of earth and the like that are also present before [the perceiver] would absurdly become objects too.
