Now, if you think that [nacre's] object-hood is [justified] because it is the cause, through awakening the latent impression that causes the cognition of silver, and thereby is indirectly the cause of the silver-cognition — that too does not cohere. Because the eye and the like, being also causes, would absurdly become objects. Now, if object-hood is desired through [the thing's] appearing [in cognition] — that too is incoherent. Because it is untenable that the silver-appearance has nacre as its object. Whatever appears in a cognition — that is the object of that [cognition]. And here, the experience of silver contradicts the supposition that nacre is the object. And thus <s>Śālikanātha</s> has stated in the <s>Nyāyavīthī</s>:

children.text: atra brūmo ya evārtho yasyāṃ saṃvidi bhāsate/
children.translated_text: 'Here we say: whatever object appears in whatever cognition —

children.text: vedyaḥ sa eva nānyad dhi vedyāvedyatvalakṣaṇam//
children.translated_text: that alone is its object of knowledge; for no other definition of knowability and unknowability [exists].

children.text: idaṃ rajatam ity atra rajataṃ tv avabhāsate/
children.translated_text: In "this is silver," silver is what appears;

children.text: tad eva tena vedyaṃ syān na tu śuktir avedanāt//
children.translated_text: that alone would be the object of knowledge thereby, not nacre, since it is not cognized.
Therefore, the appearance of one thing as another is refuted by experience itself;

children.text: anyasmin bhāsamāne hi na paraṃ bhāsate yataḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: for when one thing appears, the other does not appear.' Thus.

children.text:
kiṃ ca mithyājānānotpattau sāmagrī na samasti/ kiṃ kevalānīndriyādīni kāraṇāni
          doṣadūṣitāni vā/ nādyaḥ/ teṣāṃ samīcīnajñānajananasāmarthyopalambhāt/ anyathā samīcīnaṃ
          rajatajñānaṃ kadācid udayam āsādayet/ na dvitīyaḥ/ doṣāṇām
          autsargikakāryaprasavaśaktipratibandhamātraprabhāvatvāt/ na hi duṣṭaṃ kuṭajabījaṃ
          vaṭāṅkuraṃ janayitum īṣṭe/ na vā tailakaluṣitaṃ śālibījam aśālyaṅkurajananāyālam/ kiṃ tu
          svakāryaṃ na karoti/
children.translated_text: Moreover, the aggregate of causes for the production of erroneous cognition does not exist. Are the sense-organs and the like alone the causes, or [are they] vitiated by defects? Not the first — because their capacity to produce correct cognition is observed. Otherwise, correct cognition of silver would at some time arise [from nacre]. Not the second — because defects have the power merely to obstruct the productive capacity of the natural effect. For a defective <s>kutaja</s> seed is not able to produce a banyan sprout. Nor is a rice seed contaminated with oil capable of producing a non-rice sprout. Rather, it simply does not produce its own [natural] effect.

children.text: nanu dāvadahanadagdhasya vetrabījasya kadalīkāṇḍajanakatvaṃ dṛṣṭam iti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: 'But it is observed that the seed of a reed burned by a forest fire generates a banana stalk.'

children.text:
tan na sthāne/ dagdhasyāvetrabījatvena doṣāṇāṃ viparītakāryakāritvaṃ praty anudāharaṇāt/
          na ca bhasmakadoṣadūṣitasya kaukṣeyasyāśuśukṣaṇer bahvannapacanasāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭam ity
          eṣṭavyam/ aśitapītādyāhārapariṇatau jāṭharasya jātavedasaḥ śaktatvāt/ tad uktam :
children.translated_text: That is not apt — because, since the burned [seed] is no longer a reed-seed, it is not an instance for defects producing a contrary effect. Nor should one maintain that the fire in the stomach, when vitiated by the defect of calcium powder, has the capacity to digest large quantities of food — because the digestive fire is capable of [digesting] the transformation of consumed food, drink, and the like [through its own power]. As stated:
'There is no cause for the production of erroneous cognition;

children.text: doṣāś cen na hi doṣāṇāṃ kāryaśaktivighātatā//
children.translated_text: if [you say] defects [are the cause] — no, for defects have [only] the power to obstruct [normal] effect-production.
In [cases like] calcium powder and the like, defect-hood [consists] precisely in the obstruction of the effect;
for the production of [digestive] juices is the [natural] effect of the fire dwelling in the stomach.' Thus.

children.text:
api cāsaty apy arthe jñānaprādurbhāvābhyupagame samīcīnasthale ’pi jñānānāṃ
          svagocaravyabhicāraśaṅkāṅkurasaṃbhavena niraṅkuśo vyavahāro lupyate/ tad āha:
children.translated_text: Moreover, if the arising of cognition even in the absence of an [corresponding] object is accepted, then even in the case of correct [cognition], the sprout of doubt regarding the deviation of cognitions from their own objects would arise — and unrestrained practical activity would be destroyed. As stated:

children.text: yadi cārthaṃ parityajya kācid buddhiḥ prakāśate/
children.translated_text: 'If some cognition manifests abandoning [its proper] object,
then, being deviant with respect to its own object, how can it be a cause of trust?' Thus.

children.text:
nanu rajatagocaraikaviśiṣṭajñānānaṅgīkāre viśiṣṭavyavahāro na sidhyet/ atas tatsiddhaye
          ’pi viparyayo ’ṅgīkārya iti cen
children.translated_text: Objection: 'If a single cognition qualified by silver is not accepted, qualified practical activity would not be established. Therefore, for the establishment of that [practical activity] too, error (<s>viparyaya</s>) should be accepted.'

children.text:
na/ idaṃ rajatam iti grahaṇasmaraṇābhidhasya bodhadvayasya vyavahārakāraṇatvāṅgīkārāt/
          yady evaṃ idaṃ śuktikāśakalaṃ tad rajatam ity ato ’pi viśiṣṭavyavahāraḥ syād iti/ tan na/
          tatredam iti purovartidravyamātragrahaṇasya
          doṣadūṣitacakṣurjanyatvenānākalitaśuktitvādiviśeṣitasya sāmānyamātragrahaṇarūpatvād
          rajatam iti jñānasyāsaṃnihitaviṣayasya saṃprayogaliṅgādyaprasūtatayā
          sadṛśāvabodhitasaṃskāramātraprabhavatvena pariśeṣaprāptasmṛtibhāvasya doṣahetukatayā
          gṛhītatattāṃśapramoṣād grahaṇamātratvopapatteḥ/ tad apy uktam :
children.translated_text: No — because the duality of cognitions — apprehension and memory — designated as 'this' and 'silver' respectively, is accepted as the cause of practical activity. If so, [the objection is:] 'From "this is a piece of nacre, that is silver," qualified practical activity would follow too.' No — because 'this,' the mere apprehension of the substance present before [the perceiver], being produced by the eye vitiated by defects and being a mere apprehension of the universal without the specific qualifications such as nacre-hood being discerned, [has the nature of] mere grasping; and 'silver,' the cognition whose object is not present, being generated solely from latent impressions awakened by similar [previous] cognitions and not born from sensory contact, inferential marks, or the like, having by elimination attained the status of memory, and being caused by a defect — since the 'that'-component of the grasped [content] is lost — amounts to mere grasping. As stated:

children.text: nanv atra rajatābhāsaḥ katham eṣa ghaṭiṣyate/
children.translated_text: 'But here, how will this appearance of silver be explained?
It is said: a piece of nacre is apprehended without [its] specific differences.
The specific features of nacre that would be the causes of differentiation from silver —

children.text: te na jñātā abhibhavāj jñātā sāmānyarūpatā//
children.translated_text: those are not cognized, due to being overpowered; [only] the generic form is cognized.

children.text: anantaraṃ ca rajatasmṛtir jātā tayāpi ca/
children.translated_text: Then, the memory of silver arises; and by that [memory] too,
due to the defect of the mind, without the reflective awareness of the "that"-component —
having silver as its object, without being discriminated from nacre —
the appearance of silver through memory will be justified.

children.text: na hy asaṃnihitaṃ tāvat pratyakṣaṃ rajataṃ bhavet/
children.translated_text: For silver that is not present cannot be a direct perception;
and due to the absence of inferential marks and the like, it is not the object of any other means of knowledge.

children.text: pariśeṣāt smṛtir iti niścayo jāyate punaḥ/
children.translated_text: By elimination, [the conviction arises that] it is memory' — thus the ascertainment arises again.

children.text:
nanu kim idam ekaikaṃ vyavahārakāraṇam uta saṃbhūya/ na prathamaḥ/ deśabhedena
          pravṛttiprasaṅgāt/ na caramaḥ/ prayatnāyaugapadyāj jñānāyaugapadyāt ityādinā
          jñānayaugapadyaniṣedhāt/ ato jñānadvayaṃ hetur ity ayuktaṃ vaca iti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Is each of these [cognitions] individually the cause of practical activity, or [only] conjointly? Not the first — because there would be the absurd consequence of engagement based on [each cognition's] different location. Not the latter — because, since by [the principle] "due to the non-simultaneity of effort, there is non-simultaneity of cognition" and the like, the simultaneity of cognitions is denied — therefore, the statement that a pair of cognitions is the cause is unjust.'

children.text:
maivaṃ vocaḥ/ avinaśyatoḥ sahāvasthānaniṣedhe ’pi vinaśyadavinaśyatoḥ
          sahāvasthānasyāniṣiddhatvena nirantarotpannayos tadupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: Do not say so! Although the co-existence of the two imperishable [entities — apprehension and recollection] is prohibited, since the co-existence of the perishing and the imperishable is not prohibited, their [simultaneous occurrence] is tenable, as they arise in unbroken succession.

children.text:
nanu rajatajñānād rajatārthī rajate pravartatāṃ nāma/ paurastye vastuni kathaṃ pravṛttiḥ
          syād iti cen
children.translated_text: Now, let one who desires silver, from the cognition of silver, proceed toward silver. But how could there be activity toward the object lying in front? If [one argues] thus —

children.text:
na/ svarūpato viṣayataś cāgṛhītabhedayor grahaṇasmaraṇayoḥ
          saṃnihitarajatagocarajñānasārūpyeṇa vastutaḥ parasparaṃ vibhinnayor apy
          abhedocitasāmānādhikaraṇyavyapadeśahetutvopapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: No. Because, for apprehension and recollection — whose difference is not grasped either in their essential nature or in their objects — through their similarity to the cognition of silver that is present before one, though they are in reality mutually different, the fitness for being the cause of designation through co-referential usage (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) appropriate to non-difference is tenable.
How [can there be] similarity of apprehension and recollection to the cognition of silver that is present?

children.text:
yathā caitat tathā niśamyatām/ saṃnihitarajatagocaraṃ hi vijñānam idamaṃśarajatāṃśayor
          asaṃsargaṃ nāvagāhate/ tayoḥ saṃsṛṣṭatvenāsaṃsargasyaivābhāvāt/ nāpi svagataṃ bhedam/
          ekajñānatvāt/ evaṃ grahaṇasmaraṇe api doṣavaśād vidyamānam apīdamaṃśarajatāṃśayor
          asaṃsargaṃ bhedaṃ nāvagāhete
iti/ bhedāgrahaṇam eva sārūpyam/ tad uktaṃ gurumatānusāribhiḥ :
children.translated_text: Thus, the non-apprehension of difference is itself the similarity. As stated by those who follow the teacher's doctrine:

How this is so — please listen. For the cognition pertaining to silver that is present does not apprehend the non-connection between the 'this'-aspect and the 'silver'-aspect — because, since those two are connected, there is simply no non-connection. Nor [does it apprehend] the internal difference — because it is a single cognition. Similarly, apprehension and recollection too, due to a defect, do not apprehend the non-connection and difference between the 'this'-aspect and the 'silver'-aspect, even though [these differences] exist.
'These apprehension and recollection do not make discrimination shine forth,

children.text: samyagrajatabodhāc ca bhinne yady api tattvataḥ//
children.translated_text: and though truly different from the cognition of real silver,
nevertheless, when they appear as [if] undifferentiated, because of the equality of non-grasping of difference,
the cognition of real silver has a single object directly present.',

children.text: tato bhinne abuddhvā ca grahaṇasmaraṇe ime/
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, not having cognized the difference, these apprehension and recollection —
people merely think [them to be] of the same form;
through appearing as directly present and through grasping the same object,
the awareness of non-distinctness is thus established.',
'And the conventional usage, similar to that, proceeds from that very [non-apprehension of difference].'

children.text:
evam agṛhītavivekam āpannasaṃnihitarūpyajñānasārūpyaṃ grahaṇasmaraṇadvayam
          ayathāvyavahārahetur iti siddham/
children.translated_text: Thus it is established that the pair of apprehension and recollection, in which discrimination is not grasped and which has attained similarity to the cognition of silver that is present, is the cause of the erroneous conventional usage.

children.text:
yady evam ayathāvyavahāro grahaṇasmaraṇajanyas tarhi pītaḥ śaṅkha ityādau sa na siddhas
          tatra tayor abhāvād iti cen
children.translated_text: If so, [then] since the erroneous conventional usage is produced by apprehension and recollection, in [cases like] 'The conch is yellow,' it would not be established — because those two [apprehension and recollection of different objects] are absent there. If [one argues] thus —

children.text:
na/ agṛhītavivekayoḥ prāptasamīcīnasaṃsargajñānasārūpyatve grahaṇayor eva
          vyavahārasaṃpādakatvopapatteḥ/ nayanaraśmivartinaḥ pittadravyasya pītimā doṣavaśād
          dravyarahito gṛhyate/ śaṅkho ’py akalitaśuklaguṇaḥ svarūpato gṛhyate/ tad anayor
          guṇaguṇinoḥ saṃsargayogyayor asaṃsargāgrahasārūpyāt pītatapanīyapiṇḍapratyayāvailakṣaṇyād
          vyavahāra upapadyate/ yathoktam :
children.translated_text: No. Because, when there are two apprehensions in which discrimination is not grasped and which have attained the similarity of correct perception-of-what-is-present, it is tenable that apprehensions alone bring about the conventional usage. The yellowness of the bile-substance residing in the rays of the eye is grasped, due to a defect, as devoid of [its own] substance. The conch too is grasped in its essential nature, without the white quality being discerned. Since those two — quality and substance-possessor — are fit for conjunction, from the similarity [consisting in] the non-grasping of their non-conjunction, the conventional usage is justified by its non-distinctness from the cognition of a lump of heated gold. As stated:
'In the cognition of a yellow conch, the yellowness of the bile
residing in the sense-organ is grasped as devoid of substance, due to a defect.',
'And the whiteness of the conch is not grasped, due to a defect of the sense-organ;
mere substance alone appears, devoid of [visible] form.',

children.text: guṇe dravyavyapekṣe ca dravye ca guṇakāṅkṣiṇi/
children.translated_text: 'When the quality, dependent on substance, and the substance, expecting a quality,

children.text: bhāsamāne tayor buddhir asaṃbandhaṃ na budhyate//
children.translated_text: appear — the cognition does not cognize their non-connection.',
'When these two cognitions appear the same, with the appearance of real yellowness,

children.text: vyavahāro ’pi tattulya evam atrāpi yujyate// iti/
children.translated_text: the conventional usage, similar to that, is likewise justified here too.' Thus.

children.text:
nanv idaṃ rajatam iti bhrāntijñānānabhyupagame rajataprasakter asattvān nedaṃ rajatam iti
          niṣedhaḥ kathaṃ kaladhautābhāvaṃ bodhayatīti cet
children.translated_text: Now, if the erroneous cognition 'This is silver' is not accepted, since the attribution of silver is unreal — how does the negation 'This is not silver' convey the absence of silver? If [one argues] thus —

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ/bhedāgrahaprasañjitasya śuktau rajatavyavahārasya niṣedhasvīkāreṇa
          kalpanālāghavasadbhāvāt/ tad uktaṃ pañcikāprakaraṇe :
children.translated_text: This is no fault. Because there is parsimony of construction (<s>kalpanālāghava</s>) in accepting the negation of the silver-convention that was occasioned by the non-grasping of difference in relation to the shell. As stated in the section of the <s>Pañcikā</s>:
'Even the [cognition of] false existence, because of prompting conventional usage similar to [the real],
deceives people with respect to the silver-convention portion.
Therefore, the sublating cognition (<s>bādhakapratyaya</s>) is considered to be sublating (<s>bādhaka</s>),
because of blocking the silver-convention that was about to obtain.' Thus.

children.text:
tad anena prācīnayor jñānayoḥ satyatve kathaṃ bhramatvaprasiddhir iti śaṅkā parākṛtā/
          ayathāvyavahārapravartakatvena tadupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: By this, the doubt — 'If the two prior cognitions are real, how is the well-known status of error [established]?' — has been dispelled. Because it [error] is tenable through being the prompter of erroneous conventional usage.

children.text:
kiṃ ca nedaṃ rajatam iti bādhakāvabodho nābhāvam avagāhate/ bhāvavyatirekeṇābhāvasya
          durgrahaṇatvāt/
children.translated_text: Moreover, the sublating cognition 'This is not silver' does not apprehend absence — because absence is difficult to grasp independently of [some positive] being.

children.text: yady evam aṅga nāstīti pratyayasya kim ālambanam/ aparathā māhāyānikapakṣānupraveśa

children.translated_text: if [one argues] thus,
If so, then what is the object-support of the cognition 'It does not exist'? Otherwise, one would enter the <s>Māhāyānika</s> (Mahāyāna Buddhist) position —

children.text:
maivaṃ bhāṣiṣṭhāḥ/ abhāvasya dharmipratiyoginirūpaṇādhīnanirūpyatvenāvaśyābhyupagamanīye
          dṛśye pratiyoginy adṛśye vā smaryamāṇe ’dhikaraṇamātrabuddher eva nāstīti
          vyavahāropapattāv atiriktābhāvakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvāt/ tad uktam amṛtakalāyām :
children.translated_text: do not speak thus! Because absence, having its determination dependent on the specification of the property-bearer and counter-positive, since the necessarily-accepted visible counter-positive — or the invisible one being remembered — [is sufficient], the conventional usage 'It does not exist' is justified by the bare cognition of the substrate alone, and there is no means of knowledge for the construction of an absence over and above [that]. As stated in the <s>Amṛtakalā</s>:
'Here it is said: the cognition of a thing such as a plot of ground is twofold —
one has a conjoined object; the other has the bare [thing] alone as its object.',
'And the one whose object is the bare [thing] alone is also declared to be twofold —

children.text: pratiyoginy adṛśye ca dṛśye ca pratiyogini//
children.translated_text: when the counter-positive is invisible, and when the counter-positive is visible.',

children.text: tatra tanmātradhīr yeyaṃ smṛte ca pratiyogini/
children.translated_text: 'Therein, that cognition of the bare [thing] alone, when the counter-positive is remembered —
that very [cognition] is the non-existence, on that plot of ground, of the counter-positive such as a pot and the like.'

children.text:
ata eva ca prābhākaramatānusāribhiḥ pramāṇapārāyaṇe pratyakṣādīni pañcaiva pramāṇāni
          prapañcitāni/
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the followers of the <s>Prābhākara</s> doctrine have elaborated in the <s>Pramāṇapārāyaṇa</s> that the means of valid knowledge are five only, beginning with perception.

children.text:
nanv evam abhāvasyābhāve nakārasya vaiyarthyam āpadyeta/ anuśāsanavirodhaś cāpated iti
          cet
children.translated_text: Now, if absence itself is absent, then the letter <s>na</s> (the negative particle) would become meaningless. And the contradiction with grammar would result — if [one argues] thus,

children.text:
tad etad vārtam/ ekonapañcāśad varṇānāṃ madhye kasyāpi varṇasyābhāvārthatvādarśanena
          varṇasya sato nakārasya tadarthatvānupapatteḥ/ na caivam anuśāsanavirodhaḥ/
          tadanyatadabhāvatadviruddheṣv artheṣv anuśāsanasyaivam arthaḥ syāt/ tathā hi : cetanānāṃ
          madhye kaścana kasyacic chatruḥ kaścana kasyacin mitraṃ kaścana kasyacid udāsīnas
          tathaivācetanānām api/ tadanyapadena tadudāsīno nakārārthaḥ/ viruddhapadena śatrur
          nakārārthaḥ/ tadabhāvapadena mitraṃ nakārārthaḥ/ tathā cābrāhmaṇapada evaitat trayaṃ
          pratīyate śūdra ity udāsīno yavana iti śatruḥ kṣatriya iti mitram/ evaṃ sarvatra
          nañprayogasthale draṣṭavyam iti na kaścid abhāvo bhāvavyatiriktaḥ saṃbhavati/ tasmād
          uktayā rītyā bhramabādhaprasiddhyā vivādādhyāsitāḥ pratyayā yathārthāḥ pratyayatvād
          daṇḍīti pratyayavad iti siddham/
children.translated_text: that is groundless. Because, among the forty-nine phonemes, since no phoneme whatsoever is seen to have absence as its meaning, it is untenable that the existing phoneme <s>na</s> has absence as its meaning. Nor is there thus any contradiction with grammar. The grammatical rule applies to meanings [designated as] 'different from that' (<s>tadanya</s>), 'the absence of that' (<s>tadabhāva</s>), and 'the opposite of that' (<s>tadviruddha</s>). For thus: among conscious beings, some are enemies of some, some are friends of some, some are indifferent to some — and likewise among non-conscious things. By the term 'different from that,' the indifferent one is the meaning of <s>na</s>. By the term 'opposite,' the enemy is the meaning of <s>na</s>. By the term 'absence of that,' the friend is the meaning of <s>na</s>. And thus, in the word <s>abrāhmaṇa</s> (non-Brāhmaṇa), all three are cognized: <s>Śūdra</s> as the indifferent; <s>Yavana</s> as the enemy; <s>Kṣatriya</s> as the friend. Thus, in every instance of the use of the negative particle, this should be observed — hence no absence separate from a positive entity is possible. Therefore, by the method stated, through the well-known [phenomena of] error and sublation, the cognitions over which there is dispute are valid — being cognitions, like [the cognition] of a man with a stick — thus it is established.

children.text:
tad apare na kṣamante/ iha khalu nikhilaprekṣāvān samīhitatatsādhanayor anyatarapravedane
          pravartate/ na ca rajatam arthayamānasya śuktikāśakalajñānaṃ tadrūpam anubhāvayituṃ
          prabhavati/ śuktikāśakalasya samīhitatatsādhanayor anyatarabhāvābhāvāt/ nāpi
          rajatasmaraṇaṃ purovartini pravṛttikāraṇam/ tasyānubhavapāratantryatayānubhavadeśa eva
          pravartakatvāt/ nāpi bhedāgraho vyavahārakāraṇam/ grahaṇanibandhatvāc
          cetanavyavahārasya/
children.translated_text: Others do not accept that. In this [matter], surely every discerning person engages [in action] upon ascertaining either the desired [object] or its means. And the cognition of a piece of shell cannot make one experience [something] of its form to one who desires silver — because a piece of shell is neither the desired [object] nor its means. Nor is the recollection of silver the cause of activity toward what is in front — because, being dependent on [past] experience, it has its prompting capacity only at the place of [that] experience. Nor is the non-apprehension of difference the cause of conventional usage — because the conventional usage of conscious beings is grounded in apprehension.

children.text:
nanu na vayam ekaikasya kāraṇatvaṃ brūmahe yenaivam upālabhyemahi/ kiṃ tv
          agṛhītavivekasya jñānadvayasya prāptasamīcīnapuraḥsthitarajatajñānasārūpyasyety ayukto

children.translated_text: if [one argues] thus,

But we do not assert the causality of each one individually, such that we should be criticized in this way. Rather, [we assert the causality] of the pair of cognitions in which discrimination is not grasped, which has attained the similarity of correct perception-of-what-is-present — hence this criticism is unjust —

children.text:
tad apy ayuktam/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ tathā hi: samīcīnarajatāvabhāsasārūpyaṃ bhāsamānaṃ
          pravartakaṃ sattāmātreṇa vā/ ādye vikalpe bhedāgrahāparaparyāyasya sārūpyasya
          samīcīnasaṃnibhe ime jñāne iti viśeṣākāreṇa gṛhyamāṇasya pravṛttikāraṇatvaṃ kiṃ vānayor
          eva svarūpato viṣayataś ca mitho bhedāgraho vidyata iti sāmānyākāreṇa gṛhyamāṇasya
          sārūpyasya/ nādyaḥ/ samīcīnajñānavat tatsaṃnibhajñānasya
          taducitavyavahārapravartakatvānupapatteḥ/ na khalu gosaṃnibho gavaya ity avabhāso
          gavārthinaṃ gavaye pravartayati/ na dvitīyaḥ/ vyāhatatvāt/ na khalv anākalitabhedasyānayor
          iti anayor iti grahe bhedāgraha iti ca pratipattir bhavati/ ataḥ pariśeṣāt sattāmātreṇa
          bhedāgraharūpasya sārūpyasya vyavahārakāraṇatvam aṅgīkartavyam/ evam evāstv iti cet,
          tarhīdam iha saṃpradhāryam: kim ayaṃ bhedāgrahaḥ samāropotpādanakrameṇa vyavahārakāraṇam
          astūtānutpāditāropa eva svayam iti/ na ca dvitīyaḥ pakṣa eva śreyān/ tāvataiva
          vyavahārotpattāv āropasya gauravadoṣaduṣṭatvād iti mantavyam/ viśiṣṭavyavahārasya
          viśiṣṭajñānapūrvakatvaniyamenājñānapūrvakatvānupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: that too is unjust, because the alternatives do not hold. For thus: does the similarity to the appearance of real silver, as it appears, prompt [activity] by its mere existence, or [by something else]? In the first alternative: is it the similarity — which is synonymous with the non-grasping of difference — grasped through the specific form 'These two cognitions resemble the correct one' that is the cause of activity, or is it the similarity grasped through the general form 'There is simply a non-grasping of the mutual difference of these two, both in essential nature and in object'? Not the first — because, like correct cognition, the cognition that resembles it cannot prompt the conventional usage appropriate to that [correct cognition]. For the appearance 'A <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) resembles a cow' does not prompt one who desires a cow toward the <s>gavaya</s>. Nor the second — because it is self-contradictory. For one who has not discerned the difference, the cognition 'of these two' and the cognition 'non-grasping of difference' cannot [simultaneously] arise. Therefore, by elimination, it must be accepted that the similarity consisting in the non-grasping of difference causes the conventional usage by its mere existence. If [one says] 'Let it be so' — then this should be deliberated here: does this non-grasping of difference cause the conventional usage through the procedure of producing a superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>), or does it, without producing a superimposition, cause [it] by itself? Nor should it be thought that the second alternative alone is better — because, if the conventional usage arises from that much alone, the superimposition would be tainted by the fault of superfluity. [That is not right,] because of the rule that specific conventional usage requires specific cognition as its antecedent, [hence] it cannot be preceded by mere ignorance.

children.text:
nanv ayaṃ vyavahāro nājñānapūrvaka ity anākalitaparābhisaṃdhiḥ svasiddhāntasiddhārthād
          yadi kaścic chaṅketa sa prativaktavyaḥ/ śuktikāviṣayasya grahaṇasyāsamīhitaviṣayatvena
          rajatārthipravṛttihetutvāsaṃbhavād anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ rajatajñānasya samīhitaviṣayatvena
          pravṛttihetutvasaṃbhavāc cedamarthābhisaṃbhinnagrahaviviktasyāpi rajatasmaraṇasya
          kāraṇatvaṃ vaktavyam/ tac ca vaktuṃ na śakyate/ jānāti icchati tataḥ pravartata iti
          nyāyena jñānecchāpravṛttīnāṃ samānaviṣayatvena bhāvyam/ tathā
          cedaṃkārāspadābhimukhapravṛttasya rajatārthinas tadicchā nibandhanam/ anyathānyad icchann
          anyad vyavaharatīti vyāhanyeta/ tathā ca yadīdaṃkārāspadaṃ rajatāvabhāsagocaratāṃ nācaret
          kathaṃ rajatārthī tad icchet/ yady arajatatvāgrahaṇād iti brūyāt/ rajatatvāgrahāt kasmād
          ayaṃ nopekṣeteti/ yugapat tadbhavabhedāgrahābhedāgrahanibandhanābhyāṃ purataḥ pṛṣṭhataś
          cākṛṣyamāṇaḥ puruṣo dolāyamānatayā rūpyāropam antareṇopādānapakṣa eva na vyavasthāpyata
          ity anicchatāpy acchamatinā samāropaḥ samāśrayaṇīyaḥ/ yathāha: bhedāgrahād idaṃkārāspade
          rajatatvam āropya tajjātīyasyopakārahetubhāvam anusmṛtya tajjātīyatvenāsyāpi tad anumāya
          tadarthī pravartata iti prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ praśasyaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, [if anyone says] 'This conventional usage is not preceded by ignorance' — if some person, not perceiving the opponent's intention, doubts [this] regarding what is established by one's own <s>siddhānta</s>, he should be answered [thus]: Since the apprehension pertaining to the shell, being of an undesired object, cannot be the cause of the activity of one who desires silver — as established through positive and negative concomitance — and since the cognition of silver, being of a desired object, can be the cause of activity, the causality of the recollection of silver — even when separated from the apprehension conjoined with the 'this'-meaning — must be stated. And that cannot be stated. Because, by the principle 'one knows, desires, and then acts,' knowledge, desire, and activity must have the same object. And thus, for one who desires silver and acts toward the substrate of the 'this'-reference, desire for that [substrate] is the basis; otherwise, it would be contradicted that one desires one thing and acts toward another. And thus, if the substrate of the 'this'-reference did not enter the domain of the silver-appearance, how would one who desires silver desire it? If [one says] 'Because of not grasping its non-silver-nature' — then why would he not be indifferent [to it], because of not grasping its silver-nature? Being pulled simultaneously from front and back by the grounds of non-grasping of its being-that and non-grasping of its difference — the person, swaying like a swing, cannot be established on the position of [mere] mention (<s>upadāna</s>) without [the position of] the superimposition of silver. Therefore, superimposition must be resorted to, even unwillingly, by one of clear intellect. As he says: 'From the non-grasping of difference, having superimposed silver-hood on the substrate of the "this"-reference, and remembering the beneficial nature of things of that class, and inferring that this too, being of that class, [is beneficial] — one who desires that acts [toward it]' — the first position is commendable.

children.text:
na ca taṭastharajatasmaraṇapakṣe ’pi hetor gṛhītatvenāyaṃ mārgaḥ samāna iti vācyam/
          rajatatvasya hetoḥ pakṣadharmatvābhāvāt/ na ca pakṣadharmatāyā abhāve ’pi vyāptibalād
          gamakatvaṃ śaṅkyam/ vyāptipakṣadharmatāvalliṅgasyaiva gamakatvāṅgīkārāt/ tad āhuḥ
          śabarasvāminaḥ: jñātasaṃbandhasyaiva puṃso liṅgaviśiṣṭadharmyekadeśadarśanāl
          liṅgiviśiṣṭadharmyekadeśabuddhir anumānam iti/ ācāryo ’pi avocat :
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that even in the position of remembering silver at a distance, this path is the same because the reason is grasped. Because the reason — silverness — lacks the property of belonging to the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>). And one should not suspect that even in the absence of the property of belonging to the subject, there is inferential capacity through the force of invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) — because only a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that possesses both concomitance and the property of belonging to the subject is accepted as an instrument of inference. Thus <s>Śabarasvāmin</s> stated: "Inference is the cognition of the subject as qualified by the inferable property, arising from the perception of a part of the subject qualified by the logical mark, for a person whose knowledge of the relation [between mark and inferable property] is established." The master (<s>ācārya</s>) also stated:

children.text: sa eṣa cobhayātmā yo gamye gamaka iṣyate/
children.translated_text: "That [logical mark] is indeed of a twofold nature — it is accepted as both the inferred and the indicator;
with one part unestablished, it does not indicate, because of the non-establishment of the inferred." Thus.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu bhavatpakṣe ’pi puraḥsthitasyedamarthasya paramārthato rajatatvaṃ nāstīti na
          rajatatvaṃ dharmyekadeśa iti cen na/
children.translated_text: Objection: "In your position too, since silverness does not really exist in the object present before one, silverness is not a part of the subject" — if so, no;

children.text:
yakṣānurūpo balir iti nyāyenānumityābhāsānuguṇasyaikadeśasya vidyamānatvāt/ tathā ca
          prayogaḥ:
children.translated_text: because by the maxim "the offering should befit the deity," a part [of the subject] conforming to the semblance of inference does exist. And thus the formulation [of the inference]:
"The silver-cognition that is the subject of dispute has [something] present before one as its object,
because it invariably prompts one who desires silver to act toward that [present object].

children.text: yad uktasādhanaṃ tad uktasādhyaṃ yathobhayavādisaṃmataṃ satyarajatajñānam/
children.translated_text: Whatever possesses the stated means of proof possesses the stated property to be proved — like a cognition of real silver, accepted by both disputants."
"The shell-fragment that is the subject of dispute is the object of silver-cognition,
because it is the object of the activity of one who desires silver through the intermediary [of that cognition], or because it is expressible by a word co-referential with the word 'silver' —
like real silver."
reference marker

children.text:
yad uktaṃ rajatajñānasya śuktikālambanatve ’nubhavavirodha iti tad apy ayuktam/
          vikalpāsahatvāt/ tathā hi: tatra kiṃ rajatākārapratītiṃ prati śukter ālambanatve
          ’nubhavavirodha udbhāvyata idamaṃśasya vā/ nādyaḥ/ anaṅgīkāraparāhatatvāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/
          idaṃtāniyatadeśādhikaraṇasya cākacakyaviśiṣṭasya vastuno rajatajñānālambanatvam
          anavalambamānasya bhavata evānubhavavirodhāt/ idaṃ rajatam iti sāmānādhikaraṇyena
          purovartiny aṅgulinirdeśapūrvakam upādānādivyavahāradarśanāc ca/
children.translated_text: As for the statement that if silver-cognition has the shell as its object, there is a conflict with experience — that too is unjustified. Because it cannot withstand analysis. For: therein, is the conflict with experience raised regarding the shell being the object of the cognition in the form of silver, or regarding the 'this'-part? Not the first — because it is defeated by non-acceptance [of the premise]. Not the second — because for you yourself, who do not accept the shell-fragment — a real thing qualified by glitter and situated in a location determined by 'this'-ness — as the object of silver-cognition, there is a conflict with experience. And because the transactional behavior of referring to what is present before one with a finger-pointing preceded by 'this is silver,' in co-referential usage, is observed.
reference marker

children.text:
yac coktam : doṣāṇām autsargikakāryaprasavaśaktipratibandhakatayā viparītakāritvaṃ
          nāstīti/ tad apy ayuktam/ dāvadagdhavetrabījādau tathā darśanāt/ na ca dagdhasya
          vetrabījatvaṃ nāstīti mantavyam/ śyāmasya ghaṭasya raktatāmātreṇa
          ghaṭatvanivṛttiprasaṅgāt/
children.translated_text: And as for the statement that defects (<s>doṣas</s>) do not produce contrary effects because they obstruct the power of the natural effect-production — that too is unjustified. Because this is observed in the case of forest-burned bamboo seeds and the like. And one should not think that the burned [seed] does not have the nature of a bamboo seed — because there would be the consequence that merely by [a pot] becoming red, the pot-ness of a dark-colored pot would cease.

children.text:
nanu ghaṭo ’yam ity anuvṛttayoḥ pratyayaprayogayoḥ sadbhāvād ghaṭatvasya sadbhāva iti
          cen
children.translated_text: Objection: "Because the cognition 'this is a pot' and its usage persist, pot-ness exists" — if so,

children.text:
na/ atrāpīdaṃ vetrabījam iti tayoḥ samānatvāt/ tathā bhasmakadoṣadūṣitasya jāṭharāgner
          bahvannapacanasāmarthyaṃ dṛśyate/ na ca bahvannapacanasāmartyaṃ jāṭharasyaiva jātavedaso
          na bhasmakavyādher iti vaktuṃ yuktam/ tasya mandam alpapacanasāmarthye ’pi sahasā
          mahatpacanasya bhasmakavyādhisāhāyakam antareṇānupapatteḥ/ anyathā sarveṣāṃ tathāpatteḥ/

kiṃ ca jñānānāṃ yathārthavyavahārakāraṇatve ’pi doṣavaśād
          ayathārthavyavahārakāraṇatvam aṅgīkurvāṇo bhavān eva paryanuyojyo bhavati/ tad uktaṃ
          bhāṣye: yaś cobhayoḥ samāno doṣo dyotate tatra kaś codyo bhavatīti/ atrāpy uktam:
children.translated_text: Moreover, you yourself — who, while accepting that cognitions are causes of veridical behavior, also accept that through the force of defects they become causes of non-veridical behavior — you yourself are the one who should be questioned. As stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: "And whatever fault appears equally in both [positions], what objection can be raised there?" Here too it has been said:

no — because here too, the cognition and usage 'this is a bamboo seed' are equally [present]. Similarly, the digestive fire vitiated by the disease <s>bhasmaka</s> is observed to have the capacity to digest a great quantity of food. And it is not proper to say that the capacity to digest much food belongs to the digestive fire alone and not to the <s>bhasmaka</s> disease — because for something that is naturally feeble and has only the capacity to digest small quantities, the sudden digestion of large quantities without the assistance of the <s>bhasmaka</s> disease is impossible. Otherwise, everyone would have such [capacity].
reference marker

children.text: yaś cobhayoḥ samo doṣaḥ parihāro ’pi va samaḥ/
children.translated_text: "And whatever fault is equal in both, the resolution too is equal;
neither [party] alone should be questioned in such an investigation of the matter." Thus.

children.text:
tathāpi māmakasyānumānasya kiṃ dūṣaṇaṃ dattam āsīt/ yady anumānadūṣaṇaṃ vinā na
          parituṣyati hanta kālātyayāpadiṣṭatā/ kṛṣṇavartmānuṣṇatvānumānavat/ etāvantaṃ kālaṃ yad
          idaṃ rajatam ity abhād asau śuktir iti pratyakṣeṇa prācīnapratyayasyāyathārthatvaṃ
          pravedayatā yathārthatvānumānasyāpahṛtaviṣayatvād bādhyatvasaṃbhavāt/
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, what refutation has been given against my inference? If [the opponent] is not satisfied without a refutation of the inference — well then, [my inference is vitiated by] supersession by a later cognition (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭatā</s>). Like the inference that fire is not hot. For the perception 'this shell' — which announces the non-veridicality of the prior cognition 'this is silver' which had persisted for that long — [demonstrates that] the inference of veridicality has its subject-matter overridden, hence it is possible for it to be sublated.
reference marker

children.text:
yac coktaṃ svagocaravyabhicāre sarvānāśvāsaprasaṅga iti/ tad asāmpratam/ saṃvidāṃ kvacit
          saṃvādivyavahārajanakatve ’pi na sarvatra tacchaṅkayā pravṛttyuccheda iti yathā tāvake
          mate tathā māmake ’py asau panthā na vārita iti samānayogakṣematvāt/ tautātitamatam
          avalambya vidhivivekaṃ vyākurvāṇair ācāryavācaspatimiśrair bodhakatvena svataḥ prāmāṇyaṃ
          nāvyabhicāreṇeti nyāyakaṇikāyāṃ pratyapādi/ tasmād aviśvāsaśaṅkānavakāśaṃ labhate/
children.translated_text: And as for the statement that if [cognition] deviates with respect to its own domain, there would be the consequence of universal untrustworthiness — that is improper. Just as in your position, even though cognitions sometimes produce concordant behavior, one does not cease from activity everywhere out of suspicion of that [deviance] — so too in my position that path is not blocked, since the predicament is equal. Relying on the position of <s>Tautātita</s> [another name for <s>Prabhākara</s>], the master <s>Vācaspatimiśra</s>, while elucidating the discrimination of injunctions, demonstrated in the <s>Nyāyakaṇikā</s> that intrinsic validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>) [is established] through indicative capacity, not through non-deviation. Therefore, the suspicion of untrustworthiness finds no occasion.
reference marker

children.text: nanu mādhyamikamatāvalambanena rajatādivibhramālambanam asad iti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: "By adopting the <s>Mādhyamika</s> position, the object of illusions such as silver and the like is non-existent" — if so,
— because what is non-existent is incapable of appearing as immediately present. And because activity prompted by the desire to obtain it would be impossible.
that is unjustified

children.text:
nanu vijñānam eva vāsanādisvakāraṇasāmarthyāsāditadṛṣṭāntasiddhasvabhāvaviśeṣam
          asatprakāśanasamarthanam upajātam/ asatprakāśanaśaktir avidyā saṃvṛtir iti paryāyāḥ/
          tasmād avidyāvaśād asanto bhāntīti cet
children.translated_text: Objection: "Consciousness itself, having arisen with a particular nature established by proven examples, produced by the power of its own causes such as latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) and the like, is capable of manifesting the non-existent. The power of manifesting the non-existent is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), also called <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional [truth]) — these are synonyms. Therefore, through the force of <s>avidyā</s>, non-existent things appear" — if so,

children.text: tad api vaktum aśakyam/ śakyasya durnirūpyatvāt/
children.translated_text: that too cannot be maintained. Because what is [supposedly] capable is impossible to define.

children.text:
kim atra śakyaṃ kāryaṃ jñāpyaṃ vā/ nādyaḥ/ asataḥ kāraṇatvānupapatteḥ/ na dvitīyaḥ/
          śakyasya kāraṇatvenāṅgīkṛtatvāt/ jñānād anyasya jñānasyānupalabdheś ca/ upalabdhau vā
          tasyāpi jñāpyatvena jñāpakāntarāpekṣāyām anavasthāpatteś ca/
children.translated_text: What is this capable [entity] here — a cause or something to be made known? Not the first — because causation by a non-existent is impossible. Not the second — because the capable [entity] has been accepted as a cause. And because no cognition other than cognition is apprehended. Or if it is apprehended, since that too would require another indicator to make it known, as requiring another indicator, there would be an infinite regress.

children.text:
athaitaddoṣaparijihīṣayā vijñānaṃ sadrūpam evāsataḥ prakāśakam iti pakṣīkriyata iti
          cet
children.translated_text: If, with the desire to avoid this fault, the position is adopted that consciousness, which is of the nature of the real, is the manifester of the non-existent — if so,

children.text:
atra devānāṃpriyaḥ praṣṭavyaḥ punaḥ/ asau sadasatoḥ saṃbandho nirūpyanirūpakabhāvo
          ’vinābhāvo vā/ nādyaḥ/ asata upakārādhāratvāyogenānupakṛtatayā nirūpyatvānupapatteḥ/ na
          caramaḥ/ dhūmadhūmadhvajayor iva tadutpattilakṣaṇasya śiṃśapāvṛkṣayor iva
          tādātmyalakṣaṇasya vā avinābhāvanidānasya sadasator asaṃbhavāt/ tasmād vijñānam
          evāsatprakāśakam ity asadvādinām ayam asatpralāpa ity āropyamāṇaṃ nāsat/
children.translated_text: here the dear fellow should be asked again: is that relation between the existent and the non-existent one of determinandum-determinans (<s>nirūpyanirūpakabhāva</s>) or invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>)? Not the first — because since the non-existent cannot serve as a substrate of benefit, and thus not being benefited, its being a determinandum is impossible. Not the last — because the ground of invariable concomitance — whether it be origination (as between smoke and fire) or identity (as between <s>śiṃśapā</s> [a type of tree] and tree) — is impossible between the existent and the non-existent. Therefore, the statement of those who hold that the non-existent [exists] — that "consciousness alone manifests the non-existent" — is idle prattle of proponents of non-existence. What is being superimposed is not non-existent.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu vijñānavādinayānusāreṇa pratīyamānaṃ rajataṃ jñānātmakam/ tatra ca yuktir
          abhidhīyate: yad yathānubhūyate tat tathā/ anyathātvaṃ tu balavadbādhakopanipātād
          āsthīyata ity ubhayavādisaṃmato ’rthaḥ/ tatra ca nedaṃ rajatam iti niṣiddhedaṃbhāvaṃ
          rajatam arthād āntarajñānarūpam avatiṣṭhate/ na cedaṃtayā niṣedhe saty anidaṃtayā ca bahir
          api vyavasthopapatteḥ kutaḥ saṃvidākārateti vācyam/ vyavahitasyāparokṣatvānupapattāv
          aparokṣasya vijñānasya kakṣīkartavyatvāt/ tathā ca prayogaḥ:
children.translated_text: Objection: "Following the approach of the <s>Vijñānavāda</s> (Consciousness-only school), the silver that is perceived is of the nature of cognition. And the reasoning [is] stated thus: whatever is experienced in a certain way, that is [in fact] so. Its being otherwise is accepted only upon the intervention of a stronger sublating [cognition] — this is a meaning accepted by both disputants. And therein, when [the sublating cognition] 'this is not silver' negates its 'this'-ness, the silver, by implication, remains as [something] of the nature of internal cognition. And it should not be said: 'When the this-ness is negated, since the non-this-ness establishes [the silver's] externality as well, why [call it] a form of consciousness?' — because what is separated [from the perceiver] cannot be immediately present, and [therefore] immediately present consciousness must be accepted. And thus the formulation:
"The subject of dispute is a form of consciousness,
because of being immediately present without sense-contact,
like consciousness [itself]." Thus.

children.text:
tad anupapannam/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ bādhako ’vabodhaḥ kiṃ sākṣāj jñānākāratāṃ bodhayaty
          arthād vā/ nādyaḥ/ nedaṃ rajatam iti pratyayasya rajatavivekamātragocarasya
          jñānābhedagocaratāyām anubhavavirodhāt/ nedaṃ rajatam iti rajatasya purovartitvapratiṣedho
          jñānākāratāṃ kalpayatīti cet — tad etad vārtam/ prasaktapratiṣedhātmano bādhakāvabodhasya
          tatraiva sattvāt pratiṣedhopapatteḥ/ vijñānākāratvasādhanam apy avijñānākāre bahiṣṭhe
          sākṣipratyakṣe bhāvarūpājñāne vartata iti savyabhicāraḥ/
children.translated_text: That is untenable — because it cannot withstand analysis. Does the sublating cognition directly reveal the nature of being a form of cognition, or by implication? Not the first — because there would be a conflict with experience, since the cognition 'this is not silver' has as its scope only the discrimination from silver, and [ascribing to it] the scope of non-difference from cognition [would conflict with experience]. If it is said that 'this is not silver' — the negation of the silver's being in front — posits [its] being a form of cognition — that is mere talk. Because the sublating cognition, whose nature is the negation of what is being attributed, exists precisely there [in the domain of attribution], and thus negation is justified. And the proof of being a form of consciousness also falls on positive ignorance (<s>bhāvarūpājñāna</s>), which is external and established by witness-consciousness (<s>sākṣipratyakṣa</s>), and which is not a form of consciousness — hence [the proof] is inconclusive (<s>savyabhicāra</s>).
reference marker

children.text:
nanv anyathākhyātivādimatānusāreṇa rajatasya deśāntarasattvena bhāvyam/ anyathā tasya
          pratiṣedhapratiyogitvānupapatteḥ/ na hi kaścit prekṣāvāñ śaśaviṣāṇaṃ pratiṣeddhuṃ
          prabhavati/ tad uktam :
children.translated_text: Objection: "Following the <s>Anyathākhyāti</s> (theory of erroneous cognition as cognition-of-something-elsewhere), the silver must exist in another place. Otherwise, its being the counter-positive of the negation is impossible. For no discerning person is capable of negating a hare's horn. As stated:
'The qualification of the qualificand is indeed positive, consisting of the absence of absence;
the counter-positiveness of a [real] entity is [its] being of the nature of the absence of absence.' Thus.

children.text: tathā ca tasya deśāntarasattvam āśrayaṇīyam iti cet
children.translated_text: And therefore, the existence of that [silver] in another place must be resorted to" — if so,

children.text:
tad api na pramāṇapaddhatim adhyāste/ asataḥ saṃsargasyeva kaladhautasya
          niṣedhapratiyogitvopapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: that too does not tread the path of valid cognition. Because the counter-positiveness of negation is possible even for a non-existent connection, just as for gold [in the shell].
reference marker

children.text:
nanv idaṃ rajatam iti jñānam ekam anekaṃ vā/ na tāvad ādyaḥ/ apasiddhāntāpatter
          asaṃbhavāc ca/ tathā hi/ śuktīdamaṃśendriyasaṃprayogād idamākārāntaḥkaraṇa

pariṇāmarūpam ekaṃ jñānaṃ jāyate/ na ca tatra kaladhautaṃ viṣayabhāvam ākalpayitum
          utsahate/ asaṃprayuktatvāt tasya/ viṣayatvāṅgīkāre sarvajñatvāpatteḥ/ na ca
          cakṣuranvayavyatirekānuvidhāyitayā tajjñānasya tajjanyatvaṃ vācyam/ idamaṃśajñānotpattau
          tadupakṣayopapatteḥ/ na cāpi saṃskārād rajatajñānasya janma/ smṛtitvāpatteḥ/
          athendriyadoṣasya tatkaraṇatvam/ tad apy ayuktam/ svātantryeṇa tasya
          jñānahetutvānupapatteḥ/ na hi grahaṇasmaraṇābhyām anyaḥ prakāraḥ samasti/ tasmād
          idamaṃśarajatatādātmyaviṣayam ekaṃ vijñānaṃ na ghaṭate/ nāpy anekam akhyātimatāpatter iti
          cet —
children.translated_text: modification having the 'this'-form arises. And in that [cognition], one cannot venture to attribute the status of object to silver — because it is not in sense-contact [with the senses]. Because if its objecthood were accepted, there would be the consequence of omniscience. And one should not say that the cognition of silver is produced by it on the ground that it follows the presence and absence of the eye — because its subservience in the production of the 'this'-part cognition is justified. Nor is the silver-cognition born from latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — because there would be the consequence of its being memory. If the sense-organ's defect is its cause — that too is unjustified, because the defect cannot independently be the cause of cognition. For there is no mode [of cognition] other than apprehension and remembering. Therefore, a single cognition having as its object the identity of the 'this'-part and silver is not possible. Nor is [the cognition] multiple — because there would be the consequence of [falling into] the <s>Akhyāti</s> (non-apprehension) doctrine" — if so,

Objection: "Is the cognition 'this is silver' one or many? Not the first — because there would be the fallacy of contradicting one's own doctrine, and because [a single cognition] is impossible. For: from the sense-contact of the shell with the 'this'-part, a single cognition in the form of an internal organ
reference marker

children.text:
ucyate/ prathamaṃ doṣakaluṣitena cakṣuṣedaṃtāmātraviṣayāntaḥkaraṇavṛttir utpadyate/
          anantaraṃ tayā vṛttyā caitanyāvaraṇābhibhave sati tac caitanyam abhivyajyate/ paścād
          idamaṃśacaitanyaniṣṭhā avidyā rāgādidoṣakaluṣitā kaladhautākāreṇa pariṇamate/
          idamākārāntaḥkaraṇapariṇāmāvacchinnacaitanyaniṣṭhā kaladhautagocarapariṇāmasaṃskārasacivā
          kaladhautajñānābhāsākāreṇa pariṇamate/ tau ca rajatavṛttipariṇāmau svādhiṣṭhānena
          sākṣicaitanyenāvyavadhānena bhāsyete/ tathā ca savṛttikāyā avidyāyāḥ
          sākṣibhāsyatvābhyupagame vṛttyantaravedyatvābhāvān nānavasthā/ yady apy antaḥkaraṇavṛttir
          avidyāvṛttiś ceti dve ime jñāne tathāpi viṣayādhīnaṃ phalam/ jñāto ghaṭa iti
          viṣayāvacchinnatayā phalapratīteḥ[/] tadviṣayaś ca satyamithyābhūtayor
          idamaṃśarajatāṃśayor anyonyātmakatayaikatvam āpannaḥ/ tasmād viṣayāvacchinnaphalasyāpy
          ekatvāj jñānaikyam upacaryate/ tad uktam:
children.translated_text: It is explained: first, a mental modification (<s>antaḥkaraṇavṛtti</s>) whose object is mere 'this-ness' is produced by the eye vitiated by defects. Next, when the obstruction covering consciousness is overcome by that modification, that consciousness is manifested. Afterwards, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which resides in the consciousness associated with the 'this'-aspect, vitiated by defects such as attachment and the like, transforms in the form of silver (<s>kaladhautākāra</s>). [That avidyā], which resides in the consciousness delimited by the mental modification in the form of 'this,' accompanied by the latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the transformation pertaining to silver, transforms in the form of the semblance of silver-knowledge. And those two transformations in the form of silver-cognition are illuminated without mediation by the witness-consciousness (<s>sākṣicaitanya</s>) that is their substratum. And thus, when the <s>avidyā</s> together with its modification is accepted as illuminated by the witness, since there is no need for it to be known by another modification, there is no infinite regress. Although there are two cognitions -- the mental modification and the <s>avidyā</s>-modification -- nevertheless the fruit depends on the object. Because the fruit is experienced as delimited by the object, as in 'the pot is known.' And the object of those two -- the 'this'-aspect and the silver-aspect, which are real and false respectively -- having attained unity through being of each other's nature. Therefore, since the fruit delimited by the object is also one, the unity of cognition is figuratively spoken of. Thus stated:
reference marker
<s>Avidyā</s> residing in the consciousness of the 'this'-aspect of the nacre expands
accompanied by the latent impressions of defects such as attachment, in the form of silver.
Likewise, [avidyā] residing in the consciousness released by the modification in the form of 'this,'
that [avidyā] also transforms as the semblance of silver-cognition.
Due to the unity of the real and the false [aspects], the object of those [two] is considered one;
due to the unity of the fruit dependent on that, the unity of cognition is figuratively spoken of.
reference marker

children.text:
pañcapādikāyām api phalaikyāj jñānaikyam upacaryata ity abhiprāyeṇa “sā caikam eva jñānam
          ekaphalaṃ janayati” ity uktam/
children.translated_text: In the <s>Pañcapādikā</s> too, with the intent that 'the unity of cognition is figuratively spoken of from the unity of the fruit,' it was stated: 'and that produces a single cognition having a single fruit.'
reference marker

children.text:
nanu śuktikāmastake bhāvyamānasya kaladhautasya tatraiva satyatvābhyupagame nedaṃ rajatam
          iti niṣedhaḥ kathaṃ prabhaved iti cen na/ prātibhāsikasatyatve ’pi
          vyāvahārikasatyatvābhāvena pratipannopādhau pratiyogitvasaṃbhavāt/ tad uktaṃ
          pañcapādikāvivaraṇe: trividhaṃ sattvam/ paramārthasattvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ/ arthakriyāsāmarthyaṃ
          sattvaṃ māyopādhikam ākāśādeḥ/ avidyopādhikaṃ sattvaṃ rajatāder iti/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'If the silver imagined on the surface of the nacre is accepted as real there, how could the negation "this is not silver" be possible?' -- Not so! Because even though there is <s>prātibhāsika</s> (phenomenal/illusory) reality, since there is an absence of <s>vyāvahārika</s> (conventional/empirical) reality, counter-correlate-hood in the apprehended limiting adjunct is possible. Thus stated in the <s>Pañcapādikāvivaraṇa</s>: 'Reality is threefold. The reality of <s>Brahman</s> is absolute reality (<s>pāramārthasattva</s>). The reality of space and the like, conditioned by <s>māyā</s>, is the reality [consisting in] the capacity for causal efficacy. The reality of silver and the like, conditioned by <s>avidyā</s>, is [illusory reality].'
reference marker
Elsewhere too it is stated:
In the three times, at the time of the knower, and at the time of cognition,
from the absence of sublation, the threefold reality of entities is accepted.
The reality of <s>Brahman</s> is ultimate (<s>tāttvika</s>); that of space and the like is conventional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>);
that of silver and the like is accepted as phenomenal (<s>prātibhāsika</s>).
That which is sublated by a worldly means of knowledge at a worldly moment of sublation --

children.text: tat prātibhāsikaṃ sattvaṃ bādhyaṃ saty eva mātari//
children.translated_text: that is phenomenal reality, sublated even while the cause (<s>mātṛ</s>) persists.
That which is sublated by a Vedic means of knowledge at a Vedic moment of sublation --

children.text: tad vyāvahārikaṃ sattvaṃ bādhyaṃ mātrā sahaiva tat// iti ca/
children.translated_text: that is conventional reality; it is sublated together with the cause itself.
reference marker

children.text:
tataḥ khyātibādhānyathānupapattyā bhrāntigocarasya māyāmayasya rajatādeḥ
          sadasadvilakṣaṇatvalakṣaṇam anirvacanīyatvaṃ siddham/ tad

children.translated_text: Thus stated the teacher <s>Citsukha</s>:

Therefore, from the impossibility of otherwise accounting for the appearance (<s>khyāti</s>), the sublation, and [the cognition] 'otherwise' -- the indeterminability (<s>anirvacanīyatva</s>), characterized as being different from both real and unreal, of the object of error such as silver and the like, which is constituted by <s>māyā</s>, is established.
That which, individually, does not enter the path of inquiry through [the categories of] existence and non-existence --

children.text: gāhate tad anirvācyam āhur vedāntavādinaḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: the <s>Vedāntins</s> declare that to be indeterminable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>).
reference marker

children.text:
nanu māyāvidyayoḥ svāśrayavyāmohahetutvatadabhāvābhyāṃ bhedasya jāgarūkatvenāvidyāmayatve
          vaktavye māyāmayatvoktir āropyasyāyukteti cet —
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Since <s>māyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> differ in that [<s>avidyā</s>] causes delusion of its own substratum while [<s>māyā</s>] does not, and since the superimposed [silver] is constituted by <s>avidyā</s> [not <s>māyā</s>], the statement that it is constituted by <s>māyā</s> is inappropriate for the superimposed [object].' --

children.text:
tad ayuktam/ anirvacanīyatvatattvābhāsapratibandhakatvādilakṣaṇajātasya māyāvidyayoḥ
          samānatvāt/ kiṃ cāśrayaśabdena draṣṭocyate kartā vā/ nādyaḥ/
          mantrauṣadhādinimittamāyādarśinas tasya vyāmohadarśanāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/ viṣṇoḥ
          svāśritamāyayaiva rāmāvatāre mohitatvena tatra māyāvitvasyāprayojakatvāt/
          bādhaniścayamantrādipratīkārabodhayor eva prayojakatvāt/ aparathā paṅgvandhavat kartāpi
          vyāmuhyeta/ na cecchānuvidhānānanuvidhānābhyāṃ tayor bheda iti bhaṇitavyam/ māyāsthale
          maṇimantrauṣadhādiprayogavad avidyāsthale ’pi
          dvicandrakeśoṇḍrakādivibhramanimittāṅgulyavaṣṭambhādāv api svātantryopalambhāt/ ata eva
          tatra tatra śrutismṛtibhāṣyādiṣu māyāvidyayor abhedena vyavahāraḥ saṃgacchate/ kvacid
          vikṣepaprādhānyenāvaraṇaprādhānyena ca māyāvidyayor bhede tadvyavahāro na virudhyate/ tad
          uktam :
children.translated_text: That is not correct. Because <s>māyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> share the same class of characteristics -- such as indeterminability, being an obstruction to the appearance of reality, and the like. Moreover, does the word 'substratum' (<s>āśraya</s>) mean the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) or the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>)? Not the first -- because the seer of <s>māyā</s> produced by the cause of <s>mantras</s>, herbs, and the like is also observed to be deluded. Not the second -- because <s>Viṣṇu</s>, being deluded by His own <s>māyā</s> in the <s>Rāma</s> incarnation, [shows that] being a <s>māyāvin</s> (wielder of <s>māyā</s>) is not the cause [of delusion]; rather, the absence of sublation-knowledge and of means of counteraction such as <s>mantras</s> is the cause. Otherwise, like a lame blind person, even the agent would be deluded. Nor should it be said that the difference between those two is through conformity and non-conformity to will -- because in the case of <s>avidyā</s> too, as in the case of <s>māyā</s> with the use of gems, <s>mantras</s>, herbs, and the like, independence is observed even in the support of the finger and the like in the case of the error of double moon, hair-like floaters, and the like. Therefore, the usage of <s>māyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> as non-different in various <s>Śrutis</s>, <s>Smṛtis</s>, commentaries, and the like is consistent. Somewhere, the difference between <s>māyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> -- with the predominance of projection (<s>vikṣepa</s>) and the predominance of concealment (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) respectively -- does not contradict that usage. Thus stated:
reference marker
<s>Māyā</s> projects, or is under the control of the Lord's will;
<s>Avidyā</s> conceals reality, or follows independently.
reference marker

children.text: nanv avidyāsadbhāve kiṃ pramāṇam/ aham ajño mām anyaṃ ca na jānāmīti

children.translated_text: itself --

children.text:
pratibhāsa eva/ nanu jñānābhāvaviṣayo ’yaṃ
          nābhipretam arthaṃ gamayatīti cet — na tāvad anupalabdhivādinaś codyam etat/
          parokṣapratibhāsahetutvāt tasyāḥ/ ayam api parokṣapratibhāsa eveti cet — na tāval
          liṅgaśabdānupapadyamānārthajanyaḥ/ jñātakaraṇatvāt teṣām/ na caitat sāmagrīkāle jñānam
          asti/ anubhūyate vā/ anupalabdhyā janyata iti cet — na tāvad iyam ajñātā karaṇam/
          pratyakṣetarasya jñātakaraṇatvaniyamāt/ nāpi jñātaiva karaṇam/ anupalabdhyanavasthānāt/ na
          ca yathā pareṣām abhāvagrahaṇe yogyānupalabdhiḥ sahakāriṇī tathā naḥ karaṇam iti śaṅkyam/
          jñānakaraṇa iva sahakāriṇi jñātatvaniyamābhāvāt/ astu vā tathā jñeyābhāvagrahaṇe karaṇam/
          jñānābhāvagrahaṇe karaṇaṃ na bhavaty eveti vakṣyate/
children.translated_text: the very appearance 'I am ignorant; I do not know myself or anything else.' Objection: 'This has the absence of knowledge as its object and does not convey the intended meaning' -- this objection does not come from the proponent of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhivādin</s>), because non-apprehension is the cause of indirect appearance. Objection: 'This too is an indirect appearance' -- not so, because it is not produced by an object unattainable through inferential mark, word, and the like, since those [means] have cognized instruments. Nor does this cognition exist at the time of the causal aggregate, nor is it experienced. Objection: 'It is produced by non-apprehension' -- not so, because non-apprehension is not an uncognized instrument, since there is the rule that what is other than perception has a cognized instrument. Nor is it a cognized instrument, because of the infinite regress of non-apprehension. Nor should it be suspected that non-apprehension is an instrument for us in the way that for others, qualified non-apprehension is an auxiliary in the apprehension of absence -- because there is no rule that an auxiliary, like a causal instrument of knowledge, must be cognized. Or alternatively, let it be the instrument for the apprehension of the absence of the knowable; it will be stated that it cannot be the instrument for the apprehension of the absence of knowledge.
Objection: 'What is the proof for the existence of <s>avidyā</s>?' The direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>)
reference marker

children.text:
pratyakṣābhāvavāde tu pratyakṣeṇa tāvad dharmipratiyogijñānayoḥ sator ātmani
          jñānamātrābhāvagrahaṇaṃ na brūyāt/ ghaṭavati bhūtale ghaṭābhāvasyeva jñānamātrābhāvasya
          grahītum aśakyatvāt/ tayor asatos tu sutarām/ kāraṇābhāvāt/ ato ’pi yogyānupalabdhyā vā
          phalaliṅgādyabhāvena vātmani jñānamātrābhāvagrahaṇaṃ durlabham iti paramate ’py ayaṃ
          nyāyaḥ samānaḥ/ tad evam ātmani pratyakṣeṇa vānyena vā jñānamātrābhāvasya grahaṇam aśakyam
          iti sthitam/
children.translated_text: In the doctrine of perception-of-absence, however, one should not say that the mere absence of knowledge in the self is apprehended by perception when the cognitions of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) and the counter-correlate are present -- because, just as on a ground that contains a pot, the absence of the pot cannot be apprehended, so too the mere absence of knowledge cannot be apprehended. And all the more so when those [cognitions] are absent -- because of the absence of a cause. Moreover, by this reasoning, even in the opposing view, the apprehension of the mere absence of knowledge in the self is difficult to obtain through qualified non-apprehension or through the absence of inferential marks and the like.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu jñānaviśeṣābhāvaḥ pratyakṣeṇa gṛhyatām/ na tāvat smaraṇābhāvaḥ/ abhāvagrahaṇe
          pratiyogismaraṇasya kāraṇatvāt/ nāpy anubhavābhāvaḥ/ tasyāvarjanīyatvāt/ nanv ātmani
          ghaṭānubhavābhāvaḥ pratyakṣaviṣayas tarhy aham ajña iti jñānasāmānyavacano jānātir
          jñānaviśeṣe ’nubhave lakṣaṇayā vartanīyaḥ/ lakṣaṇā ca saṃbandhe ’nupapattau ca satyāṃ
          vartate/ saṃbandhas tāvad anubhavatvajñānatvayor ekavyaktisamāveśo vyāpyavyāpakabhāvo vā
          vidyata eva/ anupapattiṃ tu na paśyāmaḥ/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Let the absence of a particular knowledge be apprehended by perception.' Not the absence of memory -- because memory of the counter-correlate is a cause in the apprehension of absence. Nor the absence of experience -- because that is unavoidable. Objection: 'If the absence of the experience of a pot in the self is the object of perception, then the verb "to know" (<s>jānāti</s>) in "I am ignorant" (<s>aham ajñaḥ</s>), which denotes knowledge in general, should be taken figuratively (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) as referring to the particular knowledge that is experience.' And figurative usage operates when there is a relation and an impossibility [of the primary meaning]. The relation -- the co-occurrence in a single instance of experience-hood and knowledge-hood, or the pervaded-pervader relation -- certainly exists. But we do not see the impossibility [of the primary meaning].

children.text: nanv anubhavābhāve pratyakṣasya prameyalābhas tenaiva tasyārthavattā sidhyati/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'In the absence of experience, perception obtains its object (<s>prameya</s>); thereby its purposefulness is established.'
True. But this is the purpose, not the impossibility [of the primary meaning] -- because of mutual dependence.

children.text:
nanv aham ajña ity atra nañ ātmani jñānamātrābhāvaṃ na brūte/ jñānavati tasmiṃs
          tadabhāvāt/ nāpy anubhavābhāvam/ jñānoktes tadanabhidhāyakatvāt/ nairarthakyaṃ ca na
          yuktam ity anayaivānupapattyā lakṣaṇeti cet —
children.translated_text: Objection: 'In "I am ignorant" (<s>aham ajñaḥ</s>), the negative particle <s>na</s> does not denote the mere absence of knowledge in the self -- because there is absence of that in one who possesses knowledge. Nor does it denote the absence of experience -- because the word denoting knowledge does not express that. And purposelessness is not appropriate; therefore by this very impossibility [there is] figurative usage.' --
Let <s>avidyā</s> of the described nature be its referent!
'But there is doubt!' -- No,

children.text:
asamatvāt koṭidvayasya/ anyatra hi pratiyoginivṛttir nañarthaḥ/ atra tu
          pratiyogivyāpyanivṛttir iti/ jānātisamabhivyāhṛtasya nañaḥ kvacid
          uktalakṣaṇāvidyāviṣayatvasiddhim antareṇa na saṃdeha ity avaśyaṃbhāvena saiva
          jānātisamabhivyāhṛtasya nañaḥ sarvatra tadviṣayatvam avagamayati vilumpati
          jñānābhāvakoṭyantaram iti kva saṃdehāvakāśaḥ/ tad evaṃ lakṣaṇāhetvabhāve ’nubhavābhāvo ’py
          ātmani na pratyakṣeṇa gṛhyata iti pariśeṣād uktalakṣaṇāvidyaivājña iti pratibhāsasya
          viṣaya iti sthitam/
children.translated_text: because the two alternatives are not on equal footing. Elsewhere, the meaning of the negative particle is the exclusion of the counter-correlate; but here it is the exclusion of what is pervaded by the counter-correlate. Without establishing that the negative particle conjoined with <s>jānāti</s> (to know) sometimes has the described <s>avidyā</s> as its object, there is no doubt [about its meaning]; and since this is inevitably the case, that very [avidyā] -- by making known its being the object of the negative particle conjoined with <s>jānāti</s> everywhere -- eliminates the alternative of the absence-of-knowledge interpretation. So where is the room for doubt? Thus, when the cause of figurative usage is absent and the absence of experience too is not apprehended in the self by perception, by the method of elimination, <s>avidyā</s> of the described nature alone is the object of the appearance 'I am ignorant' -- this is established.
reference marker

children.text:
astu vā jñānābhāvapratibhāsaḥ/ ayam abhāvaś ca pratiyogī yatra niṣidhyate na tatas
          tattvāntaram anyadadhikaraṇabhāvāt/ mā bhūd anyabhāvatvam anyābhāvatvaṃ tu syāt/ nanu tad
          api viruddham/ satyaṃ sati bhede/ sa ca pramāṇāt/ tac ca sati pratiyogyabhāvādhikaraṇatas
          tattvāntare/ nanu ghaṭavati bhūtale ghaṭābhāvamitivyavahṛtī syātām iti cet — mā bhūtām ete
          pratiyoginā sahānubhūyamāne ’dhikaraṇe/ pratiyogismaraṇe saty anubhūyamāne ’dhikaraṇe tu
          syātām/ evam apy upapattau na tattvāntaraviṣayatvaṃ kalpyam/ kānupapattir iti ced
          bādhakābhāvas tāvad ukta eva/ bādhakaṃ tu kalpanāgauravam eva/ tathā hi tattvāntaratvaṃ
          tāvad ekaṃ kalpyam/ tasyāparokṣatvāyendriyasaṃnikarṣaḥ kalpyaḥ/ sa ca saṃyogādir na
          bhavatīti saṃyuktaviśeṣaṇatvādiḥ kalpya ity ato varam uktalakṣaṇasyādhikaraṇasya
          vyavahāraviṣaye ’ṅgīkāraḥ/ sati caivaṃ jñānābhāvenāpi pratiyogismṛtau satyām anubhūyamānam
          adhikaraṇaṃ jñātaiva/ sa ca na kevalam antaḥkaraṇam/ jaḍatvāt/ nāpi kevala ātmaiva/
          apariṇāmitvād aguṇatvāc ca/ ata ubhayor abhedādhyāsaḥ/ ātmādhyāsaś coktalakṣaṇāvidyātmety
          āyātam avidyāyām evāham ajña iti pratibhāsaḥ pramāṇam iti/
children.translated_text: Or let there be the appearance of the absence of knowledge. But this absence, where the counter-correlate is negated, is not a separate reality from that [locus] -- because of being a different substratum. 'Let it not be a different entity, but let it be a different absence' -- but that too is contradictory. True, if there is difference. And that [difference requires] a means of knowledge. And that [requires] a separate reality from the substratum-and-counter-correlate-absence. Objection: 'On a ground containing a pot, there would be the usage "absence of pot"' -- let there not be! These [usages occur] when the substratum is experienced together with the counter-correlate. But when the memory of the counter-correlate is present and the substratum is being experienced, they would occur. Even so, when [the usage] is explicable, the object should not be construed as a separate reality. 'What is the impossibility?' -- the absence of a defeater has already been stated. But the defeater is the excess of postulation (<s>kalpanāgaurava</s>) itself. For thus: first, a separate reality must be postulated; then, for its immediacy, a sense-organ contact must be postulated; and since that cannot be conjunction and the like, conjunction-with-a-qualified-entity and the like must be postulated -- therefore, it is better to accept the described substratum as the domain of worldly usage. And if so, even in the case of the absence of knowledge, when the memory of the counter-correlate is present, the experienced substratum is the knower himself. And that is not merely the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) -- because of being insentient. Nor is it merely the self alone -- because of being non-transforming and without qualities. Therefore, [it is] the superimposition of non-difference of both. And the superimposition upon the self is of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> of the described kind -- this is the conclusion. The appearance 'I am ignorant' is the valid means of knowledge for <s>avidyā</s> itself.
reference marker

children.text:
anumānaṃ ca — vivādapadaṃ pramāṇajñānaṃ
          svaprāgabhāvavyatirikta-svaviṣayāvaraṇasvanivartyasvadeśagatavastvantarapūrvakam
          aprakāśitārthaprakāśakatvāt/ andhakāre prathamotpannapradīpaprabhāvad iti/ vastupūrvakam
          ity ukta ātmavastupūrvakatvenārthāntaratā/ tadarthaṃ vastvantareti/ tathāpi viṣayabhūte
          vastvantare ’rthāntaratā/ tadarthaṃ svadeśagateti/ adṛṣṭādikaṃ pratyādeṣṭuṃ svanivartyeti/
          uttarajñānanivartyaṃ prathamajñānaṃ nivartayituṃ svaviṣayāvaraṇeti/ prāgabhāvaṃ
          pratikṣeptuṃ svaprāgabhāvavyatirikteti/ svaprāgabhāvavyatiriktapūrvakam ity ukte
          viṣayeṇārthāntaratā/ tadarthaṃ viṣayāvaraṇeti/ tādṛśam andhakāraṃ vyāseddhuṃ
          svanivartyeti/ viṣayagatām ajñātatāṃ nirākartuṃ svadeśagateti/ mithyājñānam apohituṃ
          vastvantareti/ dhārāvāhikavijñāne vyabhicāraṃ vyāseddhum aprakāśiteti/
          madhyavartipradīpaprabhāyāṃ sādhyasādhanavaidhuryapratirodhāya prathamotpannaviśeṣaṇam/
          saurālokavyāptadeśasthapradīpaprabhāpratikṣepāyāndhakāreti/
children.translated_text: And the inference is: the disputed valid cognition (<s>pramāṇajñāna</s>) is preceded by a real entity at its own location that is removable by itself, that is the concealment of its own object, that is different from its own prior absence — because it illuminates what was not previously illuminated — like the light of a lamp first produced in darkness. 'Preceded by a real entity' is stated — [meaning] preceded by the real entity that is the self; [the qualifier] 'a different entity' is to avoid the charge of irrelevance. For that purpose, 'a different entity.' Even so, there would be irrelevance regarding a different entity that is the object — for that purpose, 'at its own location.' To preclude [the objection of] unseen destiny (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) and the like, 'removable by itself.' To exclude the first knowledge's being removable by a later knowledge, 'concealment of its own object.' To counter the prior absence, 'different from its own prior absence.' If one states 'preceded by something different from its own prior absence,' there is irrelevance regarding the object — for that purpose, 'concealment of the object.' To exclude such darkness [as a counter-example], 'removable by itself.' To negate the unknownness pertaining to the object, 'at its own location.' To counter false knowledge, 'a different entity.' To exclude the case of streaming cognition [as a counter-example], 'not previously illuminated.' The qualification 'first produced' [in the example] is to prevent the defect of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and <s>sādhana</s> (probans) being vitiated in the case of a lamp-light in the middle [of other lights]. 'In darkness' is to counter the lamp-light in a place pervaded by sunlight.

children.text:
na ca jñānasādhake pramāṇe vyabhicāraḥ śaṅkanīyaḥ/ vipratipannaṃ praty
          asattvanivṛttimātrasya pramāṇakṛtyatvāt/ tad uktaṃ devatādhikaraṇe kalpatarukārair
          anumānādibhir asattvanivṛttiḥ kriyata iti/ nanu sādhanavikalo dṛṣṭānta iti cen na/
          prakāśaśabdena tamovirodhyākārasya vivakṣitatvāt/ tad uktaṃ vivaraṇavivaraṇe
          sahajasarvajñaviṣṇubhaṭṭopādhyāyaiḥ — na cātra pakṣadṛṣṭāntayor ekaprakāśarūpānanvayaḥ
          śaṅkanīyaḥ/ tamovirodhyākāro hi prakāśaśabdavācyaḥ/ tenākāreṇaikyam ubhayatrāstīti/
          narendragiriśrīcaraṇais tv ittham uktam — aprakāśitaprakāśavyavahārahetutvaṃ hetvarthaḥ/
          tasya cobhayatrānugatatvān nāsiddhyādir iti/
children.translated_text: Nor should deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) be suspected in the means of knowledge that produces cognition. Because with respect to what is disputed, the function of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is merely the removal of non-being [of knowledge]. As stated by the author of the <s>Kalpataru</s> in the <s>devatādhikaraṇa</s>: 'Through inference and the like, the removal of non-being is accomplished.' Now, if the example lacks the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) — no, because by the word 'illumination' (<s>prakāśa</s>), the form that is the opposite of darkness is intended. As stated in the <s>Vivaraṇavivaraṇa</s> by <s>Sahajasarvajña Viṣṇubhaṭṭopādhyāya</s>: 'Nor should the failure of the common property of a single form of illumination between the thesis and the example be suspected. For what is denoted by the word <s>prakāśa</s> is the form that is the opposite of darkness. With that form, there is unity in both cases.' But the venerable <s>Narendragiri</s> stated thus: 'The meaning of the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is being the cause of the practical usage of illuminating what is not [yet] illuminated. And since that is present in both cases, there is no [defect of] unestablishedness and the like.'
reference marker

children.text: śruteś ca/ bhūyaś cānte viśvamāyānivṛttiḥ ityādikā śrutiḥ/
children.translated_text: And from <s>śruti</s>: 'And at the end, the cessation of the universal <s>māyā</s>' — such is the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: taraty avidyāṃ vitatāṃ hṛdi yasmin niveśite/
children.translated_text: He who, having settled [<s>Brahman</s>] in the heart, crosses over the extended <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),

children.text: yogī māyām ameyāya tasmai vidyātmane namaḥ// iti ca/
children.translated_text: that <s>yogin</s> [crosses over] the immeasurable <s>māyā</s> — homage to Him whose nature is knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>). Thus also.

children.text:
etenaitat pratyuktaṃ yad uktaṃ bhāskareṇa kṣapaṇakacaraṇaṃ pramāṇaśaraṇe
          bhedābhedavādināṃ bhāvarūpam ajñānaṃ nāsti kiṃ tu jñānābhāva iti/ tathā ca
          bhāskarapraṇītaśārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣyagranthaḥ/ yad eva pararūpādarśanaṃ saivāvidyeti
          bhāvarūpājñānānabhyupagame jīveśvarādivibhāgānupapatteḥ/ na ca bhāvikaḥ paramātmano ’ṃśo
          jīva iti vācyam/
children.translated_text: By this, the following is refuted — what was stated by <s>Bhāskara</s>, following the <s>Kṣapaṇaka</s> (Jaina) path, among the <s>bhedābheda</s> (difference-and-identity) proponents who take refuge in <s>pramāṇa</s>: 'there is no <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance) having a positive nature; rather it is merely the absence of knowledge.' And thus the work of <s>Bhāskara</s>, the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣya</s>. [He says:] 'The very non-seeing of the other's form is <s>avidyā</s>' — but without accepting positively-natured ignorance, the distinction of <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord), and the like is impossible. Nor should one say that the <s>jīva</s> is a real part (<s>aṃśa</s>) of the Supreme Self —
Partless, actionless, peaceful, faultless, stainless —
because of contradiction with such <s>śrutis</s>.
reference marker

children.text:
kecana śāktāḥ — śaktiṃ māyāśabdārthabhūtāṃ jagatkāraṇatvenāṅgīkṛtāṃ satyām abhyupetya
          mātuliṅgagadākheṭavidhāriṇī mahālakṣmīs tasyāḥ prathamāvatāra iti varṇayanti/ sā ca
          kālarātriḥ sarasvatīti dve śaktī utpādya brahmāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ śriyaṃ ca striyam utpādayām
          āsa/ svayaṃ mithunaṃ janayitvā svasute apy āha — aham iva yuvām api mithunam utpādayatam
          iti/ tataḥ kālarātrir mahādevaṃ puruṣaṃ svarāṃ striyaṃ ca janayām āsa/ sarasvatī ca viṣṇuṃ
          puruṣaṃ gaurīṃ ca striyam udapādayat/ tataś cādir vivāham akarod akārayac ca/ evaṃ
          brahmaṇe svarāṃ viṣṇave śriyaṃ śivāya gaurīṃ dattvā śaktiyuktānāṃ teṣāṃ
          sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārākhyāni karmāṇi pratyapādayad iti/ tad etanmataṃ
          śrutyādimūlapramāṇavidhuratayā svotprekṣāmātraparikalpitam iti svarūpavyākriyaiva
          nirākriyety upekṣaṇīyam/ tataś cānirvacanīyānādyavidyālasitaḥ pratyagātmani pratīyamānaḥ
          pramātṛtvādiprapañca ity alam atiprasaṅgena/
