children.translated_text: Certain <s>Śāktas</s> (Goddess-worshippers), having accepted as real the <s>śakti</s> (power) that is the meaning of the word <s>māyā</s> and is accepted as the cause of the world, describe <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, who holds a citron, mace, and shield, as the first incarnation of that [<s>śakti</s>]. And she, having produced two powers — <s>Kālarātri</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s> — created <s>Brahmā</s> as male and <s>Śrī</s> as female. Having herself produced the couple, she said to her own children: 'Just as I [did], you two also produce a couple.' Then <s>Kālarātri</s> produced <s>Mahādeva</s> as male and <s>Svarā</s> as female. And <s>Sarasvatī</s> produced <s>Viṣṇu</s> as male and <s>Gaurī</s> as female. Then the primal one (<s>Ādi</s>) performed and caused to be performed the marriages. Thus, having given <s>Svarā</s> to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śrī</s> to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Gaurī</s> to <s>Śiva</s>, she assigned to them, now endowed with their <s>śaktis</s>, the functions called creation, preservation, and dissolution. This doctrine, being devoid of root authority in <s>śruti</s> and the like, and being fabricated merely from its own imagination, is refuted by its very nature — hence it is to be disregarded. Therefore, the phenomenal world of knower-hood and the like, which appears upon the inner self adorned by beginningless, indefinable <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — but enough of this excessive elaboration.
reference marker

children.text:
nanu kimarthaṃ pramātṛtvādīnām āvidyakatvaṃ nigadyate/ brahmajñānena nivartanāya jīvasya
          brahmabhāvāya vā/
children.translated_text: Now, for what purpose is it said that knower-hood and the like are products of <s>avidyā</s>? Is it for the removal [of bondage] through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, or for the <s>jīva</s> to become <s>Brahman</s>?

children.text:
na prathamaḥ/ śāstraprāmāṇyād eva satyasyāpi jñānena nivṛtter upapatteḥ/ upalambhāc ca/
          tathā hi —
children.translated_text: Not the first — because it is consistent that even what is real can be removed by knowledge, on the authority of scripture alone. And because it is observed. For thus —
Having seen the bridge (<s>setu</s>), a slayer of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> would be freed from the sin of <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a brahmin).

children.text:
ityādinā pāpaṃ sanīsrasyate/ viṣayadoṣadarśanena rāgo dandahyate/ tārkṣyadhyānena viṣaṃ
          śamyate/ evaṃ kartṛtvādibandhaḥ pāramārthiko ’pi tattvajñānena nivartyeta/
children.translated_text: By such statements, sin is shaken off. Through seeing the defects of sense-objects, attachment is burned away. Through meditating on <s>Tārkṣya</s> (Garuḍa), poison is pacified. Similarly, even though the bondage of agentship and the like is ultimately real, it could be removed by the knowledge of reality.

children.text:
na caramaḥ/ aupādhikasya jīvabhāvasyopādhinivṛttyā nivṛttau brahmabhāvasaṃbhavāt/ tasmād
          bandhasyāvidyakatvavācoyuktiḥ sāvadyeti cet —
children.translated_text: Nor the second — because when the <s>jīva</s>-state, which is conditioned by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), ceases through the removal of the limiting adjuncts, the state of <s>Brahman</s> is possible. Therefore, the verbal claim that bondage is a product of <s>avidyā</s> is defective — if so,

children.text:
naitad anavadyam/ satyasyātmavaj jñānanivartyatvānupapatteḥ/ bandhasya mithyātvam
          antareṇa śāstraprāmāṇyād api tadasiddheś ca/ śāstram api
children.translated_text: that is not flawless. Because what is real cannot be removed by knowledge, unlike the self. And because without the unreality of bondage, even on the authority of scripture, its [removal] is not established. For scripture too
reference marker

operates by accepting the word-power recognized in common usage and the fitness of the word-meaning — by the principle: 'A word whose capacity is known from common usage is informative in the <s>Veda</s> as well.'

children.text:
it nyāyena lokāvalokitāṃ padaśaktiṃ padārthayogyatāṃ corarīkṛtya pracaratīti/ aparathā
          ādityo yūpaḥ yajamānaḥ prastaraḥ ityādivākyastomasya yathāśrute ’rthe prāmāṇyāpatteḥ/
          vaidikyāḥ kriyāyāḥ samakṣakṣayitayā pāratrikaphalakaraṇatvānyathānupapattyā apūrvāṅgīkaraṇānupapatteś

ca/ loke ca śuktivyaktitattvābhivyaktāv apanīyamānasyāropitasya mithyātvadṛṣṭau
          taddṛṣṭāntāvaṣṭambhenātmatattvasākṣātkāravidyāpanodyasyāvidyakasya bandhasya
          mithyātvānumānasaṃbhavāt/ vimataṃ mithyā adhiṣṭhānatattvajñānanivartyatvāc
          chuktikārūpyavad iti/ na ca vimataṃ satyaṃ bhāsamānatvād iti pratiprayoge samānabalatayā
          bādhapratirodhaḥ/ pratirodhabhiyānyataradoṣatvasaṃbhavād iti vaditavyam/
          marumarīcikodakādau savyabhicārāt/ abādhitatvena viśeṣaṇān na doṣa iti cet — maivaṃ
          bhāṣiṣṭhāḥ/ viśeṣaṇāsiddheḥ/
children.translated_text: And because, in the world, when the reality of a nacre-object is revealed and the superimposed [silver] being removed is seen to be unreal — relying on that illustration, an inference of the unreality of bondage, which is a product of <s>avidyā</s> removed by the direct knowledge of the reality of the self, is possible: 'the disputed [bondage] is unreal, because it is removable by the knowledge of the reality of the substrate, like the silver in nacre.' Nor should one say that in the counter-inference — 'the disputed [bondage] is real, because it appears' — since the two are of equal force, there is resistance to sublation (<s>bādha</s>). [Nor should one say:] 'because of the fear of counter-resistance, there is the possibility of either being defective.' Because in desert-mirage water and the like, there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) [of the counter-inference]. If one says 'there is no defect because of the qualifier "unsublated"' — do not say so, because the qualifier is unestablished.

Otherwise, the mass of sentences such as 'the sun is the sacrificial post,' 'the sacrificer is the grass-bundle,' and the like would absurdly have authoritativeness in their literal meaning. And because, since the Vedic rite is seen to perish simultaneously [upon completion], the acceptance of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency) — which is possible only through the impossibility of explaining the production of a result in the other world [without it] — would be impossible.

children.text:
tatredaṃ bhavān pṛṣṭo vyācaṣṭām/ katipayapuruṣakatipayakālābādhitatvaṃ hetuviśeṣaṇaṃ
          kriyate sarvathā bādhavaidhuryaṃ vā/ na prathamaḥ/
children.translated_text: Here, let the gentleman, being asked, explain: is the qualifier of the reason 'being unsublated by a certain number of persons for a certain period,' or is it 'the complete absence of sublation in every way?' Not the first —
reference marker
An object inferred even with effort by skilled reasoners
is demonstrated quite otherwise by others who are more expert —

children.text:
iti nyāyena tricaturapratipattṛpratipāditasyāpi pratipattrantareṇa prakārāntaram
          urarīkṛtya pratipādanāt/ nāpi caramaḥ/ sarvathā bādhavaidhuryasyāsarvajñadurjñeyatvāt/
          yady evaṃ hanta tarhi jñānātmano ’pi satyatvaṃ nāvagamyata iti cet — maivaṃ maṃsthāḥ/ tat
          satyaṃ sa ātmā ity āgamasaṃvādagateḥ/ na ca prapañce ’py ayaṃ nyāya iti mantavyam/
          tādṛśasyāgamasyānupalambhāt/ pratyutādvitīyatvaṃ śrāvayantyāḥ śruteḥ prapañcamithyātva eva
          pakṣapātāt/ nanu kalpanāmātraśarīrasya pakṣasapakṣavipakṣādeḥ sarvasulabhatvena
          jayaparājayavyavasthayā kathaṃ kathā pratheta/ kātra kathaṃtā/
children.translated_text: by this principle, because even what has been established by three or four cognizers can be demonstrated in another way by another cognition, having accepted a different mode. Nor the second — because the complete absence of sublation in every way is unknowable to one who is not omniscient. If so — well then, the reality of the self as knowledge is also not ascertained — if so, do not think that. Because through the concordance of scripture — '<s>tat satyam</s>, <s>sa ātmā</s>' (that is the truth, that is the self) — its reality is established. Nor should one think this principle applies to the phenomenal world also — because no such scripture is found. On the contrary, the <s>śruti</s> that proclaims non-duality shows partiality precisely toward the unreality of the phenomenal world. Now, since the thesis, co-thesis, counter-thesis, and the like, whose body is mere conceptual construction, are easily available to all, how could a debate proceed with a fixed determination of victory and defeat? What difficulty is there?
reference marker

children.text:
evaṃ tricaturajñānajanmano nādhikā matiḥ iti nyāyena tricaturakakṣyāviśrāntasya
          tattadābhāsalakṣaṇānāliṅgitasya dūṣaṇabhūṣaṇādes tatra kathāṅgatvāṅgīkārāt/ ata evoktaṃ
          khaṇḍanakāreṇa — vyāvahārikīṃ pramāṇasattām ādāya vicārārambhaḥ iti/ na ca bhedagrāhibhiḥ
          pramāṇair advaitaśruter jaghanyateti śaṅkyam/ brahmaṇi pāramārthikasatyatvena
          tadāvedikāyās tattvāvedanalakṣaṇaprāmāṇyāyāḥ śruter vyāvahārikapramāṇabhāvānāṃ
          pratyakṣādīnāṃ ca vibhinnaviṣayatayā parasparaṃ bādhyabādhakabhāvāsaṃbhavāt/ tad apy uktaṃ
          tenaiva —
children.translated_text: By the principle 'an intellect born from three or four [cognitions] of ignorance has no further [power],' because what rests at the level of three or four [logical levels] — the semblances of refutation, embellishment, and the like that are not grasped [as ultimately real] — their status as parts of debate is accepted there. Therefore, the author of the <s>Khaṇḍana</s> (<s>Śrīharṣa</s>) stated: 'The inquiry begins by accepting the transactional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) reality of <s>pramāṇa</s>.' Nor should it be suspected that perception and other [<s>pramāṇas</s>] that grasp difference make the <s>advaita-śruti</s> (scripture of non-duality) subordinate. Because the <s>śruti</s>, which has as its ultimate reality (<s>pāramārthikasatya</s>) <s>Brahman</s> and which has the authority of revealing reality, and the transactional means of valid knowledge such as perception — since they have different domains — the relation of sublating and being sublated between them is impossible. As stated by the same [<s>Śrīharṣa</s>]:
The sublation of that <s>advaita-śruti</s> by perception is refuted;

children.text: nānumānādi taṃ kartuṃ tavāpi kṣamate mate//
children.translated_text: nor is inference and the like capable of doing so, even in your view.
If you are wealthy in intellect, then give your wisdom for the sublation of that [<s>śruti</s>],
if you wish to cast the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) obtained in hand into the ocean.

children.text:
tasmāt tattvajñānena nivartanāyāsya bandhasyājñānakalpitatvam aṅgīkartavyam/ yata uktaṃ
          yato jñānam ajñānasya nivartakam iti/
children.translated_text: Therefore, for removal through the knowledge of reality, this bondage must be accepted as fabricated by ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>). As stated: 'because knowledge is the remover of ignorance.'
reference marker

children.text:
yad uktaṃ satyasyāpi duritasya setudarśanena nivṛttir upalabhyata iti/ tad ayuktam/
          vihitakriyānuṣṭhānena janitasya dharmasyādharmanivartakatvadhrauvyāt/ dharmeṇa pāpam
          apanudanti iti śruteḥ/ pramāṇavastuparatantraśālinyā darśanakriyāyāś
          coditapuruṣaprayatnatantratvābhāvena vidhānāsaṃbhavāt/
children.translated_text: What was said — that even real sin is observed to be removed by seeing a bridge — that is not right. Because the invariable [rule] is that <s>dharma</s> (merit), generated by the performance of an enjoined act, is the remover of <s>adharma</s> (demerit). From the <s>śruti</s>: 'By <s>dharma</s> they dispel sin.' And because the act of seeing, being dependent on the object as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, cannot be enjoined since it is not subject to deliberate human effort.
One would be freed from the sin of killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by bathing in that great ocean —

children.text:
ityādismṛtivihitabrahmacaryāṅgasahitadūrataradeśagamanasādhyabrahma-hanananivṛttiphalakasetusnānapraśaṃsārthatvāt/
          yasya hi darśanamātreṇaiva duritopaśamaḥ kim uta snānena/ anyathā dūragamanānarthakyaṃ
          prasajjeta/ tatra kharādīnām apy anarthanivṛttir āpatet/ andhasya na syāc ca/
children.translated_text: because [such statements] are intended to praise the bathing at the bridge (<s>setu</s>), which yields the fruit of removing the killing of a brahmin and which is accomplished through distant travel accompanied by celibacy and other disciplines enjoined by <s>smṛti</s>. For one whose mere seeing pacifies sin, how much more [effective] is bathing! Otherwise, the purposelessness of the distant travel would absurdly follow. In that case, even donkeys and the like would have their calamities removed. And for the blind, [liberation] would not occur.
Now —

children.text: agnicit kapilā rājā satī bhikṣur mahodadhiḥ/
children.translated_text: One who has built the fire-altar (<s>agnicita</s>), a tawny cow, a king, a virtuous woman (<s>satī</s>), a mendicant, and the great ocean —

children.text: dṛṣṭamātrāḥ punanty ete tasmāt paśyeta nityaśaḥ//
children.translated_text: these purify by being merely seen; therefore one should see [them] always.

children.text: iti kvacid darśanakriyāyā api vidhānaṃ darīdṛśyata iti cet —
children.translated_text: If somewhere even the act of seeing appears to be enjoined — if so,

children.text:
maivaṃ vocaḥ/ tatrāpy anayaivānupapattyāgnicidādyarghaparicaryādāv eva
          tātparyāvadhāraṇāt/ yac coktaṃ viṣayadoṣadarśanād rāgo dandahyata iti/ tatra
          viṣayadoṣadarśanena virodhabhūtānabhiratisaṃjñakavairāgyaikaprādurbhāvād rāganivṛttau
          tadadarśanamātram iti na vyabhicāraḥ/ yad api tārkṣyadhyānādinā viṣādi satyaṃ vinaśyatīti/
          tan na śliṣyate/ tatrāpi mantraprayogādikriyāyā eva viṣādyapanodakatvāt/ dhyānasya
          pramātvābhāvāc ca/ yad avādy aupādhikasya jīvabhāvasyopādhinivṛttyā nivṛttau
          brahmabhāvopapatter na tadartham arthavaitathyakathanam iti/ tad api
          kāśakuśāvalambanakalpam/ vikalpāsahatvāt/ kim upādheḥ satyatvam abhipretya mithyātvaṃ vā/
          na prathamaḥ/ pramāṇābhāvāt/ nāparaḥ/ iṣṭāpatteḥ/ tasmād āvidyako bheda iti śrutāv
          advitīyatvopapattaye ’bhidhīyate na tu vyasanitayā/
children.translated_text: Do not say so! Because even there, by this very impossibility, the purport is determined to be in the service of fire-altar construction (<s>agniciti</s>) and the like. As for the statement that attachment is burned by seeing the faults of objects — therein, through seeing the faults of objects, since only dispassion — designated as non-attachment, which is the contrary [of attachment] — arises, the cessation of attachment is merely the non-perception of that [attachment]; hence there is no deviation. As for the [claim] that poison and the like are truly destroyed by meditation on <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) and the like — that does not cohere. Because even there, it is the action of applying <s>mantras</s> and the like that removes poison and the like. And because meditation lacks the status of a valid means of knowledge. As for the statement that, since the <s>jīva</s>-state is conditioned (<s>aupādhika</s>), upon the removal of the limiting condition, the <s>Brahman</s>-state is justified, and therefore there is no need to declare the falsity of objects — that too is like grasping at <s>kāśa</s> and <s>kuśa</s> grass [i.e., grasping at straws]. Because [it] cannot withstand the alternatives. Is the reality or the falsity of the limiting condition intended? Not the first — because there is no means of valid knowledge [for a real limiting condition within non-dual <s>Brahman</s>]. Not the latter — because [then] the desired conclusion is conceded. Therefore, [the statement] 'difference is rooted in <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)' is stated in <s>Śruti</s> for the purpose of justifying [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being without a second — not out of an obsessive attachment [to the thesis of falsity].

children.text:
yadi vastutaḥ sarvopadravarahitam ātmatattvaṃ tarhi kathaṃkāraṃ dehādirūpaṃ kārāgāraṃ
          kāraṃkāraṃ punaḥ punas tatra praviśati/ tad atiphalgu/ avidyāyā anāditvena dattottaratvāt/
          ato nivṛttyupāya evānveṣaṇīyaḥ prekṣāvatā/ na tu vismayaḥ kartavyaḥ/ tataś ca
          tattvamasādividyayā tadavidyānivṛttau niratiśayānandātmalābharūpaparamapuruṣārthaḥ
          setsyati/ tathā cāpastambasmṛtiḥ — ātmalābhān na paraṃ vidyata iti/
children.translated_text: If the reality of the self (<s>ātman</s>) is truly free from all afflictions, then how does it enter again and again into the prison-house in the form of the body and the like? That is exceedingly flimsy — because the answer has already been given through the beginninglessness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Therefore, the discerning person should seek only the means of its cessation — not wonder [at its existence]. And thus, through the knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) of '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' ('That thou art') and the like, upon the cessation of that <s>avidyā</s>, the supreme human goal — in the form of the attainment of the self that is unsurpassed bliss — will be accomplished. And thus the <s>Āpastamba Smṛti</s> [states]: 'There is nothing higher than the attainment of the self.'

children.text: nanv asau nityalabdhaḥ/ na hi svayam eva svasyālabdho bhavati/
children.translated_text: Objection: 'But that [self] is eternally attained! For one's own self is never unattained by oneself.'

children.text:
satyam/ kiṃ tv anādimāyāsaṃbandhāt kṣīrodakavat samudācāravṛttitāṃ na labhate/ tathā ca
          yathā śabarādibhir bālyāt svasutaiḥ saha vardhito rājaputras tajjātīyam ātmānam avagacchan
          bandhubhir ya evaṃbhūto rājā sa tvam asīti bodhite svarūpe labdhasvarūpa iva bhavati tathā
          veśyāsthānīyayānādyavidyayā svabhāvāntaraṃ nīta ātmā mātṛsthānīyayā tat tvam asītyādikayā
          śrutyā svabhāvaṃ nīyate/ etad āhus traividyavṛddhāḥ —
children.translated_text: True. But due to the beginningless association with <s>māyā</s> (illusion), [the self] does not obtain [recognition of] its own nature in conventional practice — like [butter in] milk. And thus, just as a prince who has been raised from childhood with the sons of <s>Śabaras</s> (forest-dwelling tribes) and the like, understanding himself to be of their kind, when informed by his kinsmen 'you who are such [a person] are the king' — upon being instructed about his true nature, becomes as if one who has [newly] attained his own nature — so too the self, having been led to a nature other [than its own] by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which is like a courtesan, is brought back to its own nature by the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation), which is like a mother, through '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' ('That thou art') and the like. This is what the elders learned in the three <s>Vedas</s> say:

children.text: nīcānāṃ vasatau tadīyatanayaiḥ sārdhaṃ ciraṃ vardhitas
children.translated_text: 'Raised for a long time in the dwelling of lowly people together with their sons,

children.text: tajjātīyam avaiti rājatanayaḥ svātmānam apy añjasā/
children.translated_text: the king's son easily understands himself to be of their kind.

children.text: saṃvāde mahadādibhiḥ saha vasaṃs tadvad bhavet pūruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>Puruṣa</s> (soul), dwelling [in association] with <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle) and the rest,
falsely considers himself to be enmeshed in the web of happiness and sorrow — alas!

children.text: dātā bhogaparaḥ samagravibhavo yaḥ śāsitā duṣkṛtām
children.translated_text: The one who is a giver, devoted to enjoyments, of complete sovereignty, the ruler of wrongdoers —

children.text: rājā sa tvam asīti rakṣitṛmukhāc chrutvā yathāvat sa tu/
children.translated_text: "You are that king!" — having heard this from the mouths of the protectors, properly,

children.text: rājībhūya jayārtham eva yatate tadvat pumān bodhitaḥ/
children.translated_text: he, having become king, strives for victory alone. Likewise, a person, enlightened

children.text: śrutyā tat tvam asīty apāsya duritaṃ brahmaiva saṃpadyate//
children.translated_text: by the <s>Śruti</s> "That thou art" — casting off sin, becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself.'

children.text:
etenaitat pratyuktaṃ yad uktaṃ paraiḥ kiṃ dvayos tādātmyam ekasya vā/ nādyaḥ/
          advaitabhaṅgaprasaṅgāt/ na dvitīyaḥ/ asaṃbhavād iti/
children.translated_text: By this, the following objection raised by others is answered: 'Is the identity [expressed by "That thou art"] of two [entities] or of one? Not the first — because the consequence would be the breaking of non-duality. Not the second — because it is impossible.'

children.text:
tan na/ avidyāparikalpitabhedanivṛttiparatvena tat tvam
          asyāditādātmyavādaprāmāṇyopapatteḥ/ tau ca paryanuyogaparihārāv agrāhiṣātāṃ
          manīṣibhiḥ/
children.translated_text: Not so — because the authority of the identity-statements such as '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' is justified as being oriented toward the removal of difference imagined through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). And these two — the objection and its resolution — have been grasped by the wise:

children.text: na dvayor asti tādātmyaṃ na caikasyādvayatvataḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The identity of two [entities] does not exist; nor [is there identity] of one, because of [its being] non-dual;
the invalidity of <s>Śruti</s> [does not follow] in this way — merely from the cessation of superimposition.' Thus.

children.text:
tataś ca tat tvam asīti tattvaṃpadārthaśravaṇamananabhāvanābalabhuvā
          sākṣātkāreṇānādyavidyānivṛttau saccidānandaikarasabrahmāvirbhāvaḥ saṃpatsyata iti brahmaṇo
          jijñāsyatvaṃ prathamasūtroktaṃ yuktam/
children.translated_text: And thus, through the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) — born from the force of hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), reflection (<s>manana</s>), and meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) on the meaning of the words '<s>tat</s>' (That) and '<s>tvam</s>' (thou) in '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' — upon the cessation of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the manifestation of <s>Brahman</s>, whose single essence is existence-consciousness-bliss (<s>saccidānanda</s>), will come about. Thus, the statement in the first <s>sūtra</s> that <s>Brahman</s> is to be inquired into is justified.

children.text: ajñātaṃ viṣayo brahma jñātaṃ tac ca prayojanam/
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahman</s>, unknown, is the subject-matter; <s>Brahman</s>, known, is the purpose;

children.text: mumukṣur adhikārī syāt saṃbandhaḥ śaktitaḥ sruteḥ// iti/
children.translated_text: the seeker of liberation would be the qualified student; the relation is that of the capacity of the <s>Śruti</s>.' Thus.

children.text:
janmādy asya yataḥ iti dvitīyasūtre brahma svarūpalakṣaṇataṭasthalakṣaṇābhyāṃ nyarūpi/
          tatra svarūpāntargatatve sati vyāvartakaṃ svarūpalakṣaṇaṃ satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma
          ityādivedāntaiḥ pratipāditam/ tasya satyajñānādyātmakasvarūpāntargatatve sati
          vyāvartakatvāt/ taṭasthalakṣaṇaṃ yato vā imāni ityādīni vākyāni nirūpayanti
          jagajjanmādikāraṇatvena/ tad uktaṃ vivaraṇe —
children.translated_text: In the second <s>sūtra</s>, '<s>janmādy asya yataḥ</s>' ('From which [arises] the birth and the rest of this [universe]'), <s>Brahman</s> was defined by both the essential definition (<s>svarūpalakṣaṇa</s>) and the incidental definition (<s>taṭasthalakṣaṇa</s>). Therein, the essential definition — that which, while being within the essential nature, is differentiating — is taught by <s>Vedānta</s> [passages] such as '<s>satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma</s>' ('Truth, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>') and the like. Because it is differentiating while being within the essential nature of truth, knowledge, and the like. The incidental definition is set forth by passages such as '<s>yato vā imāni</s>' ('From which indeed these [beings arise]') and the like, through [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being the cause of the origination, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe. As stated in the <s>Vivaraṇa</s>:
'The origination, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe — from which cause these are accomplished —
that is indicated by the two definitions: the essential and the incidental.' Thus.

children.text:
śāstrayonitvāt iti tṛtīyasūtre prathamavarṇakena ṣaṣṭhīsamāsam āśritya sarvajñatvaṃ
          pratyapādi/ dvitīyavarṇakena bahuvrīhisamāsam abhyupagamya brahmaṇo vedāntapramāṇakatvaṃ
          pratyajñāyi/
children.translated_text: In the third <s>sūtra</s>, '<s>śāstrayonitvāt</s>' ('Because [<s>Brahman</s>] is the source of scripture'), by the first interpretation, adopting the genitive compound (<s>ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa</s>), [<s>Brahman</s>'s] omniscience was demonstrated. By the second interpretation, accepting the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, it was acknowledged that <s>Brahman</s> is knowable through the <s>Vedānta</s> as the means of knowledge.

children.text:
tat tu samanvayāt iti caturthe sūtre prathamavarṇakena vedāntānāṃ brahmaṇi tātparyaṃ
          pratyapādi/ dvitīyavarṇakena vedāntānāṃ pratipattividhiśeṣatayā brahmapratipādakatvaṃ
          pratyakṣe 'pi/ diṅmātram atra pradarśitam/ śiṣṭaṃ śāstra eva spaṣṭam iti sakalaṃ
          samañjasam//
children.translated_text: In the fourth <s>sūtra</s>, '<s>tat tu samanvayāt</s>' ('But that, because of consistency'), by the first interpretation, the purport of the <s>Vedānta</s> [passages] in [establishing] <s>Brahman</s> was demonstrated. By the second interpretation, even in [the view that] the <s>Vedānta</s> [passages] teach <s>Brahman</s> as a complement to injunctions of meditation — [the purport in <s>Brahman</s> was shown] through direct perception too. Only the gist has been indicated here. The rest is clear in the scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) itself — thus everything is well-established.
May there be prosperity!
Thus concludes the illustrious <s>Śāṅkara</s> (Advaita Vedānta) philosophy — the crest-jewel of all philosophical systems — in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
Thus the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s> is completed.
